found_in: 2.218.x on the branch, 2026-09-07, by the CR-076 lane running its neighbours' suites before pushing
introduced_in: unknown — NOT this lane. Proved by running the same file in a private worktree at 32f41e34, the commit this session started from: the SAME SIX cases fail there, 6 failed / 7 passed / 1 skipped, identical names.
escape_reason: Nothing runs this file on a schedule, so a red that arrives with a product change sits until somebody happens to run the neighbours of what they are editing. The first assertion is 'assert queued == sent' and the print vendor was never handed the batch; the other five then assert 0 == 1 because nothing was sent. The suite stubs apps.integrations.services.dispatch_outbound_batch, which used to resolve to nothing - that module has since grown a real adapter and a provider_connection_status check, and provider_seam's own docstring says a print row now rests queued with provider_not_connected. So the likely cause is the product moving under a signed test rather than the test being wrong, and it is filed rather than guessed at. Same result with JOBS_EAGER on and off.
prevention: Whoever owns the print dispatch path decides whether the suite must configure a provider connection or whether the seam changed shape; either way the six cases are CR-049 task 8's own contract and must go green or be amended with a ruling. Until then this row is what stops it reading as camouflage in a suite that already has other reds.

title: The customer portal never applies a language: PortalApp calls changeLanguage nowhere, so a tenant's language setting and an account's preferred_language both have no effect on any portal screen
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/PortalApp.tsx (zero i18n references); every customer portal screen
found_in: the Product Owner on the live product, 2026-09-07: 'Language setting does not work in customer portal'
introduced_in: present since the portal shipped — the staff shell gained changeLanguage when DEF-SHL-3964 was fixed and the portal was never given the same treatment
escape_reason: The staff app and the portal have SEPARATE shells, and only the staff one was ever wired. ShellWithSession reads the tenant regional block and calls i18n.changeLanguage; PortalApp has zero i18n references and is served no regional block at all, so there is nothing to call it with. Nothing fails: every portal string resolves, in the default language, and every test asserts the English it was written against. It is the same shape as DEF-SHL-3964 one shell along - that defect's own fix comment records that changeLanguage was called NOWHERE in the application, and the portal stayed in that state after the staff app left it.
prevention: Three sources exist and the portal uses none: the tenant setting the staff shell already reads, accounts.preferred_language (BR-CUS-064, a real column), and the browser locale the guest help routes already honour through ?locale=. A signed-in customer should get their account's preference, falling back to the tenant setting; a guest has no account, so the tenant setting with the browser as last resort. The general check: a second shell inherits none of the first shell's wiring, so every global the app applies once - language, regional format, theme - must be asked about again the day a second shell is added.

reported_by: an AI lane (self-reported, from a sibling lane's honest SKIP report)
title: G5, the tenant-isolation gate, looked for pytest in the runner's own interpreter and reported SKIP over 264 runnable isolation tests — hiding a recorded proof that was RED with 3 failures
surface: 10-scripts/gates/g05_isolation.py; the tenant-isolation guarantee (CLAUDE.md hard rule 1) on a multi-tenant product
found_in: 2026-09-07, following a lane's honest report that G5 SKIPPED during its verification sweep — the lane said it would rather name the gap than let a SKIP read as a pass
introduced_in: the gate's own importlib.util.find_spec('pytest') check, which asks about the RUNNER's interpreter rather than searching for one that can run the suite
escape_reason: It is law 7's 'incapable of passing' shape, and the SKIP is what hid it: a gate reporting neither pass nor fail reads as absence of news rather than absence of checking. On this machine bare python3 has neither pytest nor Django and python3.12 has both, so the suite was always runnable - 264 tests collect in 15 seconds. Worse, the skip masked the gate's SECOND half: once the interpreter is resolved it immediately reports that the recorded proof is stale AND WAS RED WHEN TAKEN, 3 isolation tests failing on 2026-09-05. Nobody could see that while the gate skipped. This is the SECOND time this exact mistake was made: G120 was written with sys.executable days earlier, announced the application would not start over a branch that boots perfectly, and was corrected the same way - the lesson did not travel between two gates.
prevention: Resolve an interpreter that can import both pytest and Django, name what was tried, and SKIP only when none exists. The wider habit: a gate that shells out must never ask whether the RUNNER can do the job - it must find something that can. Worth a sweep of every gate using sys.executable or find_spec, since two have now had this bug independently.

title: The customer portal offers eleven languages where the Product Owner ruled English and Spanish only
surface: 06-backend/apps/portal/selectors.py PORTAL_LOCALES; the language picker on CWP-024 and the guest language dropdown that reads it
found_in: step 0 of the DEF-CWP-4440 lane, 2026-09-07 - grepping the registers before building turned up the ruling
introduced_in: PORTAL_LOCALES shipped with eleven codes in CR-068 wave G; the PO ruled two on 2026-09-05 and the constant was never narrowed
escape_reason: No gate reads a PO ruling. The ruling was recorded in the decision log on 2026-09-06 and in one runbook page, and reached neither the portal module's business rules nor any code or test, so nothing anywhere could go red over it. It is the same shape as CLAUDE.md's B14 rule-count line, wrong five times: ratifying a rule and implementing it are two acts and only the first feels like the work.
fixed_commit: d1df45be + a4894307, 2.219.1, 2026-09-07 — BUILT. PO 2026-09-07: 'currently in drop down show only 2 elnglish and spanish'. PORTAL_LOCALES eleven -> ('en','es'). ⚠ THIS ROW'S OWN PREVENTION TEXT IS SUPERSEDED AND IS LEFT ABOVE ONLY AS THE RECORD OF WHAT WAS FEARED: it said narrowing to 'en, es and es-MX' was one line but that the stored de and hi values had to be decided first. Both halves moved. The Spanish is 'es' ALONE - the PO ruled TWO - and es-MX is now the third option a reader already on it sees. The stored-value question was ANSWERED rather than migrated: nobody's choice is reset, and both pickers list the offer plus the reader's own current language where it is neither, through one function (offeredLocales in portal/components/language.ts) so the guest dropdown and CWP-024's cannot show different lists. The guest dropdown was ALSO not reading PORTAL_LOCALES at all - it drew the front end's LOCALE_CODES, the CATALOGUE registry - so the offer now travels on GET portal/public/front and BR-CWP-106 records the rule. Narrowing the OFFER did not move the RESOLUTION: a de account still reads German, on the wire and on screen. RED FIRST: backend 3 failed on the old constant, vitest 7 + 4 + 2 + 1 failed. GREEN: backend 24, the portal suite 706 passed (the 9 that failed were 5s timeouts on a loaded box and pass 49/49 at 30s), tsc 0, G13/G31/G82 PASS. BROWSER on pine-hill in Chromium at 1440x1000: a guest on an en tenant sees English + Espanol; on an es-MX tenant three, with Espanol de Mexico; a de customer sees three with Deutsch, the control NOT blank, over Ubersicht/Rechnungen/Verbrauch/Zahlungen/Anliegen/Meine Daten; after choosing Espanol, two and German gone. ⚠ A SCREENSHOT AND NOTHING ELSE FOUND THE LAST BUG IN IT: the caption read '2 Sprachen verfuegbar.' under a list of THREE, because the helper counted the server's offer and not the rendered list. Fixed, tested, and now asserted on the glass. ⚠ DEF-CWP-4468 (the two-row header) is NOT closed by this and was measured, not assumed: the control shrank 186px -> 105px and the header is still 1100x95 with the nav at 848x79. DEF-CWP-4491 filed (the preference endpoint stores any string as a language) and DEF-4498 (two lanes, one scratchpad filename, one commit message).
prevention: Narrowing PORTAL_LOCALES to en, es and es-MX is one line - but accounts already hold de and hi, and Preferences.tsx renders value={held.locale} against options built from that list, so a narrowed list leaves a blank select over a value the account still carries. The fix has to decide what happens to those stored values (offer the held code as an extra option, or migrate it) before the constant moves. BR-CWP-105 records the ruling and this hazard where the next lane will meet it.

title: The template DESIGNER drew the template LIST's screen id, so a fault photographed on one was filed against the other
surface: SET-10, the template designer (Settings - Configure - Templates - one template); 07-frontend/src/routing/screenIds.ts
found_in: 2026-09-07, rebuilding SET-10 against the design the Product Owner supplied
introduced_in: CR-016 addendum, 2026-08-19 - the screen-id map keys on the ROUTE, and the catalogue and the designer share one route with a ?template= parameter between them
escape_reason: No check compares a badge with the screen it is drawn over. G29 asks whether every id in the map is one an authority defines, which SET-09 is; screenIds.test.tsx asserts the map equals App.tsx's routes, and both screens ARE that one route. The badge is rendered chrome, so no DOM test reads it and no gate looks at rendered output at all (hard-won law 6). r10's own id function has made the distinction since the prototype was drawn - s.tplView ? SET-10. + s.tplView : SET-09 - and nobody had read it.
prevention: ScreenRoute.whenPresent resolves a DETAIL opened over a LIST at the same address, keyed on a parameter's PRESENCE rather than its value, because the value is a template code and enumerating 38 of them is a list that goes stale the day a class is seeded. A named case in screenIds.test.tsx pins both screens and pins the sibling tabs that must not move with it. The general form is worth a sweep: every route where a ?param= replaces the whole screen has this bug waiting.

title: A raw message key reached a clerk's screen: the variant badge for a not-live variant rendered templates.detail.state.not-live
surface: SET-10's variant tabs; 07-frontend/src/features/notifications/TemplateDetail.tsx and all eleven locale catalogues
found_in: 2026-09-07, rebuilding SET-10 - checking every key the new head and rail would need turned up a key the OLD screen was already asking for and not getting
introduced_in: DEF-212 (3), 2026-08-18 - the commit that split 'Inactive' into four states named one of them not-live in code and notLive in the catalogues
escape_reason: The key was built by interpolation and i18n/index.ts sets keySeparator false, so the catalogue key is one flat string that must match character for character. tsc cannot see it - t() takes a string. G15 checks the eleven catalogues hold the SAME keys as each other, and they do: the key is missing from all eleven equally, so parity is perfect and the badge is still wrong. TemplateDetail.test.tsx asserts variantStateOf returns not-live, which it does; no test renders that badge, and reaching the state needs a variant with versions and nothing published, which no fixture had. This is G32's shape one layer out - a resolvable-looking key that resolves to nothing.
prevention: A literal key per state in a Record keyed on the state union, so a state added without a key is a compile error and every key-scanning check in the repo can read the strings. The wider habit: an interpolated t() key is invisible to every check this repo has, and the only cure is to write the key out.

title: The preview strip's Default variant badge was drawn over every variant, including the ones it was denying
surface: SET-10's preview strip; PreviewPane in 07-frontend/src/features/notifications/TemplateDetail.tsx
found_in: 2026-09-07, matching the preview strip to the design, whose second screenshot shows the NON-default state
introduced_in: CR-007, 2026-08-17 - the strip asked variants.find(v => v.is_default), which is a question about the template rather than about the open variant
escape_reason: BR-NOT-001 makes a default variant mandatory, so the condition is true on every template this product can serve - the badge could never be absent and no fixture could show it absent. A check that cannot fail is invisible to a test suite: every case asserting the pill is present passed, and no case could assert it away because no lawful payload makes it go. It reads as correct in review because the expression mentions is_default.
prevention: The strip now asks about the SELECTED variant and draws Set as default when that one is not the default, which is the design's own second state and the thing that makes the two cases distinguishable at all. The habit is law 7's second question applied to UI: ask what would make this condition FALSE, and if no lawful payload does, it is not a condition.

title: Two tables holding what each utility pays Bynry have no row-level security, and the migration that skipped it cited a precedent that says the opposite
surface: backend
introduced_in: 2026-09-02 tenancy/0021 (CR-039 wave F)
escape_reason: The isolation gate G5 was reporting SKIP for two days (DEF-GOV-4441) because it looked for pytest in the wrong interpreter, so the case that names unprotected tables never ran. Before that it ran on sqlite, where row-level security does not exist (DEF-GOV-4024). The tables were added 2026-09-02; the first run that could see them was 2026-09-07.
prevention: G5 now resolves an interpreter that has pytest, and prove_isolation.py runs against real PostgreSQL under a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role. The deeper prevention is to read the signed schema contract rather than a sibling migration's summary of it: B2 section 3 lists subscriptions FIRST among the tables that must carry a policy, and tenancy/0021 cited subscriptions as its precedent for carrying none.

title: The same language is named two different ways in the staff app and the customer portal
surface: Settings > Regional (staff) draws 'Espanol (Mexico)' from LOCALE_REGISTRY.nativeLabel; the portal's Preferences picker, its Help page and the new guest language dropdown all draw 'Espanol de Mexico' from languageName()
found_in: a test assertion in the DEF-CWP-4440 lane, 2026-09-07 - the guest dropdown test asserted the registry's spelling and got the Intl one
introduced_in: languageName() was added for US-CWP-071's language table and derives names from Intl.DisplayNames; LOCALE_REGISTRY.nativeLabel predates it and holds the PO's own S48 picker mock-up spellings
escape_reason: Both functions are correct in isolation and each is used consistently within its own half of the product, so no test compares them and no gate could. B14 rule 34 is the rule this offends - one pair of words for one thing, everywhere - and it names two specific words rather than the general shape, so nothing generalises it to language names. It is only visible to a person who sets the language on Settings and then opens the portal, which is exactly the walkthrough this lane happened to do.
prevention: Pick one and make the other read it. LOCALE_REGISTRY.nativeLabel is the ratified spelling (from the PO's own picker mock-up) and needs no Intl at runtime; languageName could return it and fall back to Intl for a code the registry does not carry. A test that asserts the two agree for all eleven codes is what keeps them together afterwards.

title: Every value on the bill-ready email is an em-dash: bills are queued for delivery with no render context, so the customer name, service address, bill number, both dates, the period and all four summary figures print as named absences
surface: 06-backend/apps/billing/delivery_seam.py::queue_bill_delivery — it passed no render_context; Settings > Notifications > Messages needing attention, and every queued bill
found_in: the Product Owner on the live product, 2026-09-07, after DEF-PAY-4409 fixed the receipt: '(a) Fix all of them now'
introduced_in: present since bills were first queued for delivery (US-BIL-023, 2026-08-11) — the parameter was never passed
escape_reason: The renderer behaves exactly as designed and the template is right: rendering.py says a queue row does NOT hold the balance or the date, the caller must supply them at queue time, and a missing token becomes a NAMED ABSENCE. So nothing raises, nothing fails, and the email is well formed. Worse, the column's own docstring FORBADE supplying them - written 2026-08-17 off BR-NOT-012's 'non-invoice notices' phrase, which is a rule about tenant CUSTOM FIELDS - so a lane reading the model would conclude the em-dashes were correct. BR-NOT-027 (PO, CONFIRMED 2026-08-30) superseded that and says its reach includes the bill. Nothing reconciled the two.
prevention: Build the context from invoices.bill_payload - the instance locked at issue that the printed bill renders from - so the covering email and the enclosure cannot state different numbers and the bill run makes no extra query. A test asserts the stored column off a real issued bill, not only that a helper can build one: the first version of that test was green with the keyword deleted.

title: Four more callers queue a document without naming its values: the disconnect and dunning generators build a context, render with it, then drop it; a staff resend copies the pin and the recipient but not the figures; and both send-test buttons queue the real wording with nothing in it
surface: 06-backend/apps/notifications/notices.py (generate_disconnect_notice, generate_reminder) · api.py (POST /outbound/{id}/resend) · rule_service.py (queue_test, the SET-12 test send, and the SET-10 designer's send test)
found_in: the letters lane, 2026-09-07, enumerating every caller of queue_document by AST after the PO ruled '(a) Fix all of them now'
introduced_in: each as it was written: the notice generators 2026-08-15, the resend 2026-08-16, the two send tests 2026-08-17 and CR-048 B7
escape_reason: Every one is green and truthful. The notice generators are the sharpest case: the context is BUILT four lines above the queue write and handed to _render, so the artifact returned to the caller carries the balance and the cut date while the queue row a customer's letter is actually rendered from carries nothing - the same notice reads 'pay 443.70 USD by 09/17/2026' in one place and 'pay -- by --' in the other, and no test compares the two. frozen_documents.py even NAMES this in its own docstring ('generate_disconnect_notice and generate_reminder both call queue_document without one') and nobody read it as a defect.
prevention: Pass the context that is already in hand. For the resend, carry the stored column forward DECODED, since queue_document encodes on the way in. For a send test there is no document, so it takes template_preview.sample_context - the same visibly-sample values the preview pane already renders from, so a test message and a preview of one class cannot disagree.

title: The collections ladder's letters name no values, so a disconnection notice reads 'Your account is past due in the amount of --. Please pay by -- to avoid service interruption'
surface: 06-backend/apps/payments/notices.py::send_reminders and send_disconnect_notices — the two bulk senders the S35 modals and ladder.run_ladder both call
found_in: the letters lane, 2026-09-07, on the seeded Brazos Bend utility, sending a real 10-day notice to a real debtor
introduced_in: present since the bulk senders were written (US-PAY-015, 2026-08-11)
escape_reason: Same shape as DEF-PAY-4409 and invisible for the same reason: the renderer prints the named absence OQ-117 ratified, so the letter is well formed and every test passes. The tests assert the COUNT of queue rows and the toast ('Sent 4 checkmark') because that is what US-PAY-015's cases are about; not one of them reads what the letter says. This is the legal step before switching somebody's water off.
prevention: One batched read for the whole selection through billing_seam.outstanding_positions - the same figure collections_read.ladder_board sums to draw the number a clerk reads before pressing Send - plus customers' own published account and premise-cell reads, so the letter and the screen that authorised it cannot state different amounts. A test asserts the stored column off the row the real bulk sender wrote: the first version called the helper directly and was green with the context deleted.

title: Every disconnect notice the collections ladder has ever queued is pinned to a template class that does not exist, so it can never be rendered and will never be sent — while the ladder records that the customer was warned and advances them a tier
surface: 06-backend/apps/payments/notices.py::send_disconnect_notices — template_code=f"{template_code}_{tier}" composes disconnect_notice_first_10_day; the three seeded classes are disconnect_notice_10_day, _5_day and _48_hour
found_in: the letters lane, 2026-09-07, sending a real 10-day notice on the seeded utility and reading template_pin_unresolved in the queue write's problems
introduced_in: 2026-08-11, when send_disconnect_notices was written; the tier constants (first_10_day, second_5_day, final_48_hour) and the template codes have never matched
escape_reason: The queue write REPORTS an unresolved pin and returns SUCCESS - a row exists, the count is right, the toast says Sent, notice_history is written and the tier advances - so every US-PAY-015 case passes. Nothing downstream looks: render_for_dispatch would refuse, but no provider is connected so no dispatch has ever run. apps/notifications/notices.py wrote the exact warning down on 2026-08-17 beside TIER_TO_CLASS ('an explicit map, not a f-string on the tier name: a name-derived class would silently invent disconnect_notice_<anything>') and its sibling went on doing it. CR-048 wave B task B10 found the same disease in this same file for plan notices and fixed only that branch.
prevention: An explicit map, and a test that sends through the real function and asserts the QUEUED ROW carries a resolved pin - not that the map is internally tidy. The first version of that test asserted the map against the catalogue and was GREEN with the f-string restored.

title: A bill's queue rows are pinned to a BILLING template on every channel, which the notifications renderer cannot load — so the bill-ready email and the bill-ready SMS can never be produced at all, whatever figures they carry
surface: 06-backend/apps/notifications/services.py::queue_document — ONE pin serves every channel of a document, and _pinned keeps billing's pin; rule_catalog.EVENTS['bill_ready'].template_classes names email_bill_ready and sms_bill_ready and nothing reads it at queue time
found_in: the letters lane, 2026-09-07, queueing a bill for a paperless account on the seeded utility: both rows carry a bill_template_versions id, and render_for_dispatch refuses both
introduced_in: present since bills were first queued (2026-08-11); invisible while no account had elected email, which customers/0034 made possible on 2026-08-31
escape_reason: outbound_messages.template_id is POLYMORPHIC and delivery_seam.py says so in its own words (94 of 181 rows on a development database carried a BILL template's id). For pdf_print that is correct - billing's own page writer makes that document. Nobody asked the mirror question about the EMAIL row. No provider is connected, so no dispatch cycle has ever tried to render one, and the queue write reports render_context_not_checked rather than a failure.
prevention: The event already names the wording per channel. Pinning per channel is a change to the ONE write path inside a bill run with idempotency consequences, so it is filed rather than taken here. Until then the figures are stamped and correct and only the wording is missing - the Messages needing attention panel shows all eleven values above 'No wording is published yet'.

title: The friendly reminder is pinned to collections_reminder_<tone>, a template class nothing in this platform seeds or catalogues, so it can never render either
surface: 06-backend/apps/payments/notices.py::send_reminders — template_code defaults to 'collections_reminder' and the tone is appended; the seeded reminder wordings are 'dunning', 'email_past_due' and 'sms_past_due'
found_in: the letters lane, 2026-09-07, while fixing DEF-PAY-4451 (the disconnect tier's codes) — the same fault on the branch beside it
introduced_in: 2026-08-11, with send_reminders itself
escape_reason: Identical to DEF-PAY-4451: an unresolved pin is a PROBLEM on a successful write, so the row exists, the history is recorded and every test passes. It was not fixed in the same change because WHICH class a reminder should pin is a real question and the tier map was not: notifications.notices uses 'dunning' for the friendly step (BR-NOT-008), SET-12's past_due event names 'email_past_due' and 'sms_past_due', and the three TONES BR-PAY-035 ratifies are variants a tenant adds rather than classes this platform seeds. Guessing would put a customer's letter on wording nobody chose.
prevention: Answer which class the friendly reminder pins - it is BR-NOT-008's question and the answer is probably 'dunning' - then apply the same explicit map DEF-PAY-4451 introduced, with the same test that sends through the real function and asserts a resolved pin on the queued row.

title: The corrected-bill email asks 'What changed: {correction_reason}' and this product holds no customer-facing sentence for a correction reason anywhere, only internal codes like wrong_read
surface: 06-backend/apps/notifications/seed_templates.py::EMAIL_CORRECTED_BILL_BODY · billing/correction_reasons.py (SEEDED_REASON_CLASSES, MECHANISM_IN_WORDS)
found_in: the letters lane, 2026-09-07, building the bill-ready context: it is the one token of the corrected-bill wording that could not be filled
introduced_in: 2026-08-17, when the corrected-bill body was authored with a token no source could fill
escape_reason: The token renders as a named absence, which is correct behaviour, so nothing fails. correction_reasons.MECHANISM_IN_WORDS exists and looks like the answer but is not: it describes the MECHANISM to a clerk ('issues a corrected bill: the original is credited in full...'), not the fault to a customer. B14 rule 32 forbids an internal code in clerk-facing copy and a customer letter is further out than that; BR-NOT-015 makes the wording notifications' to own.
prevention: One customer-facing sentence per seeded reason code, authored where the wording lives, and a check that every token a seeded body declares has SOME source that can fill it - which is the general form of DEF-PAY-4409's whole family and would have found this one before the body shipped.

title: On the template screen's merge-field rail, a long field name and its sample value print on top of each other
surface: frontend
introduced_in: 2f7d93f9 (SET-10 rebuilt to the design)
escape_reason: No check in this repo reads rendered output, and an overlap is invisible to every one of them: the label and the value are both in the DOM, both readable by testing-library, and tsc, the DOM cases and every gate pass. It was found by opening the screen in a browser at 1440 and looking at it, which is hard-won law 6.
prevention: The rail's row is a two-column grid whose first column sizes to content; five of the nineteen field names are wide enough to run under the value. Give the name column a fixed share or let the pair stack when the name is long, and add a measured assertion to the template walkthrough that reads both bounding boxes and fails when they intersect.

title: The rendered document starts below the fold: three rows of controls sit between the variant tabs and the paper, so nothing of the bill is visible when a template opens
surface: SET-10, the template designer (Settings - Configure - Templates - one template); TemplateDetailPanel in 07-frontend/src/features/notifications/TemplateDetail.tsx
introduced_in: 2f7d93f9 (SET-10 rebuilt to the design, 2026-09-07)
escape_reason: No check in this repo reads rendered output, so no check can ask where an element STARTS. Measured in Chromium at 1440x900 the paper's top edge is 902px and the scroll viewport ends at 900: the document a person opened the screen to read is two pixels past the bottom of the window, and every DOM assertion passes because every element is present. The three blocks between the tabs and the paper - the refusal line, the Surfaces switcher and its heading, and the preview strip - are each individually correct and were each added by a different change.
prevention: The walkthrough now measures the paper's top edge against the scroll viewport and fails when the document opens below the fold. The general form: a screen whose whole purpose is one artefact must assert WHERE that artefact starts, not merely that it rendered.

title: In Edit-wording mode the wording editor takes 60 percent of the frame and the document takes 40; the Product Owner's 60 belongs to the document
surface: SET-10 Edit-wording mode; DESIGNER_FRAME in 07-frontend/src/features/notifications/notificationsKit.ts
introduced_in: CR-048 wave E (the designer frame was written wording-first)
escape_reason: The split is real and the assertion that guards it passed: templateDesigner.dom.test asserts lg:grid-cols-[3fr_2fr] and the walkthrough measured the rail at 55-65 percent of the frame. Both are true of a screen that gives the WRONG pane the larger share - the check pinned the ratio and never asked which pane was which. Measured at 1440: wording 662px, document 442px.
prevention: The walkthrough now names the two panes in its assertion - the DOCUMENT must be the larger one - rather than measuring an unnamed ratio. A ratio check that does not say which side is which passes on its own mirror image.

title: A System Admin chooses the page every customer receives sight unseen: the five bill layouts are five paragraphs of prose and a button, with no picture of any kind
surface: Settings - Configure - Templates - Standard bill; 07-frontend/src/features/billing/BillLayoutTab.tsx
introduced_in: US-BIL-021, 2026-08-16 (the chooser that replaced the cut designer S91-S96)
escape_reason: The screen was built to a story that asks for a LIST and a CHOICE, and it delivers both: five named layouts, one marked in use, each disabled with its reason when it cannot render. Every test asserts the five are present and choosable. Nothing asked whether a person can tell them apart, because no check in this repo looks at rendered output and the product had no route that renders a layout other than the one a bill is pinned to.
prevention: GET /bill-templates/layouts/{key}/preview.pdf renders a real sample bill through the same documents.py serialiser the customer's page comes from, so a preview cannot drift from the print. The habit: a chooser whose options differ VISUALLY has to show the difference, and if the product cannot render an unchosen option, that is the missing endpoint rather than a reason to describe it in prose.

title: On the bill-layout screen the entire left half of the panel is empty: Back to templates sits alone in a wide column and all five layout cards are crammed into the right half
surface: Settings - Configure - Templates - Standard bill; the PanelGrid wrapper in 07-frontend/src/features/notifications/TemplateCatalog.tsx
introduced_in: CR-048 E9 (a bill row opens the layout chooser from the one list)
escape_reason: PanelGrid lays each CHILD into a grid cell, and the wrapper hands it two children: a back button and the whole chooser. The button therefore claims a full column. Every DOM assertion passes - both children render, the back button works, the five cards are all present - and no check in this repo reads rendered output, so nothing could see that half the panel was white space.
prevention: The back control belongs in the page furniture, not in a layout grid cell. The general form worth a sweep: a grid whose children are heterogeneous - one control and one whole screen - is not a grid, and any PanelGrid with a bare Button as a direct child has this shape.

title: The template header draws its three actions in the opposite order from the design, with the emphasis at the wrong end: Edit wording is last and red where the design puts it first
surface: SET-10's PageHeader action row; 07-frontend/src/features/notifications/TemplateDetail.tsx
introduced_in: 2f7d93f9 (SET-10 rebuilt to the design, 2026-09-07)
escape_reason: PageHeader takes primaryAction and secondaryActions as two named slots and draws secondaries first, so the order is a property of the shared kit rather than of this screen - a screen filling both slots correctly still gets the kit's order. Nothing compares a rendered action row with the design it was built from, and the Product Owner found it by putting the two screens side by side.
prevention: PageHeader gains a leadingAction slot for the case the design actually draws, so the screen states the order rather than inheriting it. Any screen whose primary action belongs at the left has this same defect today.

title: A variant tab prints the whole template name where the design prints the variant's own short name, so four tabs read as four copies of one sentence
surface: SET-10's variant tab strip; TemplateDetailPanel in 07-frontend/src/features/notifications/TemplateDetail.tsx
introduced_in: 2f7d93f9 (SET-10 rebuilt to the design, 2026-09-07)
escape_reason: The tab label is variant.name, which is what the server serves and what every test asserts. The defect is in the DATA the seeder writes - the default variant is named after its template - and a tab strip whose four labels are near-identical is invisible to a DOM assertion that only checks each label is present. It shows only when the four are drawn side by side and read as one wrapped sentence.
prevention: The tab strip shortens a variant label that merely repeats its template's name, in the screen rather than in the data, so no seeded row has to be rewritten and a tenant's own variant names are untouched.

title: The SET-10 walkthrough has been timing out since the screen was rebuilt: it waits for designer-frame, which is now drawn only in Edit-wording mode
surface: 10-scripts/cr076_template_designer_walkthrough.mjs
introduced_in: 2f7d93f9 (SET-10 rebuilt to the design, 2026-09-07)
escape_reason: The walkthrough is the ONLY thing in this repo that reads rendered output for this screen, and it is not in any suite - it is run by hand - so a rebuild that moved its anchor selector broke it silently. Nothing failed; the script simply waits twenty seconds and exits 1 on a timeout that reads like an environment problem. Hard-won law 7's second shape: a check nobody runs is not a check, and one whose failure looks like a broken stack is worse than one that is red.
prevention: The walkthrough now opens the READING view, which is what a template opens on, and enters Edit-wording deliberately for the split measurement. A walkthrough anchored on a selector should assert what that selector MEANS - here, that a template opens on its document - so a moved anchor reads as a finding rather than as a timeout.

title: A lane ran 'pkill -f "pytest -m isolation"' to clean up its own starved runs and killed about a dozen sibling lanes' isolation runs with it
surface: the shared container — no file, commit or register row was touched; roughly 12 of 14 running isolation suites died, most of them other lanes'
found_in: self-reported by the DEF-PAY-4409 lane, 2026-09-07, immediately after running the command: the process count went from 14 to 2 and only two of the fourteen were mine
introduced_in: the moment the command was typed; nothing precedes it
escape_reason: CLAUDE.md law 11 bans git stash, git checkout --, git restore, git reset --hard and git clean, and states the general rule underneath them: any command that makes the shared working tree momentarily not-what-it-was is forbidden, whatever you wanted it for. That rule is written entirely in the vocabulary of GIT, so it does not come to mind for a command about PROCESSES - and the dangerous use here was the same one DEF-172 describes, a throwaway cleanup where the destruction is incidental to the intent. Nothing can catch it: no gate reads a process table, and the cost lands on siblings whose runs vanish with no cause they can find in their own work. The lane was trying to be considerate - freeing a saturated machine for the very lanes it then interrupted.
prevention: The ban in law 11 is about the SHARED ENVIRONMENT and not only about git. Kill by PID from your own job records, never by a pattern that matches a command any lane could be running. If a shared resource is saturated, wait or narrow your own work - do not clear the queue. And when you do it anyway: say so at once and name what died, because an unexplained disappearance sends somebody hunting in their own work for a cause that is not there (DEF-172's own lesson).

title: On an email template the first line of the wording prints twice, with a sentence explaining our own database schema between the two copies
surface: frontend
introduced_in: the CR-076 email preview block in TemplateDetail.tsx
escape_reason: Nothing in this repo reads rendered output, and both elements are correct in isolation: the derived preview line renders, the body renders, and every DOM assertion about each one passes. The duplication only exists on screen, where the same sentence appears twice about 80 pixels apart. The Product Owner found it by looking at the Welcome template and circling it.
prevention: The email preview draws firstLine(preview.body) as a stand-in preheader and then draws the whole body underneath, so the repeat is guaranteed by construction for every email template rather than being data-dependent. Either drop the derived line, or draw the body without its first line beneath it. The caption 'first line of the body - this product has no preheader field' explains our schema to a clerk and breaches B14 rule 32; a walkthrough assertion that no visible text appears twice inside the preview would catch the class.

title: An email template previews as a plain text blob while a printed one previews as a rendered page, so a clerk cannot see what the customer will actually receive
surface: frontend
introduced_in: the CR-076 preview block in TemplateDetail.tsx
escape_reason: The two branches were built and tested separately and each passes: printable and contract go through DocumentPaper, which gives the wording real typography, and email goes through a single paragraph element carrying the raw body string. No test compares the two, and no gate reads rendered output, so the difference is only visible with both open in a browser.
prevention: Give the email preview the same document treatment the printed one gets - an inbox frame with the subject, sender and body laid out the way a mail client shows them - so the answer to 'what does the customer receive' does not depend on which kind of template a clerk happens to open. A walkthrough assertion that the preview element uses more than one text style would catch a text blob.

title: prove_isolation.py wrote a receipt for a run that never finished, over a valid one, and recorded it as 0 passed and 0 failed
surface: tooling
found_in: the DEF-TEN-4446 lane, re-taking the proof after adding two migrations. The run was killed part-way by the sibling pkill of DEF-GOV-4463; that is the trigger, and this row is about what happened next
introduced_in: g05_isolation.prove(), as written
escape_reason: prove() reads the LAST LINE of pytest stdout and parses counts out of it. A pytest process that dies part-way through leaves progress dots as its last line, so _counts matches nothing and returns an empty mapping, and the receipt is written with passed 0, failed 0, errors 0, skipped 0 and a summary of twenty-seven dots. The status is FAIL, which reads exactly like an ordinary red run, and the receipt REPLACES the previous valid one on disk — so a proof that did not happen overwrote a proof that did, which is the outcome the module docstring says it exists to prevent: a refusal is never recorded. Nothing distinguishes the two except reading the summary field by eye, and the only reason this one was caught is that the lane that wrote it happened to open the file
prevention: prove() should refuse to write a receipt when the tail does not parse as a pytest summary line, exactly as it already refuses when no database is reachable: a run whose outcome cannot be read is a refusal, not a result. A sufficient check is that the tail carries one of passed, failed or no tests ran, and that passed plus failed plus errors plus skipped is greater than zero — a receipt of all zeros can only mean the parse failed, because a suite that collected nothing already returns early on returncode 5

title: The guest portal header is two rows in English because the nav was already full before the language control was added
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/shell/GuestFrame.tsx header row; every guest portal screen
found_in: looking at the DEF-CWP-4440 walkthrough screenshot, 2026-09-07 - no test or gate reads rendered output
introduced_in: the nav has grown a word at a time since CR-068 wave A; the language control ruled on 2026-09-07 was the one that took it over the line
escape_reason: No gate in this repository reads rendered output, and no test measures geometry. The nav was at 853 of about 860 available pixels in Spanish BEFORE this control existed, with two words already wrapping to two lines to fit a fixed 56px row - so it was going to break on whatever was added next. A fixed height clips rather than grows, which is invisible to every content assertion: the words are in the DOM, they are simply cut in half on screen.
prevention: The header now grows instead of clipping, so nothing is hidden in any of the eleven languages - but it is two rows at 1440px in English where it used to be one. Fixing that properly is a copy decision: shorten a nav word (Ask us for something is the longest), or move an errand out of the nav now that all six are drawn as cards on the front page. Measured alternatives that did NOT work: wrapping the outer row puts the utility name on its own line, and capping the control at 8rem measured 852x79 against 865x67 and truncates the one label the person choosing a language has to read.

title: MyAccounts.dom.test.tsx fails intermittently in a full-suite run and passes alone
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/accounts/MyAccounts.dom.test.tsx - the case named DEF-CWP-3954, the door to CWP-020
found_in: one full portal-suite run during the DEF-CWP-4440 lane, 2026-09-07: 1 failed, 702 passed, with 'expected undefined to be /pine-hill/portal/accounts/add'
introduced_in: not established - the assertion itself has been in place since 2026-09-05 and the file's last real change was DEF-CWP-4390 on 2026-09-07
escape_reason: It passes. Running the file alone gave 10 of 10 and the very next full-suite run gave 703 of 703, so nothing is red for anyone to read - which is exactly what makes an intermittent failure expensive: the lane that sees it spends its time proving the failure is not its own. Dated with git log -S against the file and the screen register: the last commits touching either are other lanes' and predate this lane.
prevention: An anchor's href read as undefined, which is a not-yet-rendered element rather than a wrong address - so the case is probably reading before the query it depends on has settled, and only loses that race under the scheduling of a 65-file run. A findBy/waitFor around that read would make it deterministic. Recorded rather than fixed because this lane could not reproduce it in two subsequent runs and a fix nobody can prove red is not a fix.

title: Every SPA server on the box was killed at once — the second broad-pattern kill in one day, and the rule that forbids it is written entirely in git examples
surface: tooling
introduced_in: not a code change — a shared-machine operating hazard
escape_reason: Nothing warns a lane that its own server was killed by a sibling. The failure a lane sees is a browser step that will not connect, which is indistinguishable from a bad build, a wrong port, or its own change — so the cost is a lane hunting in its own diff for something it did not do. Observed rather than inferred: every node server.mjs on the machine stopped inside one window, including two of mine and at least one other lane's on port 4340, while every Django runserver survived untouched. Author unknown and deliberately not guessed at.
prevention: This is DEF-GOV-4463's shape one class up: that lane ran pkill -f on a pytest pattern to free the machine and killed twelve siblings' runs with its own two, and self-reported it. CLAUDE.md law 11 already states the general form - any command that makes the shared environment momentarily not-what-it-was is forbidden, whatever you wanted it for - but every example written under that law is a git command (git stash, git checkout --, git restore, git reset --hard, git clean), so it does not come to mind for a command about processes. Two occurrences in one day says the examples are carrying the rule rather than the sentence. Kill by PID, never by pattern; and check a server is alive with no EADDRINUSE immediately before believing a page load, not once at boot.

title: DEF-GOV-4470 attributed: it was the DEF-CWP-4440 lane, and this is the exact command
surface: the shared machine - node server.mjs on 8722, 8733 and 4340; the same event DEF-GOV-4470 records as unattributed
found_in: self-reported by the DEF-CWP-4440 lane on being told every SPA server had died, 2026-09-07
introduced_in: that lane cleaning up its own walkthrough stack: for p in $(ps -eo pid,args | grep -E '[s]tubapi.mjs|[s]erver.mjs' | awk '{print $1}'); do kill -9 $p; done
category: Shared environment moved under other lanes
escape_reason: DEF-GOV-4470 says it could not be attributed, and this row is only the attribution so that half of the record is not missing. The mechanism worth keeping: stubapi.mjs was a filename that lane had invented, so that half of the pattern was genuinely private - and server.mjs sits right beside it in the same alternation and is the SPA host every lane runs. One safe term and one catastrophic term in one expression, and nothing distinguishes them by looking. The lane also used the [s]erver bracket trick so grep would not match itself, which reads as care and is care about a different hazard.
prevention: Kill by PID. Capture it at launch and kill exactly that. The test that would have caught this in one second: ask whether the pattern names a file THIS REPOSITORY SHIPS - server.mjs, manage.py, vite, pytest - because if it does, it names every lane's copy. That is a question about the string, answerable before pressing enter, which is what makes it usable where the general rule was not.

title: The is-this-file-stale test prescribed by hard-won law 12 can miss a version the repository genuinely had, because git log over a path does not list every commit whose tree held that version
surface: tooling
introduced_in: CLAUDE.md hard-won law 12's content-addressed clause
escape_reason: The test is used exactly once per incident, by hand, during a recovery — so a false miss looks like an ordinary inconclusive result and there is nothing to compare it against. It is also the SAFE direction of wrong (a miss means leave the file alone), which is why it has never been noticed: the cost is a revert left loaded in the tree, not a revert applied. On 2026-09-07 eleven locale catalogues were left in place on a miss and were in fact stale; the lane that owned them settled it with a one-line diff instead.
prevention: Measured on 07-frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json: git log --format=%H -- <path> lists 30 commits, and the commit 38e10670^ is not among them although its tree holds a definite blob for that path. git log over a pathspec performs history simplification and lists only commits it considers to have changed the path along the simplified history, so the walk does not visit every commit whose tree held a given version. Adding --full-history makes it visit them. The wider lesson is the one law 12 already states and which held here: a miss decides nothing, and the check that actually settled it was diffing the working copy against the tip and reading the result as arithmetic - one line missing, and that line traceable to a single commit with git log -S.

title: A text message previews in a 352px box, which is wider than the phone it is going to, so a clerk cannot see where the words really wrap
surface: frontend
introduced_in: the CR-048 wave E2 preview block, carried into the CR-076 rebuild
escape_reason: Nothing in this repo reads rendered output, and the class is correct in isolation: SMS_BUBBLE names max-w-[22rem], the utility compiles, and every DOM assertion about the bubble passes. 22rem is 352px, which is a desktop measure — a body that wraps to six lines on a handset wraps to three here, so the preview answers 'what will the customer get' with a shape the customer will never see. Measured in Chromium over all four SMS classes at 1440x1000: 352px on every one.
prevention: The walkthrough now measures the rendered width of preview-sms-bubble in a browser on every SMS row and fails above 200px. A class-name assertion cannot catch this — the class was always real; it was the number inside it that was wrong.

title: What a text message costs is only visible while the wording is being edited, so the person deciding whether to send it never sees that it is three messages
surface: frontend
introduced_in: the CR-048 wave E2 composer, where the meter was placed beside the textarea
escape_reason: The meter itself works and is tested: smsSegments.ts is correct, smsCost is unit-tested, and the counter renders. What nobody asked was WHO READS IT. It lives inside Composer, which only mounts when Edit wording is pressed, so the reading view — the default view, and the one a clerk uses to decide whether the wording is ready — shows a bubble with no count at all. Measured over all four SMS classes: a character count is present in the document region on none of them.
prevention: The count moves into the document region under the bubble, where the message is, and the walkthrough asserts a character count is present beside every SMS bubble WITHOUT opening the editor. It is moved rather than copied: two live counts that can disagree is worse than one in the wrong place.

title: The one template a clerk reads rather than a customer offers a Send test to me button, and there is nowhere for that test to go
surface: frontend
introduced_in: the CR-076 head action row, which draws the control for every class
escape_reason: The control is correct by the rule it was written to: BR-SHL-025 says a control renders disabled with its reason rather than being hidden, and the server does supply a reason. But that rule is about a control a person could otherwise expect to use. staff_bulk_summary is an in-app banner: there is no address, no inbox and no handset, so there is no test to send and nothing to disable. A disabled button with an explanation is still an offer, and it invites a clerk to work out why they cannot take it. Measured: the control is in the DOM on staff_bulk_summary.
prevention: The send-test control and its note are ABSENT from the DOM for the in-app shape, not disabled, and the walkthrough counts zero send-test controls on that row. The wrapper goes with the button: leaving the wrapper would leave an empty column and a stray note.

title: The one staff-facing template never says it is staff-facing, so the only signal that no customer will ever read it is a missing letterhead
surface: frontend
introduced_in: the CR-048 wave E2 in-app branch, which removed the letterhead and said so only in a code comment
escape_reason: The decision was made correctly and recorded in the right place for an engineer and the wrong place for a clerk: a docstring says 'every other template is a letter FROM the utility; this one is the product speaking to the operator', and a test asserts the letterhead's ABSENCE so a consistency pass cannot add one. Nothing says it on screen. An absence is invisible to every check this repo has, and a person reading a preview with no letterhead reads it as unfinished rather than as different — which is the same shape as DEF-CUS-3653, where a retired address kind would have returned null forever with every test green.
prevention: One sentence under the banner naming its reader, inside B14 rule 32's budget and carrying no rule id, plus the banner drawn over a sketch of the screen it appears on so the shape says it too. The walkthrough asserts the sentence is present on the in-app row.

title: The only check that can tell a real Tailwind utility from a dead one reads component files for className literals and kits for constants, so a component that keeps its classes in constants is checked by neither
surface: frontend
introduced_in: routeBUtilities.test.ts's OQ-280 kit check, which named the convention (*Kit.ts) rather than the shape (a module-level constant)
escape_reason: The gap is this check's own stated premise applied one file further out, and the check says so in its own comment: 'BOTH readers extract from className= and a component kit keeps its utilities in module-level constants'. The answer written that day scoped the fix to files named *Kit.ts. An ordinary component that declares const FOO = 'flex gap-2' and writes className={FOO} is ordinary React and is in neither reader. Measured 2026-09-07: bg-red-500 planted in such a constant in a file that IS on route-b-migrated.txt, and all ten tests passed over a class the theme deliberately deletes. This is law 7's fifth shape — a check reporting zero over a scope it silently excludes — and the exclusion had no number attached until now.
prevention: templateSurfaces.tsx moved its constants into templateSurfacesKit.ts, which the existing check already reads, and the planted class then went RED naming the file. That fixes ONE file. The general fix was attempted and is NOT shippable as written: reading every module-level constant in all 221 migrated files reports 23 orphans that are not classes at all — locale keys, enum values, a route — because a lowercase word meant for t() is utility-shaped. Scoping it to constants the same file hands to className cuts that to 5, still all false (a buttonClasses() call, a ?? fallback). The distinguishing signal is a value built only from string literals; a lane taking this should start there, and must run the false-positive count before trusting it, because a flood is what gets a grammar switched off (DEF-323).

title: The Add-entry dialog for areas gives no visible sign whether you are creating an area or a sub-area — the choice is a sentence and a dropdown
surface: frontend
introduced_in: DEF-221's fix, which added the capability without making the choice legible
escape_reason: DEF-221 was about a missing capability - the card said Areas and sub-areas and no screen could create the second half - and the fix added a parent dropdown, which closed that defect truthfully. Nothing then asked whether a person opening the dialog can TELL which of the two things they are about to create. The title, the fields and the buttons are identical for both, and the only signal is one line of helper text above a dropdown. No check in this repo reads rendered output, so it took the Product Owner opening the screen.
prevention: Make the choice explicit rather than inferred: a segmented control reading Area / Sub-area at the top of the dialog, with the parent dropdown appearing only when Sub-area is chosen, and the dialog title following the choice. The kit already has SegmentedField. Also worth checking while there: the Product Owner's screenshot shows the browser autofilling both the Code field and the parent dropdown, so the dialog opens pre-set to create a sub-area under Downtown, which contradicts the helper text directly above it - give the code input an autoComplete=off and confirm the select opens on its blank option.

title: Read validation and estimation: the two columns of inputs sit at different heights because each label carries a different amount of help text, and every field has a sentence under it
surface: frontend
introduced_in: the read-validation settings screen as built
escape_reason: Nothing in this repo reads rendered output, so a misaligned grid is invisible to every check we have: both fields render, both labels render, both help sentences render, and every DOM assertion about each one passes. The columns only disagree on screen. The Product Owner found it by opening the page.
prevention: The screen lays the thresholds out as a two-column grid where each cell is label + help + input, and the help text is a different number of lines on the left than on the right - so the left input is pushed below the right one and the pair no longer reads as a pair. Give the row a shared baseline for its inputs, or move the help beneath the input rather than above it. Separately the page is well over B14 rule 32's description budget: every single field carries an explanatory sentence, on top of a two-sentence page intro and a paragraph over the integrity checks. A walkthrough assertion that paired inputs in a row share a top edge would catch the alignment class.

title: Read validation and estimation renders its header and integrity checks and then nothing — every per-service threshold section is missing and the page ends in empty space
surface: frontend
introduced_in: unknown — the same screen showed all its service sections in an earlier screenshot the same hour
escape_reason: No check in this repo reads rendered output, and this failure leaves a page that looks deliberate: the title, the intro, the integrity-check panel and its seven chips all draw correctly, so a person who has not seen the full page cannot tell that six sections are missing. The Product Owner caught it only because they had the complete page on screen minutes earlier.
prevention: The Product Owner has two screenshots of the same URL taken minutes apart on build 2.217.0: one shows Electric with its thresholds, then Water with a Save button, then Sewer, Trash and Storm water each saying no meters on this service; the other shows the page ending after the integrity chips with a truncated panel border and the rest of the viewport blank. So the sections can render and on this load did not. First job is to establish whether it is a data-dependent path, a failed query with no error state drawn, or an error thrown after the integrity block that unmounts the rest - and whichever it is, a section that cannot be drawn must SAY so rather than leave a silence, because a page with nothing after its first panel reads as a finished page.

title: An email preview says it is from nobody, directly above a letterhead showing the utility's name
surface: frontend
introduced_in: the inbox header added with the five document shapes on 2026-09-07
escape_reason: Both halves are correct in isolation and that is why it took a browser to see. merge_field_rows reports utility_name with sample_value null and sample_unavailable 'From Settings → Company', because the five BR-TEN-017 identity tokens are STAMPED at render rather than sampled — so the screen honestly draws the em-dash it draws for every unsampled token, and the merge-fields rail has drawn the same mark for weeks. The renderer then stamps the value, so the letter underneath reads 'Brazos Bend Utilities'. Reading the row as 'we do not have this' is a misreading of a field that means 'this is not sampled', and nothing catches a mark that is right about our knowledge and wrong about the page. Seen in the printed output of the CR-076 walkthrough: 'From— To Pat Rivera Brazos Bend Utilities'.
prevention: The real fix is on the wire and is not this screen's to invent: template_preview.py should serve the values it STAMPED beside the samples, or the row should say the value exists and is not sampled. Until then the em-dash stays, because it is the idiom the rest of the screen already uses for these five tokens and composing a sender from the letterhead would be the screen inventing a fact — the thing BR-SHL-020 exists to prevent. Recorded rather than papered over.

title: The four documents a customer signs are the four that sit outside the scrolling pane, so a long agreement still pushes the page down
surface: frontend
introduced_in: the scrolling document pane of 2026-09-07, which wraps the rendered preview and not the platform-default offer
escape_reason: The pane was built around the RENDERED preview, which is the path 34 of the 38 catalogue rows take. The four contract classes take the other one: BR-NOT-002 makes a contract effective-dated, that date is a human's choice, so none of them has a published version and each draws the platform's OFFERED wording instead. Every check of the pane passed because every check looked at a template that has one. The PO's ruling — 'you give scroll option in PDF view area' — is about the document, and on these four classes the offer IS the document; the service agreement runs to about sixty lines. Found by sweeping all 38 rows rather than the six the walkthrough names.
prevention: The walkthrough's all-rows sweep now fails per row when a drawn document is not inside a scrolling pane, and it names the rows. Left RED deliberately rather than worked around: the pane's height is MEASURED by the reading view and shared with the rail, so wrapping the offer means reusing that machinery rather than adding a second scroll box, and that belongs to the lane that built it.

title: A contract says Type a body to see it render directly above the wording it has just rendered
surface: frontend
introduced_in: the preview pane's pending branch, which predates the platform-default offer being drawn in the main column
escape_reason: Both elements are right about their own question. The pending line answers 'is there a rendered preview' and the correct answer on all four contract classes is no — BR-NOT-002 makes a contract effective-dated, so none of them has a published version to render. The offer answers 'is there wording' and the correct answer is yes, and it is now drawn as a document rather than as a text blob, which is what made the contradiction visible. Nobody asked the third question, which is what the two say when read together on one screen. No DOM test can see it: each element is asserted separately and both assertions are true.
prevention: The pending line is not drawn when the payload carries a platform default, because on those four classes that offer IS the document and there is nothing for a clerk to type. Seen by screenshotting the four contract classes rather than by any assertion.

title: A push published a sibling's in-flight decision-log append and silently dropped this lane's, because the working-tree bytes changed between writing them and hashing them
surface: repo
introduced_in: the shared working tree, where push_paths.sh hashes a named path at push time rather than at the moment its author wrote it
escape_reason: Every guard in law 11 and in push_paths.sh passed. The base-versus-tip check asks whether a named path MOVED ON THE BRANCH between your base and the tip; it cannot ask whether the file on disk is still the file you wrote, and in a shared tree another lane can rewrite it in the seconds between. So the commit carried the sibling's 45-line append instead of this lane's 107-line one: the file count was right, no line vanished from the register guard's point of view, git show displayed a clean append, and nothing was lost for the sibling. What caught it was reading git diff --numstat AS ARITHMETIC — it said 45 0 where a 107-line append was expected — which is exactly the check law 11 added after DEF-1706 and the only one that could see this.
prevention: Re-derive the blob from the pinned tip and push in ONE shell invocation, so no other lane can write between the two, and then confirm your own heading is in the pushed blob rather than trusting the numstat alone. Recovered at 4a7cc22f with a clean 107/0. NOTE FOR ANYONE FOLLOWING THE TRAIL: that commit's message cites this defect as DEF-GOV-4484, which is wrong — 4484 had been taken by a sibling on another branch by the time the row was filed, and the id is DEF-GOV-4485. The citation was written before the number was verified, which is the same order-of-operations mistake the allocator's --verify step exists to prevent.

title: The seeded-list inventory guard has been red since 2026-09-04 and three days of lanes ran past it
surface: backend
introduced_in: CR-070 wave C (a07db72f, 2026-09-04) and the bank-rec/owner-category landings, none of which added its row to tests/test_cr010_reference_list_inventory.py
escape_reason: The guard did exactly its job and nobody read the output. test_cr010_reference_list_inventory.py exists to make a change to seeded vocabulary impossible without the record changing too, and it names the drifted lists in its own failure message: eight lists registered in SEED_LIST_OWNERS with no row in the inventory table. It had failed on every run since 2026-09-04. This is CLAUDE.md hard-won law 7's second shape almost word for word - proved red at birth, then never read - and the mechanism is that the failure belongs to nobody: the lane that adds a seeded list is not the lane that runs this file, and a red among other reds reads as scenery. A ninth divergence was found while fixing it and is a different fault: bank_accounts is declared in LOOKUP_LISTS and not in SEED_LIST_OWNERS, so this file's two assertions read two different registries and had become mutually unsatisfiable - one table could not satisfy both.
prevention: The eight rows are added and the ninth is named in its own table (CARDED_BUT_NOT_SEEDED), so both assertions work at full strength again and now cover those lists too: a new SEEDED list still fails the first by name, a new CARDED list still fails the second. The durable half is not another check - it is that a lane adding a seeded list owes this table a row in the same commit, which the file's own header already says. Recorded here so a three-day-old red is visible to somebody who did not run the suite.

reported_by: the CR-079 lane, found in a browser walkthrough
title: Read validation lists two checks by their internal code — row_key and unit_mismatch appear untranslated among thirteen English rule names
surface: frontend
introduced_in: the read-validation settings screen, when the two rules were added to the engine's judgment list
escape_reason: The screen renders the judgment-rule list SERVED by the engine and falls back to the raw code when a catalogue entry is missing, which is the correct fail-open for an unknown rule and is indistinguishable from a missing translation. Nothing reads rendered output, and G15 only compares catalogues with each other - a key absent from ALL ELEVEN is parity-perfect. Two rules were added to validation.JUDGMENT_RULES without their display names, and every gate, tsc and test passed.
prevention: Add metering.reads.status.row_key and .unit_mismatch to all eleven catalogues. The general form is worth a check: a rule name served by the engine and rendered with defaultValue is a raw code the moment a rule is added without its wording, so a test should assert that every entry of validation.JUDGMENT_RULES and INTEGRITY_RULES resolves to a catalogue string.

title: payment_failed_letter is a catalogue row with nothing behind it and nothing saying so: no kind, no channel, no variant, no version, no offered wording and no served reason
surface: SET-10 opened on payment_failed_letter; 06-backend/apps/notifications/catalogs.py and template_preview.py
introduced_in: unknown - the row has served this way for as long as the catalogue has listed it
escape_reason: Every OTHER template answers this screen with something: a rendered preview (34 rows), the platform's offered wording (4 contracts), or a served sentence in body_unavailable or preview_unavailable saying why not. This one answers with nulls in every one of those fields at once, so the screen has nothing to draw AND nothing to say - and BR-SHL-020's whole point is that an absent fact is NAMED. It survived because no check had ever asked the same question of every row: the DOM suite tests one fixture at a time, and the walkthrough opened four named templates until it was extended to sweep all 38. A row that renders nothing renders no error either, so it is invisible to anything counting failures.
prevention: The walkthrough now sweeps every row the catalogue serves, read off the wire rather than from a typed list, and NAMES any row it could say nothing about rather than passing over it - a clean sweep of 37 must never read as a clean sweep of 38. The fix itself is a decision rather than a patch: either the catalogue stops listing a class with no channel, or the class serves the sentence that says what it is waiting for.

reported_by: the DEF-CWP-4442 lane, reading the write path while narrowing the offer
title: The portal's own preference endpoint stores ANY string as a customer's language, including one no catalogue can draw
surface: 06-backend/apps/customers/portal_self_service.update_delivery_preferences - the locale branch; it reaches accounts.preferred_language and from there the portal shell, CWP-024's picker and the customer's letters
found_in: reading the write path on 2026-09-07 while building DEF-CWP-4442, which narrowed what the picker OFFERS and deliberately left the WRITE alone
introduced_in: CR-068 wave G, when locale joined DELIVERY_FIELDS; the two boolean siblings are coerced with bool() and the locale is passed through _clean() only
escape_reason: The endpoint's only real client is the picker, which offers valid codes, so no test ever posts an invalid one - and there is nothing to compare against on the server anyway: the eleven CATALOGUES are a front-end fact (LOCALE_CODES) and the twelve SEED_LANGUAGES are the TENANT's vocabulary, not an account's. A stored value nothing can draw fails silently in both directions: BR-CWP-105's chain steps past it to the tenant, so the customer reads a language they did not choose, and CWP-024's select renders BLANK over it - which reads exactly like a customer who has never chosen one. tsc, every unit test and every gate are green over both.
prevention: Validate the locale at the write point against what the product can DRAW rather than against what it OFFERS - the distinction BR-CWP-106 turns on. Refusing anything outside PORTAL_LOCALES would be wrong and is the reason this was not fixed in passing: accounts lawfully hold de and hi, nobody's stored choice is reset (PO ruling 2026-09-07, decision log), and a customer pressing Save on their unchanged German would have it taken away. The safe check is the eleven catalogues plus the twelve seeded codes; the seam customers.seams.tenant_languages already fetches the second half. Prove it RED by posting locale=banana and watching a 200 and a written row.

title: The all-rows template sweep prints nothing for a quarter of an hour, so a working run and a hung one look identical
surface: repo
introduced_in: the CR-076 walkthrough's section 7, added 2026-09-07, which reports only on failure and only at the end
escape_reason: The sweep speaks only when it finds something, so a clean run is silent by design — and silence is also what a hung run looks like. Over 38 rows at networkidle that is twelve to fifteen minutes of output that cannot distinguish success in progress from a page that will never settle. It is the smaller cousin of the shape hard-won law 7 keeps naming: a check whose output does not distinguish one state from another to a READER, not merely to an exit code. It was noticed while waiting on the check rather than by any check.
prevention: One line per row as it is walked, naming the code and the shape drawn, so progress is visible and a stall names the row it stalled on. Filed rather than patched mid-run: changing the script while it was verifying a sibling's fix would mean the number reported came from a different script than the one described.

title: Fire, storm water and thermal have service points and no asset type exists for any of them, so all three bill nothing
surface: 06-backend/apps/assets/services.py SEED_ASSET_TYPES and apps/tenancy/fixtures/lookup_defaults.json
found_in: the connection-half sample-data lane, 2026-09-07, after enabling all eleven services and re-running the sample load
introduced_in: CR-063 for fire and CR-062 C9 for storm water and thermal, each of which added the service without adding the thing that stands on the unit
escape_reason: Each service was wired end to end EXCEPT for the physical item. Fire is in the service catalogue, in CAPACITY_ESTATE_SERVICES, has a ratified six-size ladder and ratified prices, and gets 51 service points the moment the tenant enables it -- and there is no fire-line asset type in the twelve-row catalogue, so nothing can ever stand on those points. A capacity service is priced by a COUNT of the unit assets, so a count of zero is a lawful billable answer of nothing, which means this surfaces as a correct-looking bill with no fire line rather than as an error. Nothing compares the set of capacity services against the set of asset types that could satisfy them. Fire is the service a real utility is being onboarded on.
prevention: The asset-type catalogue carries an item for every capacity service the product sells, the seed plants them, and a test asserts that each enabled capacity service on the seeded tenant has at least one asset standing on at least one of its service points.

title: Twenty meters and sub-meters stand on a service point with no size class, so those connections cannot resolve a base charge
surface: 06-backend/apps/assets/sample_data.py and apps/metering/sample_data.py — the awkward-case and sub-meter plants
found_in: the connection-half sample-data lane, 2026-09-07, counting assets by size class on the seeded tenant
introduced_in: CR-038 W6 for the sub-meters and the earlier awkward-case plants, none of which passed a size class
escape_reason: metering.selectors.connection_size_for answers None for a connection whose meter records no size, and None is a deliberate real answer meaning nobody recorded one, so nothing raises at seed time. The refusal only arrives later, at billing, as connection_size_unresolved_for_sized_schedule, and only once a schedule carries per-size overrides. Until those overrides are seeded the twenty connections look healthy and bill on the flat rate. Ten of the twenty are the sub-meters, so a sub-metered building is precisely the case that breaks first.
prevention: The seed passes a size class on every meter and sub-meter it plants, and a test asserts that no asset standing on a service point of a banded service has a null size class on the seeded tenant.

title: Ten seeded devices exist as rows attached to no service point, so they are unreachable from the unit they belong to
surface: 06-backend/apps/assets/sample_data.py — the device plants (backflow, comms, cart, ev_charger, net_meter, pv, battery)
found_in: the connection-half sample-data lane, 2026-09-07, joining assets to service points on the seeded tenant
introduced_in: CR-038 W6, which added the device rows without attaching them
escape_reason: This is hard-won law 2 in data rather than in code. The rows exist, the equipment screens list them, every test passes and the asset count is correct, but service_point_id is null on all ten, so no unit reaches them and no capacity count includes them. A cart not on a trash service point is not billed as a cart and a PV panel not on a solar point contributes nothing to installed capacity. The seed reported them as written and nothing asked whether they were CONNECTED. None carries a certification due date either, so the certification rules have nothing to find.
prevention: Every device the seed plants is attached to the service point of the service it belongs to and carries a certification due date where its type has a certification. A test asserts no seeded asset of a billable device type is left with a null service point.

title: Every seeded meter of every service gets the SMALLEST size band, so a per-size base curve is exercised at one point
surface: 06-backend/apps/assets/sample_data.py — seed_sample_records, the meters block
found_in: the connection-half sample-data lane, 2026-09-07, measuring assets by size on the seeded tenant
introduced_in: CR-039 wave A / CR-062 C4, when the per-service size lookup was added
escape_reason: The line is seed_size_class = sizes[0] if sizes else None and it is CORRECT code for one meter; nothing compares the DISTRIBUTION of seeded sizes against the ratified ladder. Every gate and every test passes because each individual meter has a lawful size. The seeded estate carries 50 electric meters all at E-1P-100 against a six-size vocabulary and 51 water meters all at W-58 against a nine-size one, so five of six electric base prices and eight of nine water base prices can never be reached by any bill the fixture produces. The block comment even records the reason it was safe when written -- no rate schedule in the seed carries a per-size override -- and that sentence went stale the day a per-size curve was seeded, with nothing watching it.
prevention: The seed spreads sizes across the ratified ladder by customer class rather than taking the first element, and a test asserts more than one distinct size class per banded service on the seeded tenant so the curve cannot silently collapse back to one point.
