reported_by: the DEF-CWP-4442 lane, self-reported after finding its own commit message replaced by a sibling's
title: Two lanes writing a commit message to the same shared scratchpad filename silently replace each other, and the loser pushes the winner's message
surface: the session scratchpad every lane is told to use - one directory shared by every concurrent lane, with no per-lane namespace; the file at risk is whatever a lane hands to push_paths.sh as its message
found_in: 2026-09-07 - this lane wrote its commit message to scratchpad/msg1.txt, and a sibling closing OQ-AUD-1724 wrote ITS message to the same name. Found only by running tail on the file before pushing and reading a paragraph about the audit archiver's nightly job in a commit about the portal's language dropdown.
introduced_in: the scratchpad has always been per-session rather than per-lane; the collision needs two concurrent lanes and an unremarkable filename, which is the normal case
escape_reason: CLAUDE.md law 11 is entirely about the shared GIT tree - the index, a blob, an allocated id - and every check it prescribes reads commits. None of them can see this: the message is not a tracked file, so git status is clean, the numstat is right, the hunks are all yours, and the commit is byte-perfect. It is simply DESCRIBED WRONG. push_paths.sh refuses an empty message file and cannot ask whose message it is. The damage is to the record, which is the half that stays invisible - the same reason law 11's third and fourth occurrences went unnoticed twice.
prevention: Write per-lane, not per-session: a subdirectory named for the lane inside the scratchpad, which is one mkdir and is what this lane switched to. The durable form is for the guidance that hands out the scratchpad path to hand out a lane-scoped one, so the safe thing is the default rather than something each lane has to remember. Cheap check in the meantime, and it is the only thing that found this: read the first line of your message file immediately before invoking the push, and confirm it is your subject.

title: G7 has been red since 2026-09-06 on two migrations that carry no HUMAN-OWNED marker and no review-ledger row
surface: backend
introduced_in: 9b47f923 (2026-09-06), which added tenancy/0039_cr070_k_work_document_kinds.py and tenancy/0040_cr070_k_attachment_source.py
escape_reason: Migration ordering is a CLAUDE.md sensitive path, so every numbered migration is on g07's guard list and must carry HUMAN-OWNED plus HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING in its docstring and a row in 09-human-review-ledger.md naming its path. These two carry none of the three, so g07 has returned FAIL naming them on every run since they landed. The gate is working exactly as designed and its output was not read - the same shape as DEF-TEN-4486 filed the same day, and CLAUDE.md hard-won law 7's second form: proved red at birth, then never read. This lane found it by running the gate through module.run() rather than through __main__, which is the entry point run_gates uses (DEF-GOV-3733), and dated it with git log --diff-filter=A on the two paths.

Adding the two markers is one line each, but the ledger row is the substance of the protocol - it must state in plain English what was put to the Product Owner and what the signature does not cover - and only the lane that authored those migrations knows what was shown. Writing that row from outside would be a signature over a review nobody performed, which is worse than the red. The owning lane should add both markers and both rows.

BR-RAT-690's own suite proves a utility CAN state a per-size base by round-tripping through create_charge, which passes whether or not the fixture ever does it — and with the table EMPTY a per-size read and a flat read return the same figure for every tenant, so no bill, no golden test and no gate could tell the difference. title: Two front-end tests fail intermittently on an unchanged tree, so a lane cannot tell its own red from theirs
surface: frontend
introduced_in: unknown - both predate 72001025 and neither has a dated red in any lane report
escape_reason: Nothing measures whether a test is deterministic. Both cases pass often enough that the lane which wrote them saw green, and both were proved red at birth exactly as hard-won law 7 requires - the gap is law 7's newer clause, that a red proof at birth says nothing about whether the check keeps meaning the same thing later. The cost is not the two cases: it is that a lane running the suite sees seven reds, has no way to sort its own from the tree's, and the cheapest wrong move (call them all pre-existing) is exactly what DEF-CWP-4187 says destroys the signal.
prevention: Measured, not asserted: src/components/WizardFrame.dom.test.tsx TC-FRAME-5 (single-flight) fails on 3 of 3 runs of a two-file invocation and PASSES inside a 98-file run; src/features/tenancy/RoutesCyclesCosmetics.dom.test.tsx 'rule 12: the picker has a search box' fails on 1 of 3 identical runs. Both measured on a tree with none of this lane's work in it (72001025), which is what proves they are not DEF-TEN-4478's. Both look timing-shaped - a single-flight assertion and a debounced search box (IS-3, 300ms). Fix is to await the state each asserts rather than a timeout, in the lane that owns each file. Until then the honest reading of a red in either is 'unknown', not 'pre-existing'.

title: The sample fixture says a gas utility reads therm in seven places and every seeded gas read is ccf, including one note that blocks a signed price on a condition already met
surface: backend
found_in: Measured 2026-09-07 on the dev database at branch tip 35666484, by provisioning a gas-only tenant (subdomain sample-gas) through apps.tenancy.services.provision_tenant with the sample plant run inline, then querying meter_reads under app.tenant_id. ALL 198 gas reads, across the four batches sample-opening-gas.csv / sample-june-gas.csv / sample-july-gas.csv / sample-august-gas.csv, carry unit=ccf; not one carries therm. The reference customer meter G-5000 reads exactly 40.000000 ccf a month and its issued invoice line reads 'gas usage, quantity 40.000000, unit ccf'. The prose still says therm at core/sample_fixture.py lines 186, 435, 478, 1575-1578 and 1619-1629; at apps/metering/sample_data.py line 3652, the seed_sample_reads docstring, which promises 'therm on a gas one'; and at apps/metering/register_units.py line 149, which states therm is the PRIMARY of gas in SERVICE_DEFAULT_UOMS when it has been the ALT since 2026-09-02.
introduced_in: 2026-09-02, when BR-TEN-1180 / DEF-3230 swapped SERVICE_DEFAULT_UOMS for gas from (therm, ccf) to (ccf, therm) so the seeded register would agree with the signed 1.15 per ccf. The swap reached the seed map and the tests and did not reach the paragraphs that explain the fixture. core/sample_fixture.py line 1575 still quotes the pre-swap tuple as though it were current.
escape_reason: Nothing in this repo compares a sentence about the fixture against what the fixture actually seeds. DEF-3230 fixed the seed map and DEF-3096 fixed a test helper that broke on the flip; both lanes were about executable code, and the prose that explains why each figure is what it is was in neither diff. The engine has a schedule-versus-meter unit invariant that refuses a therm read against a ccf tariff, so the product cannot silently misbill on this - which is exactly why the prose could rot with every gate green and no output ever looking wrong. This was found only by seeding a gas tenant and reading meter_reads.unit out of the database, which is the one thing no check does.
fixed_commit: e95ed973 (2.220.2, DEF-RAT-4516 lane) — ALL SEVEN stale sites amended to say ccf, each stamped with the 2026-09-02 ruling that moved the seed rather than silently corrected: core/sample_fixture.py the estate-shape sentence, the consumption-scale note, the thermal-scale aside, the gas bullet of the service-by-service note and the whole GAS_FLAT_PER_CCF note; apps/metering/sample_data.seed_sample_reads' docstring, which promised 'therm on a gas one'; and apps/metering/register_units.py line 149, which called therm gas's PRIMARY when it has been the ALTERNATE since 2026-09-02. The costly site named in this row is the one that mattered most: GAS_FLAT_PER_CCF's note stated its own release condition -- 'it becomes usable the day a gas tenant declares ccf as its primary UoM' -- five days after that day arrived, so a lane grepping the constant as the note instructs was sent to rule a conversion factor nobody needed. That is exactly what happened, and the price it protected was the live 0.00 gas usage line filed as DEF-RAT-4516 and fixed in the same commit. Two more stale sites were found beyond the seven and are also fixed: tests/test_service_billing_coverage.py's estate note and tests/test_cr062_j_addendum.py, which cited GAS_FLAT_PER_CCF as the precedent for a 'recorded and read by nothing' posture gas has now left. The prevention this row asked for is delivered as the seed itself rather than as a test: gas's price is now READ from the fixture on every provisioning, so a seeded gas read whose unit did not match would fail the schedule-versus-meter unit gate and stop the bill, which no amount of prose can drift past.
prevention: The costly site is core/sample_fixture.py 1619-1629, the GAS_FLAT_PER_CCF note. It says the signed 1.15 per ccf cannot be seeded because the seeded gas register reads therm, and that it 'becomes usable the day a gas tenant declares ccf as its primary UoM, or a therm to ccf factor is ruled'. That day was 2026-09-02 and the measurement above confirms it, so a lane reading this today is sent to rule a conversion factor that is not needed. The real remaining blocker is only that seeding gas usage belongs to CR-062 group B, which the BACKBONE_USAGE_UNPRICED note one screen below states correctly. Fix: amend the seven sites to say ccf, and add a test asserting that the unit on a seeded gas read equals SERVICE_DEFAULT_UOMS gas primary, so the seed and the prose that describes it cannot drift apart again.

title: A government account has no base charge for water or electric, so its bill refuses by name
surface: backend
introduced_in: BR-RAT-108 (2026-08-21) made applies_to_customer_classes an INCLUSION list and the seeded base codes name residential, municipal, commercial and industrial only; government was never added to any of them
escape_reason: No account of that class has ever reached a seeded bill run, so the refusal never fired. title: US-TEN-007 TC-1 still asserts the gas register reads therm, four days after the ruling that made it ccf

found_in: the connection-half sample-data lane, 2026-09-07, while checking a sibling's premise about the gas unit of measure

title: THE RETENTION SCREEN WILL PRINT THE ENGLISH WORD 'partial' IN EVERY LANGUAGE, BECAUSE THE ARCHIVER GAINED A THIRD RUN STATUS AND NO CATALOGUE GAINED A KEY FOR IT. G15 compares catalogues against each other and against the keys it can SEE, and a key built by string interpolation at render time is not one of them — so eleven catalogues can be complete, agree with each other, and still have no entry for a value the server started sending today. The defaultValue makes it worse rather than better: it guarantees something readable renders, so nothing ever looks broken. There is no test either, because the only run status any fixture produces is success. The general form: a server-side enum gaining a value is a FRONT-END change nobody is told about, and the seam between them is a template literal.

The transferable habit is the one that found this: when you add a value to an enum the API serves, grep the front end for the field name and look at how it is RENDERED, not just whether it is. A dynamic key is the shape to look for.

title: allocate.py --verify reports a lane's own ids as TAKEN once its first commit is pushed, because it reads commit messages as an id source and cannot tell the caller's commit from a sibling's
surface: 10-scripts/allocate.py --verify
found_in: the DEF-RAT-4516 gas-price lane, 2026-09-07, re-verifying its three ids in the same breath as the blob re-derivation exactly as CLAUDE.md law 11 prescribes. It had pushed its code commit e95ed973, whose message ends 'Also files DEF-TEN-4514 and DEF-RAT-4515'. The very next verify answered 'defect 4514: TAKEN - a sibling pushed it. Renumber before you commit' and the same for 4515. No sibling had: git log --grep over the branch shows the only commits naming either id are that lane's own two, and the register carries exactly one row per id.
introduced_in: the design of allocate.py, which reads ids from the working tree, working-tree code, every origin ref AND commit messages. The commit-message source is deliberate and valuable - it is what caught DEF-MET-4512 for this same lane an hour earlier, an id cited from core/sample_fixture.py by a sibling whose register row was not pushed - so this is a blind spot in a good check rather than a bad check.
escape_reason: The message is CONFIDENT and NAMES A CULPRIT - 'a sibling pushed it' - where the truthful statement is 'this number appears somewhere I can see, and I cannot tell whose it is'. Nothing distinguishes the two, and the tool has no notion of the caller's own commits. It is the shape CLAUDE.md law 11 records twice about git --stat and once about git log -S: a check whose OUTPUT cannot distinguish the case a reader must act on from the case they must ignore. The cost is bounded but real and it lands at the worst possible moment - at push time, on ids already cited across a lane's whole change - so the obedient response is to renumber every citation for nothing. This lane came within one command of doing exactly that, having already renumbered once that day for a REAL collision (DEF-WRK-4513), which is what made the false one credible.
prevention: NOT FIXED HERE - the lane that found it was pricing gas, and the fix is a judgment about which refs and messages the allocator should trust. Two candidate shapes, recorded so the next reader does not start from nothing: exclude commits whose author or Claude-Session trailer matches the caller's, or - simpler and probably better - keep the finding and change the WORDS, so a hit from a COMMIT MESSAGE reads 'seen in a commit message; if that commit is yours this is not a collision' while a hit from a pushed REGISTER ROW keeps the flat refusal. The second needs no notion of identity and removes the false certainty, which is the actual defect. Meanwhile: a TAKEN verdict on your own id after your own first push is checked with git log --grep=<id> --all before renumbering anything.

title: Every bill this product prints is unstyled: the page is Courier with space-aligned columns and the HTML carries no stylesheet at all

introduced_in: 2026-08-11, the commit that added the PDF serialisation to apps/billing/documents.py: Courier was chosen so a column position would be integer arithmetic on characters and no font-metric table would have to be transcribed. reported_by: service-base-research lane (claude), self-reported after reading its own git log
title: Two lanes' commit messages crossed in the SHARED scratchpad and one commit went out under the other lane's subject line - commit 7a7638d7 says 'The Integrations screens stop reading zero' and contains the municipal base-charge research
surface: tooling
introduced_in: No commit - it is the message-file convention. push_paths.sh takes a MESSAGE FILE and reads it at push time, and the scratchpad directory /tmp/claude-0/<repo-hash>/<id>/scratchpad is shared between lanes working this repo. Two lanes both used the obvious filename msg.txt. The sibling wrote theirs and pushed ab382ca6 with it; this lane's push minutes later read the sibling's leftover bytes. Verified: 7a7638d7 carries all 11 of this lane's files and 777 insertions - the CONTENT is correct and complete - under ab382ca6's subject line, and this lane's own subject appears on no commit at all, so nobody else's record was polluted.
escape_reason: Every check in CLAUDE.md law 11 reads the TREE and none reads the MESSAGE. push_paths.sh verifies the pinned tip, refuses a moved path, refuses a vanished register line and prints the numstat - all of which passed, correctly, because the commit's CONTENT was right. The subject line is the one field nothing validates, and it is the field a person greps six weeks later. A lane searching git log for 'base charge' finds nothing; the work is in the decision log and this register instead.
prevention: Name the message file after the lane or the change, never msg.txt - the scratchpad is shared exactly like the working tree and the same law-11 reasoning applies to it. Cheaper still: pass the message through a process-substituted file or a lane-unique temp name created with mktemp, so two lanes cannot collide on the path at all. And read back the SUBJECT after pushing: git log -1 --format=%s <sha> is one command and is the only thing that would have caught this.

title: Defect id 4523 was used by two lanes for different defects - commit 5b2c20fb's subject says DEF-BIL-4523 and the only 4523 row in the register is DEF-RAT-4523, so that commit message points a reader at the wrong defect
surface: tooling
introduced_in: Both lanes computed the next free id correctly and neither could see the other: file_defect.py reads the working tree, HEAD and every origin ref, which is the PUSHED world plus this checkout, and a sibling in its own worktree has its row in none of them until it pushes. DEF-1787's exact mechanism. Here it went one step further than DEF-1787 did: DEF-BIL-4523 was never filed as a ROW at all - it exists only in commit 5b2c20fb's subject line - so the register is internally consistent and only the commit message is wrong.
escape_reason: A duplicate id in a 2,250-row register reads as a register, not an error, and this one is not even duplicated IN the register - it is an id used in prose that resolves to somebody else's row. Nothing reads commit subjects for id validity, and the citation gate checks that an id is not REPEATED rather than that it was ever ISSUED (CLAUDE.md law 7's 'looking at the wrong thing'). Found only because this lane read its own git log for an unrelated reason.
prevention: Allocate the id through file_defect.py BEFORE naming it in a commit message, so the number in the subject is a number the register holds - an id that exists only in prose can never be reconciled. allocate.py <family> --verify N in the same breath as the push is the cheap half; the durable half is that a defect is a ROW first and a sentence second.

title: REDERIVED_FROM_TIP=1 IS A CLAIM ABOUT ONE PUSH, AND REUSING IT ON THE NEXT ONE TOLD push_paths.sh TO STAND DOWN OVER THE EXACT CASE IT EXISTS TO CATCH. The CR-080 lane pushed twice. The first push ran inside a retry loop that re-fetched the tip, rebased onto it and pushed — REDERIVED_FROM_TIP=1 was true every round and the push landed correctly. Ten minutes later the same lane pushed a SECOND commit (four register files) reusing the same flag, from working-tree copies that were still the ones the FIRST push had produced. A sibling had pushed the CR-078 late-fee work in between. push_paths.sh's staleness check REFUSES when a named path moved between base and tip; the flag disables that check by design, so it published a revert BY SUBTRACTION: 112 lines of the sibling's decision-log entry, 23 lines of their CHANGELOG entry and their human-review-ledger row, all gone. Every other law-11 check passed on it — the file count was right, the lane's own edits were present, and the deleted work was not in the diff at all because it was missing from the tree the diff was taken against.
surface: 10-scripts/push_paths.sh REDERIVED_FROM_TIP escape hatch; 12-governance/02-decision-log.md, 09-human-review-ledger.md, CHANGELOG.md (restored)
found_in: the CR-080 lane's own push output, 2026-09-07 — git diff --numstat printed '13 112 12-governance/02-decision-log.md' and the lane read it
introduced_in: 2026-09-07, the CR-080 lane's second push (850a6204), by reusing REDERIVED_FROM_TIP=1 from an earlier command
escape_reason: THE GUARD WAS TURNED OFF BY THE OPERATOR, CORRECTLY THE FIRST TIME AND FALSELY THE SECOND, AND NOTHING DISTINGUISHES THE TWO. push_paths.sh already refuses a moved path and already prints the subtraction numstat; both worked exactly as written. What has no check is the FLAG'S OWN SCOPE: REDERIVED_FROM_TIP asserts 'I rebuilt every named path from this tip's bytes just now', which is true of the command that did the rebuild and false of the next command five minutes later. The script cannot tell them apart — it sees one invocation and one assertion — and the operator reaches for the same shell history line because it worked. This is hard-won law 7's 'what would make this check pass wrongly': the answer is 'a human answering a question about a DIFFERENT push', and it is not a hypothetical.
prevention: TWO, and the cheap one is a script change. (a) MAKE THE FLAG CARRY ITS EVIDENCE: have REDERIVED_FROM_TIP take the tip SHA the caller claims to have re-derived from — REDERIVED_FROM_TIP=<sha> — and refuse when it is not the tip the script just pinned. A stale reuse then names its own staleness instead of silently disabling the check, and the correct call costs one extra token. (b) THE HABIT, until (a) exists: pass the flag only in the same command that performs the rebase, never from shell history. And read the numstat the script prints — it is the one thing that caught this, exactly as DEF-1706 says it would.

surface: S21 account detail, Usage tab, under every chart
found_in: the Product Owner, on the live product, by looking at the screen
introduced_in: CR-030 W3 task 3.8, the day the tab was written
escape_reason: NOTHING COMPARES A t() CALL'S ARGUMENT NAMES WITH ITS STRING'S PLACEHOLDERS. G15 proves the eleven catalogues agree with each other and they did - all eleven were equally wrong. G18 proves the key exists and it does. tsc cannot see it: t() takes an untyped params object. And every assertion on this screen renders t(key, args) on BOTH sides of a toContain, so a wrong argument name matches itself perfectly. Hard-won law 6 again: no gate in this repo reads rendered output.

It found a third instance the same minute (the chart's aria-label). The general check - every t() call's argument names cover its string's placeholders - is owed and is mechanically easy for literal keys.

title: THE UNREAD-MONTHS CAPTION PRINTED ITS PLACEHOLDER, AND ITS TEST PINNED THE BUG: the Usage tab read {{months}} month(s) have no reading. AccountUsageTab.tsx passed {absent, total}; all eleven catalogues interpolate {{months}}. ITS TEST ASSERTED THE SAME WRONG NAMES - AccountUsageTab.test.tsx rendered t(key, {absent:1,total:4}) and matched it against the markup, so both sides were equally broken and the case passed for weeks over a screen printing braces at a clerk.
surface: S21 account detail, Usage tab, under a chart with an unread month
found_in: the Product Owner, on the live product, by looking at the screen
introduced_in: CR-030 W3 task 3.8, the day the tab was written
escape_reason: A TEST THAT RENDERS t(key, args) ON BOTH SIDES OF A toContain CAN ONLY PROVE THE CODE AGREES WITH ITSELF. It is the standard shape in this repo's frontend suites and it is right for checking that copy REACHED the screen; it is blind to whether the copy RESOLVED. Nothing else could see it either: G15 compares catalogues to each other, G18 checks the key exists, tsc does not type t()'s params, and no gate reads rendered output.
prevention: The literal English sentence is now asserted alongside the t() call - expect(html).toContain('1 month(s) have no reading') - so the two sides of the comparison no longer share a failure mode. Plus the not.toContain('{{') sweep over three payload shapes.

What no rule covers is that a park entry for a CUSTOMER-FACING string is a live defect with a note on it, while a park entry for a dead key is housekeeping - the file cannot tell them apart, so the loudest thing in it reads the same as the quietest. .kpi .v also sets text-overflow:ellipsis, so the key arrived truncated to 'customers.a...' and did not even look like a key.

surface: S21 account detail, Usage tab, the chart's accessible name
found_in: the regression assertion written for the two VISIBLE placeholders, on its first run
introduced_in: CR-030 W3 task 3.8, the day the tab was written
escape_reason: HARD-WON LAW 6 SAYS TO DIFF THE RUNNING APP AGAINST THE PROTOTYPE, AND THAT METHOD IS BLIND TO EVERYTHING A SIGHTED READER DOES NOT SEE. Every visible instance of this fault on this screen was found by a human looking; this one survived because looking is exactly the wrong instrument. A screenshot cannot check an accessible name - only markup can.

title: THE ACCOUNT DETAIL SAID THE CUSTOMER PORTAL WAS OUT OF SCOPE, OVER AN ACCOUNT THAT HAS A LOGIN: the right rail read 'The customer portal is out of scope for this version, and the paperless, SMS and portal flags are columns that were never built. No login date is shown because none exists.' All three clauses were false. CR-068 built the portal and CR-082 seeded it; accounts.paperless and accounts.sms_reminders landed 2026-08-31 and were already being served in this very payload; and the login date exists in portal_session - the screen was not reading it. PO verbatim: 'I have login portal for this account - portal access says...'
surface: S21 account detail, right rail, the Portal access panel
found_in: the Product Owner, on the live product, by looking at the screen
introduced_in: US-CUS-009, when the portal genuinely was out of scope - the sentence was TRUE the day it was typed
escape_reason: HARD-WON LAW 2'S MIRROR: A REFUSAL THAT OUTLIVED THE THING IT REFUSED. G13 asks whether a prop is passed; nothing asks whether a REFUSAL IS STILL TRUE, and the two acts - landing a feature and releasing the sentence that pointed at it - are separate, only the first of which feels like the work. Its TEST made it worse rather than catching it: the case required the string 'out of scope for this version', so the suite actively defended the false sentence. This is the fourth instance on this one screen today and the pattern is now well documented.
prevention: The sentence is DELETED rather than corrected, and the panel DERIVES every line - apps/customers/portal_seam.py walks account to customer_accounts to portal_credential to portal_session. The PO's own ruling of the same evening is the rule: derive the state, keep the specificity, and print what the derivation skipped beside what it checked. A derived panel cannot rot; a corrected sentence would have rotted the same way. And the test now reads the payload instead of pinning the copy.

title: THE USAGE TAB SHOWED 'AVERAGE WATER MONTH' BESIDE FOUR ELECTRIC FIGURES: with Electric chosen, the fifth summary figure still read Average water month - 15 kgal. It is payload.water_avg, a TOP-LEVEL served field outside every series, so it was never wired to the service picker and could not follow it however the filter was fixed. The first four figures read metrics off the filtered series and do follow. Neither monthly_usage_reads' docstring nor BR-MET-106 states a reason it must always show; the only reason on record is that r10 draws five tiles, and r10's fixture is an electric-and-water account. It now shows when its own service is on screen; the server field is unchanged.
surface: S21 account detail, Usage tab, the fifth summary figure
found_in: the Product Owner, on the live product, by looking at the screen

escape_reason: IT WAS NEVER WIRED TO THE PICKER IN THE FIRST PLACE, so no test of the picker could catch it - the four that follow the selection all passed, correctly. Nothing in this repo asks whether every figure in a row is about the same subject as the chart above it, and a fixture with both electric and water services makes the wrong answer look right: the water figure is genuinely relevant there. Copying a prototype's tile COUNT rather than its tile MEANING is the general form.

title: A lane killed other lanes' frontend servers with a pattern match — 'node server.mjs' is not a lane-scoped name
surface: process management; no repo file. The lane's own cleanup step at the end of a browser walkthrough.
found_in: 2026-09-08, self-reported. Tidying up after 10-scripts/po20260908_walkthrough.mjs the lane ran a kill loop over 'ps aux | grep -E "[r]unserver 127.0.0.1:8331|[n]ode server.mjs"'. The FIRST pattern is port-scoped and correct; the SECOND is not, and 'node server.mjs' is the exact command every lane's frontend runs. 17 PIDs were killed where 2 were intended. The five other Django backends survived (ports 8011, 8077, 8399, 8471, 8501 still answer) because the runserver half named a port; the frontend servers on 8081, 8112, 8113 and 8502 stopped listening between the two port scans.
introduced_in: this lane, 2026-09-08 — nothing in the repo did this.
escape_reason: The lane was dispatched with 'Kill by PID, never by pattern' in as many words and had killed a runaway gate sweep by PID correctly twenty minutes earlier. What defeated the rule is that the cleanup step LOOKED like a PID kill: it resolves PIDs first and then kills them one at a time, so it reads as compliant while the selection is still a pattern. No check exists or could exist — a kill is not a commit and nothing reviews it.
prevention: The damage is small and self-healing: 'node server.mjs' serves static files from dist/ and holds no state, so a lane that lost one restarts it in one command and loses nothing but the seconds. The habit that would have prevented it is the one the instruction already names, applied to the SELECTION rather than to the kill: write down the two PIDs when you START the servers and kill those two, or scope every pattern to your own port as the runserver half of this very command already did. Reported rather than silently tidied because a lane whose stack stopped mid-walk would otherwise read it as a broken product.

found_in: 2026-09-07, on a tenant provisioned through the real sign-up path (Cedar Falls Utilities) while proving the integrations sample-data blocks
introduced_in: the panel's original two-state headline — it has read this way since CR-039 wave B
escape_reason: The headline is a two-state choice on one boolean: run_summary() answers succeeded=False when ANY block is non-seeded, which is BR-TEN-056 clause 3 working exactly as designed, and the panel turns that single boolean into the sentence "Nothing was loaded. Every part of the sample set is listed below with the reason it could not run." On the tenant measured, twenty-nine of thirty blocks seeded 1,200-plus records and ONE failed, and the sentence a clerk reads first contradicts every line beneath it — each of which says Loaded with a count. Nothing else could see it because no gate reads rendered output (hard-won law 6), and the only way to meet it is to provision a tenant where exactly one block fails.
prevention: The panel needs a THIRD headline for the state that actually occurs most: some loaded and some did not. Two states cannot describe three, and the missing one is the common one. Suggested shape, keeping BR-TEN-056 clause 3 intact — the run still does not report success, and the headline still says so before any number: "N sample records loaded, and M part(s) could not run — each is listed below with the reason." Reserve the existing "Nothing was loaded" for seeded_total == 0, which is the only state it is true of. The test should then assert all three headlines against three fixtures rather than two against a boolean.

reported_by: walkthrough of all 50 portal screens on the CR-085 branch tip
title: Viewing a bill PDF answers 500 when the kept file is gone from storage, on a path whose own docstring says it must not
surface: GET /api/{tenant}/portal/bills/{number}/document.pdf — apps/portal/api.py bill_document_pdf, via apps/portal/seams/billing_seam.py printed_bill_bytes
introduced_in: US-CWP-034 (portal bill document), unchanged by CR-085
escape_reason: Every test and every gate supplies a document store whose bytes are present, so the only branch ever exercised is the one the code handles. There are two ways to have no original — no document row, and a document row whose bytes are gone from storage — and only the first returns None. The second raises FileNotFoundError out of document_store.fetch and reaches the customer as a raw 500. Both docstrings state the opposite: the endpoint says NOT A 500 AND NOT A RE-RENDER and the seam says if the store has no original the answer is None and the caller states the absence. Hard-won law 1 — a comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee. Found by walking all 50 portal screens against a running server whose storage root differed from the one that wrote the files, which is what a redeploy, a restored database or a moved volume looks like.
prevention: The refusal wording already exists (portal.billDocument.notKept) and is already used for the no-row case; the missing-bytes case must reach it too. A tampered document — a hash mismatch — must keep raising, because BR-NOT-027 says a tampered document refuses and never degrades. Missing is not tampered, and the two need separate answers. A test that deletes the stored file and asserts the handled refusal is what would have caught this; nothing in the suite has ever run this endpoint against an absent file.

title: The bills screen offers a download for a bill whose kept file is gone, because availability is decided from the database row and never from the store
surface: apps/portal/seams/billing_seam.py printed_bill_for — 'available' is bool(reproduction.is_original and page is not None); screen CWP-029
introduced_in: US-CWP-034 (portal bill document), unchanged by CR-085
escape_reason: Sibling of DEF-CWP-4657 and found by the test written for it. That defect was the download answering 500; this one is the screen still saying the document is available, because availability is read off the document row and nothing asks the store whether the bytes are still there. Every test supplies a store whose bytes are present, so the row and the store always agree and the two can never be seen to disagree. Since DEF-CWP-4657 the download refuses politely instead of erroring, so the harm is now a button that promises a page and then says we kept no copy of it — hard-won law 2's mirror, a live-looking control over something that is not there.
prevention: Answering this honestly needs a cheap existence check on the storage layer: DocumentStorageBackend has put, get and temporary_read_url and no exists, so the only way to know today is to read the whole PDF to decide a boolean, on every bill in a list. That is a storage-layer story touching the protocol, the filesystem adapter and the S3 adapter — deliberately not smuggled into a walkthrough fix. The test for DEF-CWP-4657 asserts available is True today and names this row, so the day an existence check lands the assertion goes red and points here.

surface: DRF DEFAULT_RENDERER_CLASSES is unset in config/settings, so BrowsableAPIRenderer is active; any refusal with Accept: text/html raises TemplateDoesNotExist: rest_framework/api.html
introduced_in: unknown — predates CR-085; no renderer classes have ever been configured
escape_reason: Every test and every walkthrough calls the API as JSON, and Django test Client plus fetch both send Accept that resolves to the JSON renderer, so the browsable renderer is never selected and its missing template is never reached. A browser NAVIGATION is the one caller that sends Accept: text/html — and that is exactly how a customer reaches an inline document link or an embedded PDF frame. Proved on three unrelated endpoints: bills/NO-SUCH-BILL/document.pdf, bills/NO-SUCH-BILL and requests/NO-SUCH-REF each answer 404 to JSON and 500 to a browser. So this is not one endpoint, it is every refusal in the product seen from a browser address bar or an iframe.
prevention: An API with no browsable UI should say so: set DEFAULT_RENDERER_CLASSES to the JSON renderer only, which also stops the API ever answering HTML by accident. That is a global settings change and wants its own proving run rather than being folded into a screen fix. The test that would have caught it is any refusal asserted with Accept: text/html; nothing in the suite has ever sent that header.

title: A collection allowance or interest rate once typed can never be cleared — a blank box is omitted from the payload, so the old figure survives
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/rating/TaxWizard.tsx taxPayload — the money loop calls decimalOut(), which returns undefined for a blank, and only sets the key when it is not undefined
found_in: 2026-09-08, building CR-087 B1's editable filing block against taxPayload. decimalOut('') is undefined and the key is then never written, so PATCH /taxes/{id} carries no collection_allowance_percent at all and the server keeps what it had. A clerk who typed 0.005 by mistake, or whose authority withdrew the allowance, empties the box, saves, sees a success toast, and the tax still keeps 0.5% of everything it remits. reported_by: CR-087 lane C, reading its own numstat
title: A push asserted REDERIVED_FROM_TIP=1 having re-derived only the shared registers and catalogues, and reverted a sibling lane in five source files
surface: commit d4d69cbf on claude/cr-75-remaining-waves-t5eob8 — apps/rating/selectors.py, api/endpoints.ts, features/rating/definitionDetail.tsx, DefinitionDetailPage.tsx and DefinitionDetail.test.tsx, reverting CR-087 lane B's tax merge in all five

escape_reason: push_paths.sh refused the push twice, correctly, both times on the base-is-the-tip check that DEF-GOV-4061 added. The escape hatch REDERIVED_FROM_TIP=1 says the author has rebuilt every named path from the tip, and it was passed after rebuilding only the eleven catalogues and the two registers — the paths that had conflicted. The five source files were still at the lane's own previous push, and a sibling had pushed to every one of them in between. Every check CLAUDE.md law 11 prescribes passed: the file count was right, the author's own hunks were present, git show carried nothing foreign, and the frontend and backend suites were green because the reverted work had its own tests in files this push did not touch. THE NUMSTAT IS WHAT CAUGHT IT, read as arithmetic rather than glanced at: 119 deletions in a file the author had only added forty lines to. That is the check the law names as the only one that sees this class, and it works.
prevention: The flag needs to name what was re-derived rather than assert it wholesale — pass the paths, and let the script refuse any named path not among them. Until it does, the operator rule is: REDERIVED_FROM_TIP applies to EVERY path on the command line or to none, and the moment a re-derivation loop covers a subset the remaining paths must be dropped from the push and sent separately. Repaired by three-way merge (base = the lane's previous push, ours = the bad commit, theirs = the sibling's tip) rather than by force, so both lanes' work is on the branch; two lanes had independently added the same multi-panel mechanism under different names, blocks and sections, and the name that landed first won.

title: The budget-billing chart overflows a 390px phone by 25px — the bar cannot shrink to make room for its own money label

escape_reason: Three things lined up and none of them is a missing test. (1) No gate in this repository reads rendered output, so a 415px document inside a 390px window is invisible to tsc, to eslint and to all 869 portal cases. title: REDERIVED_FROM_TIP=1 asserted for 20 paths when only 13 had been rebuilt - 95 lines of a sibling's CPB-18 and CPB-21 work reverted by subtraction
surface: commit 71d7c3f7 | 07-frontend/src/portal/api/portalClient.ts (-25) | 06-backend/apps/portal/seams/billing_seam.py (-41) | 06-backend/apps/portal/selectors.py (-29)
introduced_in: commit 71d7c3f7 (CR-085 wave 2)
escape_reason: The lane rebuilt the shared REGISTERS and the eleven catalogues from the tip, verified those by arithmetic, and then passed REDERIVED_FROM_TIP=1 - which asserts that property of EVERY path on the command line. Three source files it had been editing since its previous push had ALSO moved under it, and it never checked them: it had checked only the files it EXPECTED a sibling to touch. push_paths.sh's own refusal is the guard for exactly this and the flag turns it off, so the flag is the hazard. Every check in CLAUDE.md law 11 then passed: the file count was right, the lane's own hunks were all present, git show carried only its own work, and git diff --numstat printed deletions - which the lane read as its own rewrite of usage_cost_view rather than counting them. Found by G54 going red on a SIBLING's test file (missing_months absent from a type), two pushes later.
prevention: Before passing REDERIVED_FROM_TIP=1, list every path on the command line and check each one with git rev-parse <base>:<path> against <tip>:<path>; rebuild every one that moved, not only the ones a sibling was expected to touch. Better: do not pass the flag at all - a base that is genuinely the tip means there is nothing to push. The repair is git show <tip>:<path> then patch -p1 with git diff <base> <mine> -- <path>, then diff against the tip and confirm every remaining deletion is a line your own hunk replaced.

title: notifications spells a plan 'plan' and tenancy spells it 'payment_plan', so the document store can never be asked about one directly

surface: 12-governance/10-defect-log.csv: DEF-4497 with DEF-MET-4497, DEF-TEN-4512 with DEF-WRK-4512, DEF-CWP-4710 with DEF-TEN-4710. Reported by 10-scripts/gates/g17_duplicate_ids.py number_collisions()

It hides because run_gates today reports 76 PASS, 40 FAIL, 7 SKIP, so a lane asking whether it broke anything sees no difference, which is DEF-490 word for word about this same gate. The allocator is NOT the hole: allocate.py has read the optional module segment since it was written (its own comment says the number is never a namespace) and answers TAKEN, a sibling pushed it, for 4497, 4512 and 4710 today; file_defect.py has read it since 13c489a29 on 2026-09-03. (2) Make a NEW red survivable in a suite with 40 failures: have run_gates store each gate FAIL detail and print which details CHANGED since the last recorded run, so a fresh share is distinguishable from a carried one without reading 40 paragraphs. (3) The numbers themselves: renumber the LATER id of each pair and record the move in its row, per DEF-GOV-4405. For 4512 and 4710 the later id is also the cheap one, DEF-TEN-4512 being cited nowhere outside the register and DEF-CWP-4710 once. For 4497 it is not: the later DEF-4497 is cited from six files (apps/rating/base_size_amounts.py, sample_data.py, models.py, two test files, CHANGELOG) while DEF-MET-4497 is cited once, so that pair needs a judgment rather than the rule. title: DEF-GOV-4723 names a cause that is not true, so its prevention sends the next lane to teach two tools something both already do
surface: 12-governance/10-defect-log.csv, the DEF-GOV-4723 row: its escape_reason and its prevention
introduced_in: 2026-09-09, when DEF-GOV-4723 was filed for the 4710 collision
category: wrong diagnosis in a register row
escape_reason: NOTHING IN THIS REPO CHECKS WHETHER AN escape_reason IS TRUE. G67 asks only whether a CLOSED row names a file that mentions its id, G46 checks the vocabularies, and no gate reads a diagnosis at all. The row states that allocate.py computes the next free number from digits alone and that file_defect.py matches DEF- followed by digits, so a module-tagged id is invisible to both. Both were false on the day it was written: allocate.py has carried the pattern DEF-(?:[A-Z]{3}-)?(\d{3,5}) since it was created on 2026-09-04, with a comment saying the module is never a namespace and DEF-CWP-3740 and DEF-GOV-3740 are one number, and file_defect.py has carried the same optional segment since 13c489a29 on 2026-09-03. The row also says no gate reads the module segment, while G17 number_collisions() had been printing 4710 is claimed by 2 different ids by name since 3e567ad93 the night before. The cost is not the wrong sentence, it is the prevention built on it: it sends the next lane to teach the prefix to tools that already read it, and never mentions the two things that would have stopped this (re-verify at push time, and read the gate).
prevention: Correct the row in place through close_defect.py byte-splice discipline, never a csv writer (law 11): the true cause is an allocation taken from a stale world and never re-verified at push time, and the true escape is that G17 reported the collision and nobody read it. Not edited here on purpose, because amending another lane row is a separate act from recording that it is wrong, and because the two ids in that pair have to move first. More generally: an escape_reason that names a TOOL as the hole should be checked against that tool before the row is filed, which is one grep and is the same discipline law 1 already asks for about comments that claim a guarantee.

title: G106 reports zero phantom citations over 1,014 backend files it silently excludes, and one of them cites DEF-MET-4512, a third claimant of 4512 that no register ever issued
surface: 10-scripts/gates/g106_cited_ids_exist.py through gates/common.py code_files(), which is 06-backend/apps plus 07-frontend/src and nothing else; the live citation is 06-backend/core/sample_fixture.py:3711 and :3816

escape_reason: G106 PASS line counts the citations and the source files it READ and never says what it did not read. code_files() is 06-backend/apps plus 07-frontend/src, so 06-backend/core and 06-backend/tests are outside it: 1,014 .py files carrying 6,523 OQ/DEF citations. prevention: Two halves. (a) Print the excluded count beside the read count in G106 PASS line, so the blind spot has a number the day anybody looks; that costs one sentence and is the part law 7 asks for. (b) Widen the scan to every .py under 06-backend, or add a second census over the excluded tree, and land the six existing phantoms in g106_phantom_citations.txt with reasons rather than as a fresh red. Separately, DEF-MET-4512 needs either a register row of its own or a corrected citation: it cannot keep pointing at a number two other rows already hold. title: A commit-tree push left the whole U6 Plan tab as a loaded revert on disk while two lanes were still reading the file
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/metering/UnitDetailPage.tsx, working tree only
introduced_in: 8dfe75d54 pushing over b90a75455, 2026-09-10
escape_reason: DEF-2474 again, in its exact recorded shape: commit-tree builds from the PINNED TIP and updates NO FILE ON DISK, which is precisely why it is safe for the branch and precisely why it leaves the tree behind. The U6 lane pushed the Plan tab in b90a75455; the account lane, working from a copy read before that, pushed 8dfe75d54 correctly - the COMMIT carries both lanes work - and the disk copy it left behind was its own pre-U6 blob. So UnitDetailPage.tsx sat 45 lines short of the branch, holding the old Rate schedules fact row, the bare Yes/No on Locked and Vacant standby, the primary-tier Change plan and the retired plan-history block: every single thing the U6 lane had just removed. EVERY CHECK PASSED OVER IT. git status showed the file as modified, which is indistinguishable from a lane typing in it. Both lanes post-push subtraction checks were clean because they read COMMITS and the commits are fine. The damage is in what was LEFT BEHIND, which is DEF-2474's own sentence. EXPOSURE, STATED HONESTLY: push_paths.sh would very likely have REFUSED a push naming this path, because the path moved between base and tip - so the branch was probably never at risk. The real exposure was to READERS. Two lanes were still running in this tree, and anything reading that file - a lane gathering context, a vitest run, a grep - would have seen the pre-U6 Plan tab and concluded the U6 work was not done. That is law 12's actual failure mode: a wrong conclusion, not lost work.
prevention: The content-addressed test in law 12 is the only thing that found this and it should be run ROUTINELY rather than only after a suspected rewind: for every path differing from the tip, is its exact blob an OLDER version of that same path? A hit proves no lane authored the content, so it is a stale revert and safe to restore by writing the tip's bytes and re-setting the mode from git ls-tree. Run it whenever a lane finishes, because a finished lane's disk copy has no owner left to correct it. For catalogues and other append-shaped files the blob test misses, compare KEY SETS instead of bytes: a working copy missing a key the tip has is a revert, and a key it retires with its caller is legitimate - that distinction cannot be made from a numstat. The durable fix belongs in push_paths.sh: after a successful commit-tree push it should write the new tip's bytes over every path it just pushed, because the one thing that procedure cannot do is move the files, and every caller has to remember to do it by hand.

title: The units list departs from its drawn frame in eight places, and the vacancy sentence lived in a tooltip a keyboard cannot reach

escape_reason: No gate in this repo reads rendered output, so a column in the wrong order, a header naming both halves of one cell, asset numbers where the frame draws a count, five glyphs where B14 rule 15 caps at two plus an overflow, and an empty state offering a create it cannot complete all pass every check. The vacancy sentence is the sharpest of them: it was a title= attribute, which IS in the row's HTML - so the assertion written to guarantee it read the attribute and was green while a clerk saw a bare dash and a keyboard reached nothing.
prevention: UnitsListFrame.test.tsx strips the markup before reading a sentence, counts the VISIBLE row actions rather than checking presence, and asserts the count cell in both its states. Every case was shown red against the branch tip first. The B14 rule 15 overflow the product never had is now a kit component, so the second half of that rule is buildable rather than merely ratified.

reported_by: found in a browser walking the three unit dialogs (hard-won law 6)
title: One screen writes a property two ways: Currently on reads address-first and the picker beside it reads number-first
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/metering/UnitsListPage.tsx premisesPickerOptions — rendered by MoveUnitModal's Move to and by the units-list premise filter

It is only visible as an inconsistency when both are on screen together, which is a screenshot and not an assertion.
