reported_by: picked up as unowned reds after three lanes reported them and left them
title: Ten assertions on the property page described the screen as it was before the 9 September redesign, and stayed red for a day
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/metering/PremisesPage.test.tsx, JurisdictionField.dom.test.tsx, PremisesServicesNotRecorded.dom.test.tsx
escape_reason: 5ca82a824 rebuilt the property page onto the blueprint's drawn frame and ten assertions were left describing the screen as it was before. FOUR SEPARATE CHANGES, EVERY ONE OF THEM CORRECT: the Jurisdiction label became City limits (the frame's word, row 5); the fact rows went from a two-column grid to the drawn THIRTEEN IN ONE COLUMN; the kicker became the bare word Premise with the property number moved down to the identity line; and the common-area split left the Units tile for fact row 13, where it NAMES the areas instead of counting them. Nothing was lost - four facts moved and one word changed - and this was CHECKED against CR-089-p019 row by row rather than assumed, because a stale-test verdict that is wrong hides a real regression. THE FAILURES READ AS SOMETHING ELSE, which is why three lanes passed over them: 'Unable to find a label with the text of: Jurisdiction' reads as a missing control, not a renamed word, and on a row that decides whether an outside-city surcharge multiplies every bill at an address. This is the SECOND time this same commit did this - DEF-MET-4760 was the same shape in a sibling file that morning, and its own fix did not sweep for others.
prevention: Assert a visible label ONCE, as a named constant anchored to the catalogue, never as a literal repeated across cases about something else - so a rewording fails one case whose name says the label moved, with the reason beside it. Both files carry that anchor now, as PremisesServices.dom.test.tsx already did. TWO SHARPER LESSONS THAN THAT. First: when you repair one stale-label file, GREP FOR THE SAME LITERAL EVERYWHERE ELSE in the same commit - DEF-MET-4760 fixed one file and left an identical break in its sibling, and that omission is the whole reason this row exists. Second, from my own first draft of the replacement: an order assertion that searched the whole document matched the TAB named Common areas rather than fact row 13 and reported a correct screen as out of order - five of the six tabs share a name with a row somewhere, so a positional assertion must be anchored to the region it is about. A check looking at the wrong thing fails as convincingly as a real defect.

reported_by: the PO, on the live product
title: The building picker's help promised parcel search its labels could never do, and both boxes said nothing about typing
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/metering/AddUnitsWizard.tsx · UnitsListPage.premisesPickerOptions · components/FormModal.filterOptions
escape_reason: Three faults on one form, and only one of them is the search. FIRST, the building box's placeholder was metering.units.filter.premisePlaceholder - the units LIST FILTER's string, borrowed. On a filter Any premise is correct and means no filter applied; on a box a clerk must type into it says nothing about typing at all. SECOND, and this is the report search does not work: the help line said By address, property number or parcel and premisesPickerOptions built labels from address and premise_no ONLY, while SearchSelectField's filterOptions matches on the label. So a clerk typing a parcel got No matching options and ALWAYS WOULD HAVE - a written promise the control could not keep, indistinguishable from that property does not exist. THIRD, the plan box's placeholder was a sentence about leaving the field BLANK, on a box you type into, duplicated word for word by the control directly beneath it. Every check passed: the keys exist in all eleven catalogues, the control is the house search control, tsc and every test are green. NOTHING ASKS WHETHER A HELP LINE IS TRUE OF THE CONTROL IT SITS UNDER. The same shape as DEF-MET-4758 one screen over, where three states rendered as one sentence.
prevention: When a control's copy names what it searches, the fields it searches are a LIST and that list belongs in a test beside the copy - one case per leg, so a promise that stops being true fails rather than rots. That is what AddUnitsPickersInvite.test.ts now does, proved red on the parcel leg first with expected [] to deeply equal ['p-1'], which is the empty result the clerk actually saw. Second: a placeholder borrowed from another screen carries that screen's MEANING with it. Any premise means no filter applied on a filter and nothing at all on a picker, so grep a placeholder key's other callers before reusing it. Third, still open and NOT fixed here: the picker holds one page of 200 rows and filters client-side, so a tenant past 200 properties cannot find the rest by any term - the list screen searches server-side and the picker does not. Recorded as DEF-MET-4805 rather than smuggled into a copy fix.

title: The building picker holds one page of 200 properties and filters them in the browser, so a larger utility cannot find the rest
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/metering/AddUnitsWizard.tsx premisesQuery
escape_reason: The picker asks getPremises with per 200 once and SearchSelectField filters that array in the browser. So the box searches the FIRST 200 PROPERTIES and nothing else, silently: a clerk at a utility with 250 addresses types a real one and gets No matching options, which is the same sentence they get for a property that does not exist. The premises LIST screen does not work this way - it declares searchFields address, premise_no, owner_manager and searches SERVER-SIDE - so one product searches properties two ways and only one of them scales. NFR-3 says every list is server-paginated and NFR-5 forbids a hard cap; a 200-row window that decides what is findable is both, wearing a page size. It is invisible to every check because 200 is larger than any seeded tenant, so no fixture reaches it.
prevention: A picker over a table that can grow is a SEARCH, not a page. It should send the term to the server the way the list screen already does and drop the client-side filter, which also removes the ceiling rather than raising it. NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: it needs an endpoint parameter and a debounced request per keystroke, which is a change rather than the copy fix DEF-MET-4804 asked for, and mixing them would ship an unreviewed behaviour change inside a wording fix. The general rule worth keeping: whenever a control loads N rows and filters them locally, write down what happens at N+1 - if the answer is a silent empty result, the number is a cap and it needs saying out loud.

title: A plan's outside-city surcharge prints the stored multiplier into a percentage sentence, so 15% reads as '1.15 more'
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/rating/PlanSummaryCard.tsx:776 and PlanWizard.tsx:4603
introduced_in: unknown - present since the summary card was written
escape_reason: The field is NAMED outsideCityFactorPercentDisplay and is assigned detail.outside_city_factor - the stored MULTIPLIER - and lands in the template rating.planSummary.term.surcharge, which is '{{percent}} more'. So a plan carrying a 15 percent surcharge renders '1.15 more' on the plan page and on the wizard's review step, and a clerk reading it sees a number that is neither the multiplier's meaning nor the percentage. The server already serves outside_city_percent_display beside the factor and endpoints.ts already types it, so the right value was one word away. NO TEST CAN CATCH IT AND THAT IS THE POINT: every fixture in the suite sets outside_city_factor to null, so only the ABSENCE branch is ever exercised and the formatting branch has never been rendered by any check. The name of the variable asserts the very thing that is false, which is why reading the line does not reveal it - hard-won law 1 in a variable name rather than a comment.
prevention: When a served object carries BOTH a raw value and a display form of the same fact, the display form is the only one a screen may read, and the raw one should be typed or named so that passing it to a view is visibly wrong. Here outside_city_factor and outside_city_percent_display sit adjacent in the same payload and differ by one word. Second and more general: a fixture that only ever sets a field to null tests the absence and NOTHING else, so a formatting branch guarded by a value no fixture supplies is unexercised by construction - when a field has a present branch and an absent branch, the suite needs a fixture for each or the check is half a check.

reported_by: the CR-087 conformance read, all five tabs
title: Nine drawn facts across four Plans-and-Rates tabs are absent from screens although the server already sends them
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/rating/ - rate schedule detail, tax overview, charge code overview, plan overview
introduced_in: CR-087 waves, various
escape_reason: The single largest category across the whole pass, and the same one that dominated the Premises and Units pass. On rate schedules alone: the customer class (account_type_id, served, read by the plan wizard, read nowhere here), the size count (size_count, served - and the LIST already prints '9 sizes' while the DETAIL prints an em-dash and a sentence saying sizes are not priced separately, from the same object), the next scheduled change (scheduled_change, served, drawn by the list, unread by the detail), and the per-account reasons an impact could not be priced (five reasons counted server-side, replaced on screen by a sentence listing the possibilities). On the tax overview, PREMISES IN SCOPE has a server read that nothing on the page calls. On the charge overview, applies_to_customer_classes and amount_display are served and unrendered. Every one passes every check because a screen that does not read a field is indistinguishable from a field that does not exist.
prevention: The check that finds these is one query, not one test: for each detail screen, list the keys its endpoint serves and subtract the keys the component reads. A non-empty remainder is not automatically a defect - some fields are genuinely for other consumers - but it is always a QUESTION, and nobody has been asking it. Note the sharpest instance as the pattern to look for: the SAME object printed a real figure on the list and an em-dash plus a sentence explaining the absence on the detail. When two screens disagree about whether a fact exists, one of them is reading it.

reported_by: the CR-087 conformance read, four of five tabs
title: Eleven live sentences across Plans and Rates describe a product that stopped existing, several naming the very gap that was since filled
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/rating/ - rate schedule detail, discount wizard, plan detail, charge code detail
introduced_in: various, oldest superseded 2026-08-21
escape_reason: Hard-won law 1 on a user-visible string, eleven times. The audit tab tells a clerk that nothing records the change note, and tariff_versions.change_reason has recorded it since 21 August. The plan's audit tab says a plan version does not carry its own start date 'and when it does, this will say so'. A rate schedule detail says sizes are not priced separately while the list prints the size count from the same object. The discount wizard's typeNotPriceable names the wrong pair of types - the predicate was corrected by DEF-2802 on 31 August and the sentence it prints was not. The charge code and tax Plans tabs each render one sentence saying they cannot name what they exist to name. NOTHING IN THIS REPO ASKS WHETHER A SENTENCE IS STILL TRUE. Each was accurate when written; each is now a confident false statement to the person least able to check it.
prevention: A sentence that explains an ABSENCE has a lifetime, and the thing that ends it is the absence being filled - so the sentence needs a test that fires when its subject arrives, in the same commit that writes it. That is hard-won law 2's hold-expiry rule applied to prose rather than to a control: assert that the field the sentence says is unavailable is still absent from the payload, and the day the server starts sending it the suite goes red and names the sentence. Cheap, mechanical, and it would have caught at least four of these eleven. For the rest - a sentence naming a rule id, a predicate, or another screen's behaviour - the habit is to grep for the sentence when you change the thing it describes, which is the same discipline as grepping for a control when you land the screen it was holding.

reported_by: the CR-087 conformance read, charge codes and taxes lanes independently
title: The CR-087 tab-merge and tile wave reached discounts and stopped before taxes and charge codes, in the same two files
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/rating/definitionDetail.tsx and DefinitionDetailPage.tsx
escape_reason: One change request, one pair of files, three kinds of definition - and the work landed for one of them. The discount has three tabs, three overview blocks and the fixed tile row; the tax and the charge code still have five tabs, one flat field list, and KPI strips carrying hard-coded em-dashes. The charge code's own source says so at definitionDetail.tsx:97-99, and the discount's fix carries a comment calling the em-dash 'furniture, not a stated absence' - the exact thing still shipping on its two siblings. Both lanes found this independently without seeing each other's work, which is what makes it a cause rather than a coincidence. It is invisible to every check because each kind's own tests assert its own current shape, so all three are green while only one matches the design.
prevention: When a change request applies one shape to N kinds that share a component, the acceptance is per KIND and not per change request - list them and tick them, or the last ones silently inherit 'not done'. This is the same shape as a validator covering a column with more than one writer (DEF-MET-4757 today) and a rule ratified without its pointer moving: the work and the enumeration of where the work applies are two acts, and only the first feels like the work. Concretely here: definitionDetail.tsx declares the three kinds in one place, so a test asserting the three carry the same tab count and the same tile contract would have failed the day the wave stopped.

title: A tax correction endpoint is served, typed and called by nothing, while the button that should call it opens a wizard that refuses everything
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/rating/TaxWizard.tsx and api/endpoints.ts correctTax
introduced_in: unknown - the tab it pointed at was renamed by CR-087
escape_reason: Hard-won law 2 in BOTH directions on one screen. POST /taxes/{id}/corrections is implemented and routed, correctTax is typed in endpoints.ts - and no component calls it. Meanwhile Edit is live on a tax already in force, opens TaxWizard, and the wizard refuses every field and says the route has not been built and nothing here can be saved. The wizard's own exception note says the correction form lives on the Versions tab; CR-087 renamed that tab to Audit and it now renders a stated absence. So the door was built, the room it opened into was renamed, and the sign still points at the old name. Every check passes: the endpoint has tests, the type compiles, the wizard's refusal is asserted, and nothing anywhere asks whether a served write has a caller.
prevention: A write endpoint with no caller is the mirror of a dead control and G13 cannot see it - G13 asks whether a prop is passed, not whether a served route is reachable. The check is mechanical and does not exist: for each write route the API declares, grep the front end for its wrapper; a route with zero call sites is either unfinished or unreachable, and both need saying. Second, and this is the part that bit here: when a tab is RENAMED, grep for prose and comments naming the old tab - this refusal pointed at 'the Versions tab' and survived the rename that made the sentence false, which is the same class as DEF-RAT-4808's eleven stale sentences.

reported_by: the CR-087 conformance read, three lanes independently
title: One Plans key exists in none of the eleven catalogues, and five languages render whole Rate-schedule and Charge-code screens in English
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/rating/PlanSummaryCard.tsx:440 and the eleven locale catalogues
introduced_in: various
escape_reason: Two faults that the same gate is blind to for opposite reasons. FIRST, rating.planSummary.absent.noUsage is in ZERO of the eleven catalogues, so it reaches a clerk as the raw key or as nothing; its seven siblings are all present. G15 compares the ten catalogues against en.json, and a key absent from en.json too is absent from the comparison - law 7's report-zero-over-a-scope-it-excludes shape, already recorded for exactly this gate. SECOND, es-MX, hi, id-ID, ja-JP and ko-KR carry 88 of 97 rating.rateDetail keys and 50 of 70 rating.chargeWizard keys BYTE-IDENTICAL TO ENGLISH, including whole sentences. Key parity passes because the keys are all there; B14 rule 35 says a catalogue is written in its own language and is RATIFIED AND UNENFORCED, because no gate can read a sentence for language.
prevention: The zero-catalogue key needs a check at the RAISE SITE rather than at the catalogue - the same instrument def4742EnglishOnlyKeys.test.ts already applies to three metering files, extended to rating: for every literal key in the guarded files, is it in all eleven? That test also prints the size of its own blind spot, which is the only honest way to report a check that cannot cover its whole subject. The byte-identical-to-English half is not mechanically fixable and should not pretend to be: it needs a speaker of each language, and the honest interim is to mark those catalogues NATIVE-REVIEW-OWED in the commit rather than implying eleven fluent authors.

title: The plan price card is fed the stored MULTIPLIER where its template wants a percentage — 1.15 renders as "1.15 more", and on a new plan as "not set"
surface: S10 plan wizard step 8 (review) and the plan's Overview tab — Band 5, the Outside the city limits row
introduced_in: CR-087 D4, when PlanSummaryCard was written; the percent field CR-087 D1 added was never wired to it
escape_reason: Both adapters pass outside_city_factor into a cell templated '{{percent}} more', and EVERY fixture sets that factor to null (PlanDetail.test.tsx:118, cr087ClassSizeGrid.dom.test.tsx:218) — so only the absentValue branch has ever rendered and the assertion that exists cannot fail on the bug (hard-won law 7, 'looking at the wrong thing'). The wizard half is worse: step 2 writes outside_city_percent and NO control writes outside_city_factor, so a clerk who has just typed 15 sees 'not set' on the review. No gate reads rendered output.
prevention: The card's input field is renamed outsideCitySurchargeDisplay so the name says what it must hold; the plan page passes the server's outside_city_percent_display and the wizard renders the typed percent through rating.plan.surcharge.percentValue. The durable half is a fixture rule rather than a gate: a money-adjacent cell whose only exercised branch is its absence is untested, so a fixture must set a non-null value.

title: rating.planSummary.absent.noUsage is called by the price card and exists in NONE of the eleven catalogues — the USAGE cell reaches a clerk as the raw key
surface: S10 plan wizard step 8 and the plan's Overview tab — Band 1 (Rate schedule), the USAGE cell of any service whose schedule card is not on the scanned page
introduced_in: CR-087 D4/E1, PlanSummaryCard.tsx:440 — seven sibling absent.* keys were added and this eighth was called and never written
escape_reason: G15's parity check compares the eleven catalogues TO EACH OTHER and never to the call sites, so a key missing from all eleven is perfectly consistent and passes — the same blind spot DEF-MET-4769 was filed for. tsc cannot see it because t() takes any string. The branch is reachable whenever a bound schedule falls off the scanned catalogue page, which no fixture reproduces.
prevention: The key is written in all eleven through 10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py. The durable half is the blind spot itself: parity between catalogues cannot answer 'is every key that is CALLED present', and a check that reads t() call sites and compares them to en.json is the shape that would. Named, not built — a new gate is the last resort and needs the PO's agreement.

title: The per-service minimum was declared on the price card's input and rendered by NO band — the figure a clerk typed on step 3 never appeared on the review it was there to be reviewed on
surface: S10 plan wizard step 8 (review) and the plan's Overview tab — PlanSummaryInput.services[].minimum_amount
introduced_in: CR-087 D4, when PlanSummaryInput was declared; the field was carried by both adapters and read by no band
escape_reason: Hard-won law 2 in its plainest form: a field that is passed and never read. G13 asks whether a prop is PASSED — both adapters passed it — and nothing asks whether anything renders it. tsc is happy because the field is consumed by the object literal. No gate reads rendered output, and the drawn frames (CR-087-p101 §3, p105 §8) draw no minimum column, so a reader diffing against the drawing would conclude the absence was correct.
prevention: It is drawn now as the Band 1 row footnote beside the base's attribution (rating.planSummary.serviceFloor), which is DEF-2418's established 'one fact about the row, stated once' mechanism and adds no column to either frame. The general shape — a declared input field no band reads — is mechanically reachable: PLAN_SUMMARY_BAND_ORDER is already exported so a reorder is a failing test, and the same file could assert every PlanSummaryInput field is referenced. Named, not built.

title: The unit resolution screen promises THREE labelled minimum sources and two of them are now the same figure from the same place
surface: S15 unit resolution display — minimum_bill.services[] and minimum_bill.schedules[], apps/metering/selectors.py:6863
introduced_in: PO ruling 2026-09-10 — plan_services.minimum_amount moved onto tariff_versions.minimum_bill (rating/0030+0031), so the per-service row now reads through to the schedule the row beneath it already showed
escape_reason: The read still returns three lists and its docstring still says 'the screen shows three labelled figures and says they are three', which was true when written. Nothing compares a docstring to what the rows now hold, and both rows are individually correct — the duplication is only visible to a person looking at the rendered screen, which is hard-won law 6's standing gap.
prevention: Not fixed in passing: which of the two rows the screen keeps is a layout decision on a screen this lane does not own, and the read is money-adjacent. The source label is corrected to rate_schedule so the row no longer CLAIMS to come from the plan, which is the half that was actually false. Filed for the metering lane to resolve with the drawing in front of it.

title: Plan wizard step 7 declared NO validate at all, so a blank start date walked to step 8 — the drawn spec records the fix as landed and it had never been built
surface: S10 plan wizard step 7 (Eligibility) — planWizardSteps, PLAN_WIZARD_STEPS[6]
introduced_in: never built — CR-087-p099 §3 describes the check as done ('It is checked here') and only steps 1, 2 and 3 ever declared a validate
escape_reason: Hard-won law 1 in its purest form: the conformance document states the guarantee and no code implements it, and a document is not the guarantee. Nothing compares a step's declared validate against the fields that step collects, and step 8's own refusal (rating.plans.no_effective_from) meant the product never LOST the check — it just asked for it one screen from the end, which is a worse screen and not a broken one, so no suite could see it.
prevention: Step 7 now declares validate: () => draft.effective_from.trim() !== '', refusing Continue and never Save draft (BR-RAT-031). Step 8's refusal STAYS, because it is the server's rule restated at the commit and it is what a resumed draft that jumps straight to step 8 still meets. The general shape — a required field on a step with no validate — is mechanically reachable and is named rather than built (a new gate is the last resort and needs the PO's agreement).

title: The plan's service list was an eleven-cell checkbox grid, which B14 rule 9 forbids by name and the drawn frame replaces with one select plus chips
surface: S10 plan wizard step 2 (Services) — the SERVICES THIS PLAN COVERS field
introduced_in: CR-087 D1 — the ruling of 2026-09-08 made the list eleven rows and kept the grid; the frame's own COMPONENTS row names MultiSelectField and ChipList
escape_reason: B14 rule 9 is RATIFIED and UNENFORCED — no gate in this repo reads rendered output — and the file's own docstring described the three-column grid of toggle tiles as r10's shape, so the next lane reading the code learned the wrong thing. This is not a rule-38 divergence: the drawing and the UI rules said the same thing and only the code differed, which is rule 36's breach (e) on a second screen.
prevention: It composes the kit's ChipMultiSelect. The kit LACKED the piece the screen needed — an option that is present and not choosable, with its reason — so the option gained OPTIONAL disabled+reason fields rather than the screen keeping its grid or dropping BR-RAT-024's restored clause (the switched-off services are named INSIDE the list, greyed, with where to switch them on). That is rule 36's own instruction and rule 38's caveat: absent on every other call site, so nothing existing moves. The DOM test asserts the reason is in the VISIBLE text and not on a title.

title: The plan Audit tab printed an em-dash on every row but one and a sentence explaining the em-dash, while the date it needed sat four inches away under the version number
surface: S10 plan detail, Audit tab — the EFFECTIVE column and the panel still headed Versions
introduced_in: OQ-324 left plan_versions with no effective_from deliberately, and the column was built to state that absence rather than to state the fact the row does carry
escape_reason: The absence was CORRECT about the data and wrong about the screen, so nothing could see it: the sentence was true, the cell rendered, the tests asserted the sentence and passed. CR-087-p112 records it as the drawn defect word for word and the drawing's proposed fix (a range from the next version's start) cannot be built on the data as stored — so a lane reading only the drawing would have added a column OQ-324 reserves for the PO.
prevention: Put to the PO with that constraint; the ruling was 'one date is good enough'. The column is now Changed and shows the version row's own created_at, which was already stored and already rendered a few pixels away — no column, no migration, no ruling on OQ-324. The panel inside the tab is renamed Audit (the earlier rename landed on the tab strip only) and the callout drops its internal 'that has not been decided' clause, which is B14 rule 32 clause 4 and rule 33's zero-words-of-rationale. The test asserts the DATE rather than the absence, because the previous version could pass over a column showing nothing at all.

title: Step 7 said the same fact THREE times and its heading said the opposite — 'Who may be put on this plan' over 'Nothing here refuses anybody'
surface: S10 plan wizard step 7 (Eligibility) — StepHead heading and hint, the + Add rule button, the Rules · all must pass · N list header
introduced_in: CR-087 D4 — the fix for exactly this contradiction landed on the PANEL and not on the step head, so the corrected pair was added beneath the wording it was meant to replace
escape_reason: The step head is drawn on every step of all five wizards from a shared component, so the sentence a lane edits is the panel's and the head's lives one indirection away. Nothing in this repository reads a sentence against the behaviour it describes (B14 rule 34's own status line), and B14 rule 32's description budget is UNENFORCED. A screen can say a thing three times, in two directions, with every gate green.
prevention: StepHead's hintKey is now OPTIONAL — absent on step 7, present and unchanged on every other step, so nothing existing moves — and the heading matches the panel. '+ Add rule' becomes '+ Add a note' and 'Rules · all must pass' becomes 'Notes', because the screen's own prose says it is documentation and nothing evaluates it. The test now asserts the surviving sentence AND refuses the removed one (not.toContain 'all must pass'), which is the only way a half-landed rename shows up as red.

title: merge_register.py's collision guard could not see a module-tagged id, so it printed 'no duplicate id' over a live duplicate
surface: 10-scripts/merge_register.py — the .csv and .md id patterns
introduced_in: PO ruling 2026-09-03 minted OQ-<MOD>-nnnn and DEF-<MOD>-nnnn; this script's patterns were written before it and never learned the segment
escape_reason: Hard-won law 7's 'reporting zero over a scope it silently excludes', in its worst form: the excluded scope is the only part of the register anybody is still writing to. (?:DEF|OQ|CR)-\\d+ does not partially match DEF-RAT-4826, it matches NOTHING, so the guard counted zero ids across the whole recent tail and truthfully reported no duplicate. CLAUDE.md already records this blindness for file_defect.py, gates/common.py, g08, g17, g38 and g50 — merge_register.py is not on that list and is the one whose entire job is finding a duplicate id.
prevention: Both patterns now carry CLAUDE.md's own optional module segment with the load-bearing lookahead — (?:[A-Z]{3}-)?\\d{3,5}(?!\\d) — so bare ids still resolve and nothing is renumbered. PROVED on a real collision rather than a hypothetical: two lanes took DEF-RAT-4826 in the shared tree on 2026-09-10, the guard printed 'no duplicate id' and exited 0; it now names the id and exits 1. The other five tools CLAUDE.md lists are still blind and are named here rather than swept, because each is a different lane's file.

title: Four columns the rate-schedule API serves and no screen on S11 ever read — customer class, size count, next scheduled change, and the per-account reasons an impact could not be priced
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/rating/RateScheduleDetail.tsx · 07-frontend/src/features/rating/RateScheduleWizard.tsx
escape_reason: A served column that nothing renders is invisible to every check this repo has: the field is in the API type, the endpoint returns it, tsc and eslint pass because nobody dereferences an unused property, and no gate reads rendered output. Worse, TWO of the four were already drawn by a NEIGHBOURING screen from the SAME object, so the product contradicted itself in the open: the rate-schedules list printed '9 sizes' from size_count while the detail's tile printed an em-dash beside a sentence saying the schedule does not price sizes separately. Every suite was green on both.
prevention: When a screen states an absence, the check is not 'is the sentence rendered' but 'does the API already answer this'. A gate could compare each *Absent/em-dash tile against the fields its own endpoint type declares; nothing like that exists. Cheaper and available today: when two surfaces show one fact, make them call ONE function, which is what sizesText now is for the list cell and the detail tile.

title: Three sentences on the rate-schedule screens described the code when they were written and describe nothing now — one of them tells an auditor that nothing records a version's change note

Nothing records it yet' — tariff_versions.change_reason has recorded it since DEF-280 closed on 21 August. title: The rate-schedule wizard's last step read back the pricing ALREADY IN FORCE instead of the draft the clerk had just typed, one press from activating it

And a reference count feeding a delete lock must be re-derived whenever a rule creates a new KIND of reference: BR-RAT-088 made a reference with no row in any join table, and a count written before that rule could not have known. A sibling lane had already found the reporting half of this and wrote in its own docstring that widening the LOCK was a separate decision; this is that decision taken.

title: Five of the eleven catalogues render the whole rate-schedule detail screen in English — 88 of its 97 keys byte-identical to en.json, and every parity check passes

title: The tax correction door is served, typed and called by nothing, behind a refusal that had stopped being true

title: One shared count component, two different argument sets — the tax wizard's last screen showed a reach larger than the truth

title: A push re-derived its blobs from one tip and committed them against another, reverting eleven catalogue values including a PO-ruled label
surface: 07-frontend/src/i18n/locales/*.json (eleven files) — commit 8c40dcf0c, restored by 5ee2dc49b

title: The tax wizard offered Save changes on every tax the server refuses to edit — the client used a date test and the server uses is_draft

Here that is status !== draft, which tax_row already serves. And the browser walk is what compares them: a test on either side alone passes.

surface: [frontend] features/rating/ChargeCodeWizard.tsx BasicsStep (the ArrivesWithField) + ChargeDraft / emptyChargeDraft / chargePayload; the grid help line rating.chargeWizard.perSize.classIsNotReach pointed at a control the previous step did not have

title: B14 RULE 10 WAS UNMEETABLE ON THE CHARGE WIZARD, NOT MERELY UNMET, AND THE TYPE CONTROL WAS NEVER REVISITED WHEN THE FIFTH TYPE LANDED - the drawn frame marks TYPE*, HOW THE AMOUNT IS WORKED OUT* and AMOUNT*; none carried an asterisk. surface: [frontend] features/rating/DefinitionDetailPage.tsx definitionTabFrom (the silent fallback) and DefinitionTabBody's PLANS_TAB branch · [backend] apps/rating/api.py had no charges/{id}/plans route and apps/rating/selectors.charge_used_by counts only the named route
introduced_in: (a) 2026-09-08, when CR-087 C2/B2 renamed the discount's and the tax's tab and left the charge; (b) and (c) since CHG-01 shipped
escape_reason: definitionTabFrom cannot tell a MISTYPED tab from a SYNONYM, so a link to a screen that exists opens a different screen with no error and no log - the same shape as the hold-expiry test that asserted a screen was registered at one address while the router mounted it at another. GET /charges/{id}/plans serves BOTH routes with the route as a WORD on each row, paged from the server (NFR-3). charge_used_by is deliberately untouched: it feeds the DELETE lock and widening a lock is a different decision from widening a screen count.

title: A RESURRECTION CHECK RUN FROM A STALE LOCAL HEAD REPORTED A REAL REVERT AS A FALSE ALARM, TWICE, TO THE PRODUCT OWNER
surface: 10-scripts/ (ad-hoc git log -S resurrection check); 07-frontend/src/i18n/locales/*.json
found_in: the CR-087 coordinating lane, on the third re-verification after the rate-schedules lane insisted
introduced_in: the ad-hoc check itself, written this session
escape_reason: The check asked 'has this key ever been retired?' with git log -S '"<key>"' HEAD -- <catalogue>, and local HEAD was 15 commits behind the tip, so the retirement commit f429885d3 was NOT REACHABLE and the walk returned zero commits. Zero commits was then read as 'the key is simply new' rather than as 'my history is too short to answer'. Law 12 says run check_head_current.sh before you believe a grep; a history query is a grep over commits and nothing distinguishes 'no such commit' from 'no such commit HERE'. The rate-schedules lane was right all three times and was told twice it was wrong, which is the expensive half: a confident not-yours report tells every later reader not to look.
prevention: Any git log / git log -S / git show used as EVIDENCE must name an explicit ref that is the remote tip, not bare HEAD - git log -S ... origin/<branch> -- <path>. And a zero result from a history walk is not a negative finding until the walk is proved able to see a known-positive commit.

title: A DIFF'S '<' COUNT IS NOT A LOSS COUNT, AND sync_stale_tree.py PHRASES IT AS ONE - ONE STALE ID WAS RELAYED TO THREE LANES AS TWELVE LOST ROWS
surface: 10-scripts/sync_stale_tree.py (the LEFT verdict line)
found_in: the CR-087 coordinating lane, re-measuring before correcting three running lanes
introduced_in: sync_stale_tree.py as written
escape_reason: The tool's advisory verdict counts diff lines beginning '<' and prints 'loses N line(s) the tip has'. diff reports a CHANGED line and a MOVED line as one '<' plus one '>', so on an append-only register whose rows are in a different order, and on a catalogue whose values were deliberately reworded, the count is not a loss count at all. It read 12 on 12-governance/10-defect-log.csv where the true defect was ONE stale duplicate id plus six stray CRLF endings, and read 3 on every locale catalogue where the true answer was zero - those three keys were the discounts lane's live rewording of a rule the branch text still states the old way. The verdict is explicitly advisory and the tool acts on neither, so nothing was destroyed; the cost was that a human-facing number was wrong and was relayed to three lanes as fact.
prevention: State the verdict content-addressed rather than positionally: the number that means something is 'branch lines absent from the tree ANYWHERE in the file', not the count of diff '<' lines. For an append-only register, compare id SETS. Phrase an advisory count as 'N lines differ' unless it has actually been proved to be a loss.

title: Three sibling tabs answering one question — which plans carry this definition — ship two different answers to NFR-3 and B14 rule 16
surface: S13 tax Plans tab, S11 rate schedule Plans tab, CHG-01 charge code Plans tab
escape_reason: Three lanes built the same shape from the same blueprint on the same day and could not see each other. The charge code tab paginates (ListPager, page/per, a server read taking {page, per}); the rate schedule and tax tabs use the kit PlainTable with no toolbar and no footer, each recording a B14 rule 16 divergence in its own conformance file on the grounds that the drawing draws neither and the read is bounded by the tenant plan catalogue rather than by accounts. Both readings are defensible and both are written down; what is wrong is that there are two. No gate compares two screens with each other, and B14 rule 36 names this exact shape — how a product acquires four different chips.
prevention: Where one question gets a tab on more than one object, the answer belongs to the KIND once, not to each tab. A reach list is either a DataTable everywhere or a PlainTable everywhere; whichever is chosen, the three read it from one place. Until then the divergence is recorded in all three conformance files rather than left for a reader to discover by opening two tabs.

title: THREE ENDPOINT IMPORTS LEFT DEAD ON THE BRANCH BY A LANE-COLLISION WORKAROUND, AND THE NOTE EXPLAINING THEM OUTLIVED THE COLLISION

reported_by: the Product Owner, who asked whether the eleven running background tasks were healthy
title: rev(1) HANGS FOREVER AT 90% CPU ON ANY NON-ASCII LINE, AND EIGHT OF THEM RAN FOR UP TO 11.8 HOURS DEGRADING EVERY LANE'S TEST RUNS
surface: the container's /usr/bin/rev (util-linux 2.39.3); any shell idiom using it on a repo file
found_in: the CR-087 coordinating lane, after the PO asked whether eleven running background tasks were healthy
introduced_in: the environment image; first triggered by a lane using rev | cut | rev to read a long register line
escape_reason: REPRODUCED: 'hello world' | rev returns instantly; 'hello - world' with an em-dash instead of the hyphen NEVER RETURNS and spins at ~90% CPU. Every multibyte character tested hangs the same way: em-dash, middot, warning sign, e-acute, right-arrow. rev is stock util-linux 2.39.3 and handles pure ASCII correctly, so nothing about the invocation looks wrong. In THIS repo that makes it a landmine on nearly every shared file - the defect register, the decision log, all eleven locale catalogues and CLAUDE.md itself are dense with em-dashes, middots and warning signs. Two things hid it. First, a hung background command is indistinguishable in the task panel from one still working: eight of these accumulated across four separate invocations, the oldest running 11 hours 48 minutes, and the panel showed them as simply 'running'. Second, NOTHING IN THIS REPO MEASURES THE MACHINE - no gate reads load average, so 8 spinners pinning a 4-core box to a load of 6.33 produced no red anywhere. The cost landed on other lanes as unexplained slowness: the taxes lane's full 123-gate suite exited 124 (a timeout, which it correctly refused to report as green), and the same lane ran 'pkill -f vitest' to stop runs 'competing for CPU' - an unscoped pattern it self-flagged as risky, reached for because the real cause was invisible. Killing rev is not enough either: the parent loop respawns one per iteration, and 'timeout -s KILL' reaps the wrapper while the rev in the pipeline survives, so a bounded call still leaks a spinner.
prevention: NEVER use rev in this container. To take the tail of a long line use grep -o '.\{0,N\}$', or awk/python, all of which are instant and multibyte-safe. More generally: when a background command has run far longer than its work could plausibly need, read the process table and the load average before assuming it is still working - 'ps -eo pid,etimes,pcpu --sort=-pcpu' and 'uptime' answer in one command each. A task panel reports that a process EXISTS, never that it is making progress.

title: NO GATE RUNS THE FRONT-END TEST SUITE, SO A RED VITEST SAT ON THE BRANCH THROUGH A FULL 123-GATE RUN THAT NEVER MENTIONED IT
surface: 10-scripts/gates/run_gates.py — the merge verdict; 07-frontend/src/features/rating/PlanWizard.test.tsx
found_in: the CR-087 coordinating lane, running the rating vitest suite by hand after a container restart
introduced_in: the gate suite as built; the red itself by 2357827ec, 2026-09-10
escape_reason: G98 shells out to 'npm run lint' and a lint error blocks merge. A dozen gates shell out to pytest, so a backend failure blocks merge. NOTHING shells out to vitest - verified by searching every gate for a subprocess invocation of the front-end test runner, which returns none; every mention of vitest inside a gate is prose explaining why THAT gate exists because vitest cannot see something. So the front-end suite is simply outside the merge verdict, and the verdict reads as authoritative over the whole repo. It bit today: 2357827ec rewrote three second-approval sentences in all eleven catalogues to implement the PO's ruling that a second approval applies only where a threshold is set, and left PlanWizard.test.tsx asserting the 2026-08-21 wording. The suite was RED on the branch for hours. A full 123-gate run over that exact tip reported 80 PASS, 40 FAIL, MERGE BLOCKED - naming forty reasons and not this one - and its own run-over-run line said '0 newly failing', truthfully, of everything it can see. This is hard-won law 7's 'reporting zero over a scope it silently excludes', one level up: not a gate with a blind spot, but a whole test suite outside the verdict, with no number printed anywhere to say so. It is also the mirror of the discounts lane's own lesson that turning a rule off does not turn off the sentences describing it - here the sentences changed and the assertion describing them did not.
prevention: Either add a gate that runs the front-end suite the way G98 runs eslint - through 'npm run', SKIPping with a named reason when npm or node_modules are absent, so it can never silently pass - or, if that is judged too slow for every run, have run_gates PRINT what it does not cover beside what it does. A declared blind spot with no number attached is indistinguishable from an empty one. Until then, a lane changing clerk-facing copy greps the catalogues AND the test files for the old sentence, not just the component.

title:
EVERY FIELD IN THE CUSTOMER PORTAL MISSES B14 RULE 39's FIELD ANATOMY, AND THE CAUSE IS ONE SHARED COMPONENT PLUS A MISSING PARAGRAPH RESET. Rule 39 (ratified 2026-09-11) puts label to input at 5px, input to helper at 6px and field to field at 20px, about 1:1:4, and says the figures are ratified rather than the ordering because 'the helper must READ as attached to the input above it'. Measured with getComputedStyle on the running app at 390 AND 1280 (identical at both) across CWP-015, CWP-016, CWP-019, CWP-012 and CWP-006: label to input is 4px everywhere; input to helper is 17px on all three helpers in the guest set; field to field is 12px on /enrol and /sign-in and 16px on /report and /track - neither is 20 and the two do not agree with each other. Ratio measured 4:17:12 and 4:17:16 against a ratified 5:6:20. MECHANISM, both halves: primitives.tsx FormField is one 'flex flex-col gap-1' so label-to-input and input-to-helper can never differ by design (4px), and the helper is a bare

with no m-0 in a stylesheet that has NO p margin reset - probed live, a bare

computes margin 13px top and bottom, so 4+13=17 above and the same 13 pushes helper-to-next-label to 25px on /enrol and 29px on /report and /track. The helper still reads as attached, at a 1.5x to 1.7x margin where the ruling's own figures give 3.3x. The same 13px rides on FormField's error paragraph. Other portal components already write m-0 on every

by hand; the component every form composes does not. --sp-1 through --sp-7 all resolve to the empty string, which rule 39 states about itself.
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/components/primitives.tsx FormField - and through it CWP-006, CWP-012, CWP-015, CWP-016, CWP-018, CWP-019 and every other portal form
introduced_in: CR-068 wave B (FormField), predating rule 39
escape_reason: No gate in this repository reads computed spacing - rule 39 says so in its own status column, 'UNENFORCED'. A gap that comes from a UA default paragraph margin is invisible in source: nothing in FormField.tsx mentions 13px, and a reader checking the class list sees gap-1 and concludes 4px. It took getComputedStyle in a real engine to see it.
fixed_commit: CR-085 step 2 lane 2, 0982be2e2 - /sign-in and /enrol moved off gap-3 and /track and /report off Card's block gap onto their own gap-5 field stack, which is the kit's own 20px (TwoUp). The BEFORE figures ARE browser-measured at 390 and 1280 (12 on /sign-in and /enrol, 16 on /track and /report); the AFTER re-measurement is 10-scripts/cr085_lane2_guest_walkthrough.mjs and is recorded there rather than claimed here. Card was NOT moved - it is the kit's and four other lanes' screens compose it. /pay and /start-service remain
prevention: Declare the scale as --sp-N tokens, give FormField three explicit gaps instead of one container gap, and put m-0 on the helper and error paragraphs - or reset p margin once in the portal stylesheet. Then a gate that reads getComputedStyle on the anchors rule 39 lists, which is the only kind of check that can see this class of defect at all.

title: CPB-24 AS WRITTEN WOULD PRINT A RAW CATALOGUE KEY ON THE LIVE LANDING PAGE IN ELEVEN LANGUAGES. The Customer Portal Blueprint's specification CPB-24, 'The two dead hold sentences are retired', says of both keys that they 'sit in all eleven catalogues and are rendered by NO SOURCE FILE AT ALL' and that done looks like 'The two keys are gone from all eleven catalogues and no screen changes, because nothing rendered them.' Checked at b4063d1e6: portal.held.signIn is indeed dead - eleven catalogues, no render site anywhere in 07-frontend or 06-backend. portal.held.card IS NOT. FrontPageView.tsx line 237 renders it for the what_things_cost card, whose CR-068 R3 hold is still correct because the blueprint's own screen 08 - a public prices and fees page - is genuinely unbuilt. Screenshotted live at 390 and 1280 on 2026-09-11: the landing page reads 'Opens with the next release.' under What things cost right now. t() answers a missing key WITH THE KEY, so executing CPB-24 as specified puts the literal string portal.held.card on the busiest page in the portal, in all eleven languages - the exact defect G27 exists to prevent. CPB-24 must be narrowed to one key before anybody works it.
surface: 05-prototype/SMARTBillHub Customer Portal Blueprint.pdf CPB-24 (pages 110 and 113) vs 07-frontend/src/portal/guest/FrontPageView.tsx:237
introduced_in: the blueprint pass of 2026-09-08
escape_reason: The blueprint dates itself honestly - 'every as-built statement here was true at 2.232.0, commit d940f460, on 8 September 2026, and must be re-verified before it is trusted' - and the re-verification is exactly what nothing does automatically. A specification whose acceptance sentence is 'no screen changes' is one no reviewer thinks to open a screen for.
fixed_commit: CR-085 step 2 lane 2 · 2.235.0 — CPB-24 narrowed to one key: portal.held.signIn retired from eleven catalogues, portal.held.card kept because FrontPageView.tsx renders it under What things cost
prevention: Narrow CPB-24 to portal.held.signIn. More generally: a spec that says 'rendered by no source file' should carry the grep that proved it and the date, so the next reader re-runs a command rather than trusting a sentence - the same reason DEF-CWP-3943's own row now needs splitting.

title: ENROLMENT'S 'Continue' IS LIVE WITH ALL THREE REQUIRED FIELDS EMPTY, ON THE ONE GUEST FORM THAT LOCKS AFTER THREE WRONG TRIES. Measured live at 390 and 1280 on 2026-09-11: on /enrol step 1 (CWP-016) the Continue button is enabled with account number, postcode and last name all blank, so an empty submission reaches findAccount and spends one of the three tries the screen itself warns about - 'Three wrong tries locks this form for fifteen minutes.' (BR-CWP-036). Every other guest form in the lane guards its commit and names the reason: /report draws 'Send this report' disabled with title 'Fill in the marked fields.' and /track draws 'Look it up' disabled with title 'Fill in both boxes.', both through the kit's CommitButton with a ready prop. Enrol.tsx composes WorkingButton with no ready guard at all, so the kit has the answer and this screen does not use it.
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/signin/Enrol.tsx CWP-016 step 1
introduced_in: CR-068 wave E
escape_reason: Enrol.dom.test.tsx's 13 cases all fill the fields before pressing Continue, so the empty-submit path is exercised by nothing; and the two components that get this right - CommitButton with ready, versus WorkingButton without - look interchangeable in a diff. Nothing counts which commits are guarded.
fixed_commit: CR-085 step 2 lane 2 · 2.235.0 — CommitButton with a ready guard and portal.enrol.notReady in eleven languages; an empty submission no longer reaches findAccount or spends one of BR-CWP-036's three tries
prevention: Compose CommitButton with ready on every guest form so a screen cannot opt out by choosing the other button, and add one case per form that presses the commit with nothing typed and asserts the reason rather than a network call.

title: CWP-028 LOSES ITS WHOLE HEAD WHEN A BILL WILL NOT LOAD - no heading, no kicker, no back link, one grey sentence on an empty page. Measured in a browser 2026-09-11 at 390 and 1280: a 500 on GET /portal/bills/{number} renders exactly 'We could not read this bill.' and nothing else, so a customer has no title telling them which bill failed and no way back to the list except the browser's own button. The loading branch is the same. Bills.tsx fixed precisely this for CWP-027 under DEF-CWP-4000 and records the fix in its own comment ('THE HEAD IS BUILT ONCE AND RENDERS ON EVERY BRANCH'); BillDetail.tsx builds its PageHeader after the two early returns, so the sibling screen never got it.
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/bills/BillDetail.tsx lines 92-104 - the failed and !bill early returns
introduced_in: CR-085 (c) redraw of CWP-028
escape_reason: BillDetail.dom.test.tsx asserts the failed sentence renders; no test asserts that the HEAD renders beside it. A test for an early-return branch naturally asserts the thing the branch was written to show, so the frame going missing is invisible to it, and no gate reads rendered output.
prevention: When a screen's head is hoisted out of the happy path for one screen, grep the module for its siblings' early returns in the same commit - CWP-028, CWP-029, CWP-030 and CWP-031 all have the same shape. Assert the h1 in the failed and loading cases, not only the sentence.

title: CWP-031 PRINTS A RAW ISO DATE INSIDE 'Came back to us on 2026-08-16.' WHILE THE SAME ROW'S SENT COLUMN IS 08/05/2026 - and the sentence draws at all when the field is merely absent. Routes() renders t('portal.documents.cameBack', {date: route.returned_on}) with the server's raw ISO string; every other date on the screen goes through usePortalDate and the tenant's own MM/DD/YYYY. Two date formats on one row. The filter is routes.filter(r => r.returned_on !== null), so a route object without the key at all (undefined) passes it and a customer reads 'Came back to us on .' - a claim that their bill bounced, with an empty date, on every row. Seen in a browser 2026-09-11: four of four rows.
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/documents/Documents.tsx Routes() lines 506-516 - cameBack
introduced_in: CR-068 wave G
escape_reason: Documents.dom.test.tsx never plants a returned route, so the sentence is never rendered by a test; and Routes() does not take asDate as a parameter, so nothing in the file's own types could have said it was missing one. DEF-CWP-4204 swept raw dates on the request screens and this file was not in that sweep.
prevention: Pass asDate into every presenter that renders a date, so a raw one is a missing argument rather than a judgement call; and test presence-of-a-fact filters with the field ABSENT as well as null, because a server that stops sending a key is the common way this class fires.

title: A THIRD DEAD HOLD SENTENCE - portal.bills.payHeld sits in all ELEVEN catalogues and is rendered by no source file at all. 'Online payment arrives later this year' was the reason the Pay control on CWP-027 was held; the door was opened to /pay-now and the wording was never taken out, which is exactly CPB-24's finding one screen further on. Verified 2026-09-11: the key is present in de, en, es, es-MX, fr-FR, hi, id-ID, it-IT, ja-JP, ko-KR and pt-BR, and grep over 07-frontend/src finds no consumer. CPB-24 names portal.held.card and portal.held.signIn and stops there, so a spec that exists to retire dead hold sentences would leave this one behind.
surface: 07-frontend/src/i18n/locales/*.json portal.bills.payHeld (11 files)
introduced_in: the CWP-027 pay-door release
escape_reason: No gate asks whether a catalogue key has a consumer; G32 asks the opposite question (does a rendered key resolve) and truthfully reports zero over the keys it can see. A key with no reader costs nothing at runtime, so nothing ever goes red for it, and the eleven translations make it look maintained.
prevention: When a hold is released, delete its sentence in the same commit that opens the door - and widen CPB-24 from two named keys to the RULE (no catalogue key without a consumer), because naming instances leaves the next one standing.

title: CWP-030 PRINTS ITS OWN HEADING TWICE ON A FIRST BILL - 'Why is this bill different?' as the h1 and 'WHY IS THIS BILL DIFFERENT?' as the section title immediately under it, with the one-line answer below. Measured in a browser 2026-09-11 at 390 and 1280 with compared:false. The compared branch words its section title from the comparison ('AGAINST LAST MONTH'), so the duplication only appears on the branch a customer meets in their FIRST MONTH of service - the worst month to look unfinished in.
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/bills/BillComparison.tsx - the compared:false branch's SectionTitle
introduced_in: CR-068 wave H
escape_reason: BillComparison.dom.test.tsx asserts the first-bill SENTENCE is present; a duplicated heading is two correct strings, so every assertion about either one passes. Nothing counts how many times one string renders.
prevention: Where a section title is derived, assert the first-bill branch renders the h1 ONCE - and prefer no section title at all over one that repeats the page title, per B14 rule 32's description budget.

title: CWP-055's THREE HELPER SENTENCES ARE NOT BOUND TO THEIR INPUTS - aria-describedby is null on all three fields, so a screen reader never reads 'A sentence or two is plenty.' or 'Optional. We keep it as evidence, not as a meter reading.' Measured with getComputedStyle and getAttribute in a browser 2026-09-11 at 1280. The helper is a sibling paragraph carrying the browser's DEFAULT 13px margins, and the field wrapper is gap-1 (4px), so the rhythm on screen is label-to-input 4px against a helper sitting 13px below - which is B14 rule 39's named failure ('the helper must READ as attached to the input above it') as well as the accessibility one. Rule 39 ratifies 5px / 6px / 20px and this form measures 4px / 13px / 16px.
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/requests/DisputeBill.tsx - What are you questioning, Why, Your own reading today
introduced_in: CR-068 wave I
escape_reason: A helper rendered as a sibling paragraph IS in the DOM and IS visible, so every toContain and getByText assertion passes; aria-describedby is the one thing that distinguishes attached from merely adjacent and nothing asserts it. B14 rule 39 was ratified 2026-09-11 and says of itself that it is entirely unbuilt, so no gate reads computed spacing either.
prevention: Bind every helper with aria-describedby in the shared Field component rather than per screen, so a helper that is not attached cannot be written; and assert the attribute, not the text.

title: ON A PHONE THE BILLS LIST HAS NO DOOR TO THE PRINTED BILL - the two row-action controls exist only inside the desktop table, which is display:none below 768px. Measured in a browser 2026-09-11: at 1280 each row carries View and Print as 32x32 anchors pointing at /bills/{n} and /bills/{n}/document; at 390 the table is hidden and BillCard draws month, number, period, amount, status and Pay - and nothing at all pointing at /document. A customer on the device the portal is designed for first (skill SKILL.md: 390 is THE DESIGN TARGET) cannot reach the document their landlord asked for from the list; the only remaining path is two taps deeper, through the bill's own page. The same controls carry no visible word at either width - aria-label and title only - which the blueprint's own standard A forbids for the portal because a phone has no hover.
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/bills/Bills.tsx - BillCard (390) against the PortalListTable icons (>=768)
introduced_in: CR-085 (c) redraw of CWP-027
escape_reason: Bills.dom.test.tsx asserts the print door by ADDRESS, which is exactly right - and jsdom has no viewport, so the desktop branch and the card branch both render and the assertion passes over a control no phone can see. A door tested at one width is not a door at both.
prevention: Where a screen renders two layouts from one source, assert each door inside the branch that owns it - and when a branch drops a control, either the other branch carries it or the drop is written down as a decision.

title: CWP-029's DOCUMENT PREVIEW IS 165 PIXELS WIDE ON A PHONE - a letter-size bill rendered at about a fifth of the width the drawing gives it, on the device the portal is designed for first. Measured with getBoundingClientRect 2026-09-11: the object is 605x783 inside a 1026px column at 1280, and 165x213 inside a 316px column at 390. DocumentPreview hardcodes w-[62%] with no responsive step, so the sixty-two per cent that leaves margin on a desk leaves an unreadable thumbnail on a phone - and the drawing's phone frame gives the document the page. The same component also carries three arbitrary Tailwind values the skill's never-do list forbids by name: w-[62%], aspect-[8.5/11] and bg-[white].
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/components/primitives.tsx DocumentPreview - w-[62%]
introduced_in: DEF-CWP-3983's fix
escape_reason: PrintedBill.dom.test.tsx asserts the object exists and points at ?view=1, which is the right assertion and says nothing about its rendered size; jsdom has no layout, so no unit test can measure a percentage width. The defect it was fixing was the preview's ABSENCE, and a present preview reads as a finished one.
prevention: A percentage width on a fixed-aspect box needs a width breakpoint, not one number - and any component whose whole job is to be READ should be measured in pixels at 390 in the same walk that proves it exists.

title: A REFUSAL ON A CommitButton IS RENDERED AS A title= TOOLTIP AND NOTHING ELSE, SO ON A PHONE THE PAY BUTTON IS DEAD AND SILENT. Measured in a browser: on /pay the disabled control carries title='Fill in both boxes first.', aria-label null, aria-describedby null, and that sentence appears NOWHERE in the page text. On /pay-now with held_reason no_payment_provider_connected, and again with account_is_cash_only, the whole rendered body contains no refusal at all - a disabled 'Pay $191.00' over a consequence box still promising the payment. A title tooltip needs a mouse and a second of hover; the customer portal's design target is 390px, where it does not exist, and it is not an accessible name either. HeldButton, 1,080 lines up in the same file, renders the identical kind of sentence as a visible span - which is why /autopay says 'We cannot draft payments yet' out loud while the screen that takes the money says nothing. CR-068 R3 and BR-CWP-056 both require a control that may not be used to be VISIBLE, DISABLED and CARRYING ITS REASON; the third clause is unmet everywhere CommitButton is used. THIS IS THE STANDING CAUSE OF DEF-CWP-4152, which is therefore still true as a user-visible fact rather than fixed.
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/components/primitives.tsx CommitButton - and through it CWP-038 /pay-now, CWP-002 /pay, CWP-003 /pay/check, CWP-039 /payment-methods
introduced_in: CR-068 phase 5 - CommitButton has rendered its reason as title= since it was written
escape_reason: Nothing asks whether a refusal is SEEN. G32 asks only that a message_key RESOLVES, and this one always did - the sentence is computed correctly by heldSentence() and handed to the component, which then puts it somewhere a phone cannot show. Every DOM test passes because the string IS in the DOM, as an attribute. tsc passes, eslint passes, and PayNow.dom.test.tsx asserts the reason through the wrapper exactly as its own comment says it does - reading the attribute. The blueprint's own R-01 states the general rule and states the reason ('a phone has no hover'), for icons, and nobody carried it to tooltips.
prevention: One component, one change: CommitButton should render its reason the way HeldButton already does - a visible span under the control - so the kit has ONE answer to 'this cannot be pressed and here is why'. Then assert it as rendered TEXT, not as an attribute: expect(screen.getByText(reason)) rather than toHaveAttribute('title'). The general habit: when two components in one kit answer the same question two ways, one of them is wrong, and the one that is wrong is the one no phone can read.

title: CWP-038 GOES ON PROMISING THE PAYMENT OVER A BUTTON THAT CANNOT BE PRESSED. With can_pay false and held_reason no_payment_provider_connected, the rendered screen reads 'WHAT THIS WILL DO / Takes $191.00 from Bank account ....4417. / Clears bill BL-2608-0141 in full. / Emails you a receipt. / A payment cannot be changed afterwards, only reversed.' above a disabled Pay button. Reproduced again with account_is_cash_only. The box is drawn on 'panel !== null' alone and never asks whether the payment can happen - the preview prices an allocation whether or not the tenant has a processor. Read with DEF-CWP-4851 (the refusal is invisible) the screen a cash-only customer meets is a confident four-line promise, a dead button, and no explanation anywhere on the page. Blueprint section 06 screen 35 is explicit that this button 'is the last thing read before money moves'.
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/payments/PayNow.tsx - the WHAT THIS WILL DO consequence box on CWP-038
introduced_in: CR-068 phase 5 wave, PayNow.tsx - the box has been gated on panel!==null since it was written
escape_reason: The box and the button are two components with two correct-looking conditions and no test asks about their COMBINATION. PayNow.dom.test.tsx exercises the held case and asserts the Pay control; it does not assert what else the screen is saying at that moment. A screenshot would show it instantly and nothing in this repo reads rendered output.
prevention: Gate the consequence box on the same fact as the commit - if the payment cannot be made, the screen should not describe it happening. And the general form: when a screen has a REFUSAL state, walk the whole rendered body in that state rather than the one control the refusal is attached to; the fault is usually what the rest of the page is still saying.

title: A DECLINED OR REFUSED PAYMENT ON CWP-038 IS A DEAD END: THE SCREEN RENDERS ZERO CONTROLS. Measured in a browser at both widths - outcome 'declined' gives controls []; outcome 'refused' gives controls []. The page says 'Your payment was declined / DECLINED / No money was taken. Try another card or bank account.' and offers no way to do either: no Back, no retry, no door to /payment-methods, and the form the customer filled in is gone. 'Try again' is rendered for no_answer ONLY. A refusal that names an action is a promise the action is reachable, and this one names two that are not - the exact shape DEF-CWP-3972 was filed for one control over, on the outcome a real acquirer produces most often. Blueprint section 06 screen 35's DECLINED state is explicit and says the opposite: 'Says the bank declined it and what to try; the amount and method stay selected.'
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/payments/PayNow.tsx Confirmation() - CWP-038's declined and refused outcomes
introduced_in: CR-068 phase 5 wave, PayNow.tsx Confirmation()
escape_reason: Each outcome was tested for the SENTENCE it renders and not for whether the person can get anywhere from it. The three outcome strings are individually correct and were individually asserted. Nothing in this repo asks 'how does a user leave this state' - the doors work is about a screen's inbound link and there is no equivalent question for an outbound one.
prevention: Confirmation() should offer 'Try again' on declined too - it returns to the form with the amount and the method kept, which is what the drawing asks for - and a door to /payment-methods, which is where 'try another card' happens. And write the check as a floor rather than as a string: every terminal state of a money flow renders at least one control.

title: CWP-038 KEEPS THE COMMIT LIVE WHILE THE PRICED PANEL BESIDE IT DESCRIBES A DIFFERENT PAYMENT. Type into 'Another amount' and the button relabels immediately - it is computed locally from the typed string - while 'panel' still holds the PREVIOUS preview, because the effect clears it only when the amount is unpriceable, and 'ready' is gated on 'panel !== null'. Seen on screen at one instant: button 'Pay $40.00', WHAT THIS WILL DO 'Takes $191.00 ... Clears bill BL-2608-0141 in full', rail PAYING $191.00 / LEFT OWING $0.00, total 'You are paying $191.00'. The window is at least PRICE_AFTER_MS (250ms) plus a round trip, on every keystroke. Two consequences: (a) the one figure the customer reads before money moves disagrees with the allocation BR-CWP-058 exists to show them, and the file's own docstring says 'NOT ONE FIGURE ON THIS SCREEN IS COMPUTED HERE' - the button label is the exception; (b) a press inside the window sends the new amount with the PREVIOUS amount's idempotency_key, which is the string hard rule 6 and US-CWP-045 TC-7 make load-bearing.
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/payments/PayNow.tsx - the preview effect and the commit button's label, CWP-038
introduced_in: CR-068 phase 5 wave, PayNow.tsx - the debounced preview effect
escape_reason: A unit test sets state and asserts the settled render; it cannot see a 250ms window. The walkthrough that found it was stubbing the preview, so the disagreement persisted long enough to photograph - on a real server it corrects itself after a round trip, which is exactly why nobody has seen it. The mechanism is in the source and was confirmed there: the effect's cleanup clears the timer, never the panel.
prevention: Clear the panel when the priced amount changes, so the commit is not ready until the server has priced what the button says - the screen already has a 'Working out where it goes.' sentence for that state. Re-mint or re-confirm the key when the amount changes. General form: when a button's label is computed locally and the panel beside it is served, they can disagree, and the money path is the place that costs.

title: CWP-040's NEXT FEW PRINTS A RAW ISO DATE TO A CUSTOMER - '2026-08-22' - ON THE ONE SCREEN THAT SAYS WHEN MONEY WILL LEAVE THEIR ACCOUNT. Two clicks away /payments renders 08/13/2026 and /payment-methods renders 06/02/2026, both in the tenant's own MM/DD/YYYY through usePortalDate(); this table interpolates slot.scheduled_on straight into the cell. It is DEF-CWP-4197's family exactly - the fourth screen to be found doing it - and DEF-CWP-4131's own prevention note says 'grep every sibling screen that renders the same KIND of value'. The grep was of wave Q, then of the guest screens; /autopay was in neither. The consequence is not cosmetic on this screen: the drawing's whole point is that a customer reads the date a draft will be taken before agreeing to it, and an ISO string is the format nobody in North America reads a bank date in.
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/methods/Autopay.tsx - the NEXT FEW table's DATE column, CWP-040
introduced_in: CR-068 phase 5 wave, Autopay.tsx NEXT FEW table - never in DEF-CWP-4197's grep
escape_reason: Autopay.dom.test.tsx asserts the row exists and what its state chip says; it does not assert the date's SHAPE, and a test that rendered the component outside the date provider would pass either way. Nothing greps for an ISO literal reaching a customer, and the two previous sweeps were scoped to the wave that was being worked on rather than to the fact.
prevention: Render it through usePortalDate() like every sibling table. Then make the sweep a check rather than a habit: a walkthrough assertion that no customer-facing cell matches /\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}/ would have caught all four occurrences and will catch the fifth.

title: CWP-040's 'How much' HELPER OFFERS A CEILING THE PRODUCT DOES NOT HAVE: 'Or set a ceiling and we will ring you above it.' There is no ceiling control anywhere on the screen and there is no column behind one - PortalAutopay.ceiling's own type comment reads 'Always null: accounts has no column for a ceiling'. So the sentence tells a customer they can protect themselves from an unexpectedly large draft and then offers no way to. Blueprint section 06 screen 40 draws 'Never take more than' as a real select with its own explanation ('A limit protects you from an unexpectedly large bill - anything above it waits for you'); the product has neither the control nor the column, and its copy says otherwise. Hard-won law 1 in customer-facing prose - a sentence claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee. Two honest fixes and they are different products: cut the sentence, or build the ceiling.
surface: 07-frontend/src/portal/methods/Autopay.tsx - the How much helper, and portal.autopay.howMuchHelper in all eleven catalogues
introduced_in: CR-068 phase 5 wave, portal.autopay.howMuchHelper
escape_reason: A catalogue key is checked for existing in eleven files and for resolving; nothing asks whether the sentence is TRUE. The key was written alongside a drawing that HAS the control, which is how the wording arrived before the capability - and the capability was then correctly not built, because there is no column, leaving the wording behind. G32's blind spot in one line: a refusal or a helper that resolves is not a refusal or a helper that is true.
prevention: Cut the clause until the column exists, and keep the rest ('The whole balance on each bill'). More generally: when a drawing's control is deliberately not built, grep the catalogue for the words that described it - the helper text is where a cut control leaves its ghost.

title: THE PORTAL'S FIELD ANATOMY IS 4 / 17 / 12 AGAINST B14 RULE 39's RATIFIED 5 / 6 / 20, AND THE RHYTHM IS INVERTED: THE HELPER SITS FURTHER FROM ITS OWN INPUT THAN ITS FIELD SITS FROM THE NEXT ONE. Measured with getComputedStyle on /pay and on /payment-methods's add form, both widths: label to input 4px (FormField's gap-1); input to helper 17px; field block to next field 12px on /pay and 16px on the add form. title: THIRTY-SIX ARBITRARY SPACING VALUES ARE WRITTEN INTO THE FRONT END IN TAILWIND BRACKETS, AND THEY INCLUDE ALL FOUR NUMBERS B14 RULE 39 BANS BY NAME. Counted over every non-test .tsx in 07-frontend/src for a padding, margin or gap utility carrying a bracketed value: 36 occurrences. py-[3px] x11, gap-[2px] x6, py-[7px] x4, pl-[18px] x3, gap-[5px] x3, px-[9px] x2, gap-[18px] x2, pb-[18px] x2, and one each of px-[14.4px], gap-[0.4rem] and mt-[0.35rem]. Rule 39: 'NO AD-HOC 3 / 7 / 9 / 14 ANYWHERE' - 3, 7, 9 and 14 are all four present, and px-[14.4px] is a FRACTIONAL pixel, which no scale of any kind can contain. Four of the 36 are in the customer portal (gap-[2px] twice in primitives.tsx, px-[9px] py-[3px] in PortalScreenIdTag.tsx, which renders on EVERY portal screen); the other 32 are the staff app. The skill file's own never-do list names this exact shape first: 'Arbitrary values - mt-[13px], w-[347px], text-[15px]. Use the scale.' NOTE ON THE COUNT, because this row is also a correction: this lane first reported ZERO arbitrary values in the portal. The regex ended in \b immediately after the closing bracket, and \b cannot hold between ] and a space, so the check returned 0 truthfully over everything it could see. A sibling lane naming px-[9px] in its own findings is what exposed it.
surface: frontend
introduced_in: across many waves; no single one chose it
escape_reason: B14 rule 21 is enforced for whether a file may use Tailwind at all and nothing checks WHICH utility it then writes. An arbitrary value compiles, renders exactly as typed and passes every assertion, so it is only ever visible to somebody counting - and nobody was counting until rule 39 was ratified.

reported_by: CR-085 step 2 lane 8, self-reported the minute it was noticed
title: pkill -f MATCHES THE SHELL THAT IS RUNNING IT, SO A LANE TIDYING UP ITS OWN BUILD KILLED ITS OWN COMMAND AND EVERY SIBLING'S BUILD WITH IT. On 2026-09-11 at ~09:28 a lane ran a compound background command that began 'pkill -f "vite build"' to drop its own stale bundle before rebuilding. -f matches against the FULL COMMAND LINE, and the command line of the bash process running the compound command CONTAINS the string 'vite build' - so it killed itself (exit 144, SIGKILL) before the tsc and vitest runs that followed it in the same chain, which is how it was noticed: the redirect target /tmp/claude-0/tsc.txt was never even created. What made it worth filing rather than shrugging at is the OTHER half: six sibling lanes share this container, and a pattern-matched kill cannot tell a sibling's vite build from the author's own. No work is lost - a killed build re-runs - but a sibling watching a build die for no reason has no way to know why, and the container was at load 168 where a rebuild is twenty minutes.
surface: the shared container; any lane's own shell commands
introduced_in: the lane's own command, not a repo change
escape_reason: CLAUDE.md's instruction to lanes names the shared STACK - do not restart, re-seed or pkill it - and reads as being about the running demo rather than about pattern-matched kills in general, which is exactly the shape hard-won law 11 records for the git stash ban: the rule is read as being about the obvious case and the dangerous use is an incidental tidy-up where the rule never comes to mind. Nothing mechanical can see it: a pkill that works and a pkill that kills a sibling look identical from the author's side.
prevention: Never pattern-kill in a shared container. Kill by PID from a job you started ('kill $!' or the background task id), or simply let the stale process finish - a build you no longer want costs nothing but time. If a pattern really is the only way, exclude your own process ('pkill -f PATTERN' can never do that safely) and say in the report which siblings may have been hit.

reported_by: Product Owner, asking what five background tasks were
title: pgrep -f MATCHES THE SHELL RUNNING IT, so 'until ! pgrep -f X' never exits: four waiters spent 40 minutes waiting for themselves
surface: background waiters launched from the working session (no repo file)
found_in: The PO asked what the five running background tasks were. Load average 0.00, and neither awaited job existed: ps showed no g18 gate and no lane-4 walkthrough running. pgrep -f 'node 10-scripts/cr085_lane4_home_walkthrough' returned 29272 and 30900 — THE TWO WAITERS THEMSELVES; pgrep -f 'g18_i18n_call_sites' returned 15125 and 15664, likewise.
introduced_in: not a repo commit — a shell pattern used ad hoc by a lane and by the merge lane
escape_reason: pgrep -f matches the FULL COMMAND LINE of every process, and the waiting shell's own command line CONTAINS the pattern because the pattern is written inside its until-loop. pgrep excludes only itself, never its parent shell. So 'until ! pgrep -f X; do sleep; done' is satisfied only when the shell asking the question stops existing — it waits for its own death. Nothing can see it: the loop is not an error, the exit code is never produced, the task simply stays 'Running' forever, and load average reads 0.00 while five tasks appear busy. THIS IS THE MIRROR OF DEF-GOV-4933, filed by another lane the same day: there 'pkill -f' matched the shell running it and killed itself plus every sibling's build. Same root cause, opposite symptom — one kills itself, the other can never finish. A fifth waiter died differently and is worth naming with them: it waited for the words 'checks passed' in a log whose run had crashed, so the phrase it wanted could never be written.
prevention: Never write a readiness check whose pattern appears in its own command line. Wait on a PID captured at launch ('while kill -0 $PID 2>/dev/null'), or on a SENTINEL the job writes when it ends ('EXIT=' appended by the job itself) — and pair any 'wait for a phrase' with a 'wait for the job to have stopped', because a crashed run writes a stack trace and never the phrase. If pgrep must be used, exclude self and parents: pgrep -f X | grep -vE "^($$|$PPID)$". Any waiter older than its job's plausible runtime is this bug until proved otherwise.
