title: CLAUDE.md's one-line summary of B14 rule 33 names a kind the rule does not have, gives one cap where there are five, and drops the zero-words clause
surface: CLAUDE.md · 04-docs/02-decisions/14-ui-conventions.md rule 33
found_in: CR-092 step 1 lane 1 self-reported citing B14 rule 32 where rule 33 is stricter, saying it had read CLAUDE.md's summary instead of the rule; verified against B14's own row by the coordinator
introduced_in: the summary as first written, 2026-08-30
escape_reason: CLAUDE.md is the file every session reads first and B14 is the authority it points at, so a paraphrase in the pointer is what most lanes actually apply. This one said 'a refusal sentence caps at five or six words'. Rule 33 has no kind called a refusal; it names FIVE kinds with FIVE caps (label 3 words, fact 6, instruction 6 PER SENTENCE, consequence 6 per sentence at most two, rationale ZERO), and the rationale clause is the one governing helper text that explains WHY - the commonest breach on the screens this CR is auditing. Nothing checks a pointer against the document it points at. SECOND such defect in CLAUDE.md found today after DEF-4952's rule COUNT: same root cause, different shapes - one quoted a maximum as a total, this paraphrased a five-part rule into one narrower clause.
prevention: A pointer to a rule carries the rule's ID and where to read it, never a restatement of what it says - a restatement is a second copy that drifts, which is law 5's one-generated-file-committed-once applied to prose. Where a summary is genuinely useful it must say it is lossy and name what it omits.

title: A SECOND FILE CARRIES THE FALSE 'GET /settings/services is System-Admin-only' CLAIM, AND IT IS THE FILE A LANE WOULD EDIT. title: The field-anatomy instrument exits 0 whether the rule is met or broken, and the coordinator's briefing told a lane to use it as its red proof
surface: 10-scripts/render-checks/cr092-lane3-field-anatomy.mjs
found_in: CR-092 step 2 wave A, self-reported: it ran the instrument against the fully-broken pre-fix tree and got exit 0, then against the fixed tree and got exit 0. Its exit code asserts only that every screen yielded fields; the verdict block is the real output.
introduced_in: the instrument as first written, CR-092 step 1 lane 3
escape_reason: The instrument measures 29 fields across five screens in a real browser and prints a correct verdict - the MEASUREMENT is sound and was the most valuable thing step 1 produced. What does not work is its exit code, which cannot distinguish a tree where 0 of 18 fields obey the rule from one where 18 of 18 do. Law 7's third habit says a check's output must distinguish pass from fail TO A READER, not merely to an exit code; here it is the reverse, and the exit code is the half a script reads. It matters because the coordinator's wave A briefing named this instrument as the lane's red proof AND its green proof, so a lane wiring it into CI or a land script would have shipped a guard that can never fail. The same shape is live one layer up: run_gates.py prints MERGE BLOCKED and a background wrapper around it still reports success.
prevention: An instrument that prints a verdict must exit non-zero on a failing verdict, or it is a report and must not be called a check - and a briefing must not name a report as a proof. Where a tool is used both ways, say which output is authoritative in its own docstring.

surface: frontend
found_in: ce623f444 (v2.237.1), read in source and confirmed against the tenant's asset_types catalog 2026-09-12
introduced_in: the string as written — git log -S 'typeEditHelp' shows it has always claimed the tab move
escape_reason: Nothing compares a helper SENTENCE with what the control beside it can actually do. G32 resolves message keys, G15 checks catalogue parity, tsc and eslint see a string, and every toContain assertion passes over any words at all. The sentence is also true-sounding and domain-plausible, which is the worst combination: a reviewer reading AssetRegistryPage.tsx has no reason to go and check what typesForTab returns. And it was invisible in the product for a second reason on top of the first — the control it describes did nothing, so no clerk could ever have discovered the promise was false.
prevention: The generalisable check is a source one and it is cheap: where a helper sentence names an OUTCOME ('moves', 'closes', 'recomputes', 'cannot be'), the same file must hold the code that produces it. Narrower and immediately writable: a DOM case that opens the edit dialog on each of the three tabs and asserts every option's category equals the tab — which is the fact that makes the sentence false — so the day somebody widens typesForTab the sentence becomes true and the case says so.

reported_by: CR-092-BRC01 step 2 lane 4 (the four actions), measuring the five date inputs in Chromium at 1440 and 1280 against a private stack after fixing DEF-MET-4974's bounds
title: THREE ASSET SCREENS PROPOSE NO DATE AT ALL AGAINST BR-PAY-033, BECAUSE App.tsx MOUNTS ALL THREE WITH NO PROPS AND THE PREFILL COMES FROM ONE — AND THE SAME ABSENCE SILENTLY VOIDED A DATE BOUND THAT PASSED ITS OWN UNIT TEST. BR-PAY-033 (refined PO 2026-08-09) says 'the UI ALWAYS proposes a pre-filled default date', and DatePickerField honours it faithfully for whatever its consumer passes as prefill. AssetReassignPage, AssetLogMaintenancePage and AssetRetireWizard each read today from props.pageProps.today; App.tsx:995, :996 and :1007 mount all three as <AssetReassignPage />, <AssetLogMaintenancePage /> and <AssetRetireWizard /> with NO PROPS AT ALL, so today was the empty string, prefill was undefined, and every one of those three date inputs rendered value='' in the shipped product. Measured in Chromium at 1440 and 1280 on pine-hill asset E-5000: effective_date value='', date value='', retire_date value=''. THE SHARPER HALF IS HOW IT WAS FOUND: this lane added max={today} to the log-repair date for DEF-MET-4974, its unit test went green, and the browser measured max=null - because the TEST passes today='2026-08-16' explicitly and the ROUTER passes nothing. A green suite and a browser that disagreed, over a prop that does not exist at runtime. That is CLAUDE.md hard-won law 2 exactly: a component with an optional prop that nothing passes is dead UI. FIXED IN THIS COMMIT: components/DateCell.tsx gains todayInZone(timeZone), and the three pages read props.pageProps.today ?? todayInZone(timeZone). The TENANT's zone and not UTC on purpose - billingOpsShared's todayIso() slices an ISO instant, which is right for the write it stamps and wrong for a max of 'not in the future', where a tenant behind UTC would be refused their own today for several hours every evening. useRegional already resolves the tenant zone on all three screens (IS-8).
surface: 07-frontend/src/App.tsx:995,996,1007 (the three mounts, no props) · 07-frontend/src/features/assets/AssetFlowPages.tsx (both pages' today) · AssetRetireWizard.tsx (retire's) · 07-frontend/src/components/DateCell.tsx (todayInZone, added here)
introduced_in: CR-028 AST-W4 (2026-08-22) - the three screens became full-page routes and the today prop, which a modal's host used to pass, stopped being passed by anything
escape_reason: EVERY UNIT TEST PASSES THE PROP THE ROUTER DOES NOT, SO THE FIXTURE COULD NOT TELL A WIRED SCREEN FROM AN UNWIRED ONE. All 34 cases in AssetLifecycle.test.tsx render these pages with today='2026-08-16', which is the fixture supplying what App.tsx omits - the same shape as mounting a routed component outside its real path pattern (hard-won law 2's fixture clause). G13 asks whether a prop is PASSED to a component that declares it, and today IS declared and IS optional, so an absent optional prop is exactly what G13 tolerates by design. tsc cannot see it: props.pageProps.today ?? '' is valid TypeScript whether anything passes it or not. And nothing in this repository reads rendered output, so 'does this date field propose a date' has never been asked of any screen. It was found only by measuring the browser after a green test claimed a bound that was not there.
prevention: FIXED HERE, and the durable guard is the test that now exists beside it: AssetLifecycle.test.tsx asserts the bound AND the prefill on a page rendered WITHOUT the today prop, which is the way App.tsx mounts it - proved red against the old code and green after. THE GENERAL SHAPE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE ROW: a fixture that supplies a prop the router does not is indistinguishable from a wired screen to every check this repo owns, so a screen's test should mount it the way the ROUTER does at least once. A mechanical version is reachable and narrow: for every element of App.tsx's route table, compare the props passed at the mount against the component's own optional props, and report the ones nothing ever passes - source-readable, no browser needed.

title: NFR-3 - THE THREE LISTS INSIDE AN ASSET ANSWER THE WHOLE HISTORY AND TAKE NO PAGE PARAMETER, AND THE MAINTENANCE ONE IS IN NO REGISTER ROW AT ALL. DEF-MET-4968 files the FRONT half of this - the three tabs are hand-built tables with no pager - and its own sequencing note says adopting DataTable before the endpoints carry an envelope would recreate inside the asset the honest-envelope-over-unbounded-query shape DEF-MET-4951 filed on the registry. DEF-MET-4962 files the REGISTRY reads. Nothing filed the three server endpoints themselves, so the work-order list beside them is paged and these three are not - one asset detail screen, two conventions.
surface: 06-backend/apps/assets/api.py asset_reads, asset_assignments and asset_maintenance (no parse_list_params, no paginator, a bare list or a bare rows key) with 06-backend/apps/assets/selectors.py asset_reads at 1095, assignments at 1001 and maintenance at 1044 (each materialises the whole set with list(...)). Screens S50 Reads, Assignment history and Work and maintenance
found_in: MEASURED with CaptureQueriesContext against real PostgreSQL on the seeded estate, 2026-09-12. Query counts are FINE - two to four each, wave B batched the name and unit lookups - and that is exactly why nothing sees it: the cost is the PAYLOAD and it grows one row at a time with the history. pine-hill meter with 26 reads answers 7,013 bytes, which is 292 bytes per folded row and no upper bound; a quarter-hourly interval meter reaches a page of fifty in half a day and 35,000 rows in a year. The largest asset_maintenance history on any tenant is 2 rows and the largest assignment history is 1, so no screen anybody has opened has ever shown the shape.

escape_reason: NFR-3 is named by no gate in this repository. G114 polices the SHAPE of a paged envelope and never asks whether an endpoint has one; DRF registers StandardPagination as the default pagination class, so an endpoint that simply never calls the paginator is silently exempt and looks identical to one that does not need paging. And the fixture hides it in the one direction that matters: every asset on every seeded tenant has one assignment row, at most two maintenance rows and at most 26 reads, so a page of fifty is the whole list on every row anybody has ever looked at. The same premise failure as DEF-PAY-4221 - the correctness argument was the old ideal customer profile, written in prose, and the sentence changed somewhere else.

prevention: A check that enumerates every list-shaped route and fails one whose view never reaches the paginator - the same enumeration NFR-3 needs and no gate performs. Short of that, a per-endpoint case asserting the response carries count and results and that page 2 differs from page 1, over a fixture seeded past the page boundary rather than at the size of a demo tenant.

title: A PYTHON ASSERTION INSIDE A BASH PUSH SCRIPT FIRED, PRINTED ITS TRACEBACK, AND THE SCRIPT PUSHED ANYWAY - SO A DUPLICATE REGISTER ROW REACHED THE BRANCH UNDER A NUMSTAT THAT READ 1 0. Self-reported by CR-094-BRC01 step 1 lane 4 on 2026-09-12. The rebuild followed law 11 exactly: re-pin the tip, rebuild the blob as the tip's bytes plus one appended line, prove the prefix byte-identical, check for duplicate ids, hash, commit-tree, push. The duplicate check was a 'python3 -c' with an assert, under 'set -e'. It FIRED - AssertionError printed, exit 1 - and bash carried straight on to git commit-tree and git push. DEF-CUS-5079 landed twice, byte-identical (1,925 bytes each), because a sibling's pathspec commit had already carried the lane's uncommitted row onto the branch while the blob was being built. Every check law 11 prescribes passed on it and each was TRUE: file count 1, own hunk present, prefix byte-identical to the tip, and 'git diff --numstat' printing exactly '1 0' - one line added, none deleted. The arithmetic was right and the content was a duplicate. Fixed the same minute by pushing the tip's bytes with the FINAL line removed, proved a strict prefix; the register now holds no duplicate id anywhere.
surface: the lane's own ad-hoc rebuild shell, not a committed script; the pattern is any 'set -e' bash that runs a python assertion as a statement rather than testing its status. 12-governance/10-defect-log.csv was the casualty
found_in: CR-094-BRC01 step 1 lane 4, reading its own pushed register back before declaring done
introduced_in: the lane's own rebuild shell, 2026-09-12
escape_reason: 'set -e' does not abort on a failing command in every position bash allows, and the failure is SILENT-ADJACENT rather than silent: the traceback scrolls past between a 'PREFIX BYTE-IDENTICAL' line and a 'pushed <sha>' line, both of which read as success. This is law 7's 'incapable of failing' shape wearing a passing costume, and it defeats the whole of law 11 because law 11's checks all ask what a commit CONTAINS and none asks whether the content is already there.
prevention: Make the duplicate check the thing that produces the blob, not a step beside it - a script that cannot emit a file with a duplicate id cannot push one. Failing that, run the check as its own command and test its exit status explicitly ('python3 ... || exit 1'), because 'set -e' is not a guarantee you can lean on. And the durable form: 10-scripts/push_paths.sh already refuses a VANISHED register line (DEF-2837); a DUPLICATED id is the same guard in the other direction and belongs in push_register_guard.py, where the next lane inherits it instead of remembering it.

title: THE ENDING-SERVICE WALKTHROUGH'S STEP-RAIL READER MATCHED NOTHING — MEASUREMENT #1 OF THE FIVE ITS OWN HEADER CLAIMS HAS NEVER ONCE FIRED, AND A WHOLE AUDIT WAS SIGNED OVER IT

escape_reason: The selector was [class*='step'], ol li, nav ol li. WizardFrame renders the rail as <nav data-wizard='rail'><button data-wizard-step='1'> — no ol, no li, and every class a Tailwind utility, so not one of the three alternatives could ever match. Proved by measuring both selectors against the same live DOM in one evaluate, so the numbers cannot be attributed to a page that had not loaded. The general habit, and it is the one this cost: when an instrument reports an ABSENCE, check that it can report a PRESENCE — run it against a screen you know has the thing. title: push_paths guards the TIP moving and not the WORKING TREE moving between re-derivation and hashing
surface: 10-scripts/push_paths.sh step 2 · 10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py · 07-frontend/src/i18n/locales/*.json · commit 2544d531f
found_in: CR-094-BRC01 wave M (Send statement), 2026-09-13
introduced_in: push_paths.sh, CR-056
escape_reason: Law 11's re-derivation protects the blob against a stale BASE: read the tip's bytes, re-apply your edits, push. It says nothing about the interval between that re-read and the hash. In a tree eight lanes share, a sibling running i18n_fanin in that window rewrites all eleven catalogues in place, and push_paths then hashes the WORKING-TREE bytes, which now hold their fifteen keys as well as my four. push_paths step 2 cannot see it: it compares base to tip, and the tip never moved for these paths. Every other check in law 11 passes as well - zero deletions, my own keys present, the right file count. The only thing that caught it was reading the numstat AS ARITHMETIC (19 insertions for 4 keys) and then reading the hunks, which is the check DEF-182 added for exactly this shape.
prevention: push_paths could digest each named path when the run begins and again immediately before hashing, refusing when one changed underneath it - that narrows the window from minutes to milliseconds. Available today with no tooling change: for any file owned by a generator, run the generator LAST, immediately before the push, instead of re-deriving early and pushing later.

title: A sibling's whole-file locale write subtracted eight refusal keys that had already been faned in, and the only thing that saw it was a refusal-key guard ten minutes into a test run
surface: 07-frontend/src/i18n/locales/*.json (all eleven)
introduced_in: 2026-09-13, between the BR-CUS-1054 lane's two i18n_fanin runs
escape_reason: Nothing watches a catalogue for a key that LEAVES. i18n_fanin guarantees parity and refuses a silent overwrite, and both held: the eleven files stayed the same size as each other and no value was reworded — eight keys were simply absent again, so G15's parity check and G32's resolve check were both TRUE of a catalogue that had lost them. The loss stayed invisible until a service RAISED one of the eight and core.refusal_catalogue.assert_resolves fired, fifteen tests at a time, ten minutes into a pytest run. Had the lane not raised those refusals in its own tests, the keys would have reached the branch missing and a clerk would have met a refusal as silence.
prevention: Two, and the first is the cheap one. (1) RE-DERIVE A CATALOGUE FROM THE PINNED TIP AT PUSH TIME rather than pushing the working-tree copy — that is what saved these eight: the push blob was rebuilt as tip plus this lane's keys, so all eight are on the branch even though the shared tree had lost them. (2) The durable fix is a check that reads a catalogue for a key that DISAPPEARED between two commits, the way push_register_guard.py already refuses a VANISHED register line — parity and resolvability are both blind to a key that left every catalogue at once.

title: REDERIVED_FROM_TIP=1 turns off push_paths' only staleness guard for EVERY named path, and a lane that re-derived three of twelve reverted two rule rows and tripled its own CHANGELOG entry
surface: 10-scripts/push_paths.sh (step 1b) · 04-docs/05-modules/03-customers/02-business-rules.md · CHANGELOG.md
introduced_in: 10-scripts/push_paths.sh step 1b, DEF-GOV-4061 (2026-09-05) — the escape hatch arrived with the base-is-the-tip refusal it exists to unlock
escape_reason: The flag is ALL-OR-NOTHING and the assertion it stands for is PER-PATH. A lane re-derived the three files it knew every lane appends to (decision log, review ledger, CHANGELOG), correctly, then passed REDERIVED_FROM_TIP=1 for a push naming TWELVE paths - which switched the moved-path refusal off for the other nine as well. One of those nine, the customers business-rules file, had been edited an hour earlier and never rebuilt, so wave M's BUILT amendments to BR-CUS-036 (2872 bytes down to 1998) and BR-CUS-1052 (3537 down to 1535) left the branch by subtraction. push_paths says in its own words that the closing numstat is then the only proof; it printed 5 insertions and 5 deletions, which is exactly what THREE edited rows look like if nobody counts them. The push_register_guard covers registers, not rule tables. Separately the re-derivation script appended the author's own block twice per run - 'the tip, plus any block the working copy has that the tip lacks, plus my block' counts the author's own block under both of the last two clauses - so a CHANGELOG entry landed three times, and no check compares a rebuilt file against itself for duplicated sections.
prevention: Make the assertion per-path rather than per-push: REDERIVED_FROM_TIP should NAME the paths it covers and push_paths should keep the moved-path refusal on for every path not named. Free and immediate, and both faults were visible in it: read the closing numstat AS ARITHMETIC - three edited rows are 3 and 3, never 5 and 5 - and before pushing a rebuilt file assert that no section heading appears in it more often than in the source.

title: Two lanes shipped 2.246.0, and the CHANGELOG then published one version number against two different products
surface: CHANGELOG.md · 07-frontend/package.json · 07-frontend/package-lock.json · 06-backend/pyproject.toml
introduced_in: 2026-09-13, while the BR-CUS-1054 and the adjustments lanes were both bumping
escape_reason: A version IS allocated from the remote and BOTH lanes did that correctly — the arithmetic was never wrong. What is wrong is that a version, unlike a defect id, is CLAIMED in three tracked files, and a lane claims it by editing the shared working tree long before it pushes. allocate.py asks every remote branch and says so in its own output: 'still free on every branch (this tree not counted)'. The one place the number was already taken is the one place it does not look, and in a tree eight lanes share that is the common case rather than the rare one. It answered '2.246.0 free' while 07-frontend/package.json in that same tree already read 2.246.0. The second half is worse and is what reached the branch: the superseded CHANGELOG heading was written into the shared tree as 2.246.0, and a sibling's whole-file commit of CHANGELOG.md published it before the renumber — DEF-168 mechanism five — so the collision outlived the moment it was caught. Nothing anywhere reads CHANGELOG.md for a repeated heading, so the branch carried two '## [2.246.0]' blocks describing two different products, which is exactly what step 7 of the change process exists to prevent: a tester reporting a defect says 'which build?' and 2.246.0 answered with two.
prevention: Two, and they are independent. (1) allocate.py version should READ the working tree's three version files as a third source and WARN when the tree already holds the number it is about to hand out — it must still not COUNT the tree (that would make an unpushed bump reserve a number), but staying silent about it is the whole of this defect. It caught the clash twice by --verify and both times only because a human read the line and compared it with package.json by hand. (2) A gate that refuses a repeated '## [x.y.z]' heading in CHANGELOG.md. It is three lines, it is deterministic, and it catches the visible damage whatever caused it — including the case where a sibling's whole-file commit publishes a draft entry that its author is about to renumber.

title: The per-session scratchpad is SHARED between lanes, so two lanes writing msgN.txt cross commit messages — a commit lands describing work it does not contain
surface: the scratchpad directory named in each lane's system prompt (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-SMARTBillHub/<uuid>/scratchpad) + 10-scripts/push_paths.sh's MSG_FILE argument
introduced_in: environmental - present since lanes began sharing one box; first observed 2026-09-13
escape_reason: The scratchpad path carries a session uuid, so every lane is told it is 'session-specific, isolated from the project' and reasonably believes a generic filename there is private. It is not: the directory holds msg1..msg21, msg-a, msg-b and COMMIT/COMMIT2/COMMIT3 written by other lanes on 09-10, 09-11 and 09-12, and msg6/msg7/msg8 appeared during this wave without this lane creating them. push_paths.sh is NOT at fault - it reads the caller's path with commit-tree -F and mktemps its index correctly. Nothing anywhere compares a commit's subject with its contents, so a crossed message is invisible to every check law 11 prescribes: the file count is right, every hunk is the author's, and git diff --numstat is clean.
prevention: Name every message file for its wave, never msgN.txt - e.g. msg-cr094-waveN-4.txt - and read the subject back from the pushed sha before reporting done (git log --format=%s -1 <sha>). Measured cost when it goes wrong: commit c442cbb54 carries this wave's seven record files under another lane's subject about a CHANGELOG deletion, and 37996c2cd carries the customer-edit lane's files under this wave's subject - so the branch history describes two changes that are not in the commits naming them.

title: A backgrounded job that writes a shared register can land AFTER the lane supersedes it, silently reverting the tree
surface: 12-governance/02-decision-log.md · any long-running append run with run_in_background
found_in: CR-094-BRC01 wave M (Send statement), 2026-09-13
introduced_in: shared-tree working practice
escape_reason: An append to the decision log was run in the background and appeared to hang - its safety check was O(n-squared) over a 20k-line register. The lane rewrote it with a set-based check, ran that, pushed, and moved on. The ORIGINAL job then finished and wrote its whole-file copy - old tip plus the entry - over the register. The result was a working copy 285 lines SHORT of the tip with the lane's own later correction reverted, sitting in a tree eight lanes share: the next pathspec commit naming that file would have published the subtraction of 285 lines with a correct file count, its own hunks present, and nothing in the diff to notice. Every check in laws 11 and 12 passes on it because they all read COMMITS and the damage is in what was LEFT BEHIND. Nothing raised it - the branch was correct, so no gate, no test and no push guard had anything to look at. It surfaced only because the task-completion notification arrived and was read as a claim to verify rather than as noise.
prevention: Two things. (1) Never background a write to a shared register - background the READ or the analysis, do the write in the foreground where it is over before the next command runs. (2) When a background job that touches a shared file completes, re-verify that file against the tip before trusting the tree: git diff --numstat <tip> -- <path> must print nothing. A completion notification for a job you superseded is not noise; it is the only signal this failure produces.

title: Two node imports in a TEST file failed the production frontend image, and three lanes each correctly dated the red as not theirs
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/customers/accountActionOverlays.dom.test.tsx · the frontend Docker image
escape_reason: The frontend image runs 'npm run build' = 'tsc --noEmit && vite build', deliberately, so a type error fails the image rather than shipping in it. vitest resolves node: builtins at RUN time and never asks tsc about them, so the test passed everywhere while the build could not complete. The repo has a documented house pattern for exactly this (a string-split dynamic import, used by wizardRailCensus.test.ts and routeBUtilities.test.ts, whose comment says in terms that it keeps tsc happy without an @types/node this tsconfig does not carry) and the new file used plain static imports instead. THE REAL ESCAPE IS OWNERSHIP: tsc DID report it, and at least three separate lanes saw the two errors, ran git log -S, correctly dated them to another lane's commit, and correctly reported them as not theirs. Every one of them followed hard-won law 7's habit exactly. Nobody fixed it, because the lane that introduced it had finished -- so the first person to meet the failure was the Product Owner running docker compose.
prevention: Law 7's habit says read the failures you did not cause and DATE them. That is necessary and it is not sufficient for a red that BLOCKS THE BUILD: a type error is not a suite failure somebody else can own later, it is a broken image, and a red that fails 'npm run build' belongs to whoever next sees it. No gate runs the production build command, which is why tsc's own output was the only signal and it was read three times without being acted on.

reported_by: the Product Owner, deployed build v2.253.0, tenant Ottumwa Water Works: opened GET /integrations/page-policy and got Server Error (500)
title: A crashed page-policy call and a switched-off basemap draw the same grey square and say the same sentence
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/assets/AssetMapTab.tsx:263-267 (tileUrl + policyAnswered) and :562 (the assets.map.noTileHost line)
introduced_in: the DEF-INT-4287 repair itself, 2026-09-06
escape_reason: policyAnswered is computed as 'policy.data !== undefined || policy.isError', so an ERRORED policy call is folded into the answered state; tileUrl is then tileUrlFor(undefined) = null, and the screen renders assets.map.noTileHost, whose meaning is 'the utility switched the basemap off'. A 500 from GET /integrations/page-policy therefore tells a clerk the utility turned the map off. The file's own comment three lines above the render names this exact hazard - 'A tenant who switched the map service off and a product whose tiles are being refused draw the identical grey square, and that is exactly the shape hard-won law 7 warns about' - and the code collapses the two states anyway, which is hard-won law 1: a comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee. Found because the PO opened the endpoint on the deployed build for tenant ottumwa-water-works and got Server Error (500); on this branch the same endpoint answers 200 unauthenticated, 200 authenticated, and 404 for an unknown tenant, so the crash is that deployment's and the misreporting is ours. No test covers the error branch: the map's tests supply a policy that resolves.
prevention: An error state is not a value state. Where a screen degrades on a failed read, the failure must render a DIFFERENT sentence from the legitimate empty, and a test must drive the rejected query - not just the resolved one. The general form: whenever a comment in the file describes two states that must not be confused, that comment is a test case that has not been written yet.

reported_by: Meter Reads step 1, measure lane B, measured on the running stack
title: The read-batch detail returns every row unsliced and is re-fetched after every per-row edit: 20 MB at the cap
surface: GET /read-batches/{id} in 06-backend/apps/metering — read_batch_rows · the stage-3 validate table in UploadReadsWizard.tsx
introduced_in: the read-batch detail read; never given the window that the accounts/ETL runner received
escape_reason: DEF-766 taught the IMPORT runner to serve its reject list as a window - rejects_window {total, offset, limit} on GET /imports/{id}, with ?reject_offset and ?reject_limit - and that fix NEVER REACHED read-batches. GET /read-batches/{id} reads only ?severity; read_batch_rows returns every row unsliced; the batch cap is 50,000. That is NFR-3, still breached, on the same shape DEF-PAY-4221 already names elsewhere: correct at 3,000 connections and wrong against a product now scoped to 40,000 accounts. ⚠ THE COORDINATOR'S OWN BRIEFING ASSERTED THE OPPOSITE - that this list already travelled as a window - which is why it is recorded here: a hand-off repeating a fix that landed on a NEIGHBOURING endpoint is how a breach survives a measurement pass.

A list re-fetched after every row edit multiplies the payload by the number of rows a clerk touches, so the cost is quadratic in the thing the screen exists to do.

title: sync_stale_tree.py aborts on any path with a non-ASCII name, so every push_paths.sh run leaves the tree half-synced
surface: 10-scripts/sync_stale_tree.py
introduced_in: sync_stale_tree.py, at birth
escape_reason: paths_differing() reads 'git diff --name-only', which C-QUOTES a path containing a non-ASCII byte, and hands that quoted string straight to 'git show <tip>:<path>' — which exits 128. The Meter Reads blueprint PDF has an em-dash in its filename and reached this branch in merge ad4243e2, so the sync now raises GitError partway through EVERY run. push_paths.sh catches it and says the push succeeded, which it did — but the tree sync did not, the restored/removed report is never printed, and every path after the PDF in the list is silently never synced. A tool that prints nothing looks exactly like a tool that had nothing to do (hard-won law 7: a check's output must distinguish pass from fail to a READER). Nothing in the repo exercised a non-ASCII path; the tool was proved on four sabotages and this was not one of them.
prevention: Read the path list with 'git -c core.quotePath=false diff --name-only -z' and split on NUL — no quoting, no escaping, and the bytes that come out are the bytes git wants back. Then add a case that puts a file with a non-ASCII name in the differing set and proves the sync completes over it, because the four existing sabotage proofs all used ASCII paths.

title: push_paths.sh step 6 crashes on a blueprint PDF's filename, so EVERY push leaves the shared tree unsynced
surface: 10-scripts/sync_stale_tree.py
found_in: 2.x — observed on two consecutive pushes, 2026-09-14 (commits 222ddf4d and 126efa46)
introduced_in: whenever a path containing a space reached the repo — the six blueprint PDFs under 05-prototype/
escape_reason: The push SUCCEEDS and the script says so, then the sync half dies in a traceback and returns 0 by design ('a failure here must never be reported as a failed push'). The line a lane reads is 'pushed <sha>', and the half that moves the FILES — the half CLAUDE.md law 12 depends on after a commit-tree push, because the commit is fine and the TREE is the loaded revert — silently never runs. Nothing counts how often it fails. git show is given a path that arrives already shell-quoted with octal escapes, so '05-prototype/03 SMARTBillHub ... Meter Reads blueprint.pdf' returns 128 and the whole sync abandons every remaining path.
prevention: Read paths with -z or core.quotePath=false so a filename with a space or a non-ASCII character is never quoted into the argument; make the sync print what it SKIPPED beside what it moved (law 7: a declared blind spot with no NUMBER is indistinguishable from an empty one); and let a per-path failure skip that path rather than abandon the rest.

title: close_defect.py's byte-spliced status change was reverted twice on disk inside ten minutes by a sibling's whole-file write

title: A prefix-proof written as 'diff ... && echo ok' reports nothing when it FAILS, and the push went ahead over it
surface: the hand procedure in CLAUDE.md law 11, as used by the merge lane
found_in: 2026-09-14, reading push_paths.sh's numstat after pushing DEF-MET-5221
introduced_in: the idiom has been used verbatim all session
escape_reason: Law 11 prescribes proving the prefix with 'diff <(head -c N new) tip'. Written as 'diff ... >/dev/null && echo PREFIX ok', a PASS prints a line and a FAILURE prints NOTHING and does not stop the script - so the absence of the success line is the only signal, and an absent line is exactly what a busy operator does not notice. I did not notice. The push then carried two other lanes' in-flight register work (a DEF-MET-5204 status edit and a whole DEF-GOV-5222 row) under my authorship - DEF-168 mechanism five, the third occurrence today and the first caused by the guard rather than by skipping one. prevention: Never write a proof as 'check && echo ok'. Write it so the FAILURE is what speaks and stops: 'diff ... || { echo REFUSED; exit 1; }'. Better, use the tool that owns the file - file_defect.py appends raw bytes and close_defect.py splices one line, and neither can carry a neighbour's row. Best, note that push_paths.sh ALREADY refuses a vanished register line; what it cannot see is an ADDED one, because an append is the safe shape and a neighbour's append rides along inside it.

title: I overwrote a sibling's uncommitted defect row by cp-ing the pinned tip over the shared register, then restored it
surface: 12-governance/10-defect-log.csv — DEF-BIL-5242, a sibling's in-flight row, present in my working tree and in no commit anywhere
found_in: CR-101-BRC03 §06 lane, 2026-09-14, immediately after the cp, by diffing my working copy against the pinned tip BEFORE pushing
introduced_in: this lane, the same session — push_paths.sh refused because I had passed the tip as the base, and my re-derivation was 'cp the tip bytes over the working file' instead of 'take the tip bytes and re-apply MY edit to a copy'
escape_reason: LAW 11's RE-DERIVATION CLAUSE SAYS TO REBUILD A FILE AS 'THE PINNED TIP PLUS YOUR OWN HUNKS', AND I DID THE FIRST HALF DESTRUCTIVELY. cp-ing the tip over a shared file in the working tree is indistinguishable in effect from git checkout -- path, which law 11 explicitly bans, and I reached for it precisely while trying to obey law 11. NOTHING WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: the row was UNCOMMITTED and in no commit anywhere, so git status, git diff against the tip, the file count, the hunks and push_paths.sh's own staleness check all pass over it — the damage is in what was left behind, not in what was pushed, which is DEF-2474's shape arriving through a different door. It was found only because I diffed the working copy against the tip and READ the output before cp-ing, so the row was still in my own scrollback; had I sent that diff to /dev/null the row would have been gone with no trace and its author would have re-filed it as a new id.
prevention: Re-derive into a TEMP FILE, never over the shared one: git show TIP:path > tmp, re-apply your edit to tmp, and move tmp into place only after diffing tmp against the working copy and confirming every difference is yours. Mechanically: push_paths.sh already refuses a path that MOVED UNDER YOU; the mirror guard is wanted — a helper that refuses to overwrite a working file whose current content exists in NO commit, because that content exists nowhere else and the overwrite is unrecoverable.

title: The bill run's Check screen counts every chip in the browser from an unpaginated findings payload - at 10,000 accounts that is ~660,000 SQL statements and ten thousand rows on the wire, per refresh

The docstring's reason for not paginating (a page would make ready.length a page size) is only true because the screen counts rows it was sent, so serving counts removes the reason. title: A cycle run never checks that an account's consumption starts where its last BILL ended - the anchor is the previous READ, and the final-bill path has the check the cycle path lacks
surface: 06-backend/apps/metering/selectors.py billing_reads_for_unit (consumption is stored as current minus prior times multiplier); 06-backend/apps/billing/runs.py _readings_for; compare 06-backend/apps/billing/cut_bill.py which DOES anchor on the last issued period end
introduced_in: the cycle run path has never had it; cut_bill.py shows the shape that is missing
escape_reason: Billing does not compute the delta - it asks metering through the billing_reads_for_unit seam for consumption over a period, and metering answers with a figure it stored as (current - prior) x multiplier when the read was taken. The prior is the previous READ on that meter. Nothing verifies that the previous read is the one the account's last ISSUED bill actually used. The run-level Continuous / no gap, no overlap check on Scope compares run PERIODS, not an account's reads, so it passes over this. The final-bill path in cut_bill.py anchors on the day after the last issued period end - the cycle path has no equivalent. Found by the PO asking where the check was.
prevention: On the cycle path, per account, compare the read the period opens from against the read the last issued invoice closed on, and raise a decision rather than billing silently when they disagree. A skipped read, a re-read, a meter exchange or a bill that was drafted and never issued can all put them out of step, and the failure is money in both directions - a gap bills nobody for real consumption, an overlap bills a customer twice. cut_bill.py already models the anchor; reuse its shape rather than inventing one.

title: A decision on the Check screen records a choice and never re-prices the accounts it touched, and sign-off gates only on UNRESOLVED breaks so a decided-but-stale draft walks through
surface: 06-backend/apps/billing/decisions.py resolve_cases (records, does not re-price); apps/billing/api.py run_exception_resolve; the BR-BIL-053 gate in apps/billing/runs.py; drawn strip sub-line 'updates as you decide' on p051
introduced_in: the decisions path has never re-priced; the drawn behaviour is marked NEW on p052 item 7
escape_reason: resolve_cases takes bill_run, case_id, choice, reason, case_ids, amount and unit - there is no re-price parameter and no re-price call. The one-account retry endpoint says in its own words IT IS NOT A RE-PRICE. So a clerk can bulk-decide 44 estimated accounts under one bulk_action_id and every draft keeps its pre-decision figure. BR-BIL-053 gates phase 4 on UNRESOLVED breaks only, so a resolved-but-un-re-priced case passes the gate and the clerk signs off on stale money - under a KPI strip whose own drawn sub-line reads 'updates as you decide'. Nothing measures whether a draft is older than the decision that should have changed it.
prevention: Two halves. First a scoped re-price: calculate_run with a narrowed account list, in the same worker and on the same progress channel, taking the set a decision touched or the set a changed plan or tariff covers - the drawing marks this NEW on p052 item 7 and says why it is safe, 'the engine already guarantees it', because stages 1-6 are pure and stage 7 replaces a draft rather than adding one. Second, extend the BR-BIL-053 gate: a run cannot enter phase 4 while any draft predates a decision recorded against its account. Without the second half the first is optional, and an optional re-price is the same defect wearing a button.

title: The bill run idempotency key omits the service scope, so a second scoped run for the same cycle and period is refused as a duplicate and those accounts are never billed by anything
surface: 06-backend/apps/billing/runs.py:721 idempotency.bill_run_key(cycle_id, period_start, period_end); the DuplicateRun refusal at :724; scope_services carried through _readings_for and findings_dict
introduced_in: the key has never carried scope; scoped runs were added later and nothing widened it
escape_reason: The key is composed from cycle, period start and period end only, and the unique constraint is on tenant plus that key. But scope_services is a real parameter threaded through the whole pipeline, so a clerk can run Water only for September, consume that cycle-and-period key, and have the Sewer run for the same period refused as DuplicateRun. The first run writes no exclusion row for the accounts it did not cover, so they never enter the held queue and no catch-up run will ever find them. The result is silent under-billing that no screen, gate or test reports. Found by the Billing blueprint itself while reading section 03 for the element inventory - the document states in its own words that there is no defect row and no open question for it and that zero rows in the register mention the scope field.
prevention: Include the service scope in bill_run_key so two scoped runs over one cycle and period are different runs, and migrate existing keys with care because the constraint is tenant plus key. Until that lands, either refuse a scoped run outright with a sentence naming this limit, or write an explicit exclusion row per account the scope skipped so the held queue and catch-up can still see them. The general lesson is the one this register keeps relearning: when a new dimension is added to an operation, check every uniqueness key that operation already writes - scope_services was threaded through reads, findings and pricing and stopped at the key.

title: A killed bill-run worker could never resume: the redelivery hit start() on a running record and the checkpoint was reachable by nothing
surface: POST /billing/runs/{id}/calculate with background:true, on a deployment with a Celery worker (JOBS_EAGER=False)
found_in: CR-105-BRC03, reading blueprint p050 against apps/billing/run_resume.py and core/jobs.py
introduced_in: 2026-08-31, CR-051 task 11 — apps/billing/run_resume.py landed complete and nothing could deliver a record carrying its checkpoint
escape_reason: Every test of the resume built its own job record as a plain dict (tests/test_cr051_run_scale.py a_job_record) and called run_jobs.run_calculate_job directly, so none passed through core.jobs.start, which is the hop that refused. A worker killed by SIGKILL writes nothing, so run_job's except-Exception never runs and the record is left saying running; CELERY_TASK_ACKS_LATE redelivers the message, start() refuses a running record, and the run stayed running for ever. The one script that kills a real worker hand-wrote core_jobs.fail() before resuming, supplying the missing hop itself and passing honestly over a checkpoint production could not reach.
prevention: core.jobs.reclaim + core.jobs.resume, called by apps/tenancy/tasks.run_pending_job; tests/test_cr105_run_transport.py drives every resume case through that task rather than a hand-built record, and tc9 asserts the task body still names resume.

title: The broker's visibility_timeout was 3600s under an 8520s hard task limit, so a long bill run is re-delivered while it is still running
surface: Any bill run longer than an hour on a Celery/Redis deployment — 25,000 accounts is about 71 minutes at the measured 0.17s per account
found_in: CR-105-BRC03, while establishing what makes core.jobs.reclaim safe
introduced_in: 2026-08-19 CR-017 (Celery adopted) and unchanged when CR-051 task 30 set CELERY_TASK_TIME_LIMIT=8520 on 2026-08-31
escape_reason: No settings module declared CELERY_BROKER_TRANSPORT_OPTIONS at all, so kombu's Redis default of 3600s applied and nothing named it anywhere. The symptom was invisible because core.jobs.start() happened to refuse the second delivery with JobsError — a duplicate execution was being prevented by an unrelated guard, so the only evidence was a log line in a worker nobody reads. The day a reclaim exists that refusal stops firing and the two deliveries meet.
prevention: CELERY_BROKER_TRANSPORT_OPTIONS visibility_timeout is set from CELERY_TASK_TIME_LIMIT in one expression in config/settings/base.py, with each naming the other; tests/test_cr105_run_transport.py tc8 fails if the timeout stops being the larger of the two.

title: The kill-and-resume proof has not been able to complete, and the case that guards it only greps the script for four substrings

STILL OPEN: against the seeded dev database the pass finds no ready accounts and the proof cannot reach its kill, so it has still never completed end to end; and tc11 still only greps text. A guard that reads a script instead of running it cannot see either fault.

title: A bill-run job that FAILED is re-delivered by nothing, and the manage.py run_pending_jobs command its own code names does not exist
surface: A calculate job that hit the soft time limit or raised — the record says failed and carries a usable checkpoint, and nothing ever picks it up
found_in: CR-105-BRC03, while closing the redelivery half of the resume

escape_reason: apps/tenancy/tasks.py names manage.py run_pending_jobs twice, in a docstring and in an error message an operator reads when the broker is down, and no such command has ever existed under any app — hard-won law 1, a comment claiming a mechanism. Nothing greps an error message for a command name. The redelivery half is now built (core.jobs.resume), so a worker KILLED mid-pass resumes; a job that FAILED does not, because run_pending_job has no retry policy and Celery treats a raised task as complete.

Auto-retrying a money job is a product decision about how many times a bill run may re-attempt itself and after how long, not a lane's; and the alternative, an operator command, needs a home and a name. Both are reported rather than chosen. core.jobs.resume is the entry point either would call.

title: A byte-offset append slice replayed a sibling's already-pushed register row, duplicating DEF-BIL-5283
surface: 12-governance/10-defect-log.csv at commit 5c464e64 — two byte-identical DEF-BIL-5283 rows
found_in: G30 defect-register, on this lane's own post-push gate run
introduced_in: 2026-09-14 commit 5c464e64, this lane
escape_reason: Law 11's re-derivation was followed and the prefix proof passed — the rebuilt file's first N bytes WERE byte-identical to the tip's, because the damage was an addition at the end, not a subtraction anywhere. Every check law 11 prescribes is aimed at a REVERT and this is the opposite defect. The append slice was computed as 'the working copy minus my base', which is a statement about POSITION and not about authorship: a sibling row appended to the same shared file inside that window is inside the slice.
prevention: The duplicate is removed (both rows were asserted byte-identical first). For the next lane: replay the rows whose IDS YOU ALLOCATED, selected by id, not the byte range after your base. G30 is what caught this, which is the system working — an id is the register's primary key and the gate says so.

title: The decision log carries duplicated entries going back to 17 August, because an append derived by byte offset replays whatever a sibling wrote inside the window - and no check in the repo looks for a duplicate
surface: 12-governance/02-decision-log.md - five duplicated headings dated 2026-08-17, 2026-08-19, 2026-09-04, 2026-09-07 and 2026-09-10, plus three from 2026-09-14 already repaired
introduced_in: the byte-offset append technique, in use across many lanes since at least 2026-08-17
escape_reason: Deriving an append as tail -c +MARK means the bytes after an offset, which on a file any lane may append to is whatever ARRIVED after that offset rather than what you wrote. Every check law 11 prescribes passes on the result: it is a strict superset of the tip so the prefix proof holds, numstat shows insertions and ZERO deletions, and reading your own hunks shows your own content. A duplicate is not a revert, and nothing in this repo has ever looked for one. A lane found the same fault in its own push to the defect register today, named the mechanism as position rather than authorship, and repaired that register by id; the decision log instance was found only because the coordinator went looking after reading that report.
prevention: Two halves. Derive an append by AUTHORSHIP: keep the exact bytes in their own file from the moment they are composed and cat them onto the tip's copy, rather than appending first and recovering the block by offset. And add the check the prefix proof cannot make: after building the new file, assert that no heading or id it contains occurs more than once - a sort | uniq -d over the ## headings for this file, and over the id column for 10-defect-log.csv, would have failed loudly on every instance. The five historical duplicates are LEFT IN PLACE deliberately: they are other lanes' records, they may be legitimate re-entries, and deleting weeks of history on one reader's judgement is a larger risk than the duplication.

title: A sibling's pathspec commit published this lane's 39 uncommitted locale keys — DEF-168's mechanism, live again
surface: commit 5c464e64 'CR-105-BRC03: a killed bill-run worker resumes' carries 39 keys of 07-frontend/src/i18n/locales/*.json that belong to the bill-detail restructure and were uncommitted at the time

escape_reason: A pathspec commit takes the WHOLE working-tree content of every path it names, so naming the eleven catalogues for one lane's own keys publishes every other lane's in-flight key with them. Nothing is lost and nothing goes red, which is why it stayed invisible: the file count is right, the committing lane's own keys ARE present, and the diff is a correct-looking block of added lines. Law 11 already names this as mechanism five (DEF-168) and prescribes reading the HUNKS rather than the file count; eleven catalogues of sorted JSON is precisely the diff nobody reads.
prevention: The durable fix is not another post-push check. For the eleven catalogues specifically, the safe commit is the tip's bytes plus only your own keys, re-derived at push time — which is what caught this. The general habit, from law 11: before committing a shared file, diff it against the pinned tip and read the hunks, and if the hunks are too many to read, you are committing somebody else's work.

title: A clerk cannot enrol an account at an overridden level in one act: the enrolment request carries no override and an override needs a reason the form has no field for
surface: POST /budget-billing/enrollments (apps/billing/budget_api.py, budget_service.enroll); POST /budget-billing/{id}/override (budget.validate_override); blueprint SS05 entry 25.1 section 3, p123

Doing it as two calls would leave a customer enrolled at the computed figure when the second call fails - a partial write on a money path with no rule for the half-done state - and validate_override refuses a reason-less override, which the drawing gives no field for.
prevention: Either the enrolment request takes an optional override plus its reason and enroll validates the bound in one transaction, or the drawing gains a reason field and the PO rules on a two-step act. Until then the box is drawn and greyed with its reason, which is the blueprint's own doctrine one page earlier, and the button names the computed figure that will really be written.

title: A penalty bill's tamper fee refuses over a charge-code read that has been published since 2026-08-27: penalty_charge_line raises 'rating publishes no charge-code read' unconditionally, so WE-11's TAMPER $500.00 has never been billable and the one-time tab tells every clerk so

title: The FIRST-BILL kind cannot draft at all and never could: one_time._account_type_id reads account_type_id off customers' account_detail, and account_detail has never served that key, so every first bill refuses with 'names no consumer category'

escape_reason: A read that names a key the serializer does not have, and nothing anywhere asks whether a key exists. account_detail_dict serves twelve keys and account_type_id is not one of them - the CODE is served by account_row, the LIST serializer, and the detail serializer serves neither code nor id. So _account_type_id has answered None since 2026-08-16, deposit_line_for refuses by name on every account, and the first kind has never produced a bill through the tab. It hid because the PREVIEW did not price - prepare_first_bill needs no consumer category, so the preview answered happily and only the DRAFT refused, and no test drafts a first bill through one_time.create. Found by CR-108 wave 1 making the preview price what it shows, which is the point of that change.
prevention: A seam read that names a key should assert the key exists rather than .get() it to None - a KeyError at the seam names the missing field, where None travels three frames and becomes a business refusal about the customer's data.

title: G38 counts stated absences written as ArrivesWith and cannot see the 30 written as RunGap
surface: gates
introduced_in: 2026-08-21, when G38 was written against ArrivesWith, before RunGap existed as the second stated-absence shape
escape_reason: G38's NOTE_ELEMENTS is the literal tuple ("ArrivesWith", "ArrivesWithField"), so its whole subject is one of the two shapes this product states an absence in. Measured on 2026-09-15: 72 ArrivesWith mounts are counted and 30 RunGap mounts are invisible - 29 percent of the surface. The gate reports a true number over a scope it silently excludes, which is indistinguishable from an empty one, and B14 rule 32's own status row names RunGap as the shape that satisfies the closed-details clause - so the newer and more correct shape is the one nothing tracks. A RunGap therefore needs no expiry id and nothing notices when the thing it waits for ships in somebody else's lane, which is DEF-445 exactly.
prevention: A check that cannot cover its whole subject must print what it skipped beside what it checked. Add RunGap to NOTE_ELEMENTS with its own ruleRef-or-tracks rule, or have G38 print the RunGap count it is not checking, so a reader can tell a declared blind spot from an empty one.

title: The one-time wizard's commit bar is the standard primary, and its one commit writes a bill and posts to the ledger

escape_reason: B14 rule 6's own status column already names this hole in capitals: the danger tier is ENFORCED on rendered output for WizardFrame's commit and for ConfirmDialog's, and is 'still unchecked: a commit button that composes NEITHER shared component'. OneTimeWizardCommitBar composes neither - it builds its own Button with variant=primary - so nothing reads its class and nothing can. The act behind it is the one irreversible thing in this wizard: step 3's footer says in the drawing 'This is the first thing that writes. It creates the bill, mints its number and posts to your books', and hard rule 4 makes an issued invoice and its journal entries unamendable, so the correction is a new bill rather than an undo. prevention: A commit bar built outside WizardFrame and ConfirmDialog should take its tier from the act, and the census that pins the 30 confirm call sites should be widened to any component named CommitBar. Two wizards in one module disagreeing about the tier of the same kind of act is what a rendered-output check exists to catch.

title: Step 3 renders the priced lines and the books panel as stated absences over a server that serves both: oneTimeConfirmFactsFrom returns lines: null and posting: null, and one_time.preview has carried lines, books, posts and closing_position since 65d1e8e3

escape_reason: NOTHING IN THIS REPO READS RENDERED OUTPUT (hard-won law 6), and a truthful docstring written against a server that changed an hour later is not something any gate can catch. G13 asks whether a prop is passed and nothing asks whether an absence is still true. The screen's own tables are already built and tested against the shapes, so the gap is wiring rather than work - which is also why no test went red: each half tests itself and the question 'has the server started serving this' belonged to nobody.
prevention: The mount already names the remedy in its docstring - 'the day the preview carries line detail, a posting preview or a channel list, each becomes one line here'. A note like that is a HOLD WITH A CLOCK IN IT, and hard-won law 2 says write the test that fires when the hold expires in the same commit: assert against the SERVED payload's key set rather than against a hand-written null, so the day the server starts serving the key the suite goes red and names the file.

title: Budget ACTUAL TO DATE double-counts the settle-up month: $921.77 served where $723.02 is true, and 4 months where 3 were billed
surface: 06-backend/apps/billing/selectors.py budget_actuals_to_date — GET /budget-billing, the ACTUAL TO DATE column of the Billing > Budget Bills tab (screen 25)
introduced_in: 16b7c35f, 2026-09-14 — the commit that added budget_actuals_to_date (git log -S, one commit, never since amended)
escape_reason: the selector sums 'actual' over every budget event with a non-null actual, and BOTH the BILLED row and the SETTLED row of a settle-up month carry the same actual — budget_service._record_event copies level and actual onto the settle-up row so the year-end row can reproduce what the customer was shown. Nothing caught it because no test drives an account THROUGH a settle-up and then reads the column: the selector's own tests stop before the settle-up month, and the settle-up tests (test_us_bil_019 tc3/tc4) assert the balance and the audit row and never call the selector. The two halves were each correct and no test crossed them. months=Count('id') inflates the same way, so the column's own denominator agrees with its wrong numerator and the row looks internally consistent.
prevention: filter the sum to event=BUDGET_EVENT_BILLED rather than to actual__isnull=False — the event kind is the fact being asked for, and 'has an actual' is a proxy for it that stops being true the moment another event kind carries one. A regression test drives the frozen WE-8 chain through its settle-up month and asserts 723.02 over 3 months.

title: final_bill.py is a money path with NO HUMAN-OWNED marker and NO glob in human_owned.txt, so G7 cannot see it
surface: 06-backend/apps/billing/final_bill.py (settle_account, settle_final_bill, deposit_credit_for) vs 10-scripts/gates/human_owned.txt
introduced_in: unknown
escape_reason: G7 enforces the HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING marker only on files matching a glob in human_owned.txt, so a money path that matches no glob is not unmarked-and-caught, it is INVISIBLE - the gate reports zero over a scope it silently excludes (hard-won law 7's fifth shape). Measured 2026-09-15: grep -c final_bill human_owned.txt = 0, grep -c HUMAN-OWNED in final_bill.py = 0. Its siblings first_bill.py (list line 55) and one_time.py (line 272) both carry the glob AND the marker, which is what makes the absence read as deliberate rather than missing. final_bill.py decides the deposit APPLICATION and the closing settlement - the last bill nobody checks afterwards.
prevention: A gate that enforces a marker only within a list must also print what it did NOT look at: G7 should report the count of money-path files it skipped beside the count it checked, because a declared blind spot with no number attached is indistinguishable from an empty one. Reported by the DEF-BIL-5318 lane; a lane may not add itself to human_owned.txt, so the glob is a PO/process decision.

title: A LEVEL-PAY ASK TELLS THE CUSTOMER TO BRING A DOCUMENT THAT DOES NOT EXIST, AND TELLS THE CLERK THEY HAVE BEEN TOLD TO. POST /portal/accounts/{id}/help-paying/ask serves two routes. For route='level_pay' it still returns bring_the_document: true, and _hardship_ask_words composes the clerk's worklist sentence from HARDSHIP_ASK_NOTE, which ends 'No document is attached - the portal cannot accept an upload, and the customer has been told to bring it to the office.' There is no document in a request to level next year's payments. The customer's confirmation promises a trip to the counter and the clerk reads that one was promised, so the first thing that happens is a telephone call asking for a certificate nobody needs.
surface: Customer portal > Help paying (CWP-056) route level_pay + the staff requests worklist (REQ-01)
found_in: 679329eb (the tip, 2026-09-15) - found assembling the packet for §05 entry 25.3, reading apps/portal/services._hardship_ask for what a level-pay ask actually writes
introduced_in: CR-068 wave L1 (US-CWP-058), when HARDSHIP_ROUTE_WORDS grew its second route and the sentence around it kept one shape
escape_reason: The note template and the response body are written ONCE for BOTH routes while HARDSHIP_ROUTE_WORDS holds two, so the certificate route's wording became the shape of every route. No test asserts the composed sentence for route='level_pay' - the route map is data and the sentence around it is not, so adding a route cannot fail anything.
prevention: Drive a test from HARDSHIP_ROUTE_WORDS' own keys: for every route, assert the composed what_they_said and the response fields. A third route then cannot be added without its own assertions, and the document clause becomes per-route rather than global.

title: A FINDING ON A MONEY SCREEN WAS 'REPORTED' IN ONE DOCSTRING AND FILED NOWHERE, SO NOTHING COUNTED IT FOR FOURTEEN DAYS. apps/billing/customers_seam.level_pay_asks_waiting withholds §05 screen 25's ASKS WAITING tile and ends 'The durable fix is a FILTERABLE FACT on the request (a route or a kind column, and the account it is about), which is customers' to add and is reported rather than reached for from here.' Nothing was reported: no open question, no defect row, no change request, no business rule. The register holds no row for it and neither does customers' backlog, so the one thing standing between §05 entry 25.3 and a working queue existed only as a sentence in the file that could not do anything about it. It is CLAUDE.md hard rule 4's own lesson happening to a different subject - a finding recorded only in the file you happen to be in is a finding nobody can count. Minted now as OQ-BIL-12359.
surface: Billing > Budget Bills - §05 screen 25's ASKS WAITING tile and §05 entry 25.3's whole queue
found_in: 679329eb (the tip, 2026-09-15) - found building §05 entry 25.3, by grepping the registers for the question this docstring says was raised and finding none
introduced_in: the CR-100-BRC03 seam wave that wrote level_pay_asks_waiting, which stated the fix and filed nothing
escape_reason: No gate reads prose for a CLAIM THAT A FINDING WAS RECORDED SOMEWHERE ELSE. G08 checks a stub names an OQ that exists; nothing checks a docstring that says a thing was 'reported' against whether any register holds it, and the sentence reads like completed work to every later reader - which is exactly how it survived being read by the lanes that built 25 and 25.1.
prevention: A docstring that says a finding is reported must NAME the row - an OQ, DEF or CR id - and a lane writing one without an id is writing hard-won law 1's comment-claiming-a-guarantee. Cheapest mechanical form: a gate that greps seam and selector docstrings for 'reported', 'raised', 'filed' or 'flagged' and requires an id on the same sentence, printing what it skipped beside what it checked.

title: §05 OF THE BILLING BLUEPRINT ARGUES THE JOIN BUTTON'S WHOLE DESIGN FROM AN OPEN QUESTION THAT WAS CLOSED THE DAY BEFORE THE DRAWING IS DATED. Pages 119-120 and 128 of '04 Billing, As Built.pdf' say a customer pressing Join level pay is 'the dead-control failure, on a money screen, with an open question against it', and design the ask queue (entry 25.3) around the portal being unable to enrol. surface: 05-prototype/04 Billing, As Built.pdf §05 pages 119-120 and 128 (entries 25.3 and 25.4) + Customer portal CWP-044

title: The counter receipt has nothing to attach to: approval opens no account, so the ruled attach-to-account half never fires

prevention: When a ruling names two acts, write the test that fires when the second one becomes possible -- hard-won law 2's hold-expiry test, applied to a money path: assert by the id of the thing that must exist (an account on the request) rather than by the function being present.

title: G85, THE ONE-ADDRESS-HOME GATE, CANNOT SEE ANY ADDRESS COLUMN SPELLED `*_as_given` — IT MATCHES BY NAME AND THREE LIVE COLUMNS ARE OUTSIDE ITS ALPHABET. g85_one_address_home.ADDRESS_SHAPED is a frozenset of exact field names (address, address_line, city, postal_code, lat, lng and nine more). customers.ServiceRequest declares address_as_given and billing_address_as_given; portal.PortalApplicationDraft declares address_as_given. None of those three names is in the set, so the gate has never looked at them and reports its clean PASS over a scope that excludes them. All three columns are lawful today - the two on the request are what an applicant said before any premises exists (BR-CUS-070, evidence and not a record) and the billing one is BR-MET-1161's own mailing exception - so nothing is broken right now. What is broken is the CHECK: a declared blind spot with no number attached is indistinguishable from an empty one. Found on 2026-09-15 by CR-094-BRC01 wave 1 lane B, which was about to add address_city_as_given to service_requests and noticed that G85 would have passed it silently; the PO then ruled those columns out of the table altogether, so the immediate hazard went away and the blind spot did not.
surface: 10-scripts/gates/g85_one_address_home.py ADDRESS_SHAPED — and the three columns it cannot see: 06-backend/apps/customers/models.py::ServiceRequest.address_as_given + .billing_address_as_given, 06-backend/apps/portal/models.py::PortalApplicationDraft.address_as_given
found_in: v2.277.0 · 1b64ad92 · read while adding a column to service_requests, 2026-09-15
introduced_in: the gate's own first commit, 2026-09-04 (CR-070 §W) — ADDRESS_SHAPED never carried a _as_given spelling
escape_reason: The gate is not lying and its own docstring is careful about what it excludes and why (state and country are excluded, measured). What it never says is that its alphabet is a closed list of fifteen exact names, so ANY address column whose author spells it differently is outside the fence with no signal at all. Nothing downstream can catch that: the gate passes, its detail line reads like a full sweep, and the only way to find it is to try to add a column and notice the gate did not care.
prevention: Two halves, and the second is the durable one. (1) The gate now prints what it did NOT look at beside what it did - UNSEEN_AS_GIVEN_SPELLINGS, a hard-coded 3 with the three columns named in the comment above it - so a reader of the PASS line can tell a covered scope from an uncovered one. (2) The real fix is to make the alphabet a SUFFIX match rather than an exact-name set, so address_city_as_given, service_address_line and mailing_city are all seen and then permitted or refused by a HOMES entry. That is a wider change than a wave-1 lane should make to a gate three modules depend on, because widening the alphabet turns every currently-invisible column into a FAIL that has to be ruled on first - which is the right conversation and is not this wave's.

title: THE node_modules SYMLINK EVERY WORKTREE LANE IS TOLD TO CREATE IS NOT IGNORED BY .gitignore, SO IT SHOWS AS UNTRACKED AND CAN BE COMMITTED. Both .gitignore line 8 and 07-frontend/.gitignore line 1 read 'node_modules/' with a trailing slash, which git matches against DIRECTORIES only. The standing worktree setup instruction is 'ln -s /home/user/SMARTBillHub/07-frontend/node_modules <your-worktree>/07-frontend/node_modules' - that creates a SYMLINK, not a directory, so the pattern does not match it and 'git status' in every lane worktree prints '?? 07-frontend/node_modules'. Measured in the CR-094-BRC01 wave 1 lane B worktree on 2026-09-15 at 1b64ad92: git status --short shows the symlink as untracked alongside the lane's real files. Nothing is broken today because every lane pushes through 10-scripts/push_paths.sh with named paths, but the one forbidden command CLAUDE.md law 11 keeps having to re-ban - git add -A - would commit a symlink whose target is an absolute path outside the repository, and a clone on any other machine would get a dangling link that breaks every frontend command with no obvious cause.
surface: .gitignore line 8 and 07-frontend/.gitignore line 1 — the pattern 'node_modules/' against the symlink created by the standard worktree setup step
found_in: v2.277.0 · 1b64ad92 · git status in a lane worktree, 2026-09-15
introduced_in: the gitignore predates worktree-per-lane working; the symlink instruction arrived with it and the two were never compared
escape_reason: No gate reads .gitignore against how lanes are actually set up, and the symptom is a single '??' line in git status that every lane learns to read past because their own untracked work is listed beside it. It is invisible until somebody commits it, and then it is invisible again because a symlink in a diff looks like a one-line text file.
prevention: Add a second pattern without the trailing slash - 'node_modules' - to both files, which matches a directory, a file and a symlink alike. It is one line in each and it is safe: nothing in this repo is legitimately named node_modules other than the dependency tree. Left to the orchestrator rather than done by this lane because both files are repository-root shared files and three lanes were live in the same wave.

title: THE TENANT-ISOLATION CASE FOR THE PREMISES SEARCH COULD NOT RUN AT ALL — IT ERRORED ON A MISSING FIXTURE AND READ AS ONE BLEMISH IN A GREEN RUN
surface: 06-backend/tests/test_cr094_lane_e_address_is_picked.py
introduced_in: b87b9655 (CR-094-BRC01 capture lane E)
escape_reason: The suite defaults to in-memory sqlite, where the case is skipped by its requires_postgres mark, so nothing ever attempted it. On PostgreSQL it did not skip and did not fail: it ERRORED with fixture 'rls_probe_role' not found, and pytest reported the file as '22 passed, 1 error' — which reads as a green run with a blemish rather than as an unproven security guarantee. The rls fixture depends on rls_probe_role and pytest resolves a fixture dependency by name in the TEST MODULE's own namespace, so importing rls alone is not enough. Every other file in the repo that uses rls imports both and carries a comment saying why; this one imported rls only.
prevention: Two things, and the second is the durable one. (1) The import is restored with the reason written beside it. (2) The environment could not have proved it either way: the app role lacks CREATEROLE, so the probe-role fixture skipped with 'the tenant-isolation guarantee is UNPROVEN in this environment'. A non-superuser, non-bypassing sbh_rls_probe role now exists on this cluster, which unblocks every isolation case for every lane rather than this one file. The case now PASSES on real PostgreSQL: a premises search run as one tenant returns no row of another where both have a property on the same street.

title: A BUSINESS APPLICANT MAY STILL BE ASKED FOR A SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER ON A SERVICE REQUEST, WHICH BR-CUS-1022 FORBIDS BY NAME. The rule (PO 2026-09-01) says a person is known by SSN, licence or phone and a company by its Tax ID, and that 'a company is never asked for a driving licence and a person is never asked for a Tax ID, refused BY NAME rather than dropped'. service_requests.ssn opened on 2026-08-27, FOUR DAYS BEFORE that rule was ruled, and _clean_capture has never gated it on applicant_kind. The lane that finished BR-CUS-092(a) on 2026-09-15 built the kind gate for the two fields the PO named that day - date_of_birth and drivers_licence, both refused by name for a business - and deliberately did NOT narrow ssn in passing: narrowing a shipped capture path has its own blast radius (existing draft rows, the portal door at PORTAL_CAPTURE_FIELDS, and the signed SSN proof suite), and doing it silently inside another wave is how a change becomes invisible. customers.ssn is already gated the right way - identity_match.KIND_IDENTIFIER_FIELDS and customer_edit._validate refuse it by name for a company - so the two surfaces disagree about the same fact for the same person.
surface: 06-backend/apps/customers/service_request_service.py :: KIND_FORBIDDEN_FIELDS, which lists date_of_birth and drivers_licence for 'business' and does not list ssn
found_in: CR-094-BRC01 lane G, 2026-09-15, building the BR-CUS-1022 kind gate for the two fields the PO named that day
introduced_in: 2026-09-01, when BR-CUS-1022 was ruled four days after service_requests.ssn shipped - the rule arrived after the path and nothing walked back over it
escape_reason: NOTHING IN THIS REPO COMPARES A RULE AGAINST EVERY SURFACE IT GOVERNS. BR-CUS-1022 was applied to the customer table in the same wave that ruled it (customers 0038, identity_match, customer_edit) and the service request was another module file on another day. G32 asks whether a refusal resolves to a message; nothing asks whether a rule that names a refusal HAS one everywhere the fact is captured. The two surfaces are each internally coherent - DEF-638 class - and the contradiction exists only in the join.
prevention: The durable half is a check that reads KIND_FORBIDDEN_FIELDS against identity_match.KIND_IDENTIFIER_FIELDS and fails when a government identifier is gated on one surface and not the other, because that pair is the whole of BR-CUS-1022 in code. The fix itself is one line plus its blast radius: add ssn to KIND_FORBIDDEN_FIELDS for business, decide what happens to any existing business-kind row that already carries one (there should be none - applicant_kind has taken its person default since CR-033 removed the control on 2026-08-27), and update tests/test_br_cus_092_ssn_capture.py, which captures with applicant_kind person throughout and would not notice either way.

title: BR-CUS-092 SAID THE CAPTURE PATH REFUSED THE DRIVING LICENCE 'BY NAME' FOR TWO WEEKS AND IT NEVER DID - IT ANSWERED 'unknown field'. The row's amendment of 2026-08-31 reads, in capitals: 'CLAUSE (a) IS HALF DONE. THE DRIVING LICENCE IS NOT CAPTURED ... on the SERVICE REQUEST, where _clean_capture refuses it by name, and that half of clause (a) stands.' Measured at the tip on 2026-09-15: no spelling of the licence was in IDENTIFIER_FIELDS - not drivers_licence, not driving_licence, not drivers_license - so every one of them fell through to the unknown branch and answered VAL_UNKNOWN_LOOKUP with 'This form does not accept {{field}}', never BIZ_STATE with 'We cannot store an identity number yet'. The distinction is the whole point of that list: one refusal says WE HOLD THIS FACT AND MAY NOT STORE IT, the other says WE HAVE NEVER HEARD OF THIS FIELD, and a lane reading the rule would have gone looking for a named entry that was not there. The same paragraph was then quoted verbatim into the decision-log row of 2026-09-15 and into this wave's brief, so the wrong sentence propagated to three places before anybody ran the code.
surface: 04-docs/05-modules/03-customers/02-business-rules.md :: the BR-CUS-092 AMENDED 2026-08-31 section, second bullet
found_in: CR-094-BRC01 lane G, 2026-09-15, step 0 of the build process - checking the rule against the code before building on it
introduced_in: 2026-08-31, when the CR-056 W2 identity lane amended BR-CUS-092 after building customers.driving_licence and described the service request's refusal from memory rather than from the file
escape_reason: A BUSINESS RULE IS PROSE AND NOTHING IN THIS REPO READS PROSE FOR TRUTH. G50 and G51 compare a CITATION or a closed-defect CLAIM against a register; no check compares a sentence describing what the code does against the code. The claim was also plausible - twelve identifier names ARE refused by name in that exact function, so the sentence was true of its neighbours and false only of the one field it was about. title: EVERY METER ON A NEW BUILD IS RECORDED AS INSTALLED THE MOMENT THE CONNECTION IS COMMITTED, ON A BUILDING WHERE NOTHING HAS BEEN FITTED. assets/services.py sets stage_code = 'active' if unit_id else 'inventory', and it also REFUSES the create without an install_date when a unit is named — so an asset made against a unit is Installed, on a date, by construction. commit_connection reaches this through seams.create_asset_for_unit with the unit always supplied, so a 26-unit build with 50 meters commits 50 meters in status Installed before a crew has been anywhere near the site. Fitting them is precisely what the work orders raised by the same commit are FOR, and the wizard's own review step says the commit 'energises nothing'. The result is a reading route carrying twenty meters nobody can read and a status column that cannot distinguish a meter on a wall from a meter in a plan. BR-AST-011 is correct for its own door — a clerk assigning an existing meter to a unit IS installing it — and the defect is that a BUILD borrows that door for an asset that does not exist yet.
surface: 06-backend/apps/assets/services.py (stage_code / install_date refusal) · 06-backend/apps/metering/connections.py commit_connection step 2 via seams.create_asset_for_unit
found_in: measuring commit_connection for the PO, CR-094-BRC01, 2026-09-16 — reasoning recorded in 12-governance/02-decision-log.md under that date
