escape_reason: Both sides are individually right and nothing asks the question that spans them. The assets suite proves assign-on-create yields 'active', correctly, for the door that rule was written for; the commit suite counts meters and never reads their STATUS. No test asserts what state a newly built asset is in, so the wrong default is invisible from either module.
prevention: A build's assets need a state that means 'planned, not yet fitted', and the work order that fits one is what moves it. Until that exists, assert the status of every asset a commit creates — a count of 50 meters says nothing about whether the product believes they are on a wall.

title: allocate.py --verify SAYS 'a sibling pushed it' WHEN THE ONLY THING HOLDING THE ID IS YOUR OWN COMMIT MESSAGE, AND A LANE THAT BELIEVES IT STRANDS ITS OWN CITATION. On 2026-09-16 Lane E filed DEF-CUS-5451, cited it in commit e37a746a, and then ran the re-derivation law 11 prescribes at push time. 'allocate.py defect --verify 5451' answered 'TAKEN - a sibling pushed it. Renumber before you commit'. No sibling had: a sweep of every origin ref's register found the id nowhere, and the sole occurrence in the entire repository was that lane's own commit message, which the allocator counts as a source (its own note prints 'commit messages (+8)'). Following the instruction would have renumbered the register row away from the id the pushed commit cites, manufacturing a dangling citation on a branch - strictly worse than the collision the check exists to prevent, and the DEF-2804 shape it is meant to stop. The counting is right and the SENTENCE is wrong: 'a sibling pushed it' is an inference the data does not support.

escape_reason: The check is not lying about the COUNT - the id really is present in a reachable commit message - it is lying about WHO. Nothing downstream can catch that, because a renumber looks exactly like a correct renumber: the register gets a fresh unique id, no gate fires, and the only damage is a commit message on the branch pointing at a row that no longer exists, which is invisible to every id-existence check because the id it now names is real and belongs to somebody else later. This is law 7's third habit - a check's output must distinguish pass from fail TO A READER - and law 11's own blind spot restated: every check measures against a baseline that already contains your own earlier work, and here that work reads as a stranger's.
prevention: Say where the id was found instead of guessing who put it there: 'TAKEN - found in commit e37a746a (yours, HEAD~1) / in origin/<branch>'s register'. The provenance is already in hand when the answer is computed, and printing it turns an inference into a fact the reader can act on. Where the only holder is a commit authored in this session, the right answer is 'this id is already yours - keep it'.

title: allocate.py --verify SAYS 'a sibling pushed it' FOR AN ID THE LANE ITSELF CITED IN ITS OWN COMMIT MESSAGE, WHICH TELLS A LANE TO RENUMBER ITS OWN WORK. Measured 2026-09-16: DEF-CUS-5485 and DEF-BIL-5486 were filed in the working tree, and the lane pushed its CODE first with a message naming both ids. The verify then answered 'defect 5485: TAKEN - a sibling pushed it. Renumber before you commit' for both, while grep over the tip register and over every refs/remotes/origin branch found the ids in NO register anywhere. The detection is deliberate and right - allocate.py reads commit messages on purpose, and an id in a pushed message IS claimed - but the SENTENCE is wrong in the one way that costs something. A lane that believes it renumbers ids that are already cited in its own docstrings, tests, walkthrough script and register rows, which is a worse outcome than the collision the check exists to prevent; and a lane that learns to distrust the sentence will wave off a TRUE collision next time, which is exactly how a real red acquires protective colouring.

title: FOURTEEN SHIPPED CONNECTORS CARRY OPERATION NAMES THAT DO NOT FOLLOW THE NAMING FORMAT WE OWN, AND CR-110-BRC04 WAVE C APPLIED IT ONLY TO THE FOURTEEN THAT ARE NEW. The blueprint's p156-p158 settle our own API naming as <runner>_<noun>, where the verb is the runner that executes it - fetch (in, us), deliver (out, us), inbound (in, them), serve (out, them) - so an operation key tells a reader which of the four doors it goes through before opening a file. The five new ERPs, five card processors, three head-end meters and Badger all follow it: serve_payment, serve_bill, serve_customer, deliver_charge, deliver_refund, deliver_card_page, fetch_settlement, fetch_reading, fetch_meter_inventory, fetch_alert, fetch_billing_export. The fourteen that shipped do not, measured operation by operation: email_microsoft/google/smtp/bulk and sms_twilio name send_message where the format gives deliver_message; accounting_file names export_journal (deliver_journal); bank_lockbox_file names import_statement and import_lockbox (fetch_statement, and no key is drawn for lockbox at all); print_vendor names hand_over_batch (deliver_print_batch); gis_esri names address_search, reconcile_parcels and map_tiles (fetch_address, fetch_parcel, fetch_tile); geocoder_census names geocode_address; map_tiles_public names map_tiles; payments_kiosk names payments, account_lookup and returns (inbound_payment, serve_account, inbound_payment_return); payments_sandbox names charge, card_page and settlement; sso names sign_in (inbound_sign_in); meters_neptune360 names sixteen collect_*/push_*. Thirty-eight shipped operation names in total.

The registry validates that a name exists and is unique per manifest and nothing about its shape. This lane did not fix it in the same wave, deliberately and with a measured reason rather than for time: renaming a shipped operation is not a manifest edit. integration_run.operation records the name as DATA ALREADY WRITTEN, so a rename orphans that connector's own run history - the rows stay, and the screen that reads them stops matching. The order that works is: decide what happens to existing integration_run.operation rows (leave them, or write a compatibility map read by the runs screen); rename; then add the refusal so the thirty-ninth cannot drift. The refusal is three lines - the key's first word is one of fetch/deliver/inbound/serve and it matches the operation's own direction-and-initiative pair - and it is worth more than the rename, because it is what makes the format true for every connector after it.

title: THE KIT'S VISUALLY HIDDEN RADIO AND CHECKBOX INPUT STILL ESCAPES ITS SCROLL CONTAINER. Found while fixing DEF-CUS-5480, which was the same mechanism on FieldLabel's sr-only label and is fixed. The kit's tick and radio draw the real input as 'peer sr-only', which is position:absolute, and an absolutely positioned box is clipped by an ancestor's overflow ONLY where that ancestor is also its containing block - so with no positioned ancestor the input's containing block is the initial one, it escapes main.view's clip, and it enlarges the DOCUMENT. New Connect step 4 draws eleven of them in its service tick list; they sit near the top of the screen so nothing shows today, but a tick list below the fold on any long screen would grow a second window scrollbar that scrolls into empty grey, exactly as the forty hidden labels did. Measured on the running product at 1440x1000: eleven 'peer sr-only' inputs, every one reporting no positioned ancestor.

title: A BROAD pkill PATTERN IN A SHARED CONTAINER IS LAW 11's FORBIDDEN-COMMAND SHAPE ONE LAYER DOWN, AND THE LAW'S LIST DOES NOT NAME IT. Law 11 forbids any command that makes the WORKING TREE momentarily not-what-it-was - git stash, git checkout --, git restore, git reset --hard, git clean - because for those seconds other lanes are reading a tree you silently emptied. The same argument covers PROCESSES and the list does not: many lanes share one container, so 'pkill -f run_gates.py' matches every lane's gate run and not only your own, and 'pkill -f pytest' would match every lane's suite. The CR-110-BRC04 wave C lane ran exactly that to free CPU after starting too many parallel runs, having checked nothing but its own intent. Measured from ps afterwards: the container at that moment also held a sibling's 'run_gates.py --changed <sha>' and a sibling's 'pytest tests/ -k int_0 or cr110 or integration'. The lane's FIRST pattern was accidentally safe - the string 'int_0 or int_1' does not appear in the sibling's -k - and its second was not. No damage is detectable and none may have occurred, because a killed verification run costs a re-run rather than work. The defect is the written law being narrower than its own reasoning, which will eventually land on a lane forty minutes into a suite.
surface: CLAUDE.md hard-won law 11, the paragraph beginning 'any command that makes the working tree momentarily not-what-it-was is forbidden' - its list is tree-scoped and has no process-scoped clause

No gate reads a shell command, and a killed sibling run leaves NO trace a checker could find: the victim lane sees its own suite die and reads it as a container hiccup, the killer sees a clean ps and reads it as success. It is an absence, the one thing this repository has repeatedly proved it cannot detect (DEF-CUS-3653). It also wears the exact disguise DEF-172 named: the killing is INCIDENTAL to the intent - the lane wanted CPU, not to stop anybody - so the rule against destructive shared-state commands never comes to mind, which is the same reason 'let me stash to see the tree clean' slipped past a lane that had read the ban three lines earlier.

The safe forms cost nothing and name only your own work: kill the PIDs you started and noted, or call TaskStop with the task ids you hold. And the cure for the cause sits upstream of the cleanup - do not start more parallel runs than the container can serve, because the contention is what makes a broad kill feel reasonable in the first place.

title: THE CONNECTOR GRID DEFAULTS THE PER-API LINES TO SHOWN, SO NEPTUNE'S SIXTEEN BREAK THE ROW. Reported by the PO from the deployed product at 2.284.0: 'on nepture - don show all apis on screen - it is breaking the size of the box - you canjust mention the number'. Neptune 360 renders sixteen OperationLine rows on its card, roughly 620px of list, against neighbours four lines tall - so the whole grid row stretches to Neptune's height and Bulk email and Twilio sit in about 500px of empty space each. IntegrationsTab.tsx:502 maps every operation whenever the card has more than one and is not coming soon. The lines ARE hideable through the column chooser and the blueprint's own stated reason for that control is Neptune by name - the comment at :494 quotes p014, 'hiding the per-API lines is the one thing that makes the grid scannable again' - but the fact defaults to SHOWN, so a clerk meets the broken grid first and has to discover the chooser to repair it. A card should carry the COUNT; the sixteen named rows already have a home on the connection screen's seven-column table.
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/integrations/IntegrationsTab.tsx:498-507 and the column chooser's default fact order
found_in: the PO, from the deployed product, 2026-09-16, 2.284.0
introduced_in: CR-110-BRC04 CON-01 maintenance (2.282.1), when the per-API lines and the column chooser landed together and the fact defaulted to shown
escape_reason: The code QUOTES the drawing saying not to do this, eight lines above the loop that does it - so this is not a missed requirement but a requirement read, written down, and then not applied to the default. Every check passed because none of them looks at height: the walkthrough asserts 28 cards render, the chooser's own tests assert the three facts hide and restore, and BR-INT-028's test asserts a multi-operation card carries no aggregate WORD - which this obeys. Nothing measured a card against its neighbours, and no gate in this repo reads rendered output. The one lane that measured the grid measured WIDTH at 1280 and 1440, which is DEF-CUS-5480's lesson landing twice in one day in two different features.
prevention: The per-API lines default to hidden and the card carries a count; the chooser still turns them on. The durable check is a measurement rather than a count: assert no card in the grid exceeds its row's neighbours by more than a stated factor, on a tenant that has Neptune connected - which is the only fixture where this is visible at all.

title: FIX IT ON A CONNECTED CONNECTOR STILL OPENS THE MANAGE MODAL INSTEAD OF THE SET-UP SCREEN. Reported by the PO from the deployed product at 2.284.0: 'smtp - shows the modal - that is not correct'. DEF-INT-5513 moved the connect case to the set-up page and deliberately left case manage on ConnectModal, on the stated grounds that its screen did not exist yet. That reasoning was wrong: the set-up page IS that screen. Pressing Fix it on Custom SMTP opens a dialog offering How to sign in, Environment, Mail server, Port, Username, Password and Send bills from - field for field the same form the set-up page renders from the same manifest, plus a status header. So a connected connector is edited in a cramped scrolling dialog while a not-connected one gets the full page, and the two surfaces drift apart from here on. The blueprint draws a connected card as View + Set up - two labels, one destination - and CFG frames carry the connector's configure address in their header.
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/integrations/IntegrationsTab.tsx, case manage in Card.press() and the recipient-test branch beside it
found_in: the PO, from the deployed product, 2026-09-16, 2.284.0
introduced_in: DEF-INT-5513's fix (2.283.1), which moved connect and left manage pointing at the modal
escape_reason: The fix for DEF-INT-5513 inventoried every entry point correctly and then applied a rule it had written itself - move connect, keep manage because its screen does not exist - without re-asking whether that premise was still true after the set-up page landed. It was not. The lane even captured Fix it opening the dialog and scored it a PASS, labelled 'correct, that is manage', so the evidence was in front of it. Its test pins manage to the modal deliberately, which means the suite now DEFENDS the wrong behaviour: a later lane fixing this meets a red test asserting the modal and may take it as the rule. Nothing else could catch it - the modal and the page render the same manifest fields, so both look right in isolation and only differ when you see which surface a clerk lands on.
prevention: manage targets the set-up page, and the test that pinned it to the modal is inverted with the reason written at the assertion. The general form is the one this repo keeps meeting: when a screen lands, re-check every control that was held BECAUSE it was missing - a hold is a rule with a clock in it, and only the first half of releasing it feels like the work.

title: Three CR-110 phase-2 hold cases go RED when a wave lands correctly — they police ROUTE_WAVE from a typed list
surface: 06-backend/tests/test_cr110_phase2_partner_reference.py
escape_reason: The three cases that police the declared-but-unbuilt routes iterated a HARDCODED list of four (route, view) pairs while asserting against ROUTE_WAVE, which the same file's own hold-expiry case requires a landing wave to SHRINK. So the moment wave 5 removed its row - correctly, in eb477162 - test_every_unbuilt_route_names_its_wave, test_an_unbuilt_route_is_never_an_empty_result_set and test_the_published_specification_names_all_four_operations all went red at the tip on a true state of the world. Nothing caught it because a suite going red for the RIGHT reason and for the WRONG reason look identical, and the next lane's reflex is to edit the list rather than read it. Dated with git log -S on the assertion text, which names c2ef372f (waves 0-1, the commit that wrote both the hold and the case).
prevention: The three cases are driven off ROUTE_WAVE and a derived ROUTE_VIEWS map instead of a typed list; the equality became a SUBSET, because whether a landed route LEFT the map is the hold-expiry case's job and one assertion doing both did neither well. The specification case gained its mirror: a route that SERVES must stop advertising a 501. Waves 3 and 4 now need no edit to that file at all.

title: The published partner specification offers from/to on /partner/v1/customers, which that route does not read
surface: 06-backend/apps/integrations/partner_api.py :: partner_openapi
escape_reason: partner_openapi builds one parameter list for every operation on the manifest - from, to, page, page_size - because when it was written both served routes took a date window. Wave 2's customers route deliberately takes none: accounts are ordered by an account number allocated from a monotonic series, so a page walk cannot skip a row and a window could only hide one. The document therefore invites a partner to send from=2026-09-01, the server ignores it, and the partner receives every account while believing it asked for a month. Nothing went red because the document is generated from the manifest's operations and no check compares a published parameter against the handler that would read it - the specification is asserted for its PATHS and its refusal codes only. Wave 5's ledger has the mirror of the same gap: start_date and end_date are REQUIRED there and the document marks nothing as required.
prevention: Not fixed here: the parameter loop is one block shared by all four routes and three lanes were live in that file within the hour (law 11), so a lane passing through does not widen it. The fix belongs with partner_openapi's owner and is small - carry the accepted parameters as DATA on the Operation, the way served_path and rate_limit_per_minute already are (DEF-INT-5522's own shape), so a route that reads no window cannot advertise one. A test then asserts the published parameter set against what the handler reads.

title: posting.post() never stamps BR-LED-021 JE- number, so every bill, payment and opening-balance entry is unnumbered — 168 of 168 on the demo tenant
surface: 06-backend/apps/ledger/posting.py::post() — reaching a partner at GET /api/{utility}/partner/v1/ledger, where it is the id field
found_in: CR-110-BRC04 phase 2 wave 5, building the partner ledger read: the payload id came back null on every row. Measured against the live demo tenant — 168 posted entries, 0 carrying a number; the tenant journal_entry number series exists and sits at next_number = 1, never consumed.
introduced_in: the posting-service lane, 2026-08-11 — post_draft() takes a number parameter and stamps it, post() has no such parameter at all, and BR-LED-021 makes no distinction between the two paths
escape_reason: NOTHING IN THE PRODUCT READ THE COLUMN UNTIL AN OUTSIDE SYSTEM DID. The S56 journal list and the accounting export both carry je_number straight through to a screen or a file, where a blank cell reads as a formatting choice rather than as a missing identifier. apps/ledger/journal_api.py even DOCUMENTS the gap in its own exceptions note — an entry posts with je_number null on every host today — and no test asserts the other side of it. So the fact was written down, in prose, in one file, and counted by nothing, which is this repo own recurring shape: a finding recorded only where the author happened to be standing is a finding nobody can count. It cost nothing until a partner asked for a stable transaction reference.
prevention: A test that posts through posting.post() and asserts the entry carries a number, beside the existing post_draft() one — the two paths are covered asymmetrically today and that asymmetry IS the defect. Pending the fix, partner_api.LEDGER_NUMBER_GAP names the cause once in the envelope rather than letting a partner read the null as their own mistake, and test_the_envelope_names_the_missing_je_number_rather_than_composing_one goes red the day a number appears.

It carries a second fault the rename does not: being in Python it is English on every one of the eleven languages.

title: Four ERP manifests declare no served_path, so their published specification advertises the retired phase-1 pair
surface: GET /api/{utility}/v1/openapi.json for erp_workday, erp_sap, erp_infor, erp_msgp
escape_reason: partner_openapi falls back to a two-entry map for any operation with no served_path, and that map names /v1/payments and /v1/billing. Waves 3 and 4 retired that pair (410), so a Workday, SAP, Infor or MSGP key now reads a specification offering two addresses that answer gone. Nothing went red: the fallback is correct code doing what it was written to do, and only Aclarian's manifest declares paths. The keys themselves still work at the phase-2 addresses, which serve every connector in partner_provider_keys() - so this is a document that under-reports, not a door that is shut. Lane C was told not to touch any manifest and did not.
prevention: One line per manifest: served_path on each of the three declared operations, exactly as erp_aclarian.py carries. A gate could ask that every operation with they_call_us also names a served_path once all five declare them.

title: open_balances_for_accounts costs one SUM(allocations) per invoice, so a partner page of 1,000 bills is ~1,000 extra statements
surface: GET /api/{utility}/partner/v1/bills — the amount field (the account's balance now)
escape_reason: billing.open_balance.open_balances_for_accounts batches billing's own half in one query and then asks payments_seam.prior_position_for_account once per ACCOUNT, which inside itself sums allocations once per INVOICE of that account. Measured in pytest with CaptureQueriesContext: a one-bill page cost 17 statements and a five-bill page cost 21, the four extra being exactly those sums. Measured on the running product: the 81-bill demo page answers in 0.35s, which extrapolates to about 4s for the PO's 1,000-row page. Nothing saw it because every existing caller is a bill run or one account's screen, where the cost is per account and small; a partner page is the first caller that asks for a thousand accounts at once.
prevention: A batched allocation read for the whole cohort inside prior_position_for_account, the way billing already batches locked_bill_totals_for_accounts. Lane C's own three shared reads are asserted constant-cost by test_this_waves_shared_reads_are_made_once_per_page_not_once_per_bill; that case deliberately does NOT assert a flat total, and says why, so this defect is not pinned green by somebody else's test.

title: seams/payments.COLLECTABLE_STATUSES names two payment statuses that do not exist
surface: apps/integrations/seams/payments.py — the queryset behind GET /partner/v1/payments
escape_reason: The tuple reads ('posted','deposited','cleared','settled') and payments.models.PAYMENT_STATUSES is ('processing','cleared','failed','reversed','posted'). So deposited and settled match no row and never have; the filter is correct by accident and the comment above it - only money that actually settled is handed over - describes a vocabulary this product does not have. Nothing can see it: an IN clause with a value that never occurs is not an error, and a reader taking the tuple as the definition of settled money would believe two states are served that cannot be. Found by writing paymentPayType, which publishes the real five.
prevention: Derive the tuple from payments.models.PAYMENT_STATUSES rather than typing it, or assert membership in a test - the same discipline reference.py already keeps for every closed vocabulary it publishes.

title: Lane C moved a sibling lane's scratch git worktree by taking the same path under /tmp/claude-0
surface: /tmp/claude-0/baseline — a scratch worktree, not a repo path
escape_reason: Law 11 and law 12 are about the SHARED REPO working tree and say to dispatch each lane into its own git worktree, which lane C did. Neither says anything about the scratch directory the worktree is CREATED IN, and /tmp/claude-0 is shared by every lane in the container. A sibling already had a worktree at /tmp/claude-0/baseline, checked out at 17d5617c; lane C ran git worktree add on the same path, got fatal: already exists, and then - reading that as its own half-made worktree - ran git checkout -f inside it, moving a sibling's tree 400-odd commits under a test run. It was noticed within minutes only because ps showed two other lanes waiting on /tmp/claude-0/gates_mine.txt and gates_base.txt, which are the same collision one file along. Restored to 17d5617c, sibling's untracked files untouched, and lane C moved to a uniquely named path.
prevention: Name a scratch path after the lane, never after its purpose: /tmp/claude-0/lanec-baseline-do-not-touch rather than /tmp/claude-0/baseline. And read a fatal: already exists from git worktree add as evidence that somebody else is there, never as a leftover of your own.

title: A KEY ISSUED WHILE SANDBOX IS SELECTED LANDS ON THE PRODUCTION CONNECTION. Every write route on a connector resolves 'production first, else the only row' and takes no environment at all, so a clerk setting up a sandbox is handed a key that opens production.
surface: 06-backend/apps/integrations/services.py connection_for() / _connected_or_refuse() — POST and DELETE /integrations/{key}/key, /test, /credential, /credential/rollback and the disconnect all go through it

title: THE PARTNER APIS CARRY THE UTILITY IN THE PATH, WHICH THE BLUEPRINT FORBIDS BY NAME. All five partner routes are mounted as /api/{utility}/partner/v1/... The blueprint's Rule 1 is titled 'the tenant never appears in a partner URL' and its diagram is key to connection to tenant to app.tenant_id set to RLS does the isolating. The lane that built the route table deviated deliberately and recorded the deviation, reasoning that BR-TEN-003 reads the tenant from the path and that with no tenant context RLS FORCE returns zero rows for the credential lookup for a valid key as much as an invalid one, so the door would be incapable of passing. That reasoning has the order backwards and the blueprint answers it in the same table: resolve the key, set app.tenant_id FROM THE CONNECTION, then query, and RLS FORCE does the rest. The same row names the hazard the deviation creates - a tenant in the URL tempts somebody to set app.tenant_id from user input, which is the one thing that rule exists to prevent.
surface: 06-backend/apps/integrations/partner_api.py PARTNER_PREFIX and the five url patterns, plus erp_aclarian.py served_path if it carries the segment

title: A lane wrote its files into a SIBLING'S worktree because 'git worktree add' failed inside a pipeline and set -e could not see it
surface: 10-scripts (lane push procedure) — scratchpad/wt2, a stale worktree at fdcd0268 owned by another lane
introduced_in: 2026-09-16, while re-deriving DEF-INT-5528 onto a moved tip
escape_reason: The guard was written as 'git worktree add ... 2>&1 | tail -1' under set -e. A pipeline's exit status is its LAST command, so tail's 0 masked git's failure and the script carried on into a directory it had not created. Nothing downstream could tell: cd succeeded, cp succeeded, i18n_fanin succeeded, and the numstat that followed looked merely unfamiliar rather than wrong. No gate or test runs against another lane's worktree, so nothing in this repo could have caught it.
prevention: Never put a creating command in a pipeline under set -e. Assert the postcondition instead of trusting the exit code: refuse if the target directory already exists, create it, then verify 'git -C <wt> rev-parse HEAD' equals the intended sha before writing one byte. Restore is 'git show <sha>:<path> > <path>' per file with the mode re-set from git ls-tree — never git checkout, which law 11 bans and which would also take the owning lane's files.

title: The access log shows every utility's partner reads, because the query names a provider key instead of a tenant
surface: 06-backend/apps/integrations/partner_api.py:1264 access_log — GET /api/{utility}/integrations/{key}/access-log, screen S142 Who has been reading

A provider key is a string every utility on that connector shares, so with two utilities both on Aclarian it narrows the query by nothing; it READS like a connection narrowing, which is why four reviews passed over it. Nothing caught it because RLS FORCE scopes it on PostgreSQL (measured 2026-09-17: under one utility's context the unscoped query returned that utility's one row with the other's two present) while the whole test suite runs on in-memory SQLite, which has no row-level security at all (config/settings/test.py hardcodes it, CLAUDE.md law 14). So the leak was invisible to every test on every machine, and the product's tenant isolation on this read rested on ONE guard where this module's own house style (runners/serve.py::_connection_for) argues at length for two.
fixed_commit: 2.287.6 395f923ed (the four unscoped reads; the PO's own sighting is NOT explained by it and is now DEF-INT-5611)

Proved RED through run_gates' registry path on all four sites before the fix. tests/test_def_int_5568_partner_tenancy.py proves it on the DEFAULT SQLite suite deliberately, because that is the only vendor where the query's own scoping is observable.

title: The credential expiry sweep read every utility's credentials while its own docstring claimed it read one utility's

title: A CONNECTOR CANNOT BE BOTH DIRECTIONS: auth.mode IS ONE VALUE PER MANIFEST AND A KEY IS ISSUED ONLY WHERE IT READS they_hold_ours. PO 2026-09-17, verbatim: 'remember Invoice Cloud is both direction' — we dial InvoiceCloud to charge a card (we hold THEIR merchant secret) and InvoiceCloud dials us to read customers, bills and payments (they hold a key WE issued). Those are the two values of Manifest.auth.mode and a manifest declares exactly one. pay_invoicecloud declares we_hold_theirs, and machine_auth._partner_manifest raises BizError BR-INT-053 REFUSAL_NOT_A_PARTNER_CONNECTION on any manifest whose mode is not they_hold_ours, so 'Generate a key' is refused and the partner half can never be credentialled. Setting the mode the other way breaks the card half instead: the modal's signIn mode, the connect field slot and every adapter that presents a merchant secret read the same value. There is no third value and no per-operation override. ⚠ AND THE SET-UP SCREEN ALREADY DISAGREES WITH THE SERVER ABOUT IT: ConnectorSetupPage weIssueTheKey is (auth.mode === they_hold_ours || issuedField !== null), so a manifest carrying an issued_key field under we_hold_theirs DRAWS the key panel over a door that refuses — a live control over a dead endpoint, which is hard-won law 2's mirror image.

escape_reason: Every manifest that has ever existed runs in ONE direction, so a one-value auth.mode has never been wrong and no test could have been written for a case the product had no example of. The registry refuses a great deal at load — a bad codec, a missing idempotency mode, a reply before authenticate — but it cannot refuse a manifest for failing to describe a relationship nobody had yet asked it to describe. The front end's weIssueTheKey already carries an OR that tolerates the mixed case, which means one half of the product had quietly started allowing for it while the server had not.
fixed_commit: CR-111-BRC04 2.291.0 (the SYMPTOM only: pay_invoicecloud_partner is the reading half and a key can now be issued. The CAUSE stands - Manifest.auth is still ONE mode, one connector still cannot hold both credentials, and ConnectorSetupPage.weIssueTheKey is still wider than the server's check. What is owed is BR-INT-077 and it is a separate change with its own CR.)
prevention: When a vendor is onboarded, ask which DIRECTIONS the relationship runs in before asking what it does, and check that the manifest model can express the answer. Where a screen's predicate is WIDER than the server's for the same question (here: an OR on the field set against a strict equality on the mode), that difference is a defect in waiting and should be reconciled in the commit that introduces it, not left as a tolerance.

surface: 07-frontend/src/features/integrations/ConnectorSetupPage.tsx
escape_reason: Two misses, neither visible to any check. title: A field retired from a manifest leaves its values in integration_connection.config and freezes every later PATCH on that connection
surface: 06-backend/apps/integrations/services.py update_connection
escape_reason: update_connection merged the STORED config into the supplied changes and validated the merge, and validate_fields refuses any name the manifest does not declare. CR-110-BRC04 wave A retired 'scopes' and 'client_id' from the five ERP manifests and left their VALUES at rest, so PATCH /integrations/erp_aclarian answered 422 integrations.field.unknown for two fields the caller never sent, permanently. Nothing could see it: the suite's fixtures build configs from CURRENT manifests, so no test has a retired key at rest, and the refusal is correct code operating on rotten data. It was found only by driving the real endpoint against the demo tenant.
prevention: update_connection now prunes the STORED half to what the manifest still declares before merging, and does NOT prune the supplied half - an unknown name a caller sends is still refused by name and a secret still cannot come this way. tests/test_us_int_002_connect.py asserts BOTH directions in one case, because a test proving only the prune would pass over a validator that had stopped working. The general lesson: retiring a manifest field is a data change as well as a code change.

title: DRF RESERVES THE QUERY PARAMETER format, SO ?format=csv WAS ANSWERED BY THE FRAMEWORK WITH A 404 - THE SAME 404 THAT IS THIS SURFACE'S REFUSAL. api_settings.URL_FORMAT_OVERRIDE is 'format', so DRF reads that parameter as a request for a RENDERER before the view body runs. Only JSONRenderer and BrowsableAPIRenderer are registered, csv matches neither, and DRF raises NotFound. The CSV renderer itself was correct and so was the view's branch; the framework answered first, so the code existed and no request could reach it - hard-won law 2 arriving through a framework default. WHAT IT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED AS: a partner asking for CSV receives the five-word refusal that a stolen key receives, reads it as 'your key is bad', and goes to look at their credentials for a parameter that is in their integration document. That is exactly the confusion _not_yet_served exists to avoid. FIXED in the same wave by PartnerCsvRenderer, a negotiation entry registered on every partner view; the view still returns a plain HttpResponse built by partner_csv.render from the same shaped records the JSON branch would have serialised, so render() is never called and the two serialisations cannot drift.
surface: 06-backend/apps/integrations/partner_api.py - PARTNER_RENDERERS / PartnerCsvRenderer, and the ten partner views that now carry @renderer_classes
found_in: the CR-111 lane, 2026-09-17, calling GET /api/partner/v1/customers?format=csv for real after twelve unit tests of the renderer were green
introduced_in: this wave — found before it shipped, filed because the escape reason is the durable part
escape_reason: TWELVE UNIT TESTS OF THE RENDERER WERE GREEN AND NOT ONE OF THEM CALLED THE ROUTE. partner_csv.render is a pure function over dicts, so every case about headers, cells, line rows and paging passed while the address they describe was a 404. Nothing in this repository reads a framework default: no gate asks which renderers DRF has registered, and no gate reads rendered output at all (hard-won law 6). It was found by calling the surface for real, which is the only thing that could have found it.
prevention: When a feature is reached by a QUERY PARAMETER, check the parameter name against the framework's reserved set before choosing it - DRF reserves 'format' by default and Django reserves nothing, so the collision is invisible unless looked for. More generally: a pure-function renderer proved by unit tests is not a proved endpoint. Every new representation of an existing route needs one case that calls the route and asserts the Content-Type, which is the case that found this one.

title: GET /api/partner/v1/bill-download IS REGISTERED, ROUTED AND UNREACHABLE BY EVERY KEY THAT EXISTS: NO MANIFEST DECLARES serve_document. The route is built, mounted through _with_utility_from_key with the rest, and covered by tests. It needs the serve_document operation in the caller's key scope, and a key's scope is drawn from its manifest's own operations - so a connector that does not DECLARE serve_document can never grant it. None of the twenty-eight does. The connector that would is Invoice Cloud's, and it is blocked on DEF-INT-5574 (a manifest declares ONE auth.mode and Invoice Cloud runs in both directions). So today every call to bill-download is refused OPERATION_NOT_IN_SCOPE and the caller gets the ordinary five-word refusal, indistinguishable from a bad key. NOT A BUG IN THE ROUTE - the route behaves correctly and the refusal is right. It is a capability with no door into it, recorded so that nobody reads the green tests as evidence that a partner can download a bill. A SECOND FACT FOUND WHILE PROVING IT, worth keeping: a credential scoped to an operation its manifest does not declare makes services.start_run raise, so the route answers 500 rather than a refusal. That state is unreachable in the product because a real scope comes from the manifest, but it is why the test fixture registers a whole probe connector instead of widening a scope.
surface: 06-backend/apps/integrations/partner_api.partner_bill_download - 06-backend/apps/integrations/partner_urls.PARTNER_ROUTES - 06-backend/apps/integrations/manifests/ (none of the twenty-eight declares serve_document)
found_in: the CR-111 lane, 2026-09-17, building GET /api/partner/v1/bill-download and finding no key in the product that could call it
introduced_in: this wave declared the address; the cause is DEF-INT-5574, which blocks the manifest that would declare the operation
escape_reason: NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY ASKS WHETHER A DECLARED ROUTE HAS A CONNECTOR THAT CAN CALL IT. SERVED_ROUTES names the operation each address needs and no gate compares that set against the operations the twenty-eight manifests actually declare, so an address can be added for an operation nobody has, and every test of it passes by granting the scope in a fixture. It is the mirror of the hold-expiry problem hard-won law 2 already names: there, a door pointed at a screen that had not landed; here, a screen landed with no door pointing at it.
prevention: A test that goes RED the day the hold expires, written in the same commit as the hold - test_no_manifest_declares_serve_document_yet asserts that NO manifest declares the operation and names the first one that does, which is the signal to delete the probe fixture and point the cases at the real key. The durable version is a gate: every operation named in partner_api.SERVED_ROUTES must be declared by at least one manifest, or the address is unreachable. That gate is recommended and not built here, because the answer it would demand is DEF-INT-5574's ruling and a red gate with no lawful fix is worse than a filed row.

title: OPENING BALANCE ON THE PARTNER CUSTOMER LIST IS TWO STATEMENTS PER ACCOUNT, SO A THOUSAND-ROW PAGE WOULD HAVE COST 2,000 EXTRA. billing.open_balance.open_balances_for_accounts is batched on billing's own half and PER ACCOUNT on the seam half - its docstring says so: 'Billing's half is ONE query for the whole cohort; the seam is then asked per account, because payments' and customers' reads are theirs and this module does not reach past them to batch what they have not published as a batch (B1).' That is billing being RIGHT about the module boundary, and it makes the read unsuitable for a list. Measured: 10 statements for two accounts and 14 for four. On the largest utility this product models that is 2,000 extra statements a page and 80,000 over a 40,000-account walk. FIXED IN THE SAME WAVE, not by batching: opening_balance and remote_plan_id are served on GET /partner/v1/consumer-info - a lookup BY NUMBER, which is where the partner's document puts them and where remote_plan_id already belonged by PO ruling - and NOT on GET /partner/v1/customers, which stays at four statements a page whatever the page holds. THE RESIDUAL IS RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: consumer-info accepts many consumer_numbers, so a partner naming a thousand still pays the per-account cost. It is bounded by the page and by a route nobody walks, and the durable fix is a batched balance read published by billing's own seam.
surface: 06-backend/apps/integrations/seams/customers.py page_facts(detail=) / balance_map / as_record(with_detail=) — 06-backend/apps/billing/open_balance.py open_balances_for_accounts
found_in: test_cr110_phase2_partner_customers.py::test_a_page_costs_the_same_number_of_statements_whatever_it_holds — the existing N+1 case, which went red at '10 statements for two accounts and 14 for four'
introduced_in: this wave — caught before it shipped by a case a previous lane wrote for exactly this
escape_reason: IT DID NOT ESCAPE - it was caught, and the row exists to record WHAT caught it, because that is the reusable part. test_a_page_costs_the_same_number_of_statements_whatever_it_holds asserts that two accounts and four accounts cost the SAME number of statements, which is the only form of the assertion a slow implementation cannot satisfy; an absolute number would have gone red and taught a lane to raise it. Nothing else could have seen this: the demo tenant holds twelve accounts, every functional test passes on a per-row read, and no gate counts statements. DEF-2723 is the same shape one module along and is why the case existed.
prevention: When a field is added to a payload that pages, measure the statement count BEFORE the field is wired, not after - and read the batched selector's own docstring, because open_balances_for_accounts states its per-account half in plain words and the cost was knowable without running anything. More generally: a selector named *_for_accounts is not necessarily one query, and the plural in the name is about the ANSWER rather than about the work.

title: THE ONE GUARD THAT WOULD NOTICE A NEW WORLD-READABLE ADDRESS HAS BEEN RED SINCE 2026-09-16, AND BOTH ITS TESTS WERE RED AT ONCE. tests/test_be_default_authentication.py PUBLIC_ROUTES names the five partner addresses as api/{tenant}/partner/v1/... DEF-INT-5546 moved them to api/partner/v1/... the day before - PO 2026-09-16, 'we agreed not to use utility names in partner apis' - and this list was not moved with them. DATED FROM THE HISTORY RATHER THAN ASSUMED: git log on the file shows PUBLIC_ROUTES last moved in c2ef372f (CR-110 phase 2 waves 0-1) and DEF-INT-5546 landed in 68aadd5d after it. WHAT IT COSTS, AND IT IS WORSE THAN A RED LINE: with the spellings wrong the five real addresses match nothing in the list, so test_..._every_route_reads_the_session_or_is_named_public reports them as an unexpected public surface, AND test_..._grants_nothing_every_private_route_still_gates reports them as ungated AllowAny routes. Both halves of the file are red, and this file is the ONE guard that would notice a sixth world-readable address appearing. A guard that is red is a guard nobody reads. FIXED for the partner half in this wave - the ten real spellings plus the two CR-111 addresses, all with and without a trailing slash. A SECOND, SEPARATE RED IS LEFT ALONE AND NAMED: 58 customer-portal routes come back unclassified because they declare PortalSessionAuthentication, a third authenticator class this sweep does not know about. That is a different lane's and is not touched here.
surface: 06-backend/tests/test_be_default_authentication.py PUBLIC_ROUTES and the two sweep tests
found_in: the CR-111 lane, 2026-09-17, when adding two partner addresses made test_be_default_authentication red and the failure named 97 routes rather than 2
introduced_in: 68aadd5d DEF-INT-5546 (2026-09-16) took the utility out of the partner URLs; PUBLIC_ROUTES last moved in c2ef372f, BEFORE it, and was not moved with them
escape_reason: IT WAS RED AND NOBODY READ IT - the exact shape hard-won law 7 names as the one that dominated 2026-09-05. DEF-INT-5546's own lane ran its own suites and this file is not among the ones its lifecycle block lists; the failure appears only when the whole backend suite runs, where 58 other unclassified portal routes were already printing and a true new failure had the protective colouring of a known one. Nothing else could see it: no gate compares PUBLIC_ROUTES against the URLconf, and the list is by design a hand-maintained statement of intent.
prevention: When a route MOVES, grep for its old path string across the tests as part of the move - the spelling is the join key and nothing enforces it. The durable fix is to derive the check from the URLconf and assert the COUNT and the OWNING MODULE of the public routes rather than their literal paths, so a rename cannot silently empty the list; that is a change to a security guard and belongs in its own commit with its own red proof, not in a wave adding a connector.

title: A connector's Service address is kind=host, so a real ArcGIS URL with a path cannot be typed into the product

introduced_in: US-INT-042 wave M, 2026-09-06 — gis_esri declared base_url as kind=host from the day it was written

The product accepted the useless value and refused the only working one.

title: Nineteen kind=host fields ship a seeded default their own validator rejects - a box pre-filled with the one value it cannot save
surface: 06-backend/apps/integrations/manifests/*.py - every base_url/tile_url default=, measured over all 28 connectors

The registry already validated a default for exactly one kind (a select's default must be one of its options) and for no other, so nothing ever ran a field's own validator over its own default. The two halves lived apart: the code that JUDGES a value is in adapters/base.py and the code that WRITES one is in the manifests, and no test crossed between them. 19 of 19 scheme-bearing defaults were rejected by their own form.

title: live_calls.provision() writes a config services.connect() refuses, so neither live call can be provisioned at all

It was never called: DEF-INT-4287 records that wiring provision() into tenant provisioning is OWED and not done, so the one function that would have exercised it does not run, and the defect sat behind an unwired caller. Law 7's incapable of passing, hidden by law 2's built-not-wired.

title: pay_invoicecloud.base_url is the twentieth Service address and is still kind=host with a default its own form rejects

introduced_in: CR-110-BRC04 wave C, 2026-09-16 - same sweep as DEF-INT-5590

Nineteen sibling fields moved to kind=url on 2026-09-17; this one was left because another lane held manifests/pay_invoicecloud.py open for CR-111-BRC04 at that moment, and editing a file a sibling is mid-edit in is how law 11's revert-by-subtraction happens. Until then registry.SEEDED_DEFAULT_EXEMPTIONS carries the single named, dated entry that keeps the load-time guard from refusing the connector, and test_the_one_exemption_is_still_the_one_we_signed_up_for goes RED the day the manifest is fixed and names the entry to delete - hard-won law 2: a hold with no test that fires when it expires is a promise nobody is keeping.

title: The connector set-up screen says Check the highlighted fields and never highlighted one - error: undefined was hardcoded into every field slot
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/integrations/ConnectorSetupPage.tsx - both RENDER call sites; all 28 connectors

The banner integrations.refusal.fields reads 'Check the highlighted fields.' and the page passed a literal error: undefined into RENDER, so a clerk got a sentence at the foot of a nine-box form and no clue which box. tsc was satisfied - undefined is a legal value for an optional prop - and no gate in this repo reads rendered output, so it was found only by pasting a bad value into the running product and looking (law 6).

title: A refused field never draws a red border - .input's border shorthand beats the layered border-danger-500 utility
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/integrations/ConnectModal.tsx INVALID constant; .input in components/FormModal.css; every refused field in the integrations UI
introduced_in: e7750e9d, CR-069 wave M - INVALID has been 'input w-full border-danger-500' since it was written
escape_reason: The class IS applied and the utility IS emitted - measured in the built stylesheet - so every check that reads markup or CSS presence passes. .input declares the BORDER SHORTHAND (border: 1px solid var(--color-divider)) in an unlayered stylesheet, and an unlayered class beats any Tailwind utility layer whatever the specificity, so border-color loses every time. Only getComputedStyle on the running page shows it, and no gate in this repo reads rendered output.

Filed with the measurement - getComputedStyle borderColor is unchanged between a valid and a refused field - so the next lane can reproduce it in one command.

title: Field.default is read by nothing - the seeded phase-1 addresses are dead data, and the docstring says provisioning writes them
surface: 06-backend/apps/integrations/registry.py Field.default; the 19 manifests that declare one; the connector set-up form
introduced_in: CR-110-BRC04 wave C, 2026-09-16 - the field and its 19 values landed together with no reader
escape_reason: Hard-won law 1: a comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee. Field.default's own docstring says it is 'the value provisioning writes into the connection's config when nobody has typed one', and grep finds NO reader outside registry.validate() - live_calls.LIVE_CALL_DEFAULTS is a separate hardcoded dict of two entries, not derived from it, and the set-up form does not pre-fill from it either. title: THE DEFECT REGISTER HOLDS NINETEEN NUMBER COLLISIONS ACROSS MODULE SEGMENTS, AND THE NEWEST PAIR WAS TAKEN TODAY BY TWO LANES WHOSE ARITHMETIC WAS BOTH RIGHT. DEF-INT-5618 and DEF-GOV-5618 were filed minutes apart on 2026-09-17; allocate.py --verify said 5618 was still free to each of them, truthfully, because it reads the pushed world and neither row was pushed yet. The STRING is unique and the NUMBER is not — which is exactly the hazard CLAUDE.md spells out for CR-<nnn>-<BRCnn> ('the suffix is provenance rather than the thing that makes it unique... a number is what a person says out loud and cites from a business rule') and which nothing in this family guards. Counted at the branch tip: 19 numbers carry two different ids — 5618, 5492, 5137, 4710, 4512, 4497, 4256, 4224 and eleven more. G17 fails a duplicate CR NUMBER even when the suffixes differ; there is no equivalent for DEF, and G17 is itself already red in the standing 50, so it could not have warned about either. NOT PROPOSING A RENUMBER: both rows of every pair are pushed and cited, and respelling them would move every citation at once, which is the mass shared-file rewrite CLAUDE.md law 11 exists to prevent.
surface: 12-governance/10-defect-log.csv (19 colliding numbers) - 10-scripts/file_defect.py and 10-scripts/allocate.py (both read the PUSHED world, so two unpushed lanes get the same answer) - 10-scripts/gates/g17_duplicate_ids.py (guards the CR family and not this one)
introduced_in: 2026-09-03, the ruling that added the module segment OQ-<MOD>-nnnn / DEF-<MOD>-nnnn — one running number across the register was the stated intent and nothing enforces it; the collisions have accumulated since
escape_reason: A DUPLICATE NUMBER IN A 3,177-ROW REGISTER READS AS A REGISTER, NOT AS AN ERROR — DEF-1787's own words. Every id is unique as a STRING, so every uniqueness check that exists passes; the thing that is not unique is the number a person says out loud, and nothing compares those. allocate.py --verify is honest and cannot help: it says so itself ('it CANNOT reserve'), because nothing writes to the remote and two lanes calling it in the same second still collide. And G17, which does exactly this comparison for CR numbers, is in the standing 50 failing gates, so even the family it does cover is unguarded in practice.
fixed_commit: 1c6d052f8 (2.351.10) - the 13 carried numbers of DEF-GOV-4405 remain
prevention: Extend G17's duplicate-NUMBER check to the DEF and OQ families — it is the same comparison on a different column and the gate already exists, which is this repo's own lesson about reaching for the tool that owns the job. ⚠ Ask what would make it pass wrongly: a check keyed on the whole id string passes over every one of these 19, so it must strip the module segment first with (?:[A-Z]{3}-)? and compare the digits. And get G17 green, or the check is a paragraph rather than a guard. The 19 existing pairs stay as they are and the gate must therefore be a RATCHET — refuse a NEW collision, count the existing ones — or it can never go green and will join the standing 50 it came from.

title: THE WEBHOOK SIGNATURE VERIFIER IS BUILT FOR A SHARED SECRET AND SENDGRID'S SIGNED EVENT WEBHOOK IS ALMOST CERTAINLY ASYMMETRIC - if it is ECDSA, the one connector this style was built for cannot use it, and the security argument the design rests on does not hold for a public key
surface: apps/integrations/inbound.py verifier; registry.SIGNATURE_ALGORITHMS
found_in: 2026-09-17, raised by the lane that built it and confirmed as a dispatcher error: the brief I wrote said 'HMAC over timestamp+body' and that is an inference I made, not something the PO's setup guide states
introduced_in: the lane 4 brief of 2026-09-17, written by the dispatching session
escape_reason: NOTHING IN THE REPO COULD CATCH IT BECAUSE NO SENDGRID MANIFEST EXISTS YET - the verifier is correct for the algorithm it was told to implement, its 46 tests pass, and the wrong algorithm is only discoverable against the real provider. THE EVIDENCE IT IS WRONG IS IN THE PO'S OWN SETUP GUIDE AND I MISREAD IT: the guide says 'Turn on Signed Event Webhook then copy the Verification Key'. A shared secret is called a secret; a VERIFICATION key is the word for the PUBLIC half of a key pair. The lane that built it flagged the same doubt unprompted and did the right thing - SIGNATURE_ALGORITHMS is the single-element tuple ('hmac_sha256',) with test_signature_algorithms_are_symmetric_only pinning it, so the day somebody adds an algorithm the suite goes red and the question is asked rather than assumed. IT ALSO BREAKS THE DESIGN'S SECURITY ARGUMENT, which is the part that matters: verify() does not answer yes, it returns WHAT THE CALLER PROVED KNOWLEDGE OF, and resolve_caller then applies all six guards to that value. That is literally true for a shared-secret HMAC and FALSE for a public key, which identifies without proving possession.
prevention: Establish SendGrid's actual algorithm from their documentation BEFORE the sendgrid manifest is written - this environment cannot reach their docs, the PO has the account. If it is ECDSA, the asymmetric path is a design question and not a word added to a tuple: the verifier must stop returning a proved-knowledge value and instead identify the connection another way, which is the one thing the current shape deliberately refuses to do. Postmark is unaffected - its basic-auth password is a key WE minted, so it is a transport carrying a presented key and the argument holds.

title: THE NOTIFICATION DISPATCHER SUITE HAS 14 OF 18 CASES RED AND NOBODY HAS FILED IT - the cycle selects zero rows, and two lanes independently invented a cause
surface: backend
introduced_in: unknown; red at cd902f046 and earlier
escape_reason: tests/test_us_not_002_dispatcher.py reports 14 failed / 4 passed and has done so since at least cd902f046, the commit before this session's work. Nothing had a register row for it. The failure is silent rather than loud: no exception, no error - dispatch_cycle simply selects zero rows, so every assertion reads 'assert 0 == 1' or an empty batch list, which names no cause at all. THAT SILENCE IS WHAT MADE IT SPREAD: two lanes on 2026-09-17 each read a plausible cause into it and reported it in good faith. One attributed it to the email_bulk->sendgrid rename being mid-flight in the shared tree (disproved: every remaining email_bulk reference is a comment, and the suite fails identically at cd902f046 where the rename does not exist). The other - this session - attributed it to Redis being absent, on the strength of a kombu ConnectionError in one traceback (disproved: starting Redis changed nothing, still 14 failed). A third theory, that the integrations seam no longer publishes its adapter, is also disproved: provider_seam resolves 'dispatch_outbound_batch' and that function exists at apps/integrations/seams/notifications.py:327. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: red at cd902f046 with an identical count, so it is caused by none of 2026-09-17's work; not Redis; not the connector rename; not a missing seam attribute. WHAT IS NOT: whether the PRODUCT selects nothing (in which case no notification is dispatched at all and this is catastrophic) or the SUITE's fixture no longer sets up a dispatchable row (in which case 14 checks are dead and the product is fine). Those two readings are opposite and nothing here distinguishes them.
prevention: Establish which of the two readings is true FIRST, by driving one message through a dispatch cycle in a browser or a shell against a seeded tenant rather than through this fixture - the suite is the thing under suspicion, so it cannot be the instrument. Then either fix the product or fix the fixture. SEPARATELY, and this is the durable half: a check that fails by selecting nothing reports 'assert 0 == 1', which names no cause and invites a theory. Where a selection predicate is the thing under test, assert WHY the row was excluded (held, inactive channel, quiet hours, no template, suppressed) rather than only that the count is wrong - a failure that names the excluding clause cannot be misattributed three times by three readers.

title: THE BLUEPRINT SEARCH COMMAND CLAUDE.md PRESCRIBES CANNOT SEE A PDF WHOSE NAME HOLDS A NON-ASCII CHARACTER, AND ONE OF THE EIGHT DOES. CLAUDE.md tells every lane to check for a drawing with: git ls-tree -r --name-only <ref> | grep -i 'pdf$'. git QUOTES any path containing a byte outside ASCII, so that line ends with a double quote rather than with pdf and the grep skips it. Measured at 668a8507 across every ref: the command returns SEVEN blueprints and the branch holds EIGHT - '05-prototype/03 SMARTBillHub - Meter Reads blueprint.pdf' is invisible to it because its name contains an em dash. git -c core.quotePath=false ls-tree -r --name-only <ref> | grep -i 'pdf$' returns all eight.
surface: CLAUDE.md (the r10 pointer paragraph, and the Screen IDs section's blueprint instruction) - every lane that ran the command as written
found_in: the DEF-NOT-5637 blocked-addresses screen lane, 2026-09-17, which ran the prescribed command, then ran a per-file text extraction over 05-prototype/*.pdf and got a file the command had never mentioned
introduced_in: the DEF-GOV-5248 amendment of 2026-09-14, which added the search command to CLAUDE.md - it was correct for the seven ASCII-named blueprints that existed and silently wrong for the one that did not
escape_reason: A COMMAND IN A DOCUMENT IS A CLAIM NOTHING RE-CHECKS - this file's own general lesson, in the file that states it. The command runs, exits 0 and prints a plausible list, so it is indistinguishable from a complete one: the failure mode is an ABSENCE, and CLAUDE.md hard rule 8's closing lesson already says an absence is invisible to every check this repo has. title: GET /premises 500s ON A REAL TENANT: premises_rollup runs ONE QUERY PER UNIT through a cross-module seam, the gunicorn worker is killed mid-statement, and the connection is left unusable
surface: backend
introduced_in: present since premises_rollup was written
escape_reason: Reported from the deployed build with a full traceback: GET /api/{tenant}/premises answers 500 on a tenant with 108 premises. ROOT CAUSE READ FROM THE CODE, not inferred from the message. metering/selectors.py:533 premises_rollup computes the header's vacant count as 'sum(1 for unit in units if occupancy_of(unit) == "vacant")'. occupancy_of (selectors.py:1204) is DERIVED by design - BR-MET-036 says there is no stored occupancy column - so each call goes seams.active_account_for_unit -> customers.services:5114 -> customers.selectors:639 -> occupying_accounts_for_unit(...).first(), which is A DATABASE QUERY PER UNIT, crossing a module seam every time. One header count therefore costs N round trips. THE TRACEBACK SHOWS THE CONSEQUENCE RATHER THAN THE CAUSE, and reading it the other way round is the trap: the visible exception is psycopg 'sending query failed: another command is already in progress' raised from core/tenancy.py:188 clear_current_tenant, but four frames above it is gunicorn/workers/base.py:199 handle_abort -> sys.exit(1). THE WORKER WAS KILLED ON A TIMEOUT MID-STATEMENT; the tenancy middleware's cleanup then tried to reuse a connection abandoned half way through a query. So the 'another command in progress' error is the aftermath, and anyone who fixes THAT fixes nothing. Nothing caught it because the suite's fixtures carry a handful of units, where N round trips are imperceptible, and no test asserts a query COUNT for this path - the cost is invisible until a real utility's data arrives, and it grows with every premises they add.
prevention: Count vacancy in ONE aggregate query rather than per unit - a single Exists/LEFT JOIN over occupying accounts - and keep it behind the seam so metering still never reads customers' tables directly. THEN THE DURABLE HALF: assert the QUERY COUNT, not the answer. A test that pins premises_rollup to a fixed number of queries and runs it against two different unit counts fails the moment anyone reintroduces a per-row lookup, which an assertion about the returned figure never can. Audit occupancy_of's other callers for the same loop before closing.

A test whose subject is the DATABASE and whose assertion reads a Python list is measuring Python. And run the PostgreSQL files: a file nobody can execute is a file whose false pass nobody can see.

title: THE LIVE ADDRESS SEARCH SENDS A GEOCODER QUERY TO AN ARCGIS FEATURESERVER - q= and limit= where the service requires where= - so against Ann Arbor it is refused on every keystroke

introduced_in: CR-069 wave M, 2026-09-06 - _url has built a geocoder query since it was written
escape_reason: DEF-INT-5618 FIXED THE PARSER AND LEFT THE QUESTION. That defect found candidate_from unable to read an ArcGIS ANSWER and gave the adapter gis_layer.row_from_feature. Nothing looked at the REQUEST. _url builds '<base>?q=<typed>&f=json&limit=9' - a geocoder's parameters. An ArcGIS /query endpoint requires 'where' (or objectIds) and names its page size 'resultRecordCount'; with neither it answers an error, which _refuse_if_the_city_said_no correctly turns into a refusal, so a clerk in Ann Arbor would see the City refusing every keystroke. AND THE CODE THAT DOES IT RIGHT IS IN THE REPO WITH NO CALLER: gis_layer._query_url sends where/outFields/outSR/returnGeometry/resultOffset/resultRecordCount/orderByFields, gis_layer.layer_base strips a trailing /query so the PO's own address works, and gis_search.where_clause builds the LIKE with the single quote doubled for an O'Brien Court. This is DEF-INT-5618's exact shape one step upstream - the module that understands the City is unreachable from the screen and the module the screen reaches does not understand the City. NOT PROVED AGAINST ANN ARBOR AND CANNOT BE FROM HERE: the egress proxy refuses a2mapseg.a2gov.org (curl 000; inside Django Tunnel connection failed: 403 Forbidden), so this is read off the two files. Every fixture in the repo answers the geocoder shape, so the adapter is only ever asked questions it can answer.
prevention: Give the adapter gis_layer's query builder as DEF-INT-5618 gave it gis_layer's parser - layer_base + _query_url + gis_search.where_clause, which between them already hold the trailing-/query fix, outSR=4326, the page size and the quote escaping. Then ONE captured FeatureServer round trip as a fixture, request and reply, is what turns every green test on this path into evidence. The general form: a client proved only against fixtures written from the client has not been proved at all - and that is now true of this repo twice on the same file, once for the answer and once for the question.

title: tsc IS RED ON THE PUBLISHED TIP - a sibling's pathspec commit swept up another lane's in-flight interface field, so GisSearchResult requires a property no fixture on the branch sets
surface: 07-frontend/src/api/endpoints.ts::GisSearchResult.ranking_note_key at 475ac6ae6 - 07-frontend/src/features/metering/FindTheAddress.dom.test.tsx::answering() unchanged since 668a8507a
introduced_in: 475ac6ae6, 2026-09-17 - DEF-NOT-5637's blocked-addresses commit
escape_reason: HARD-WON LAW 11 MECHANISM FIVE, EXACTLY AS WRITTEN AND STILL NOT CAUGHT. A pathspec commit takes the WHOLE working-tree content of every path it names, so as well as reverting another lane's change it can PUBLISH one. 475ac6ae6 named endpoints.ts for its own suppressions block and carried out with it a GIS lane's uncommitted 'ranking_note_key: string | null' - a REQUIRED property - while the backend that serves it and the test fixture that constructs it were both still uncommitted in the shared tree. Every check law 11 prescribes passes on it: the file count is right, the author's own change IS present, and nobody reads 100 hunks on a 17,000-line file. The law's own remedy - git show <commit> and confirm every hunk is yours - is the one that would have caught it and is the one that does not scale to this file. THE COST IS THE WHOLE BRANCH: tsc fails on the tip because answering() builds a GisSearchResult without the required field, and tsc is the check every front-end lane runs first, so the next lane to run it inherits a red it did not cause and must date before it can dismiss - which is the trap DEF-CWP-4187 records two lanes falling into in the same words.
prevention: Green again here, because this lane's commit lands both halves - the backend that sets the key and the fixture that supplies it. The habit that would have prevented it is law 11's own last line and nothing else: COMMIT SMALL AND COMMIT OFTEN. An in-flight hunk in a shared tree is a hunk any of six lanes can publish for you, and a large generated file is where the hunk-reading check goes to die. For a file this size, prefer 'git show <commit> -- <that file>' as a SEPARATE read rather than folding it into a whole-commit review, and treat a diff you cannot finish reading as a diff you have not reviewed.

title: --reuse-db KEYS THE SHARED SQLITE TEST DATABASE ON THE MIGRATION DIGEST ALONE - so a sibling lane's in-flight MODEL edit poisons it for every lane and the failure names a table nobody touched
surface: 06-backend/config/settings/test.py DATABASES['default']['TEST']['NAME'] - the digest is over migration FILES only
introduced_in: DEF-GOV-3778's fix, 2026-09-04 - the digest that made --reuse-db work at all
escape_reason: THE SPEED-UP IS REAL AND SO IS THE HOLE IN IT. The test database file is named for a digest of every migration file, so adding or editing a migration rebuilds it automatically - which is the right key for the lane that wrote the migration and the wrong one for everybody else. A sibling mid-wave has the MODEL edited and the migration written, so the digest moves, the database is rebuilt from THEIR schema, and every other lane in the shared checkout inherits it. On 2026-09-17 that produced 'sqlite3.IntegrityError: NOT NULL constraint failed: account_types.tenant_id' on the SETUP of every test in tests/test_us_int_042_gis.py - a GIS file that names no customers table - and the same tree answered 'ProgrammingError: column account_types.tenant_id does not exist' against the dev PostgreSQL, from the opposite direction. BOTH LOOK LIKE THE READER'S OWN BREAKAGE and neither names the lane that caused it. --create-db recovers it and costs 12 minutes on that one file. The trap is law 7's fifth shape: the flag is not lying, it is answering truthfully about a database built from a schema that is nobody's tip.
prevention: Fold the MODEL files into the digest as well as the migrations, or key the file on the checkout AND the git tree hash of apps/*/models.py. Cheaper and available today: dispatch every lane into its own git worktree, which CLAUDE.md law 12 already recommends for a different reason and which gives each lane its own digest path for free. And when a fixture fails on a table your file does not name, suspect the DATABASE before the code - the error is about a schema, not about a test.

title: Per-API keys are deferred: a custom API sends the connection's one credential, not its own
surface: 06-backend/apps/integrations/custom_apis.py; 07-frontend/src/features/integrations/ConnectionDetailPage.tsx (the Add form has no Key field and the table no Key column)

title: The tenant-isolation probe cannot SET ROLE on PostgreSQL 16, so every RLS proof in the repo skips or errors
surface: 06-backend/tests/isolation_helpers.py::rls_probe_role - GRANT "<role>" TO CURRENT_USER
found_in: 2.296.0, measured on PostgreSQL 16.10
introduced_in: DEF-GOV-4036's repair
escape_reason: PostgreSQL 16 split role membership into three options - ADMIN, INHERIT and SET - and SET ROLE now requires the SET option, which a bare GRANT does not always confer. Measured here: pg_auth_members showed admin_option=t, inherit_option=f, SET_OPTION=f, and every case died on 'permission denied to set role'. The fixture then SKIPS with a message about CREATEROLE, so the whole RLS half reads as an environment limitation rather than a bug - which is exactly law 7's 'a declared blind spot with no NUMBER attached is indistinguishable from an empty one'. It is the same class as the NOSUPERUSER trap DEF-GOV-4036 already fixed in this very function: both ways of running it were impossible, in opposite directions.
prevention: One clause: GRANT "<role>" TO CURRENT_USER WITH SET TRUE (and keep ADMIN OPTION). Proved here by granting it by hand: tests/test_us_int_014_pg.py went from 4 passed / 2 errors to 5 PASSED, and tests/test_cr115_custom_apis_pg.py from 1 passed / 3 skipped to 4 PASSED - deny-by-default, cross-tenant invisibility and the WITH CHECK half all really exercised under a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role. NOT fixed here: isolation_helpers.py is shared test infrastructure outside this lane's named scope and four other lanes were running.

title: A LIVE CHARGE CODE'S PRICE MOVES WITH NO REASON, NO VERSION, NO FILING RECORD AND NO LOCK. apps/rating/services.update_charge is 23 lines - validate, write - and the charge code is the ONE place an amount can change (BR-RAT-088: 'the CHARGE CODE owns the base amount; a plan displays it, never defines it', and the plan screen says so in its own words: 'This plan shows it and cannot change it'). So PAPER at $2.00 moved to $5.00 bills $5.00 on every plan carrying it next cycle, and the only trace is an audit_log row that is pruned on a retention schedule. Compare the four neighbours in the same module: a tax refuses the in-place edit outright (BR-RAT-104) and offers a correction row; a published plan bumps its version and REQUIRES a reason (BR-RAT-037); a rate schedule refuses the save entirely; a DISCOUNT - which can only REDUCE a bill - needs submit, approve and activate. The object with the largest blast radius has the least protection of the five.
surface: [backend] 06-backend/apps/rating/services.py update_charge (~:4861) -> PATCH /charges/{id} -> S12/CHG-02 ChargeCodeWizard edit mode; every plan and rate schedule reading the code's amount or its per-size table
found_in: 2.296.0 - the uniform-verbs lane, reading what each of the five priced objects does today after the PO's 'please fix all these'
introduced_in: never built - update_charge has had no immutability guard since US-RAT-008; BR-RAT-035's audit lock guards DELETE and DEACTIVATE and was never extended to the amount
escape_reason: EVERY CHECK IN THE REPO PASSES ON IT, because none of them asks the question. BR-RAT-035's lock is a DELETE lock - selectors.charge_used_by feeds services.delete_charge and the S9 row, and nothing between it and the money fields. BR-RAT-037 is written about 'plan/tariff versions' by name, so a charge code is outside its words and outside every test that cites it. The charge tests assert that an update VALIDATES (duplicate code, formula refused, percent needs a percent) and that it writes an audit row - they assert the write SUCCEEDS, which is the defect. And there is no effective-dated storage on charges at all, so no gate could have compared a before and an after over a window that does not exist.
prevention: The three verbs, stated once for all five priced objects rather than five times differently: EDIT in place while it has never priced anything, CORRECT over the SAME window when the figure recorded was wrong, CHANGE over a NEW window when prices move. Phase A builds the reason + RateChangeLog filing record for a code IN USE; the effective-dated half (verbs 2 and 3 for a charge code) needs storage this table does not have and is filed separately for the PO to size.

title: A DISCOUNT CANNOT BE EDITED AT ALL - NOT EVEN A DRAFT NOBODY HAS SUBMITTED. apps/rating/discount_services.py has create_discount, create_discount_version, submit, approve, activate, retire and suspend, and NO update function of any kind. So a clerk who types -15 where they meant -1.5 on a version that has never been submitted, never been approved and has priced nothing has exactly one route out: draft a SECOND version carrying a change_reason and walk it through submit, approve and activate - three acts and a second person's signature above the tenant's threshold - to fix a typo in something that never existed as far as any customer is concerned. The module's own docstring already names the missing function: DISCOUNT_FIELDS' comment reads 'Every field create_discount / update_discount_version accept', and update_discount_version has never existed. The tax next door edits a draft freely for exactly this reason (correct_tax: 'A DRAFT is not history. It has never priced anything, so there is nothing to preserve and nothing to explain'); so does a draft plan; so does a charge code. The discount is the only one of the five that refuses.
surface: [backend] 06-backend/apps/rating/discount_services.py (no update path) -> no PATCH /discounts/{id}/versions/{vid} route in apps/rating/api.py -> DIS-02 DiscountWizard has no edit door for a drafted version
found_in: 2.296.0 - the uniform-verbs lane, reading what each of the five priced objects does today after the PO's 'please fix all these'
introduced_in: 2026-08-19, when the three lifecycle services were written - the file was built as a state machine and the edit verb was never part of it
escape_reason: AN ABSENCE IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY CHECK THIS REPO HAS (CLAUDE.md hard rule 8's lesson, in a different module). There is no test named after a function that does not exist; G13 asks whether a prop is passed, not whether a verb has a door; and the discount suites drive create -> submit -> approve -> activate in order, which is the path that DOES exist, so the state machine reads as complete precisely because every test walks it end to end. The one place it was written down - DISCOUNT_FIELDS' own comment naming update_discount_version - is a comment claiming a guarantee (law 1), and nothing greps a docstring for a function name.
prevention: The three verbs, stated once for all five priced objects: a draft version that has never been SUBMITTED edits in place with an audit row and no reason (it has priced nothing); a LIVE version is corrected over the same window with a reason and a link; a price CHANGE stays what it already is - a new version through submit/approve/activate, which BR-RAT-077 and BR-RAT-109 govern and which this does not touch.

title: A TYPO IN A PUBLISHED PLAN MINTS A NEW VERSION, SO THE RECORD SAYS THE PRICE CHANGED WHEN IT DID NOT. update_plan is correct as far as it goes - BR-RAT-037 bumps plans.version and writes a rate_change_log row with a required reason - but it has exactly ONE verb for two different acts. A utility that raises the minimum bill from $12.00 to $15.00 and a utility that typed $1500.00 where it meant $15.00 produce the SAME record: v4 supersedes v3, reason attached. The second one is not a new version of the plan, it is the same version stated correctly, and BR-RAT-104 already ruled the distinction next door for taxes in CR-013 part 4's SHARED rules: 'a historic typo is fixed by a documented correction version with a reason', where a correction restates the SAME window and a change gets a new one. Every UnitPlanAssignment snapshots plan_version at assignment (BR-CUS-013), so an inflated version counter is read by rows that outlive the plan.
surface: [backend] 06-backend/apps/rating/services.py update_plan (~:1521) -> PATCH /plans/{id} -> PLN-03 PlanWizard edit mode, PlanDetail's Versions tab, rate_change_log, UnitPlanAssignment.plan_version snapshots

escape_reason: IT IS A MISSING DISTINCTION RATHER THAN A WRONG RESULT, WHICH IS THE ONE SHAPE NO GATE CAN SEE. Every plan test asserts that a published edit bumps the version and demands a reason - all true, all passing, and none of them can ask whether that was the right verb for what the operator was doing. A plan gains CORRECT alongside CHANGE: a correction restates the version already recorded - same version_no, same window - writes its own rate_change_log row carrying the reason, and never bumps the counter, so the assignment snapshots that point at that version keep pointing at it.

title: THE RATE-SCHEDULE REVIEW STEP PROMISES A DATE THE CHARGE CODE CANNOT HOLD. rating.rate.review.baseOwnedNote reads, verbatim: 'Not changing, and it cannot change here. Edit the charge code and every schedule and plan carrying it follows on the same date.' There is no date. The charges table is tenant, code, name, charge_type, service, amount_rule, amount, percent, min_amount, max_amount, gl_account_id and the behaviour flags - no effective_from, no effective_to, no version table - so an edit to a charge code's amount takes effect IMMEDIATELY for every schedule and plan carrying it, on the next bill run, whatever date anybody had in mind. A clerk reading that sentence at 4pm on the 28th and typing next month's price is billing it this month. This is the SCREEN half of DEF-RAT-5712: the missing storage is the same absence, and this row is for the sentence that tells a user it is there.
surface: [frontend] 07-frontend/src/i18n/locales/*.json rating.rate.review.baseOwnedNote (all eleven catalogues) -> RAT-03 rate schedule wizard review step; the same claim in weaker form at rating.planDetail.baseRates.ownership

G33 counts words in it and passes; G15 checks all eleven catalogues hold the key and passes; the DOM tests assert the note is SHOWN, which is exactly the defect being asserted as the feature. The claim is true of the OWNERSHIP half - the plan really does follow the code - and false only in its last four words, which is why it reads as correct to anyone who knows BR-RAT-088 and has not opened models.py.
