The close-count test is NOT fixed here - it belongs to the close-count lane and the right repair is a judgment about what TC-6b should assert now that the callable exists, not a lane passing through flipping an expectation on a money-adjacent screen. THE GENERAL FIX, and it is worth more than either: a uuid-to-str comparison is silently false and a Python != on mismatched types is silently true, so any assertion about an id should compare str() to str() - and the cheaper habit is law 7 habit 2, ask what would make this check PASS wrongly, which finds the != line in one reading.

introduced_in: CR-139-BRC07 §4 (2026-09-23) — the phase-5 board carries 18 tasks: P5.1-P5.3 write, P5.4-P5.6 are the schema, P5.7 is 'front end'. The drawing's own TASK row on blueprint p070 reads 'settlements and its members, a provider settlement feed, one new number series, GET /settlements' and the read is the one item with no row
escape_reason: Nothing counts a blueprint TASK row against the CR's task board. Every existence check in the repo asks whether a cited id EXISTS, never whether an item the drawing names has an owner - so an unowned dependency is indistinguishable from a deliberate deferral, and the screen lane finds it by grepping for an endpoint that is not there. prevention: Tick every item of a screen's To-build row against a task row before the board is called complete. This lane built the read - GET /settlements, /settlements/{code}, /settlements/{code}/members - so P5.7 is wired rather than dead UI.

title: THE IMPORT RECEIPT'S FIGURES DO NOT ADD UP TO THE FILE - 95 rows in, the receipt says 72 loaded and 11 rejected, and 12 rows are on neither side
surface: 06-backend/apps/metering/import_runs.py::receipt - "rejected": int(counts.get("errors") or 0)
found_in: walking JPAYLOCKBOX on a booted stack, 2026-09-23 (CR-135 P1.14) - the run's own counts row reads created=72, errors=11, rejected_at_write=12 and the receipt printed Loaded 72 / Rejected 11 / Flagged for review 11
introduced_in: the receipt builder's original shape - rejected has read stage 3's errors since the runner shipped; it became visible when a target began refusing rows AT THE WRITE
escape_reason: receipt() reports counts['errors'], which is stage 3's rejection count, and never counts['rejected_at_write'], which the loader records for rows the WRITER refused. On the payments target 12 rows passed stage 3 and were refused at the write (11 name-only, 1 zero amount), so the receipt accounts for 83 of 95 rows and a clerk reading it cannot tell that twelve customers' money did not post. It is not payments-only: every loader sets rejected_at_write and no target's receipt reads it. Nothing catches it because BR-MET-090 makes the receipt a read of what the run recorded, so it is self-consistent by construction, and no test adds the two sides up against rows-in.
prevention: The receipt states rejected = errors + rejected_at_write, and a test asserts loaded + rejected + skipped equals rows in, on every target that has a write-time refusal. A receipt whose figures do not sum to the file is the one arithmetic a reader can do and nothing did.

title: A PAYMENTS IMPORT SHOWS PREMISES AND UNITS COPY - stage 3 says 'requires amount on every premises' and the receipt says 72 payments 'took no services from the unit they sit under'
surface: the ETL runner's stage-3 rule sentences and stage-5 receipt panels, rendered for target=payments
found_in: walking JPAYLOCKBOX on a booted stack, 2026-09-23 - stage 3 on a payments run printed 'Your utility requires amount on every premises.' and the stage-5 receipt printed 'Took services from their unit 0 / Wired to no services 72' with the sentence '72 of the 72 payments created took no services from the unit they sit under, so there is nothing to bill them for yet. Open each one and give it a service.'
introduced_in: CR-135-BRC07 P1.1, the eighth import target - one receipt screen renders every target and the premises-shaped panels were never gated off payments
escape_reason: ONE receipt screen and one rules table render every target, and the premises/units panels are drawn whenever their counts key is present rather than when the target has that concept. A payment does not sit under a unit and cannot take services from one, so the sentence is not merely irrelevant, it instructs a clerk to do something impossible on a money screen. No gate in this repo reads rendered output (hard-won law 6) and both strings come from real catalogue keys, so tsc, the locale gate and every unit case pass.
prevention: A panel is drawn from a per-target declaration of which figures that target HAS, not from a key being present in a shared counts dict; and a walkthrough that reads the stage-3 and stage-5 text for every target's own vocabulary. The general form: a screen shared by eight targets needs a test per target that the words on it belong to that target.

title: STAGE 3 PROMISES 84 WILL LOAD ON A FILE THE WRITER REFUSES 12 OF - the name-only rule flags where the writer rejects, which is the DEF-544 shape its neighbour's comment names
surface: 06-backend/apps/metering/import_rules.py::PAYMENTS_RULES PAY.NAME_ONLY_MATCH (severity WARNING, action FLAG_ONLY) against apps/payments/import_writer.create_payment_from_import, which refuses every non-clean verdict
found_in: walking JPAYLOCKBOX on a booted stack, 2026-09-23 - stage 3 read 'Will load 84 / Blocked 11', the stage-4 dry run read 'Will create 84 / Rows rejected 11', and the load created 72
escape_reason: PAY.ACCOUNT_ON_FILE carries a comment saying exactly why it is NOT a warning - 'the writer refuses this row, so flagging it would let an operator press commit expecting it to load - the shape DEF-544 names' - and PAY.NAME_ONLY_MATCH was then written as a FLAG_ONLY warning over a row the same writer refuses by name. _loadable_rows sends flagged rows to the write, create_payment_from_import raises REFUSAL_NAME_ONLY, and the row lands in rejected_at_write. A zero amount does the same: 0.00 parses cleanly at stage 3 and is refused at the write. The unit tests assert the rule flags and assert the writer refuses, separately and correctly; nothing compares the two numbers a clerk is shown before and after the button.
prevention: A test per target that runs a file whose rows hit every declared rule and asserts the stage-3 'will load' figure EQUALS the number the load creates. That is the only assertion that can see a rehearsal and a write disagreeing, and it is one line once a real file is being run.

title: THE IMPORT RECEIPT DOES NOT PRINT THE RUN'S NUMBER, so a clerk cannot tie the receipt they are reading to the Batch column on the payments list
surface: 07-frontend/src/components/workflow/Receipt.tsx - stage 5, rendered for every target; receipt() serves run_no and the screen does not draw it
found_in: walking JPAYLOCKBOX on a booted stack, 2026-09-23 - the full stage-5 text was searched for /IMP-[0-9]{6}-[0-9]+/ and there is none; the same run's number IMP-260923-02 is on the Imports list row and in every Batch cell on S33
introduced_in: the receipt screen's original shape
escape_reason: receipt() puts run_no in its payload and stage 5 renders the counts without it. Nothing fails: the server serves the field, the screen is green, and the number is reachable one screen away on the Imports list. It surfaced only because JPAYLOCKBOX check N asks for 'the number step 8's receipt printed, character for character' - the check names a thing the screen does not show, which is how an absence with no reader gets found.
prevention: The receipt carries the run's number as its first fact, and the journey's check N asserts it there. More generally: a check written as 'assert what screen X showed' is worth writing even when screen X is not built, because it is the only thing that reports the absence.

title: A STORE OR BANK FILE WITH A CURRENCY SYMBOL OR A TWO-DIGIT YEAR CANNOT BE IMPORTED, and the screen's own remedy for the year does not exist
surface: 06-backend/apps/metering/import_runs.py KIND_DECIMAL cell parse (strips commas, not currency symbols) and tenancy.services.DATE_FORMATS (seven formats, no MM/DD/YY)
found_in: walking JPAYLOCKBOX with the file as the journey describes it, 2026-09-23 - 95 rows in, 0 will load, 95 blocked: 'Every value has to be the kind of value its column holds' fired on 95 rows and 'Date paid - mapped from WHEN. 95 row(s) could not be read; the first is row 1, 09/19/26'
introduced_in: KIND_DECIMAL's parse and DATE_FORMATS' seven entries; both predate the payments target and were correct for the files they were written for
escape_reason: The comma is stripped and the dollar sign is not, so Decimal('234.50') raises and the row is rejected. BR-MET-117 rightly forbids sniffing a date format, but DATE_FORMATS offers no two-digit-year slash format at all, while DD-MMM-YY has one - so two-digit years are not forbidden in principle, this file's spelling simply is not offered. The stage-3 sentence tells the clerk to 'change the format in Settings > Regional', which for 09/19/26 is advice they cannot take. The refusal hint on the amount is over-broad in the other direction: it says 'take out thousands separators', which the parser already handles. Nothing catches either because no test and no journey had ever run a file written the way a grocery store or a bank writes one.
prevention: Decide and record whether a currency symbol is stripped on a money cell (it is unambiguous, unlike a date), and either add MM/DD/YY and DD/MM/YY to DATE_FORMATS or stop offering Settings > Regional as the remedy in that sentence. Either way, a fixture file in the vocabulary a real remittance file uses, walked end to end.

title: EVERY MAPPING PICKER IN THE IMPORT RUNNER OFFERS '- ignore -' TWICE - the server appends it to the column list and the component appends it again
surface: 07-frontend/src/components/workflow/MappingTable.tsx - the unconditional <option value={IGNORE_VALUE}> after {targets.map(...)}, over a targets list that already ends in one
found_in: walking JPAYLOCKBOX on a booted stack, 2026-09-23 - the picker's option values read account_ref, amount, paid_on, reference, payer_name, memo, __ignore__, __ignore__
introduced_in: MappingTable's original shape - target_columns() has appended the ignore entry server-side since the runner shipped
escape_reason: Both halves are individually right and each cites a rule: target_columns() appends the ignore entry because BR-MET-088 requires the choice by name, and MappingTable appends one because 'a tenant with a genuinely meaningless column must be able to say so out loud'. Neither knows about the other. It affects all eight import targets. Nothing sees it: the two options carry the same value so the select behaves correctly, tsc is happy, and no gate in this repo reads rendered output.
prevention: The component filters IGNORE_VALUE out of targets before rendering its own, or stops rendering its own and trusts the served list. A rendered-output check on any list of options that no value appears twice would find this family generally.

title: EVERY FILTER ON THE PAYMENTS LIST IS DECORATIVE - ticking Source, Status or Type changes nothing, because the page serialises the state with a config that declares no filters
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/payments/PaymentsPage.tsx - the PAGE builds config = paymentsTableConfig(...), which returns no filters key, and setState/parseTableParams both read config.filters; PaymentsTable then spreads its own filters: paymentsFilters(...) onto a SECOND config that only the FilterBar and DataTable see
found_in: walking JPAYLOCKBOX check M on a booted stack, 2026-09-23 - a real click on Source > Post leaves the box unticked, the address at ?sort=posted_at&dir=desc and the pager at 1-50 of 146; Status > Reversed and Type > Credit behave identically. The same click on the Accounts list ticks, moves the pager 72 to 68 and writes f.status=active, so it is this screen and not the kit
introduced_in: the split between the page-level config and PaymentsTable's own - the filters have been declared on the table's copy since the filter bar landed on S33
escape_reason: serializeTableParams and parseTableParams both iterate config.filters, so a filter the config does not declare is dropped on the way OUT to the URL and ignored on the way BACK IN. The page's config has no filters at all; the table's has eight. So the FilterBar renders correctly from the table's config, its onChange fires, toggleFilterOption returns a correct state, and the page then serialises that state through a config that cannot see it - the value never reaches the URL, the URL is the only store, and the controlled checkbox snaps back. Nothing catches it: the server filters correctly (146 rows, 72 with origin=import, 74 with origin=entry), G45 asks only whether a screen declaring filters RENDERS a control and it does, the unit cases test toggleFilterOption and serializeTableParams separately and both are right, and no gate in this repo reads rendered output.
prevention: One config per screen, built once and passed down - or, where a table enriches its own, the page serialises with the SAME object the bar changed. The general check is cheap and would cover every list: a rendered-output walk that ticks the first option of every declared filter and asserts the address bar gained an f.<name>.

title: EVERY IMPORTED PAYMENT IS DATED THE DAY OF THE IMPORT, NOT THE DAY THE MONEY ARRIVED - a lockbox file dated 09/19 posts and clears on 09/23
surface: 06-backend/apps/metering/import_runs.py::_payment_moment, reached from _payment_payload_from and payments.import_writer.create_payment_from_import
found_in: walking JPAYLOCKBOX end to end on a booted stack against a real PostgreSQL 16 clone, 2026-09-23 (CR-135 P1.14 check B); 72 payments imported from a file whose WHEN column said 09/19/2026 and 09/20/2026, all 72 stored posted_at=cleared_at=2026-09-23
introduced_in: CR-135-BRC07 P1.1/P1.2, 2026-09-22 - the payments import target's own adapter
escape_reason: _payment_moment takes a stage-2 date cell and returns an instant, and stage 2 writes an ISO STRING into mapped (import_run_rows.mapped holds {"paid_on": "2026-09-19"}). The function tests hasattr(value, 'year'), which is False for a string, and returns None - so paid_at is None on every row and create_payment_from_import falls back to recorded_at, the operator's business day. BR-PAY-033 and OQ-131's ruling say lateness is judged on the day the money ARRIVED; this charges a late fee to a customer who paid on time. Two tests cover the adapter and neither can see it: test_every_column_reaches_the_payload_and_none_is_dropped_in_the_adapter asserts only that the KEY paid_at is PRESENT in the payload, and it passes the string 'x-paid_on', so the value is None and the assertion is still true. The receipt agrees with itself because it reports what the run recorded. Nothing in the repo ran a real file from stage 1 to stage 5 before today. NOTE ON THIS ROW'S ID: it was first filed as DEF-PAY-6286 at 11:30 and that row was LOST - lane P5-SCREENS took the same number for a different defect and a whole-file write of the register carried mine away. Re-filed here under a verified id.
prevention: Assert the VALUE, not the key: a test that takes a stage-2 date cell exactly as import_run_rows.mapped stores it (an ISO string) and asserts the created payment's posted_at and cleared_at are that day. The general form is worth more than the fix: an adapter test that checks a key is present cannot see a None behind it, and every 'is the column dropped' test in this repo has that shape.

title: A master account shows an empty Services cell and an unexplained blank, so a clerk cannot tell a correct absence from a broken screen
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/customers - the accounts register row for an account with kind=master; customers.accounts.services.none renders 'No services' with no reason, and the premises list's master-account column renders nothing at all
found_in: 2026-09-23, PO reporting that a newly created master account 'is not taking utility service applicable also not taking plan'; investigated by the coordinator the same hour
introduced_in: not a regression - it follows from BR-CUS-1010 (2026-09-01), which hangs a master account off the ADDRESS and leaves accounts.unit_id null. Services are inherited from the unit (BR-CUS-672) and a plan needs services, so a master account correctly has neither
escape_reason: NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY CHECKS THAT A CORRECT ABSENCE EXPLAINS ITSELF. The product behaves exactly as three signed rules require and says nothing on screen about why, so the PO read a correct screen as a broken one and reported it as a bug - which cost an investigation to answer. B14 rule 32 makes a stated absence a CLOSED disclosure by default and rule 33 puts rationale at ZERO words on screen, so the honest fix is a short FACT, not an explanation - and no gate reads rendered output at all (hard-won law 6).
prevention: Where a rule produces a deliberate emptiness on a money screen, say the fact in six words or fewer - 'No services - bills through its units' rather than a blank. The general shape is worth more than this instance: an absence that follows from a rule is invisible to every check this repo has, and the only reader who can tell it from a defect is the person who wrote the rule.

surface: 06-backend/apps/tenancy/models.py OccupancyStatus (the five values: occupied tenant-billed, occupied owner-billed, landlord-billed, vacant base-only, vacant no-billing); read by tenancy/services.py, reference_sweep.py and metering/models.py only

title: core.tenancy.tenant_context CLEARS app.tenant_id on exit instead of restoring it, so every ORM statement after an api_call in a test runs unscoped - invisible on SQLite, RLS-refused or silently empty on PostgreSQL
surface: 06-backend/core/tenancy.py tenant_context() + tests/test_us_ten_helpers.api_call(), which opens a nested one around every view
found_in: CR-138-BRC07 P4.15, running a new backend test file on real PostgreSQL 16 after it was green on the default SQLite suite, 2026-09-23
introduced_in: core/tenancy.py tenant_context has always ended in an unconditional clear_current_tenant(); api_call has always nested one inside whatever the test opened
escape_reason: The default suite hardcodes in-memory SQLite and SQLite has no row-level security, so an unscoped statement behaves identically to a scoped one and the whole suite is green - CLAUDE.md hard-won law 14 exactly. On PostgreSQL the WRITE direction raises (psycopg InsufficientPrivilege: new row violates row-level security policy for table tenant_settings) and is at least loud; the READ direction returns ZERO ROWS and raises nothing, so a case asserting an absence after a request passes for entirely the wrong reason and goes on passing. Nothing counts how many of the repo's tests read or write after an api_call inside an enclosing tenant_ctx.
prevention: MEASURED: two cases in tests/test_cr138_p4_15_tone_days_and_letters.py passed on SQLite and failed on PostgreSQL; both did store -> api_call -> store, and the second store was refused because the first api_call cleared app.tenant_id while the enclosing with tenant_ctx(brazos) was still open in Python. The narrow fix in that file is a tenant_ctx per ORM call, documented on the helper. The durable fix is for tenant_context to SAVE the value it replaces and restore it in its finally (a token, as contextvars.set/reset already offer), which makes nesting safe and changes nothing for the unnested job and management-command callers it was written for. Until then the general shape has no check: G5 runs the isolation suite and nothing audits the other suites for a scoped read after a request.

title: Four of the eight collection skip sentences break B14 rule 33's six-word cap for a FACT, and one is twelve words in a status pill on a list row
surface: 07-frontend/src/i18n/locales/*.json payments.skip.* rendered by paymentsShared.ladderSkipLabel in CollectionsPage 7.3a and SendNoticeWizard step 3
found_in: CR-138-BRC07 P4.16, writing the check that every skip reason has words in all eleven catalogues, 2026-09-23
introduced_in: the sentences were written with their reasons across CR-059 CS-10 and earlier collections work; B14 rule 33 was ratified 2026-08-30 and no gate reads rendered copy length
escape_reason: No gate in this repo reads rendered output and none counts words in a catalogue sentence - CLAUDE.md says so twice (hard-won law 6, and B14's own note that most rules are RATIFIED and UNENFORCED). G15 checks PARITY across the eleven catalogues, so eleven equally-too-long sentences are parity-perfect. Rule 33 is also the rule a lane is least likely to break deliberately and most likely to break by being helpful: every one of these four reads as a considerate explanation.
prevention: MEASURED in English, words per sentence: nothing_overdue 2, already_noticed_today 5, ladder_complete 6, partial_payment_pause 6, next_step_not_due 7, payment_plan_pause 8, medical_hold 9, below_ladder_floor 12 (Too small to chase - the letter costs more than the debt). B14 rule 33 caps a FACT at six words; four are over. The fix is shorter English copy fanned through 10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py to all eleven - a copy decision, not a test lane's. skipReasonsAreShown.dom.test.tsx pins the four BY NAME and below_ladder_floor BY ITS COUNT, so shortening them turns that file red and names this row rather than the correction landing unnoticed. The general shape - a catalogue sentence nothing measures against rule 33 - is unchecked across the whole product and would need a gate that reads the catalogues with a per-key intent (LABEL, FACT, INSTRUCTION), which rule 33 implies and nothing records.

title: GET /collections/ladder takes no page and serves 40,030 rows in one response at the top of the ICP, and CollectionsPage still says clientPage is what P4.2 deletes
surface: 06-backend/apps/payments/collections_read.ladder_board() + 07-frontend/src/features/payments/CollectionsPage.tsx (clientPage over LADDER_SPEC)
found_in: CR-138-BRC07 P4.18, measuring both seeded clones on real PostgreSQL 16 before writing the statement-count check, 2026-09-23

title: 7.3d Send a notice loses the whole selection on the first Continue, so the commit reads Send 0 and the screen cannot send a notice at all
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/payments/SendNoticeWizard.tsx setNav() -> setSearchParams(params, {replace: true})
found_in: CR-138-BRC07 P4.28, mounting the wizard and walking it to step 3 to assert the letter renders before the send, 2026-09-23
introduced_in: fb3526105 (CR-138-BRC07 P4.14 + P4.27), the commit that built the wizard
escape_reason: sendNoticeWizard.dom.test.tsx NEVER MOUNTS THE WIZARD. It imports four pure functions and reads OutstandingsTab.tsx as raw text, so its 12 cases cover the handover VALIDATOR (sendNoticeHandover returns null on a hard refresh) and never the navigation that destroys the handover. The screen's own docstring reasons correctly that the selection must not go in the URL under B14 rule 31 and then hands step navigation to setSearchParams, which in react-router v6 builds a partial path and therefore drops location.state unless it is passed again. Every gate, tsc and the whole suite are green over a screen that cannot perform its one act.
fixed_commit: bbd1ed6e9 — 2.344.1; state: location.state on setNav, proved by the pinned case flipping from 'Send 0' to 'Send 1'
prevention: MEASURED by mounting the wizard at /:tenant/payments/outstandings/send-notice with {accounts:[one],asOf,currency} in router state: at start location.state is present; after one click of Continue the location is ?step=2 with state null. The one-line fix is to carry the state through the navigation - setSearchParams(params, {replace:true, state:location.state}) - or to hold the handover in component state on first mount so no later navigation can lose it; the second is the durable one because it survives any navigation, not just this call site. NOT FIXED BY THIS LANE: SendNoticeWizard.tsx is LANE P4-SCREENS-B's file and that lane is still running (law 11). noticePreviewBeforeSend.dom.test.tsx pins Send 0 by value with this id beside it, so the fix turns that file red and names this row. Blast radius checked: SendNoticeWizard is the ONLY file in 07-frontend/src that both reads location.state and calls setSearchParams.

title: SignupWizard.test.tsx CR-064 B2 has been red since the aged-meters block was inserted: no step is Working and nothing read the failure
surface: frontend
found_in: Running the neighbouring suites before a push, 2026-09-23; reproduced identically on a pristine worktree at commit a1c85682 with no local change
introduced_in: 28dee3b8 (2026-09-11) added assets:seed_sample_aged_meters to PROVISIONING_STEPS at index 4
escape_reason: The case names FIVE served blocks by key and sets progress.done to 5, and those two agreed only while the five keys were the first five of PROVISIONING_STEPS. The aged-meters block was inserted at index 4, so the row at index 5 now carries a served outcome and becomes done, the row at index 4 has no record and is not equal to done, and NO row is Working. Its own comment warns about exactly this - a positional case that names a key by hand fails for a change it is not about - and the fix applied then was to derive the KEY from the constant while leaving the COUNT typed. Nothing read the red: it is hard-won law 7's first shape, a guard proved red at birth that nobody looks at again.
prevention: The case derives its served list from PROVISIONING_STEPS.slice(0, n) rather than naming keys, so the count and the keys cannot disagree; or it asserts on the index of the last served key rather than on a typed done count.

reported_by: lane MA-UNITS, building the master account's Units tab (BR-CUS-1094)
title: occupancy_statuses is referenced by no foreign key anywhere, so no unit can declare one
surface: 06-backend/apps/tenancy/models.py OccupancyStatus (the five seeded values); apps/metering/models.py Unit (which declares no occupancy_status column); S8 Reference data - the list a tenant can edit today and nothing can use
introduced_in: the list was seeded with its five values and its structural meaning recorded in the decision log of 2026-08-16; no table was ever given a column pointing at it
escape_reason: DEF-BIL-6296 (filed the same day) says the list is READ by no line of billing or rating. This is the sharper fact one layer down and it changes what the fix costs: grep for a foreign key to occupancy_statuses across every migration and every model returns NOTHING, so there is no per-unit value for anybody to read. G74 asks whether a table is NAMED anywhere and one reader clears it - tenancy names it and metering names it in a comment, which is enough to look connected. Nothing in this repo asks whether a reference list is POINTED AT by the rows whose behaviour it claims to govern, so a table can be editable on Settings for five weeks while no record can carry its value.
prevention: The fix is not a reader, it is a column: a unit needs an occupancy_status FK, a writer (the Unit edit form and the import), a backfill decision for 1,109 existing units, and only then a consumer in gather. Saying so now stops the next lane from adding a read to billing and finding nothing to read. The durable half is the shape: a reference list whose own documentation says it changes money should fail a check when NO table declares a foreign key to it - the same question G13 asks of a UI prop, asked of a reference table.

reported_by: lane MA-UNITS, walking the master account's Units tab in a browser (hard-won law 6)
title: Every detail screen in the product carries a raw uuid in the ADDRESS BAR, which B14 rule 31 forbids
surface: S21 account detail (/{tenant}/accounts/01a0bf3d-4889-76a3-876a-2b966676b941?tab=units, photographed 2026-09-23), and every sibling route built the same way - accounts, units, premises, assets, routes, cycles
introduced_in: the routes predate B14 rule 31, which was ratified 2026-08-31 in the PO's words 'no Databse ID on screen - that is a rule'; accountDetailPath has encoded the account id since the screen was built
escape_reason: NO GATE IN THIS REPOSITORY READS RENDERED OUTPUT, and none reads a URL either. DEF-3158 closed seven sites that printed a truncated id as a CELL VALUE and did not ask about the address bar; DEF-2580 and DEF-645 are the same blind spot on other surfaces. The address bar is the most visible field a screen has - it is what a clerk copies into an email and reads down the phone - and it is the one field no check in this repo looks at. Found by a walkthrough that was pointed at a different screen.
prevention: Two halves. (1) The cheap one: every walkthrough script in 10-scripts already carries a UUID regex; make the address-bar assertion a shared helper so a new screen inherits it instead of re-deciding. (2) The real one is a routing change - detail routes keyed by the human-facing number (account_no, unit_no, premises_no) with the id resolved server-side, which is a product-wide decision and a PO question rather than a lane's. FILED rather than fixed here: this lane's screen inherits the route it is a tab on, and changing one route would leave the product with two grammars.

title: The property Units tab's unit cell is inline in a 2,000-line page, so a second tab needing it must duplicate it
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/metering/PremisesDetailPage.tsx (the UNIT column's inline cell, around line 1900) and 07-frontend/src/features/customers/MasterUnitsTab.tsx MasterUnitCell, which is its copy
escape_reason: B14 rule 43 (ratified 2026-09-20) says a piece of UI is built as a COMPONENT and that standalone code inside a page is not reuse - it was ruled after 'use it' turned out to mean 120 lines inline in a 4,186-line page. Nothing enforces it: no gate reads a file's shape, and a second copy of a cell compiles, renders and tests exactly like the first. The label-leads-number-beneath cell is the blueprint's own ruling (p23, p25) and is now written twice, so a future correction to one leaves the other drawing the old shape.

It was NOT extracted in this change because PremisesDetailPage.tsx was under two other lanes the same day and a shared-file edit on a 2,000-line page is law 11's mechanism two waiting to happen. The wider shape: when a cell is written inline, the next screen that needs it has only two choices and both are wrong - copy it, or edit a page it does not own.

reported_by: lane MA-UNITS, building the master account's Units tab (BR-CUS-1094)
title: A common area the master does not cover reads 'Always billed to the owner' beside 'Nobody' on the same row
surface: S21 account detail - Units tab (BR-CUS-1094): the Occupant cell (metering's OccupantCell, imported) and the Billed to cell, on any common-area unit with no open service agreement to a master
introduced_in: OccupantCell's common-area sentence predates this tab; the contradiction only becomes visible now that a screen prints the RUN's answer beside it
escape_reason: The two cells answer different questions and each is right about its own. OccupantCell states the general rule (BR-MET-101 - a common area is the owner's, always); Billed to states what the next bill run will actually do, and for a common area in neither covered_unit_ids nor base_charge_only_coverage the run raises nothing. Nothing compares two cells of one row: no gate reads rendered output, and each cell's own test asserts its own sentence in isolation. Reachable when a common area is created AFTER the master account - create_master_account writes agreements only for the common areas present when it runs, and metering's _attach_named_master_account is an explicit opt-in door.
prevention: The optimistic sentence is the one to soften, and it belongs to metering: 'Always billed to the owner.' is true of the rule and not of a unit no master covers. Changing it touches the property page too, which is a second screen and a second blast radius - hence filed rather than changed inside a customers tab. test_br_cus_1094_tc12 pins the current behaviour so a fix has something to go red against. The wider shape: when one screen starts printing what the RUN will do beside a sentence stating what the RULE says, any gap between rule and implementation becomes visible as a contradiction - which is the screen working, not failing.

title: The Change plan wizard answers a bare 404 on a master account, about an account that plainly exists
surface: 06-backend/apps/customers/services.py plan_change_options -> _account_and_unit_plan -> seams.unit_row(account.unit_id) with unit_id NULL; reached from the account detail's Change plan action and 07-frontend/src/features/customers/ChangePlanWizard.tsx
found_in: 2026-09-23, building BR-CUS-1093 - 10-scripts/br_cus_1093_master_services_readback.py section 4 printed NotFoundError for AC-2026-00051 and AC-2026-00052 on a clone of brazosbend, with 'reached the no_services branch: False'

escape_reason: NOTHING CHECKS THAT A REFUSAL IS ABOUT THE THING THE CALLER NAMED. The 404 is HR-1 working exactly as designed for a unit id this tenant cannot see - but the caller asked about an ACCOUNT and the account exists. G32 asks whether a refusal resolves a message_key; this one carries neither a message_key nor a br_ref, so it is invisible to it. And three live surfaces named the WRONG branch for it - BR-CUS-1093's own body, the decision-log row of 2026-09-23 and the lane briefing all said the picker refuses through no_services, which it never reaches; all three are corrected in the commit that files this.
prevention: A correct refusal must be about the thing the caller named. plan_change_options should refuse BY NAME on an account with no unit - the answer is already ruled, OQ-INT-12403 (CLOSED 2026-09-17; renumbered from OQ-INT-12398 an hour after it was minted, which is how this citation came to name the address-list question instead): a master account has no plan and null is the true answer, because the units below it may be on four different plans and picking one would invent. The durable shape: where a read crosses a module seam, what the caller sees is the SEAM's refusal about the far side, never a statement about what the caller asked for.

title: A lane renumbering its own defect id rewrote a SIBLING's citation of the number it was vacating
surface: 04-docs/05-modules/03-customers/02-business-rules.md - BR-CUS-1094's row, pushed in d1a9548dc with DEF-CUS-6306 silently changed to DEF-CUS-6310
found_in: 2026-09-23, by lane MA-SERVICES itself, in the post-push subtraction check CLAUDE.md law 11 prescribes: git diff --numstat reported 2 insertions and 2 DELETIONS on a file where only one row was mine, and a word-diff of the other row found the one changed token
introduced_in: d1a9548dc, the same lane's own push. allocate.py --verify said the id it had taken was gone (three collisions in one afternoon: DEF-MET-6302, DEF-CUS-6306, then this), and the renumber was done with a blanket sed -i over every file naming the old id - on a file a sibling had just amended to cite that same id for its OWN defect
escape_reason: NOTHING CHECKS THAT A RENUMBER TOUCHED ONLY THE AUTHOR'S OWN CITATIONS. G106 asks whether every cited id EXISTS - both 6306 and 6310 exist, so it passes either way; G17 asks about duplicates, and there is none. The id was not dangling, it was pointing at the wrong real defect, which is DEF-2804's shape exactly (OQ-1190 read as OQ-119) and the mirror-image defect CLAUDE.md names for the OQ-1330 sweep: 41 legitimate occurrences were LEFT on purpose there, and here the one legitimate occurrence was taken. The file count was right, the author's own change WAS present, and the diff showed only the two rows the author expected to see.
prevention: A renumber is a rewrite of OTHER PEOPLE'S text unless it is scoped. Never sed a shared document for an id you are vacating - list the occurrences first and change only the ones in lines you wrote. And the check that found this is the one to keep: read git diff --numstat AS ARITHMETIC after a push, and when a file reports more deletions than rows you authored, word-diff the rows you did not.

title: Our bills print no barcode BARS, so a scanner reads nothing off our own paper: documents.py's PDF writer has no filled-rectangle primitive and never calls remittance.bars()
surface: 06-backend/apps/billing/documents.py — the PDF writer (PageRule/stroke() is the only drawing primitive; the single occurrence of 'bars(' at line 1677 is a COMMENT) and the remittance stub on every bill PDF · 07-frontend/src/components/workflow/kinds.ts SCAN_PAPER_CARD, held shut because of it
found_in: Product Owner on the deployed build, 2026-09-23, verbatim: 'please enable it and also start putting bar code on bills - we are still in beta and uat - we ahve to make these changes now'
introduced_in: CR-139-BRC07 P5.10, 2026-09-23 — the task row is titled 'Billing: the remittance barcode' with the outcome 'Without it a scanner reads nothing. Which is why it ships in this phase.' The LINE shipped; the BARS did not, because the PDF writer has a horizontal-rule primitive and no filled-rectangle one
escape_reason: NOTHING ESCAPED A CHECK — two checks held it deliberately and named it, which is why this row is about the BOARD rather than about a gate. test_cr139_p5_10_the_bars_are_not_drawn_yet and test_cr139_p5_15_the_scan_card_stays_held_while_our_own_bills_carry_no_bars were both proved red at birth and both state the four things that move together. What nothing measured is whether the hold was still the right trade-off: P5.10's row is TITLED 'the remittance barcode' and was closed with half of what it names built, so the phase board reads DONE over a deliverable that is absent on the paper. A hold is a decision deferred, and nothing in this repo schedules the deferred decision — it took the PO looking at a printed bill. That is hard-won law 2's mirror one level up: not a dead control, but a correctly-written hold whose expiry nobody owned.
prevention: The decode round trip, not a call-count: a test that renders a real bill PDF, extracts the drawn rectangles from the content stream, decodes the Code 39 back to characters and asserts the result is byte-identical to remittance.compose_for_invoice's output. Asserting bars() was called, or that N rectangles were drawn, is hard-won law 7's 'looking at the wrong thing' — a barcode a scanner cannot read passes both. And a task row whose TITLE names a deliverable may not close while a hold test for that deliverable is green.

title: A clerk cannot open a till: Start counter posts service_centre where POST /counters reads service_centre_id, and never sends the REQUIRED opened_at at all
surface: 07-frontend/src/api/counterEndpoints.ts:196-209 StartCounterBody, and its one caller 07-frontend/src/features/payments/StartCounterModal.tsx:98-101 - against 06-backend/apps/payments/counters_api.py:113-121
found_in: Reported by the PO on the deployed build 2026-09-23 and reproduced: 3-3a Start counter refuses every submit. First refusal is 'Give the opening time.' (payments.counter.opened_at_required) over a form with no time field - grep -c opened_at StartCounterModal.tsx = 0. Past that, BR-PAY-1160 'a counter is a till AT a place, and this request names none', because _service_centre() is handed payload.get('service_centre_id') and the body carries service_centre
introduced_in: The two halves of CR-136-BRC07 landed the same day, 2026-09-23: LANE P2-SCREENS wrote counterEndpoints.ts against the drawing (p054-p055 Fields row, 'Two. Service centre (required) - Opening float (required)') while LANE P2-API wrote counters_api.py against BR-TEN-043 (every moment is an INPUT; this module reads no clock). Neither read the other's payload keys
escape_reason: StartCounterBody was written to match its CALLER and not its ENDPOINT, so tsc could only ever confirm the frontend agrees with itself. The interface declares service_centre and opening_float; the form passes exactly those two; both compile. The type never mentions opened_at, so its absence is not a missing property - there is no property to miss - and its service_centre spelling makes the wrong key a correct assignment. A request-body interface is the only place the wire contract is written down on this side, and nothing in this repo compares it to the payload.get() keys the endpoint reads. The one test family that could have looked - counterScreens.dom.test.tsx - never mounts StartCounterModal at all and never calls startCounter, so the submit path of the only door onto the till has no case of any kind
prevention: A contract test that asserts on the REQUEST BODY the client would send - a recording stub client, not a mocked startCounter - checked against the payload.get() keys parsed out of counters_api.py's own source. A test that mocks the endpoint wrapper asserts the caller agrees with itself, which is the same thing tsc already did and the same thing that shipped this

title: Payment detail never opens: the route guard accepts the wireframe's drawn PMT- number and the product mints PY-
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/payments/PaymentDetailPage.tsx:168 PAYMENT_REF_RE / segmentIsPaymentRef
introduced_in: CR-137-BRC07 P3.1 (the commit that added PAYMENT_REF_RE)
escape_reason: The pattern was derived from a number DRAWN IN THE BLUEPRINT (p036's example payment PMT-2609-000418, cited at 06-backend/apps/payments/cancel.py:102) instead of from core/numbering.py:358 SERIES_CATALOG, whose payment default is PY-{YY}{MM}{DD}-{0000}. B14 rule 37 says a figure drawn in a wireframe is an ILLUSTRATION, never a fact to build to, and no gate reads a wireframe. tsc, every test and every gate passed because a regex that matches nothing the product mints is still a valid regex, and the two existing tests asserted segmentIsPaymentRef on the drawn PMT- string only, so the suite agreed with the bug. Failure is silent by construction: paymentsTabFrom answers an unknown tab with Summary rather than 404, so a rejected reference lands the clerk on the Summary tab with no error and no empty state.
prevention: Derive the pattern from the numbering kernel's five PAYMENT formats rather than from one drawn example, and assert it against a rendered number from core.numbering SERIES_CATALOG rather than a hand-typed literal.

title: The "What is missing" panel explains the product to a clerk: 29 of 40 payments.problem.* strings break B14 rule 33, and two of them are pure rationale the PO named
surface: S32 Payments Summary, S34 Outstandings/Collections, the debtor page, the bad-debt report and the move/reapply plans - every caller of ProblemList in 07-frontend/src/features/payments/paymentsShared.tsx, in all eleven catalogues

It is not worked out here. * Medical protections cannot be shown here. Notices still apply them.' Measured: the payments.problem.* family is 40 keys; 29 carry at least one sentence over rule 33's six-word cap; the longest is 30 words (issued_bill_without_issue_date). Two keys are also DEAD and FALSE - no_receipt_queued (retired from RECORD_UNAVAILABLE 2026-08-18, still says receipts are 'not built' when receipts.queue_receipt_for_recorded_payment runs on every payment) and grouped_bank_credits_not_matchable (retired 2026-09-01 by CR-059 task 45, still says 'Those deposits will stay unmatched' on the same page as the control that matches them).
introduced_in: The family was written before B14 rule 33 was ratified on 2026-08-30 and was never swept afterwards. The two false sentences were left behind when their codes were retired from the server on 2026-08-18 and 2026-09-01 - the code came out and the words did not.
escape_reason: Rule 33 is RATIFIED and UNENFORCED for its five kinds - B14's own status column says so. G33 enforces the REFUSAL half only, and a payments.problem.* string is not a refusal, so no gate has ever counted a word in this family. Nothing else could see it either: the strings render inside a details closed by default, every catalogue has all 40 keys so the parity check is green, and tsc and the eleven-catalogue tests pass on a string of any length. The dead keys survived for the mirror reason - a frontend test fixture invents the code (depositsSurface.test.tsx:107, PaymentsPage.test.tsx:598), so the assertion that the sentence renders passes forever after the server stopped sending it.
prevention: A word-count test over the live payments.problem.* family in all eleven catalogues, written and proved RED on today's 29 before a word was changed, bucketing by kind and by script because a six-word English cap is not six words in Japanese (B14 rule 35). Plus the half no word count can do: an assertion that every key in the family is still emitted by the server or is explicitly listed as deleted-on-purpose, so a code retired on the backend cannot leave a false sentence rendering off a test fixture.

found_in: Sweeping the payments.problem.* family for DEF-PAY-6327. no_receipt_queued says 'Sending receipts is a separate piece of work and is not built, so the customer will not be sent one automatically' - receipts.queue_receipt_for_recorded_payment has run on every recorded payment since 2026-08-18 behind an election that is default ON, and the code left RECORD_UNAVAILABLE in the same commit. grouped_bank_credits_not_matchable says 'Those deposits will stay unmatched' - CR-059 task 45 landed match_set on 2026-09-01 and the sentence renders on the same page as the control that matches them. introduced_in: 2026-08-18 (CR-009 C-13) and 2026-09-01 (CR-059 task 45) - the two commits that made each sentence false. Neither deleted the words it falsified.
escape_reason: A REFUSAL WHOSE STATED REASON HAS STOPPED BEING TRUE. Building the thing a refusal was holding and deleting the words that refuse it are two acts, and only the first one feels like the work - so the code comes out of the server, a comment beside it records that the sentence is now false, and the sentence goes on rendering in eleven languages. Nothing could catch it: the catalogue key is still present so parity is green, and the only test that asserts the sentence renders does so off a FIXTURE that invents the code (depositsSurface.test.tsx:107, PaymentsPage.test.tsx:598), so it passes forever after the server stops sending it. Six new sites inside an already-red gate change nothing about its verdict, so the diff printed 'no new gate failures' truthfully and the breach went through. For the classes themselves: the staff app is desktop-first and verified at 1280 and 1440 only, so a min-width variant is construction for a case the product does not have - build the wide layout as the BASE rule.

title: Every deploy with a deposit rule dies: rating/0044 adds fk_plan_deposit_rules_account_type as a VALIDATING constraint over rows customers/0054 orphaned, and its "0 orphans" was measured on one empty database
surface: 06-backend/apps/rating/migrations/0044_p0_4_p0_5_deferred_fks.py (_add, the eighth FOREIGN_KEYS entry). Root cause 06-backend/apps/customers/migrations/0054_br_cus_1079_account_types_are_the_tenants.py REFERENCING=("Account","AccountSubtype","ServiceRequest"). Live second exposure apps/customers/lookups.py AccountTypeLookupHandler.used_by (same three tables).
escape_reason: Two blind spots, both of hard-won law 7 shape ("a check reporting zero over a scope it silently excludes"). FIRST, the pre-check: the docstring published "plan_deposit_rules.account_type_id 0 rows / 0 set / 0 orphans" as a fact. The arithmetic was right and the SCOPE was one seeded dev database that was migrated from empty that morning and holds zero plan_deposit_rules rows at all - re-counted as superuser 2026-09-24, still 0 rows / 0 orphans there, and charges 31. A zero on a database with no history said nothing about an environment that has some. SECOND, and worse, the docstring claims "THE CONSTRAINT IS ITS OWN PROOF". It is not, under RLS FORCE: the migration role carries app.tenant_id = the NO-TENANT sentinel in its own rolconfig, so the ADD CONSTRAINT validation scan is evaluated against the B2 s3 policy, sees ZERO rows, and marks the constraint convalidated=t having checked nothing. Measured on PostgreSQL 16.13 this run, one real orphan present: manage.py migrate exits 0, convalidated=t, orphan still there; the same database read as the app role reports charges=0 where the truth is 31. So the same file dies on a role that can see the rows and silently certifies nothing on the role that actually runs migrations. Nothing else could have caught it either - rating/0041 measured plan_deposit_rules as 0 dangling on the BETA on 2026-09-19 and that was also true of that one database; customers/0054 own stranded refusal walks only its three ORM models, and plan_deposit_rules.account_type_id is a bare UUIDField with no FK, so it was invisible to the refusal and to the PROTECTed delete alike; and the default suite runs on SQLite, where ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT does not exist and _add returns early (law 14).
prevention: A migration that adds a constraint over existing rows states which database and which date its row counts came from, in those words, and never publishes them as a property of every database - the docstring now does. A deferred FK (a bare UUIDField) is repointed by name in any migration that rebuilds the table it points at; customers/0054 could not see it and nothing made it look. And ADD CONSTRAINT is not proof under RLS FORCE: the validation scan obeys the policy, so it certifies only what the migration role can see. Adding it NOT VALID says so honestly (convalidated=f) and still refuses every future insert, update and parent delete - all three proved on PostgreSQL.

None can see whether the BACKEND reader exists. transfer_record_api.py landed 2026-09-20 in 86a28f23d and the hold's stated condition expired that day; measured at the tip on 2026-09-24, the case still passed GREEN, four days on. Either put the expiry assertion where the condition lives (a backend test that fails when the route becomes resolvable, or a walkthrough that presses the door), or do not re-point the hold - release it and file the remaining gap as its own row. Also: a hold's reason was written in three places in this file (top comment, exceptions block, test docstring) and only one was amended when the reason changed; a hold belongs in ONE place that the test cites.

title: A cancelled transfer cannot be reached from anywhere: the list excludes it by design and the record page serves it

escape_reason: Nothing checks REACHABILITY, only rendering. transfer_reads.list_queryset carries .exclude(state=STATE_CANCELLED) and TRANSFER_FILTER_STATES drops cancelled from the filter options, both deliberately and both documented - the reasoning was that offering a filter option that can never return a row is a control reporting none for a reason the user cannot see. That was sound while there was no record page. There is one now: transfer_reads.RECORD_STATES maps STATE_CANCELLED to 'cancelled', so GET /transfers/{ref} serves a cancelled sale perfectly well and the screen draws it. So the record is viewable by TYPING its address and unreachable by clicking, which no test can see because every test asserts what a list renders and none asks what a list omits. Found by surveying all ten Accounts tabs for DEF-CUS-6532, not by any check.
prevention: The PO ruled on 2026-09-24 that a record is viewable in every state. A list that EXCLUDES a state is a second, invisible way to break that ruling - the door is present on every row and the row is simply not there. Either the excluded state gets a filter chip that admits it, or the exclusion is a PO decision recorded as one. This needs a ruling rather than a fix: showing cancelled sales by default changes what a clerk sees on a live screen.

title: The kiosk inbound door and the portal payment webhook publish as PUBLIC in the OpenAPI contract
surface: 06-backend/openapi/schema.json over apps/integrations/inbound_api.py::inbound_door and apps/portal/api.py::payments_webhook
found_in: lane PARTNER-CONTRACT, while fixing DEF-INT-6529 - the partner surface was 23 of the 25 operations with this shape; these are the other two
introduced_in: US-INT-044 (kiosk door) and CR-068/US-CWP-006 (portal payment webhook), both predating 2026-09-06
escape_reason: Same mechanism as DEF-INT-6529: drf-spectacular resolves a security scheme from a view's AUTHENTICATORS, and both doors deliberately carry authentication_classes = [] because a kiosk and a payment gateway present a credential in a header, never a session cookie. The generator sees an empty authenticator list plus AllowAny - the exact shape a genuinely public route has - and emits security [{}], which in OpenAPI means this endpoint needs no credentials. Both doors DO prove a credential before acting: the kiosk reads whatever its manifest declares (a key in a header, HTTP Basic, or an HMAC over the raw body) and the webhook verifies HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body against a secret only this deployment and that gateway hold, refusing every delivery when no secret is configured. The runtime is shut; the published sign is wrong. It hid the same two ways DEF-INT-6529 did: behind tc05 in any -x run of test_be11_openapi.py, and behind DEF-INT-4256 in the authenticator sweep, which has been red since 2026-09-06 and so has not been checking the public surface at all.
prevention: DEF-INT-6529's partner fix deliberately does not reach these two. A partner always presents Authorization Bearer, so ONE http/bearer scheme describes all 23 of its operations; the kiosk door's credential is declared PER MANIFEST (a header key, HTTP Basic, or a body signature) and the webhook's arrives under either of two header spellings, so one partnerKey-shaped scheme would be a different inaccuracy rather than the truth. The machinery is already built and waiting: core.openapi.declare_the_key_schemes defines any scheme an operation names and declares only what is referenced, and apps/integrations/partner_api.partner_key_required is the decorator pattern to copy. What is needed is a decision on how to describe a per-manifest credential (most likely one scheme per declared verification style, chosen off the manifest) and one for the gateway signature. Until then both are named in tests/test_be11_openapi.py::CREDENTIALLED_BUT_PUBLISHED_AS_PUBLIC, kept APART from the genuinely-public list rather than inside it, so the blind spot carries a number instead of being indistinguishable from an empty one.

title: file_defect.py and allocate.py disagree about which defect ids are taken: one reads the register across every ref, the other also reads commit messages
surface: 10-scripts/file_defect.py::known_ids vs 10-scripts/allocate.py::numbers
introduced_in: file_defect.py's first version; the gap widened when allocate.py gained _claimed_elsewhere
escape_reason: Both tools are correct about the world they read and neither knows the other exists. known_ids() walks ONE FILE - the defect register - across the working tree, HEAD, @{upstream} and every remote ref, so it answers 'which numbers has the register seen'. allocate.numbers() additionally reads commit messages through _claimed_elsewhere, so it answers 'which numbers has anybody claimed'. A sibling pushes the FIX first and the register row minutes later, which is normal and correct, and for that window the id exists only in a commit message. On 2026-09-24 four lanes collided inside forty minutes: file_defect.py handed out 6537, 6538 and 6539 while allocate.py defect --verify called all three TAKEN. Nothing downstream would catch it - a duplicate id in a 3,975-row register reads as a register, not as an error. Every collision was caught only because lanes were told to run --verify in the same breath as the push, which is a habit rather than a guard.
prevention: Have file_defect.py DELEGATE to allocate.numbers() and take the union, rather than growing a second copy of the commit-message walk - two tools computing the next free number out of different worlds IS the defect (the DEF-GOV-3756 family), so a second implementation would be the same bug wearing a fix's clothes. It must stay best-effort and warn loudly on stderr when it degrades, because nothing may stop a lane filing a defect. MEASURED, not assumed: with the delegation in place known_ids saw 4,090 ids against 3,975 from the register alone - 115 numbers the register cannot see. NOT YET PROVED RED: at the time of measuring, none of those 115 was above the register's highest id, so the fix changes no allocation today, and a red proof needs a constructed case where the highest claimed id lives only in a commit message. Do not ship it until that proof exists.

The message names a sibling and there is none, so the honest response - renumber - throws away two correctly allocated ids and leaves the commit message pointing at rows that will never exist.
prevention: Exclude the caller's own newly pushed commits, or say WHERE the id was found instead of asserting who put it there: 'TAKEN - in the register on <ref>' and 'CLAIMED - in a commit message only (<sha> <subject>)' are different facts and a lane can act on each. A check whose output cannot distinguish a real collision from the caller's own footprint is trusted and wrong, which is hard-won law 7's third habit.

title: P3.11's handed-back measurement is wrong on a money path: a reversal inside a locked batch never touches the batch's members, so the drift it prescribes always computes to zero
surface: 12-governance/02-decision-log.md (the 2026-09-24 FIN-P3 hand-back) · 06-backend/apps/payments/bankrec_read.py batch_detail/_member_row · 07-frontend/src/features/payments/DepositBatchPage.tsx
escape_reason: The hand-back states 'P3.11 NEEDS NO BACKEND CHANGE AT ALL - MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED' and prescribes the drift as the sum of members[].amount minus batch.recorded_total, over data the screen already holds. Measured on PostgreSQL against a real locked batch: reversal._write_reversal creates the reversing row with NO deposit_batch_id, and hard rule 4 forbids updating the original's status or amount - so the reversing row is not a member and no member row moves. DEP-260808-0002: recorded_total 2388.84, sum(members) 2388.84, sum(reversals) 501.33, live 1887.51. The prescribed arithmetic yields 0.00 drift on a batch that is 501.33 short, so the tile P3.11 exists to add would have affirmed that nothing was wrong. Nothing would have caught it: the figure is arithmetically correct, sumDecimalStrings is exact, tsc and every test pass, and no gate reads a rendered figure. The measurement was written from the served payload's field list rather than from the write path that produces the drift.
prevention: When a task says a figure can be computed from data a screen already holds, CONSTRUCT THE STATE and read the figure out before writing that down - the hand-back's own worked state (a locked batch with a reversed member) takes one service call and settles it. More generally: a claim that a drift is visible in a payload is a claim about the WRITE path, not the read path, so it is checked by finding the code that creates the drift.

title: Every money column on the deposit-batch screen renders LEFT-aligned: .fin-num is out-ranked by PlainTable's own [&_td]:text-left

title: This lane destroyed lane FIN-WIRE's uncommitted defect row while re-deriving the register onto a moved tip - the recovery procedure law 11 prescribes writes the tip's bytes and has no way to see a sibling's unpushed row

escape_reason: Law 11's re-derivation clause says to rebuild a shared file as THE TIP'S BYTES PLUS YOUR OWN EDITS. In a shared working tree that instruction silently discards any sibling row that is in the tree and not yet pushed, because 'your own edits' is the only thing the rebuilding lane can identify. Every check in law 11 then passes: the prefix is byte-identical to the tip (proved), the numstat shows insertions only, the file count is right and every hunk is mine - precisely because the destroyed row was never in the tip the diff is taken against. This is DEF-CWP-3771's shape with the blind spot pointed at a SIBLING instead of at the author's own earlier commit. file_defect.py cannot help: it appends and refuses to edit, so it is safe for writing and offers nothing for rebuilding. WHAT WAS LOST, verbatim as far as it was captured before the overwrite: '"DEF-LED-6677","2026-09-25","lane FIN-WIRE 2026-09-25, wiring DEF-LED-6664s first door","The batch journal screens /edit address loads no draft: it opens an empty composer headed Edit draft entries","07-frontend/src/App.tsx:1605 mounts /finance/journal-ent...' - the remainder of the row is gone. MITIGATING AND REAL: that row carried DEF-LED-6677, which lane FIN-COPY had already pushed for a different defect, so it required renumbering in any case.
prevention: Before overwriting a shared append-only register with tip-plus-mine, diff the ID SET of the working tree against the tip and name every row that is in the tree and not in the tip - each one is either yours or a sibling's, and the ones that are not yours must be carried across or their owner told before the write. That is three lines and it is the check that was missing here. The durable form belongs in push_paths.sh, which already refuses a moved register: it could print the orphaned ids at the moment it refuses, which is exactly when the lane is about to rebuild.

title: SEWER BASE-CHARGE REVENUE WAS POINTED AT 3010 OPERATING GRANTS ON A LIVE TENANT, AND NOTHING IN THE PRODUCT COULD OBJECT. PO reported it on Ottumwa Water Works: Finance -> Chart -> Where each services revenue goes shows Sewers USAGE revenue at 4120 Sewer and its BASE-CHARGE revenue at 3010 Operating grants, so sewer standing charges have been reported as grant income. Every other service points both halves at its own account. THE SEED IS NOT THE CAUSE and that was measured, not assumed: chart.SERVICE_REVENUE_ACCOUNTS maps sewer to (4120, None) - base is None, which BR-BIL-010 makes fall back to the usage account - and on the only tenant present in all thirteen local databases (Brazos Bend Utilities) sewer reads usage 4120 Sewer / base NULL, correct. So this is ONE tenants stored configuration, not a product-wide default. THE PRODUCT DEFECT IS THE ABSENT GUARD UNDERNEATH IT: tenancy._apply_service_gl_accounts validates ONLY seams.ledger_account_is_live (the account exists, is this tenants, is not deactivated) and asks nothing about what KIND of revenue account it is, and the screens own picker revenueAccountOptions offers every ACTIVE REVENUE account - 3010 Operating grants is seeded type=revenue category=CAT_GRANTS, so it is offered in the list and accepted by the server in silence. A clerk can point any services revenue at grant income on any tenant and no check anywhere says a word.
surface: 06-backend/apps/tenancy/services.py::_apply_service_gl_accounts (the only validation is seams.ledger_account_is_live) · 07-frontend/src/features/ledger/GlServiceMapEditor.tsx::revenueAccountOptions (offers every active revenue account) · data: tenant_services.base_revenue_account_id on Ottumwa Water Works · 06-backend/apps/ledger/gl_mapping_save.py (the orchestrating save)

escape_reason: EVERY CHECK IN THE REPO ASKS WHETHER THE ACCOUNT IS REACHABLE AND NONE ASKS WHETHER IT IS SENSIBLE. The FK proves the row exists, ledger_account_is_live proves it is this tenants and live, and the pickers own test asserts it offers ACTIVE REVENUE accounts and nothing else - which it does, correctly, and 3010 Operating grants IS an active revenue account. So the guard, the picker and the test are all working exactly as written and the wrong answer passes all three. There is no test anywhere that a services revenue mapping lands in the operating-revenue band rather than in grants, contra-revenue or any other revenue category. AND NOTHING RE-READS A TENANTS STORED MAP AGAINST THE SEED - a mapping is written once and never audited, so a mistyped pick is invisible from the day it is saved until somebody reads the chart screen by eye, which is how this one was found.
prevention: Two halves, and only the second is a code change. (1) DATA: re-point Ottumwas sewer base-charge revenue at 4120 Sewer - or clear it to NULL, which is what every other unsplit service carries and which makes it fall back to 4120 by BR-BIL-010. That fixes the FUTURE only: hard rule 4 forbids UPDATE or DELETE on issued invoices, invoice lines and journal entries, so every sewer base-charge line already posted stays in 3010 and past months stay misstated until the PO rules on a correcting entry. (2) CODE: give the mapping a KIND check on both sides of the seam - refuse a revenue account whose category is not operating service revenue, by name, in _apply_service_gl_accounts, and narrow revenueAccountOptions to the same set so the wrong answer is not offered in the first place. Then assert it: a test that points sewer at 3010 and expects a named refusal is the guard this had none of.

title: THE REFUND NUMBER SERIES IS RULED AND NOT BUILT, NOTHING TRACKED THE OWED BUILD, AND THE PO HAS NOW BEEN ASKED THE SAME QUESTION TWICE. OQ-PAY-12605 was CLOSED on 2026-09-23 on the PO words (a) Its own series, RFD-26-0001 - a refund gets RFD-{YY}-{0000} as a seeded default a tenant edits on Settings -> Numbering. Nothing was built. On 2026-09-25 the same question was put to the PO again and they ruled again: b - Give refunds their own number series - it is already there in setting -> configure numbering. THE TWO ANSWERS AGREE, WHICH IS LUCK RATHER THAN PROCESS - hard-won law 13 exists because a human answering twice from memory will eventually answer differently, and then the repo holds two genuine rulings that contradict each other. AND THE SECOND HALF OF THE 2026-09-25 SENTENCE IS NOT TRUE OF THE PRODUCT, checked three ways: core/numbering.py SERIES_CATALOG holds THIRTY-ONE series and none is a refund (no REFUND constant, no case-insensitive match for refund anywhere in the file); the live number_series table read inside a transaction with app.tenant_id set holds 31 rows and WHERE series ILIKE %refund% returns none; and apps/payments/refunds_and_credits.py already says it in its own words - REFUNDS HAD NO SERIES AND STILL HAVE NO NUMBER COLUMN. The PO is remembering their own ruling of 2026-09-23, not describing a screen. WHAT IT COSTS A USER: the account ledger prints a document number on 147 of 167 lines; 19 are opening balances and correctly blank, and 1 is a refund with no number anywhere. A refund is the only money document in this product with no human reference at all - the only token it carries is reference, the CHEQUE number, which is the BANK and not ours, and it is null on every ACH refund and on every refund before it is issued.
surface: 06-backend/core/numbering.py::SERIES_CATALOG (no REFUND constant, no catalogue row) · 06-backend/apps/payments/models.py::Refund (no refund_no column) · the issue path in 06-backend/apps/payments/refunds.py (nothing allocates) · 07-frontend/src/features/payments/refundsAndCreditsShared.tsx (number starts carrying it, OWED) · 07-frontend/src/features/tenancy/SettingsNumberingTab.tsx (31 rows, no refund row) · the seeded number_series table (31 rows on every tenant)
found_in: lane RULE, 2026-09-25, verifying the second half of the PO 2026-09-25 ruling against the product: the catalogue, the live number_series table and the payments module docstring, all three
introduced_in: OQ-PAY-12605 closed 2026-09-23 on the PO ruling (a) Its own series, RFD-26-0001 - the ruling landed and the build did not, and no register row was opened to carry it
escape_reason: A RULING WITH NO ROW IS A RULING NOBODY COUNTS. The owed build was recorded in exactly the three places a person only reads if they are already in that file - a docstring in refunds_and_credits.py, a comment in test_cr138_p4_4_p4_25_refund_reads.py and a comment in refundsAndCreditsShared.tsx - and in NO register, NO change request and NO task list. So nothing added it up, nothing went red, and the only thing that surfaced it was the PO looking at an empty cell on the account ledger and asking the question a second time. This is the same shape CLAUDE.md records for the OQ-1330 misread: a finding recorded only in the file you happen to be in is a finding nobody can count, and it goes on being invisible while everyone who wrote it down believes it is written down. NO GATE COULD HAVE SEEN IT EITHER - there is no check anywhere that a CLOSED question with an owed build has a row carrying that build, which is the general form and is worth more than this instance.
prevention: Build it, and it is small but it is not a few lines - measured: (1) a REFUND constant and one SERIES_CATALOG row in GROUP_BILLING with RFD-{YY}-{0000} as the first option, which takes every tenant from 31 series to 32; (2) a tenancy migration seeding that row for every EXISTING tenant, because hard-won law 4 says a seed change never reaches a tenant that already has one, and all thirteen local databases already do; (3) a refund_no column on payments.models.Refund plus its migration; (4) an allocation at ISSUE - not at request, not at approval - so the number is minted once on the act that creates the document; (5) the number surfaced on the refunds-and-credits list and the account ledger, and the locale keys fanned in through 10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py across all eleven catalogues. NOTHING IS BACKFILLED (hard rule 4): refunds already issued carry no number and inventing one would be a reference no document ever carried. AND THE GENERAL FIX IS THE ROW ITSELF - when a ruling closes a question but leaves a build owed, open a register row for the build in the SAME commit that closes the question, or the only thing that will surface it is the PO asking again.

title: LANE CLOSE CORRUPTED A SIBLING'S DEFECT ROW BY MATCHING ON PROSE INSTEAD OF ON AN ID. surface: 12-governance/10-defect-log.csv row DEF-LED-6701; the helper was lane CLOSE's own scratch push script, not a repo tool

title: work_orders.outcome HAS NO DATABASE CHECK CONSTRAINT AND LIVE DATA ALREADY HOLDS A VALUE OUTSIDE THE FIVE DECLARED TOKENS - outcome='completed' on 1 of 39 rows
surface: work_orders.outcome (no ck_ constraint) - tokens declared at 06-backend/apps/metering/connections.py:427-438 WORK_ORDER_OUTCOMES - will show on any grouping of work-order outcomes, including the work-order status the PO is considering for the Disconnects list
found_in: 2.351.90, lane TIDY, measured against a clone of the live smartbillhub database on 2026-09-25 with app.tenant_id set inside a transaction

escape_reason: NOTHING COMPARES A DECLARED TOKEN TUPLE AGAINST THE CONSTRAINTS ON ITS OWN COLUMN. Two of the three token columns on this very table ARE constrained, so a reader glancing at pg_constraint sees a well-constrained table and does not count. The suite runs on SQLite (config/settings/test.py hardcodes it), where a CHECK this migration never wrote could not be missed either way, and the ORM's own choices field is not a database constraint - anything writing through raw SQL, a data migration or a bulk loader bypasses it silently.
prevention: MEASURED, not inferred. pg_constraint on work_orders holds exactly four CHECKs - ck_work_orders_dispatch_state, ck_work_orders_has_anchor, ck_work_orders_one_assignee, ck_work_orders_source - and none on outcome. Row counts on the clone: 22 passed, 1 completed, 16 NULL = 39. THE MECHANISM IS WORTH NAMING: 'completed' is not a near-miss spelling, it is WO_COMPLETED from WORK_ORDER_STATES (connections.py:447) - a value from the sibling STATE vocabulary written into the OUTCOME column. WHY IT MATTERS NOW: the PO is considering showing work-order status on the Disconnects list. title: A cleanup loop killed EVERY lane's frontend server: pkill -f wearing a for-loop, on a box with five live worktrees

It built a pipeline that matches a command PATTERN and kills whatever comes back, which is pkill -f with extra steps, and the rule did not come to mind because the intent was tidying up rather than killing anything. That is DEF-172's exact shape one tool over - the ban reads as being about a named command, and the dangerous use is a throwaway convenience where the name never appears. The first pattern alternative was correctly scoped (a port this lane owned); the SECOND, 'server.mjs', matches every lane's frontend on a shared box, and nothing in the pipeline could tell the two apart. prevention: Kill only PIDs you recorded when you STARTED the process, and record them at start time in a file named for your lane. Where a pattern is unavoidable it must include something only this lane owns - its own worktree path or its own port - and it must be PRINTED for reading before anything is killed, never piped straight into kill. Cheapest durable fix: a 10-scripts helper that starts a server, writes its PID to a lane-named file, and stops only what that file lists. NOTHING WAS LOST HERE - dist/ is untouched on disk and a static server restarts in seconds - but the same loop aimed at a runserver would have cost a sibling a seeded database connection mid-walk.

title: G134 READS A FUNCTION ARGUMENT AS A CLASS TOKEN AND FAILS A CORRECT FILE — buttonClasses("primary","default") IS A CALL, NOT TWO CLASSES
surface: 10-scripts/gates/ (G134 route-b-utilities-compile) · reported against 07-frontend/src/features/reports/RunDialog.tsx:205

escape_reason: G134 reported 'two class tokens render NOTHING: default and primary, asked for by RunDialog.tsx'. Nothing renders either string. The gate reads source text and cannot distinguish a call from a class name, so a correct file fails and MERGE reads BLOCKED. Cheapest correct form: resolve the token against the declared class vocabulary AND require it to appear in a className/class attribute position, not anywhere in the file's text. title: A GROUP ROW'S `path` IS NOT A FILTER SET — APPLIED VERBATIM IT OPENS ZERO ROWS
surface: 06-backend/apps/reports/slicers.py::_emit · 06-backend/apps/reports/datasets.py PAYMENTS.filters · 05-prototype/09 Reports Build Brief.pdf p12 (P2.18)
introduced_in: 2026-09-27, lane REP-P2-MODEL, with slicers.group_rows
escape_reason: group_rows' own docstring states the guarantee — 'The path IS the filter set, so the rows behind a subtotal cannot be a different query from the one that produced it' — and no check anywhere runs a path back through the runner as filters. The slicer tests assert the path's SHAPE (dimension/column/value keys) and never its EFFECT, so a path made of the right keys carrying the wrong vocabulary passes every case. Hard-won law 1: a comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee.
prevention: MEASURED on real PostgreSQL 16 against the seeded demo tenant. runner.run('ar_aging', {'group_by':'consumer_class'}) emits one group row with path [{dimension:'consumer_class', column:'account_class', value:'Residential'}] over 30 member rows. Feeding that path back as filters: runner.run('ar_aging',{'class':'Residential'}) returns 0 rows; runner.run('ar_aging',{'class':'residential'}) returns 30. THREE mismatches, each enough alone: (1) the path's dimension is 'consumer_class' and the dataset's declared FILTER is named 'class'; (2) the path's value is the DISPLAY label and the filter's vocabulary is the CODE, which the row carries in a sibling column 'account_class_code'; (3) the path's column names the display column. P2.18 built on the path as served would open a 30-row subtotal onto ZERO rows under a chip saying Residential - the outcome the task exists to prevent. The fix is for the SERVER to emit each group row's reproducing filters beside its path, derived from the dataset's declared filter names and the row's code column, never assembled client-side; and a test that runs a group row's filters back through the runner and asserts the row COUNT equals the group's own 'rows' - an effect assertion, not a shape one.

title: REVENUE ANALYSIS SERVES SEVEN COLUMNS AND ITS DECLARED DATASET DECLARES NONE OF THEM

title: 44 OF 71 DATASET DIMENSIONS OFFER A SUBTOTAL THAT CAN NEVER BE OPENED
surface: 06-backend/apps/reports/datasets.py (every Dataset.dimensions vs its .filters) · 06-backend/tests/test_rep_p2_18_drill_through.py::test_every_groupable_dimension_of_every_dataset_can_be_drilled_or_is_named

title: Screen 4.1 renders a 500 from GET /reports/schedules as 'No results match these filters' with a Clear filters link
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/reports/ScheduledTab.tsx
escape_reason: DataTable has carried a FailedWithRetry block (BR-SHL-020, A18 section 4) since it was written, behind an OPTIONAL 'error' prop, and this screen never passed it one - so an errored query falls through to the zero-results branch. G13 is the gate for a prop nothing passes, and it is green: it reads the component's OWN file, where the prop IS rendered, and cannot ask whether any of the 95 consumers supply it. No DOM test drives a failing query, so 24 passing cases and tsc say nothing about it. MEASURED: 3 of the 95 files that mount DataTable pass 'error'; the other 92 draw an emptiness over a server that failed. Reproduced in a browser at 1440 on 2026-09-27: HTTP 500 from the list endpoint, and the screen told the clerk their utility has no schedules and offered a Clear filters link with no filter applied.
prevention: Every screen that mounts DataTable needs a DOM case that drives its query to a FAILURE and asserts the retry block, not only an empty list - and the honest fix at the component level is to make 'error' non-optional, so a consumer that has not thought about failure cannot compile. A prop that is optional and free is a prop 92 screens will leave out.

title: DataTable's error prop is optional and 92 of its 95 consumers omit it, so a failed list read draws 'No results match these filters' across the product

The component's FailedWithRetry block (BR-SHL-020, A18 section 4) is therefore dead UI on 92 screens, and each of those screens renders a server failure as ZeroResults - 'No results match these filters' over a Clear filters link, with no filter applied. G13 is the gate for a prop nothing passes and is green over it: G13 reads the component's own file, where the prop IS rendered, and cannot ask whether a consumer supplies it. A prop that is optional and free is a prop 92 screens will leave out, and no gate in this repo reads rendered output. Until then, a gate that counts DataTable mounts against error passes would put a NUMBER beside the gap instead of leaving it invisible.

title: Five of Phase 4's own tests have been RED on the branch since the commit that added them (P4.1-P4.8, 2.364.0), one of them a cross-tenant 404
surface: 06-backend/tests/test_cr142_p4_schedules_api.py
escape_reason: PROVED AT THE TIP, NOT ASSERTED: a clean worktree at 2b23c5fa0 with none of this lane's files present runs the five and reports '5 failed' in 37 minutes. They are test_a_schedule_whose_report_errors_keeps_its_row_and_advances (schedules.py:441 - asserts last_job_id is None after an unregistered resource and gets a UUID, because core_jobs.enqueue accepts the job and only the HANDLER refuses the resource, so the schedule does point at a job), and four in schedules_api.py: test_BR_REP_020_another_tenants_real_user_is_refused and test_a_fifth_cadence_is_refused_above_the_database (both KeyError 'error' - the refusal envelope has no such key), test_pause_clears_the_next_run_and_resume_recomputes_it (TypeError: '>' not supported between datetime and str - the wire returns an ISO string and the test compares it to a datetime), and test_another_tenants_schedule_is_a_plain_404 (assert 200 == 404).
