title: Accounts list Services column drops a chip silently when a service point carries no service code
surface: 06-backend/apps/customers/selectors.py service_codes_for_accounts — 'if code:' skips a point whose service is null; ACC-01 Services column

No gate reads rendered output and no test asserts the chip COUNT against the unit's service points, so a dropped chip is indistinguishable from an account that genuinely holds fewer agreements. title: The rate-change impact endpoint prices NOTHING on any tenant: apps/rating/seams.py passes code_label= to a gather function that stopped taking it on 2026-09-24, and a bare except Exception turns the TypeError into a business refusal
surface: 06-backend/apps/rating/seams.py:1147 base_charge_for -- fn(service_code, plan_base, schedule_base, code['amount'], code_label=code['code']); apps/billing/gather._base_charge_for takes (service_code, plan_base, schedule_base, code_base) and no code_label since 2b5c1b4c6. Reached from apps/rating/selectors.py rate-change impact (before_inputs/after_inputs) and apps/portal/seams/rating_seam.py standing_charge_monthly. Screen RAT-03 step 4, GET /rate-schedules/{id}/impact
found_in: 2.381.1 (branch claude/kind-goldberg-k0acqg, lane RAT-REDS, found by reading the 9 reds DEF-RAT-6980 counted and asking what the refusal actually said)
introduced_in: 2b5c1b4c6, 2026-09-24 (DEF-CUS-6550, v2.351.66 -- it removed the code_label parameter to shorten a refusal sentence; the seam that passes it was not amended)
escape_reason: A BARE except Exception CANNOT TELL A PROGRAMMING ERROR FROM A DOMAIN REFUSAL, and this one reports the programming error AS a domain refusal. seams.base_charge_for catches every exception and returns refusal=type(problem).__name__; the impact selector counts that account as base_charge_refused and UNPRICED, which is a legitimate outcome it is built to produce -- so the endpoint answers 200 with worst_case_pct null and every account unpriced, a sentence the product means. PROVED, not inferred: inspect.signature(gather._base_charge_for) is (service_code, plan_base, schedule_base, code_base) and calling it with code_label= raises TypeError: got an unexpected keyword argument. Nine tests in test_br_rat_091_rate_change_impact.py have said so since 2026-09-24 and nobody read them (DEF-RAT-6980). No gate in this repo reads a suite result and every workflow in .github/workflows/ is .disabled.
prevention: Two, and the second is the one that lasts. (1) Catch what billing actually raises -- its own named refusal -- and let a TypeError propagate, because a seam that swallows every exception cannot report a broken call. (2) A cross-module seam that resolves a PRIVATE function by name (getattr(gather, '_base_charge_for')) must assert the SIGNATURE it is about to call and not merely that the attribute is callable. The seam's docstring already records that it reaches into a private function because billing publishes no public one; this is the bill coming due for it, and the check is three lines of inspect.signature in the test that already exists for the seam.

introduced_in: b82615107, 2026-09-28 (CR-144-BRC07 task H4) - the commit that moved python manage.py migrate --noinput out of docker-entrypoint.sh into the new docker-release.sh. The three reasons it gives are sound and are not reversed by this row; what it did not add is the other half, a web task that asks whether the schema it is about to serve is the one its code was written against
escape_reason: NO CHECK EXISTS THAT COULD HAVE CAUGHT A SCHEMA/CODE SPLIT, AND THE ONE CHECK THAT LOOKS LIKE IT SHOULD IS BUILT NOT TO. Before b82615107 the split was impossible by construction - every web task migrated on boot - so the invariant was held by an implementation detail and never by a check, and moving the implementation removed the guarantee with nothing going red. Three things then passed over the outage. (1) The entrypoint verifies DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE, warns on ALLOWED_HOSTS and refuses on a bypassing RLS role, and asks nothing at all about migrations. (2) /api/health is deliberately shallow and tests/test_health.py::test_health_answers_with_the_database_unreachable pins it that way, so it answered 200 throughout - correct as a liveness probe, and the exact shape of CLAUDE.md law 7's check that cannot fail when it is read as readiness. (3) compose's backend healthcheck is a bare TCP connect to 8000, so it cannot see an application error either. The entrypoint's own comment PREDICTED this failure on the day it was written - a rollout that skips it starts tasks against an older schema, and the symptom is a column-not-found error from a view rather than anything that names the deploy - which is hard-won law 1 exactly: a comment describing a guarantee is not the guarantee, and the prediction shipped with no test and no gate beside it
prevention: The web task now asks the question at boot, the only moment the answer is both knowable and cheap: docker-entrypoint.sh runs core/schema_guard.py, which distinguishes THREE outcomes rather than the two manage.py migrate --check can express - CURRENT, PENDING (it names every unapplied migration) and UNREACHABLE. It REFUSES to boot on PENDING, because a task that answers 500 to every sign-in while its probe says ok keeps a useless task in rotation and names no cause, while a task that refuses is replaced and the previous revision keeps serving. It WARNS and boots on UNREACHABLE, because migrate --check exits 1 for both pending and unreachable and a bare exit-code read would turn a thirty-second RDS failover into a crash loop. SBH_ALLOW_PENDING_MIGRATIONS=1 is the typed override for a knowingly forward-compatible migration - hard-won law 3, the unsafe option is the one you type. /api/health stays shallow and its test is untouched: the guard is at boot so the probe never gets the chance to lie. G136 holds the two halves together - it fails if the entrypoint migrates again, if it stops calling the schema guard, if docker-release.sh stops migrating, or if the runbook stops naming the one-line recovery

title: push_paths.sh's tree-sync REVERTS a lane's own work, because its content-addressed test walks LOCAL history and counts the lane's own unpushed commit as proof nobody authored it
surface: 10-scripts/push_paths.sh tree-sync / 10-scripts/sync_stale_tree.py content-addressed test
introduced_in: the content-addressed test as law 12 prescribes it — git hash-object then walk git log for this path
escape_reason: Law 12's test asks 'is this blob an OLDER version of this same path?' and treats a HIT as proof that no lane authored the content here, so the file is safe to restore from the tip. The walk reads git log for the path IN THIS CHECKOUT, which includes the lane's own local commits. So a lane that commits locally to preserve work — exactly what law 11's 'commit small and commit often' asks for — makes its own blob look like a version the repo already had, and the next push_paths.sh run restores the TIP's bytes over it. On 2026-09-28 that silently reverted this lane's finished G35 fix; it survived only because the lane had also copied the file to a scratchpad and noticed the restore line in the output. This is law 11's own blind spot in a new place, stated there as 'every check in this law protects you from SIBLINGS; none protects you from your own earlier self' — here the tool actively uses your earlier self AGAINST you.
prevention: NOT FIXED HERE, and the fix is not obvious: the walk must exclude commits that are not reachable from the pinned tip, i.e. ask 'is this blob an older version of this path ON THE REMOTE' rather than 'in this checkout'. git log <tip> -- <path> instead of git log -- <path> is the one-token version and wants proving before it is trusted. Until then: after any push_paths.sh run, read its restored/LEFT lines and check none names a file you were editing. The tool already prints them, which is what saved this one.

title: 56 walkthrough scripts in 10-scripts/ each run a bare vite build, so not one of them can drive a local stack — the browser proof this repo relies on is incapable of passing, 56 times over
surface: 10-scripts/*walkthrough*.mjs and the other walk scripts — each carries its own 'npx vite build' line
introduced_in: f0739cfc8 2026-09-28 09:09 — CR-144-BRC07 gave .env.production a remote API origin; the bare 'vite build' in each script has always resolved as production mode
escape_reason: Vite resolves an unflagged 'build' as mode production, so each script bakes https://api-smart360.bynry.com into a bundle served from 127.0.0.1; server.mjs then sends a CSP header of connect-src 'self' and the browser enforces the INTERSECTION, so every API call is refused. It fails in the most misleading way available: sign-in reports 'That email or password is incorrect.' on correct credentials, and four lanes each lost a cycle rediscovering it alone. Hard-won law 6 says diffing the running app against the drawing is what finds defects no gate looks at, and law 7 calls a check that cannot pass worse than none — this is that, 56 times, across the exact mechanism the repo depends on for browser proof. ⚠ IT IS ALSO THE THIRD OCCURRENCE OF ONE ROOT CAUSE, AND THAT PATTERN IS THE REAL FINDING: DEF-DEP-7460 fixed it in 07-frontend/Dockerfile and walked no other caller; DEF-INF-7802 fixed 11-smoke-stack.sh and 08-qa/01-e2e/stack/boot_stack.sh; these 56 are the rest. A fix applied to the caller in front of you rather than to every caller is how one defect becomes three, and the next person to fix a build line will do it again unless somebody says so.
prevention: Each script's build line becomes 'npx vite build --mode compose' — the non-deployed mode whose API base URL resolves empty by construction, which is what 11-smoke-stack.sh and boot_stack.sh now use. NOT SWEPT HERE deliberately: it is mechanical, it touches files several lanes are in, and a 56-file sweep from one lane is the shared-file rewrite law 11 exists to prevent. The durable version is a single shared boot helper the walk scripts call, so there is ONE build line in the repo rather than 58.

title: The reports RLS tests demand ZERO rows with no tenant context from two tables whose policies DELIBERATELY admit tenantless shipped rows — the test is wrong, not the product
surface: 06-backend/tests/test_cr142_p0_10_reports_rls_pg.py via tests/isolation_helpers.py::RlsProbe.denied_without_context
introduced_in: the test as written — assert_denied_without_context is a blanket zero-rows assertion and cannot express an intentional OR tenant_id IS NULL clause
escape_reason: Measured on PostgreSQL 16 as sbh_rls_probe (NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS) with Redis running, so neither the broker nor a bypassing role is involved: test_p0_10_no_tenant_context_denies_every_table fails with 'report_definitions: a query with NO tenant context returned 46 row(s)'. So the product is behaving exactly as designed and NO TENANT'S DATA IS VISIBLE TO ANOTHER; what is wrong is that the shared helper's assertion cannot express 'deny every TENANT row, admit the platform's own'. This is law 7's LOOKING AT THE WRONG THING: a test named for a guarantee it does not actually measure on these two tables. It matters because a red test that is wrong is worse than no test - it trains readers to discount the file, and the same file holds cases that DO measure real denies.
prevention: Teach the probe the distinction rather than weakening it: denied_without_context should assert zero rows WHERE tenant_id IS NOT NULL, so a table with an intentional tenantless-shipped-rows clause is still held to deny-by-default for every tenant row. NOT FIXED HERE - isolation_helpers.py is shared by the whole isolation suite and reports is not this lane's module. ⚠ DO NOT 'fix' this by adding the two tables to an exemption list: that would stop the test asking anything about them at all, and the tenant half of each table still needs the guarantee.

title: The smoke stack builds a PRODUCTION bundle, so the stack it boots cannot reach its own backend
surface: tooling

prevention: Build the smoke stack with a NON-DEPLOYED mode (vite build --mode smoke), which scripts/deployConfig.resolveApiBaseUrl returns an empty base for — same-origin, which is what server.mjs then proxies. reported_by: lane CUS-RED-VERDICT (self-found while attributing the 53 customers reds)
title: Thirteen customers .dom.test.tsx files never call afterEach(cleanup), so a case can PASS on an earlier case's DOM — one already was
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/customers — NewConnectPaymentTaken.dom.test.tsx (fixed here) plus AccountServiceChips, AccountServiceChipsUnresolved, CustomerEditDialog, NewConnectRedesignSteps45, NewConnectServicesStep, NewConnectStepRefusal, NewConnectSteps78, NewConnectUnitsStep, ParkedBuildFinishesItself, accountActionOverlays, newConnectList, newConnectSteps12Redesign (twelve still open)

escape_reason: vite.config.ts declares NO global setupFiles, on purpose, so Testing Library's automatic cleanup never runs and each .dom.test.tsx must call afterEach(cleanup) itself. Thirteen do not. Without it every render() is APPENDED to the same document.body and document.querySelector answers from the FIRST case that drew a matching node. It stayed invisible while the payment boxes were drawn only when a payment was being taken; 22cf1c575 made them always-present-and-disabled, and from that commit three cases were reading the no-payment render from three cases earlier. Measured: document.querySelectorAll('#nc_payment_amount').length was 3. A case that reads another case's DOM can neither fail honestly nor pass honestly, and NOTHING in this repo looks for a missing afterEach.
prevention: afterEach(cleanup) added to NewConnectPaymentTaken.dom.test.tsx with the measurement in its docstring. The twelve others are UNFIXED and listed above — each is a case that may be passing on a neighbour's markup right now. The cheap durable fix is a gate: every file whose first line is the jsdom pragma and which imports render from @testing-library/react must also call afterEach(cleanup). That is greppable, unlike the fault it prevents.

title: G137 could not read an ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT at all, so a constraint B2 signs in that form is checked by nothing
surface: governance · gates · G137
escape_reason: G137 parsed CREATE TABLE and CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX and nothing else. B2 addendum r26 signs discount_versions' no-overlap constraint as an ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT, deliberately, because restating forty columns of a table the ORM owns would create a second source of truth for all of them — and the gate would have read that addendum as saying NOTHING, reporting its clean 32-of-34 verdict over a guarantee it never looked for. That is the exact shape it was written to stop: a declaration that LOOKS signed and is checked by nothing (law 1), reporting zero over a scope it silently excludes (law 7, fifth shape). Nothing caught it because B2 happened to contain no ALTER form until this commit, so the gap could not show.
prevention: parse_declarations now reads ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... EXCLUDE/UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY, and _selftest() — part 0 of EVERY run() — carries a synthetic ALTER and fails the gate if it is not parsed into a checkable declaration, or if its table is miscounted as a table B2 DECLARES. Proved red then green on the module path run_gates uses (not __main__, per DEF-GOV-3733): 33 of 35 declarations compared, 2 NOT BUILT on a clone at rating/0044, 33 built on the same clone with rating/0045-0049 applied.

escape_reason: No check reads the containment posture of a new refusal. rating.selectors.AmbiguousAuthorityTax is raised from a selector that gather._taxes_for calls through the seam; the run loop in billing/runs.py catches rating_seam.PricingRefused, gather.GatherProblem and BillingRuleError, and this is none of the three, so it would propagate out of the per-account transaction and end the run. gather already holds the exact pattern at gather.py:2028, where resolution_switch.RuledPathRefused becomes a GatherProblem carrying message_key, clerk_detail and message_params (DEF-RAT-7991's plumbing). UNREACHABLE ON ALL EXISTING DATA: measured 2026-09-29 on PostgreSQL 16 databases smartbillhub and sbh_clone_d8041g, taxes holds 2 rows, 0 dated and 0 (tenant, jurisdiction, kind) groups with more than one row. title: BR-RAT-115's last-tax floor looks up tax kind 'flat', which is not a tax kind, so a flat fee is invisible to the detach guard

introduced_in: unknown — present since the BR-RAT-115 detach guard was written

title: The overlap census called a stated-end overlap SUCCESSION, which rating/0046 refuses, so the operator loop had no exit
surface: 10-scripts/rat_schedule_overlap_census.py::_classify · ::_discount_classify · tariff_versions
introduced_in: the DEF-RAT-8000 chain, 2026-09-29 (rating/0045-0047 and the census landed together)

title: rating/0046 stopped a deploy naming two remedies, and neither could be carried out - a correction copies the window and nothing moves a stated end
surface: 06-backend/apps/rating/migrations/0046_def_rat_8000_close_open_windows.py::close_open_windows · 0048 carries the same text
introduced_in: the DEF-RAT-8000 chain, 2026-09-29
escape_reason: The refusal was written as the answerable question a stopped deploy needs, and nothing checks that an instruction in a raise can be performed. Remedy one, POST /rate-schedules/id/versions/vid/corrections, COPIES the window - that is what BR-RAT-104 verb 2 means - so the correction lands on the same window and the overlap survives; measured on PostgreSQL 16, following it produced the identical refusal naming the correction row. Remedy two, give the earlier row the end date it should have had, has no door: there is no PATCH on a version, update_rate_schedule classes effective_to as price content and refuses it once activated, and filing a new version does not reach the pair because _close_open_windows_before excludes a row whose stated end already precedes the new start. The census it pointed at is not in the image either - docker-compose builds this service with context ./06-backend. So a real deploy stopped with an instruction nobody could follow, which is hard-won law 2's mirror at deploy scale.
prevention: manage.py rat_resolve_schedule_overlap is the door and lives in 06-backend where the operator already is; it reports both readings, prints the command for each, refuses to choose a date, and refuses a superseded row, a draft, an inverted window, a date that leaves the overlap, a row an issued bill was priced past, and a database with no audit_log yet. 0046's refusal now names it. All nine refusals were proved firing on real PostgreSQL 16 and the end-to-end path was proved: refusal, report, decision, apply, migrate 0046 and 0047 both OK.

title: Closing two open windows writes the same end date on both, so they overlap each other - and two chain tests error at teardown on it
surface: 06-backend/apps/rating/services.py::_close_open_windows_before · tests/test_def_rat_8001_windows_close.py · tests/test_def_rat_8050_discount_overlap_pg.py
escape_reason: NOT MINE AND NOT FIXED HERE - reported per hard-won law 7 habit 1, and dated: both tests error identically at the pristine remote tip c95a36787 with none of this lane's changes present, proved in a separate git worktree. _close_open_windows_before writes new_from minus one day on EVERY open window older than the new start, so where two were open both get the SAME end and overlap each other from the later one's start. DEF-RAT-8001 fixed the half it was written for - a second open window never healing - and its test asserts only that older windows are CLOSED, never that they do not overlap each other, so the remaining overlap passes every assertion. It surfaces as an ExclusionViolation in Django's fixture teardown, which calls check_constraints and sets the DEFERRED ex_tariff_versions_no_overlap IMMEDIATE: on the tip the two test BODIES pass and only teardown errors, so the chain's own regression net is red in a way that reads like an unrelated harness problem. Unreachable on a fully migrated estate, because 0047's constraint forbids two open windows in the first place; reachable where 0046 ran and 0047 did not.
prevention: OWED, not built. The repair is a ladder rather than one date - each open row ending the day before the NEXT row starts, which is what rating/0046 pass 1 already does - plus an assertion in test_def_rat_8001 that no two windows of one schedule overlap, not merely that the older ones are closed. It is a money path in another lane's fix and is left for a ruling rather than taken unilaterally.

title: The overlap resolver read every tenant table with no app.tenant_id, so under RLS FORCE it reported a clean estate over the live overlap
surface: 06-backend/apps/rating/management/commands/rat_resolve_schedule_overlap.py::_report · ::_resolve · ::_issued
introduced_in: DEF-RAT-8070's own fix, 2.410.17 (the command shipped unscoped)
escape_reason: PROVED ON A SUPERUSER, WHICH IS WHY IT SHIPPED. Every proof ran as the postgres role with rolsuper and rolbypassrls, where policies are skipped entirely - and Django's own system check PRINTED THE WARNING on every single run: RLS IS NOT ENFORCED on this connection, every tenant policy is skipped for every query this process makes. That line was read and passed over. tariff_versions carries tenant_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.tenant_id', true), '')::uuid with RLS ENABLED AND FORCED, so it binds the table owner too and there is no role a deployment uses that is exempt; with the setting unset the predicate is NULL and every row is invisible. Measured as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role: count(*) on tariff_versions is 0 unset and 4 set, and the command printed 'No overlapping rate-schedule window on this database' over the very pair rating/0046 was refusing to migrate past. invoices, invoice_lines and audit_log are RLS-forced too, so the issued-bill count would have answered 0 bills on the one question that gates hard rule 4. The command's own message even WARNED that a role which cannot see every tenant's rows reports exactly this - a warning is not a guard, and no test could catch it because the suite's role bypasses RLS. G126 checks that reads name their tenant in apps/integrations only; nothing asks it of a management command.
prevention: Both modes now walk the tenants and set app.tenant_id per tenant, as rating/0046 does, and every read ALSO names its tenant in SQL - two mechanisms, because a rolbypassrls role is not scoped by RLS at all and would fold every tenant's rows into one report. The clean-estate line now states how many tenants were read. tests/test_def_rat_8070_stated_end_overlap.py asserts the tenant is entered for the tenant holding the overlap - NOT that the rows come back, which passes vacuously under the suite's role and is the assertion that let this ship - plus a structural check that each SQL constant names a tenant. Both proved RED on the shipped version. Whole path re-proved end to end as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role: report, the hard-rule-4 refusal with the bill visible, apply, and the audit row.

title: rating/0046 never checked a window is well-formed, so 0047 died on PostgreSQL's own message naming no row
surface: 06-backend/apps/rating/migrations/0046_def_rat_8000_close_open_windows.py::close_open_windows · management/commands/rat_resolve_schedule_overlap.py::OVERLAP_SQL · ::_resolve
introduced_in: the DEF-RAT-8000 chain, 2026-09-29
escape_reason: 0046 validated OVERLAPS and never validated that a window is WELL-FORMED. 0047 builds daterange(effective_from, COALESCE(effective_to + 1, 'infinity')) and daterange refuses a lower bound above its upper bound, so a row whose effective_to is two or more days before its effective_from raises DataException: range lower bound must be less than or equal to range upper bound at ADD CONSTRAINT - naming no tenant, no schedule, no row and no column. That is the exact outcome 0046's docstring says it exists to prevent. It reached a live deploy: 0046 logged 0 overlap(s) need a person, was marked applied, and 0047 then died on that message. THREE THINGS HID IT. (1) The offending row was the ONLY dated version of its schedule, and the resolver's overlap query builds the range inside an EXISTS over the other versions - with no sibling the expression is never evaluated, so the report came back clean too. (2) A test planting the fault on a one-version schedule PASSES on the broken code for the same reason - measured, and the case was rewritten with a sibling. (3) The test database already carries the constraint, so the fault cannot even be stored there without dropping it first, which is why no existing case covered it. The resolver ALSO refused the row (a backwards interval compares False against everything, so the overlap guard turned the command away from the one row it was being run for).
prevention: 0046 now refuses a malformed window FIRST, naming every row, with 0047's own predicate (effective_from > effective_to + 1) rather than the looser effective_to < effective_from - an end exactly one day before the start is an EMPTY range, which is lawful and is left alone. The malformed rows are held OUT of the overlap walk so the report does not name wrong pairs beside the real fault. The resolver reports them as their own section, accepts them as a repair target, and its overlap query now requires a row to be well-formed before a range is built from it. Four cases in tests/test_def_rat_8070_stated_end_overlap.py, all proved RED on the shipped code: the report ignored the row; the resolver refused it; 0046 DID NOT RAISE; and the report crashed with the production DataException once a sibling forced the range to be built.

title: Resuming a stopped Check runs the rest of the Check inside the clerk's web request instead of handing it back to the billing worker
surface: POST /billing/runs/{id}/check/resume (check_api.run_check_resume -> core.jobs.resume -> run_pending) · clerk check F1 / U3
introduced_in: bulk bill run plan A3 (2026-09-30), check_api.run_check_resume
escape_reason: Found by READING while writing the J73 F1 harness, not yet by running it (the machine was closed to Celery runs on 2026-09-30). run_check_resume calls core_jobs.resume(job_id), which calls run_pending -> run_job synchronously in the calling process, so the remaining accounts are checked in the HTTP request. A worker killed at 1,000 of 10,000 leaves 9,000 accounts; at the measured ~0.5 s an account that is over an hour of work in a request a gunicorn worker is given 60 s for (GUNICORN_TIMEOUT). The request is killed, the job record is left 'running' again, and the clerk sees the run not carry on - F1's pass bar. Every unit test of resume runs a handful of accounts inline, where the request finishes. Separately, after a worker SIGKILL the broker (redis, acks_late) redelivers only after visibility_timeout = CELERY_TASK_TIME_LIMIT + 300 = 8,820 s, so without Resume nothing carries on for about 2.5 hours. To reproduce: 10-scripts/j73_bulk_run_harness.py f1-worker-kill on a 10,000-account database.
prevention: Resume re-enqueues to the job's own queue (core.jobs dispatch) and answers 202; a test asserts the resume endpoint returns before the job body runs (JOBS_EAGER=false).

title: Every period-bounded meter_reads read in the bulk Check casts the partition key to a date, so PostgreSQL cannot prune and plans and scans all 28 monthly partitions on every statement
surface: backend — apps/metering/selectors.py (read_at__date__gte / read_at__date__lte, 39 uses across apps/), reached by the bulk Check through billing.runs.readings_for_account and billing.gather.gather_account
found_in: 10-scripts/bbr_check_cost.py profile --explain 4, PostgreSQL 16.13, tenant b27-cost, one account with electric, two water meters, sewer and a trash cart
introduced_in: the __date lookups predate the monthly partitioning of meter_reads; Django renders read_at__date__gte as (read_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date >= ..., an expression PostgreSQL cannot use for partition pruning
escape_reason: No check reads a query plan. The statements return the right rows, so every test passes, and on SQLite (the default suite) there are no partitions at all. The cost is a FIXED per-statement tax that grows with the number of partitions (28 today, 12 more each year) rather than with the tenant, so a measurement at one size never shows it as growth. Measured, warm, same statement: as issued 2.9 ms planning + 1.6-1.9 ms execution over 28 partitions; the same window written on read_at itself (>= 2026-09-01T00:00Z and < 2026-10-01T00:00Z) 0.19-0.29 ms planning + 0.05-0.09 ms execution over one partition. The bulk Check issues 29 meter_reads statements per account, 118-154 ms of its ~300 ms DB time per account.
prevention: Filter the partition key by a half-open timestamp range (read_at >= start at 00:00 UTC and read_at < end + 1 day at 00:00 UTC) instead of __date lookups on meter_reads, and add a PostgreSQL-only test that EXPLAINs one billing read and asserts it touches one partition. Owned by metering; measurement only here, no product code changed by this lane (see 04-docs/05-modules/07-billing/19-check-cost-measured.md).

title: A payment recorded while a Check batch is running is missed by that batch AND never flagged stale: payment facts are loaded once per 500 accounts but each result is stamped checked_at when it is saved
surface: backend — apps/billing/check_engine.py CheckContext.load_payment_facts (once per chunk of 500) with check_models.BillRunAccountCheck.checked_at (auto_now, the SAVE time) and check_staleness.stale_account_ids (flags a payment only when updated_at > checked_at); S31 Check tag Paid after cut-off
found_in: 10-scripts/bbr_check_cost.py race, PostgreSQL 16.13: three accounts checked, a 120.00 payment posted Oct 1 (after the Sep 30 cut-off) recorded on the third the moment the first was saved. Saved findings for the third: [service_not_connected]; sweep stale: False; a fresh check of the same account: [paid_after_cutoff, service_not_connected]
introduced_in: B12 (payment facts asked once per 500 accounts) landing beside OQ-843 option C's staleness sweep keyed on the save-time checked_at, both 2026-09-30
escape_reason: Every test checks accounts and records payments in sequence, never a payment landing DURING a pass, so the window between the batch's one payment read and each account's save is never exercised. The window is the batch's own length: 500 accounts at the measured 683 ms each is up to 5.7 minutes in which a payment is invisible to the Check and to the sweep alike. The clerk sees the account Ready with no Paid after cut-off tag and the bill goes out without the warning. B27 would batch-load readings and plans the same way and widen the same hole to them.
prevention: Stamp each saved result with the instant its facts were READ (the batch load time), not the save time, so the sweep's updated_at > checked_at comparison covers the gap; or re-read the batch's changed payments just before each save. Keep bbr_check_cost.py race as the PostgreSQL reproduction and turn it into a test. Must land before or with B27, which batch-loads more money-relevant reads.

title: Edit the seeded BASE-W (residential water base charge code, scoped to classes [residential, municipal]) through the S12 Charge Code wizard, change only the amount (e.g. $8.00 to $8.50) and press Save: the request is refused with 'We couldn't save this charge code. BASE-W-COM already covers this class.' even though nothing about the class was touched. Root cause: chargeCodeModel.ts's draftFromCharge (line ~335) only pre-fills the wizard's single-select Customer Class field when the stored code has EXACTLY ONE class; BASE-W has two (residential + municipal), so the field silently loads as 'Every class' with no visible error or warning. On Save, chargePayload (line ~377-378) reads that empty selection and posts applies_to_customer_classes:[] -- which the backend's one-live-base-per-service-and-class guard (services.py _base_code_rules) reads as 'applies to every class', so it collides with BASE-W-COM's own (commercial, industrial) scope and refuses the save. Net effect: ANY edit to BASE-W, or any other base charge code seeded with more than one customer class, was unsavable through this screen -- the clerk had to manually re-pick a single class first, which silently narrowed the code's real scope from two classes down to one.
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/rating/chargeCodeModel.ts draftFromCharge (line ~335, single customerClass only set when classes.length===1) and chargePayload (line ~377-378, empty customerClass posts applies_to_customer_classes:[]) feeding 06-backend/apps/rating/services.py _base_code_rules (empty list read as every class, collides with sibling base code)
found_in: 2.455.0, manual E2E charge-code walkthrough, editing the seeded BASE-W (residential water base) with no field changed beyond amount
introduced_in: 2.431.0, CR-156-BRC10 wave B charge-code wizard rebuild (d7cc0a392), which added the single-select customerClass field without a path for a code seeded with more than one class

prevention: A DOM case that opens Edit on a charge code seeded with two customer classes (e.g. BASE-W), changes only the amount, and asserts the save succeeds and the original two-class scope is preserved (not silently narrowed to one class or widened to every class).

title: No screen anywhere can open a disconnect case, so the Disconnect wizard (DSC-02) can never be completed for any account. Three possible doors were checked and all three dead-end. (1) Disconnects tab -> + New -> step 1 'Choose': selecting an account, a reason and services never calls any case-opening endpoint; Continue always refuses with 'No case is open' (no_open_case, BR-CUS-039), reproduced on a live, freshly transferred account (Maria Lopez, active Residential plan, an installed water meter, water+sewer+trash services) -- not an edge-case account, an ordinary one. (2) Requests -> Approve: the outcome picker offers only 'New connection' and 'Move-in' (APPROVE_OUTCOMES = ['new_connection','move_in'], serviceRequestEndpoints.ts:165); 'Disconnect' is not a selectable outcome in this screen at all, even though the backend's own _raise_disconnect (request_jobs.py:946-978) would open a case correctly the instant outcome='disconnect' reached it -- nothing in the frontend can ever send that value. (3) The standalone POST /accounts/{id}/disconnect-case (transfer_disconnect_api.py:901-923, open_disconnect_case) opens a case directly and has zero callers anywhere in 07-frontend. Consequence: as shipped, there is no click-path that creates a disconnect case -- the entire four-step Disconnect wizard is unreachable in practice, for every account in the product, not a walk-in-only gap.
surface: 06-backend/apps/customers/transfer_disconnect_api.py:901-923 (open_disconnect_case, zero frontend callers) · 06-backend/apps/customers/request_jobs.py:946-978 (_raise_disconnect, logic is correct but unreachable because 'disconnect' is absent from APPROVE_OUTCOMES) · 07-frontend/src/features/customers/serviceRequestEndpoints.ts:165 (APPROVE_OUTCOMES = ['new_connection','move_in'] -- the frontend constant that excludes 'disconnect' as a choosable outcome) · 07-frontend/src/features/customers/DisconnectWizard.tsx step 1 ChooseStep -- never calls any case-opening endpoint itself, only reads a server preflight
found_in: 2.455.0, manual E2E walkthrough: all three doors above tried in sequence on the same live account; Requests -> Approve's outcome picker was directly observed to offer exactly two choices, confirmed rather than inferred
introduced_in: 2026-08-28, commit 8700efbb9 (DEF-2030/2031/2032, 'three workflows get their doors') gave the case-opening endpoint and _raise_disconnect their code; the two-value APPROVE_OUTCOMES restriction's own introduction was not separately dated, but it is what makes both of those unreachable from the clerk-facing Approve screen
escape_reason: Every DisconnectWizard DOM test seeds a disconnect case directly against the fixture/database before mounting the screen, because that is the only way to reach step 2 onward at all -- so no automated test ever exercises the real precondition a clerk hits starting from a cold account. The Requests-approval path looked like the intended front door, since the backend's _raise_disconnect is correct and ready, but nobody had checked it against what the Approve modal's own outcome picker actually offers -- only a human clicking through the live screens in order found the gap.
prevention: Either (a) add 'Disconnect' to APPROVE_OUTCOMES (serviceRequestEndpoints.ts:165) and wire the Approve modal's outcome picker to offer it, which routes straight to the already-correct backend _raise_disconnect with no backend change needed; or (b) add a direct 'Open disconnect case' action (e.g. on the Account page or the Disconnects tab) calling the existing POST /accounts/{id}/disconnect-case. Either closes the gap; doing neither leaves the shipped Disconnect wizard permanently unreachable through the UI. A DOM test that drives the Disconnects tab's own + New button against a freshly seeded account with no pre-existing case -- never pre-seeding one -- would have caught this immediately.

title: A One-Time Bill that reaches draft state permanently blocks its billing period, and no screen can complete, fix, or cancel it. Reproduced live: an Interim one-time bill for account AC-2026-00059 (Priya Shah, Springfield Water Utility) was auto-saved as a Draft (BL-2611-000081) when the clerk navigated away mid-wizard, with no explicit 'Save draft' confirmation. Starting a new one-time bill for the same account and period (2026-10-10 to 2026-11-10) refuses with 'Already billed for this period,' offering only a link to the existing draft. On that draft's own detail page, every action is disabled: 'Fix this bill' says (billing.bill.action.correctDraft) 'A draft is not corrected -- it is re-run,' but re-running is exactly the action that was just refused as a duplicate. 'Cancel this bill' says (billing.bill.action.voidDraft) 'A draft is not canceled -- it is simply not issued,' treating the draft as harmless -- but it is not harmless, since it is what is blocking the period. Print, Download, View-as-sent and Open-in-new-tab are all disabled too, since nothing was ever issued. Net result: the draft is a permanent, unresolvable obstruction on this account's billing period, with the product's own two disabled-button tooltips pointing at a 're-run' path that does not exist.
surface: 07-frontend/src/features/billing/oneTimeBill/OneTimeBillPage.tsx (AlreadyBilledBanner, lines ~925-947: the duplicate-period refusal links only to the existing bill's static detail page, with no resume/overwrite-draft action) · 07-frontend/src/features/billing/oneTimeBill/OneTimeSummary.tsx:135-162 (AlreadyBilledBanner's only action is billHref, a plain link) · 07-frontend/src/features/billing/BillDetailPage.tsx:517-527 (voidReason branches to billing.bill.action.voidDraft for a draft, disabling Cancel) · 07-frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json:911,922 (billing.bill.action.correctDraft and voidDraft, the two tooltips that both point at a 're-run' path with no implementation)

introduced_in: 2026-09-30, the one-time-bill redesign (04-docs/05-modules/07-billing/11-one-time-bill-redesign.md) that introduced the Account/Services/Review/Send wizard and its draft-saves-on-navigate-away behavior; the void/correct draft-reasons predate it and were written for a different shape of draft
escape_reason: Every OneTimeBillPage test drives a single successful run start-to-finish, or checks the duplicate banner appears, but none navigates away mid-wizard to produce a stranded draft and then tries to resolve it afterward -- so the round trip from draft to dead-end was never exercised. The two disabled-button tooltips also read as complete sentences on their own, which is why nobody flagged them as promising a path ('it is re-run') that the draft-duplicate check actually forecloses.
prevention: Either (a) make starting a new one-time bill for an account+period that already has a DRAFT (not an issued bill) resume or overwrite that draft instead of refusing as a duplicate -- which is what both disabled tooltips already claim happens; or (b) add a real 'Discard draft' action to the bill detail page for exactly this status, distinct from Cancel (which is correctly reserved for issued bills). A test that starts a one-time bill, abandons it mid-wizard, and then asserts a second attempt for the same period can actually complete would have caught this.

title: A charge code with a blank Kind is permanently unrecoverable, and it is invisible to a plan's base-charge-code picker. Reproduced live: charge code BASE-S ('sewer base', Active, on Springfield Water Utility) has Kind = blank -- its own detail page shows 'Kind: -' and the Edit wizard's 'What is it?' field renders disabled with 'Choose' (the placeholder) as the selected value, so Kind can never be set after creation. Because a plan's Sewer base-charge-code dropdown only offers codes it can recognise a Kind for, BASE-S never appears there; a clerk correcting an unrelated field on the plan (the effective-to date) had the dropdown re-submit with whatever code it treated as the only option, which bound Sewer's base to a stray, unrelated charge code ('CHARGE CODE SEWER', 5.00) instead. That mis-bind is what then made the whole unit refuse to price at all ('Nothing on this unit is priced. Check its plan and meters.') on a later bill attempt. The underlying BASE-S row cannot be fixed; the only way forward is a brand-new charge code.
surface: The charge-code edit wizard (CHG-02, 07-frontend/src/features/rating/ChargeCodeWizard.tsx), step 1 'What is it?' combobox -- rendered disabled whenever the stored kind does not match one of its known options, with no path to set it on an existing row. The plan's own service-base-charge-code picker (PlanWizard.tsx) silently excludes any charge code it cannot resolve a Kind for, with no indication to the clerk that codes are missing from the list for this reason.
found_in: 2.481.6 (live Springfield Water Utility tenant). BASE-S's Kind has read blank since at least the point it was first opened for this E2E walkthrough; how it came to be blank was not observed directly -- only its current, unrecoverable state was.
introduced_in: Not dated precisely; BASE-S is a tenant-seeded base charge code, so the blank Kind is either a seed-time gap or a save that bypassed the Kind-required validation at some point before this write-up
escape_reason: Every charge-code test creates or edits a code through the wizard, which has always required Kind at step 1 -- so no test exercises a row that already has a blank Kind sitting in the database, which is the only way to reach this state. The plan's base-code picker was never tested against a catalogue containing a Kind-less row, so the silent exclusion (rather than a visible 'N codes unavailable, see why' note) was never caught.
prevention: A one-time data check for any existing charge code with a null/blank kind, migrated to a real value or retired; and a DB-level NOT NULL constraint on charges.kind going forward so this state cannot recur. Separately, the plan's base-charge-code picker should state when it is excluding codes for an unresolvable Kind, rather than silently shrinking the option list to whatever remains -- that is what turned an unrelated date correction into a wrong service binding.

title: One-time bill refuses 'plan_has_no_tariff_for_service' with an empty service name, even when every charge code, plan binding, rate-schedule version and account fact involved is individually confirmed correct. Reproduced live on Springfield Water Utility: account AC-2026-00059 (Raj Patel), period 2026-11-11 to 2026-12-11, Interim one-time bill. Response: {code: BIZ-COMPLETENESS, message_key: billing.oneTime.err.nothingPriced, params: {reason: plan_has_no_tariff_for_service, service: '', service_code: null, detail: "plan ... resolves to no tariff for any service in this run's scope..."}, br_ref: BR-BIL-020}. Directly verified as not broken: the plan's three service rows (Water from BASE-W/BASE-W-COM .00, Sewer from BASE-S2 .00, Trash from BASE-T 5.00/cart), the plan's effective window (09/01/2026-12/31/2026, covering the period), the account's service agreements (Water/Sewer/Trash all 'Still open' since 10/10/2026), the account's customer class (Residential, matching every rate schedule's own class scope), the meter's assignment and size class, and each rate schedule's own in-force version. Reproduced after a full logout/login and in a fresh incognito session, ruling out browser or session cache.
surface: 06-backend/apps/billing/one_time.py and/or gather.py -- the plan_has_no_tariff_for_service path that returns service='' and service_code=null, which suggests the resolution loop is failing to enumerate services at all (an empty scope) rather than failing to price one named service. Not isolated past this point -- the fault is below what the UI and the charge-code/plan/rate-schedule/account screens can show.
found_in: 2.481.6 (live Springfield Water Utility tenant), manual E2E billing walkthrough, immediately after fixing DEF-RAT-9350's underlying charge code (creating BASE-S2 and rebinding the plan's Sewer row to it)
introduced_in: Not isolated -- first observed on this account/plan, during the same session that fixed several other charge-code problems on it; whether it predates those fixes or was introduced by one of the plan corrections made during this session is unknown
escape_reason: Every other diagnostic available from the UI (plan services table, rate schedule versions, account service agreements, customer class, meter assignment) was checked individually and each is correct, so none of the product's own screens can currently explain this refusal -- it needs engineering-level access (logs, a debugger, or a direct query against the resolution engine's intermediate state) to isolate further, which this walkthrough did not have.
prevention: The error should name which of the three services actually failed to resolve (service and service_code should never both be empty/null on a real refusal), or state plainly that the scope itself was empty and why, rather than reporting a blank service name that reads identically to 'nothing was even attempted.'

reported_by: developers@bynry.io, code-grounded research pass; corroborates a defect the team had already reported informally (their bug #5)
title: A moved-out (closed) account shows 'No services' in the Accounts list view and in any chip/badge built from the shared service-codes selector, even though its own detail page's Service table (Started/Ended columns) correctly shows the same services with their end dates. Root cause found in code: service_codes_and_drops_for_accounts (06-backend/apps/customers/selectors.py:1517) and its singular fallback service_codes_and_drops_for (same file, line 1886) both skip every agreement with agreement.ended_on is not None via an unconditional 'continue'. A closed account has every service agreement ended by definition, so both functions always return an empty code set for it -- the list's Services column and any other badge/chip fed by this selector go blank, while the detail page's own Service table reads service_agreements_for(account) directly, unfiltered, and still shows every row with its real Started/Ended dates. Matches the team's independently reported bug ('a moved-out account shows blank services in list view despite its detail view showing them correctly') and the Track A finding that a Transfer immediately followed by a Move-out on the same account surfaces this.
surface: 06-backend/apps/customers/selectors.py:1517 (service_codes_and_drops_for_accounts, feeds the Accounts list page's Services column) and :1886 (service_codes_and_drops_for, the account_row singular fallback used by the detail page's HEADER badges, runbooks, and single-account test helpers) -- both apply the same ended_on filter; the detail page's own Service CARD/table is a separate, unfiltered read and is why the two screens disagree
found_in: 2.492.1+ (live Springfield Water Utility tenant), code-grounded research pass ahead of a fresh E2E testing round; not yet re-confirmed live in the browser this pass
introduced_in: Not isolated -- the ended_on filter and its DEF-CUS-6917 skip-counting mechanism are both already in place and documented in the function's own docstring as deliberate (skipping an agreement whose service point cannot be resolved); this filing is about the ADDITIONAL, undocumented consequence that a fully-closed account (every agreement ended) silently reduces to zero services through the exact same line, which the docstring does not discuss
escape_reason: No existing test compares the list-view Services column against the detail page's Service table for the SAME closed account -- each screen's own test fixtures only ever assert against accounts with at least one still-open agreement, so the all-agreements-ended case was never exercised end to end.
prevention: Either the list/badge selector should use account.closed_at (or 'any agreement, filtered by end date relative to a reference date the caller controls') instead of unconditionally skipping every ended agreement, or the list's Services column should fall back to 'services this account HAD' for a closed account the same way the detail page's table already does, rather than rendering an unqualified empty state that reads as 'this account never had service.'

title: Production shows other utilities' charge codes inside one utility: editing plan 'Solar pilot Plan' (ottumwa-water-works, 2.526.0) lists BASE-SOL 20 times as 'Several base codes', and the Charges step lists AFTER-HRS ~13+ times - the charges table is being read across tenants (hard rule 1)
surface: 06-backend/apps/rating/plan_reads.py _base_block (pool: Charge.objects.filter(deleted_at__isnull=True, is_base=True, service__code=...)) and form_options (Charge.objects.filter(deleted_at__isnull=True, is_base=False); also Tax and Discount.objects.all()); GET plan read + GET /plans/form-options; screens Plans & Rates > Edit plan steps 1, 2 (Charges) and 4 (Review)
introduced_in: unknown - the reads have relied on RLS alone since they were written; the leak needs RLS to be ineffective on the production connection
escape_reason: These reads carry no tenant_id filter and rely on RLS alone (charges_tenant_isolation, db/rls_rating_w1.sql). charges has UNIQUE(tenant, code), so 20 live BASE-SOL rows in one result cannot belong to one tenant: the production query is returning many tenants' rows, which needs either a role that bypasses RLS (superuser/BYPASSRLS) or a charges table without ENABLE/FORCE/policy in the production database. A pooled GUC from another request would show ONE other tenant, not twenty. core/rls_guard.py checks only rolsuper/rolbypassrls of current_user at boot and is tolerated by SBH_ALLOW_RLS_BYPASSING_ROLE or config.settings.local; it never checks that tables actually carry their policies, and DEF-2760 says no deployed role's attributes were ever recorded. The isolation suite proves the policies on a test DB, never on the production DB. Unverified until someone runs on prod: SELECT tenant_id,count(*) FROM charges WHERE code='BASE-SOL' GROUP BY 1; SELECT rolsuper,rolbypassrls FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname=current_user; SELECT relrowsecurity,relforcerowsecurity FROM pg_class WHERE relname='charges'; SELECT * FROM pg_policies WHERE tablename='charges'; and check uq_charges_tenant_code exists (rules out the alternative: one tenant holding 20 duplicate rows).
prevention: Boot guard should also assert, on the live DB, that every tenant table has relrowsecurity+relforcerowsecurity and its policy (not only role attributes), and refuse the escape hatch in production; record DEF-2760's per-environment role answer. Plan-form reads should filter tenant_id explicitly as selectors.plan_builder_queryset and resolution_catalogue already do (belt and braces). Billing base resolution (resolution_catalogue) already filters tenant_id, so the bill's base choice is not taken from this pool.

escape_reason: counter_code composes CTR-{yymmdd}-{initials} and nothing stores it; _session_by_ref recomposes over the day's tills and refuses two matches, reasoning only about two DIFFERENT people sharing initials. title: Customer PDFs cannot show Hindi, Japanese or Korean text: Liberation Sans (ruled) has no Devanagari, Kana/Kanji or Hangul glyphs, so each such character prints as '?' - no worse than the Base-14 writer it replaced
surface: backend
found_in: review
introduced_in: design
escape_reason: Known consequence of the Group H ruling (decision log 2026-10-23: 'Liberation Sans has no Devanagari, Japanese or Korean glyphs ... filed as a defect, not silently patched with another font'). Measured: an 18-character Japanese agreement body prints 18 '?' on the old page_print writer AND on the tagged writer; Hindi and Korean the same. core/tagged_pdf.representable() substitutes and names every character outside the font's cmap so Pango cannot fall back to a host font. prevention: Pinned by tests/test_def_bil_f06_tagged_pdf.py::test_hindi_japanese_korean_are_no_worse_than_before (parity with the old writer, the substitution named, and no second embedded face). title: Reminders, disconnection notices, receipts and letters are not PDFs at all: they are frozen and handed to the print vendor as plain text, so the Group H ruling's 'every PDF a customer receives' has nothing to tag for them

escape_reason: Group H ruling item 4 (2026-10-23) lists reminders, disconnection notices, receipts and letters among the customer PDFs. Measured in the code: notifications/frozen_documents.py freezes the pdf_print channel as text/plain ('PRINT FREEZES THE TEXT WE ACTUALLY HAND OVER, NOT A PDF'), dispatcher._payload hands the vendor that text, and the only PDFs attached to customer email are the agreement and the move-out final bill (notifications/attachments.py callers). So no inaccessible PDF exists for these four kinds; what does not exist is the PDF. Nothing caught the mismatch because the ruling was asked as a question about PDFs and these documents were assumed to be PDFs.
prevention: Not built in lane A11Y-H: producing a PDF letter (and deciding which artefact is frozen and sent to the vendor) is CR-049 task 6, still open. title: Issuing a bill now spends about half a second rendering its tagged PDF (0.524 s against 0.0055 s before), about 17 extra minutes of one worker per 2,000-bill run - not yet measured on a real bill-run job
surface: backend
found_in: review
introduced_in: implementation
escape_reason: Measured 2026-10-23 on 4 cores, median of 5 renders after a discarded warm-up, Ann Arbor-like sample bill: WeasyPrint tagged page 0.524 s, hand-written page 0.0055 s (about 95x). Bill runs issue in background jobs (billing/run_jobs.py, core.jobs), so no 60-second web worker is at risk on a run; a single-bill issue inside a request (a correction, a one-time bill, a fee bill) adds about 0.5 s. At the top of T5 (40,000 accounts) a whole-tenant issue is about 5.8 hours of single-worker CPU if issued in one run. The cost is the PO's ruled library, not a bug; the defect is that nobody has measured it on a real job.
prevention: Measure one real cycle's issue job on PostgreSQL with the image's HarfBuzz-subset build and record wall time per 1,000 bills; if the job's time budget is short, render the tagged page in the job's own parallel workers. Do not move the render out of the issue transaction - BR-BIL-033 makes a renderable, kept document a precondition of issue.
